Chewy and are like regular brownies.  I baked them about 10 minutes longer so they weren't quite so soft.  My husband and I both love them!

I have made these 2 times for the family, and grandkids. WOW, we all love them. So soft, and chocolaty. Better than any brownie I have ate, ever. My husband never has liked brownies, in his life, and he can't get enough of these.

At first when I saw this in the grocery store, I wasn't sure it would be a good idea.  But since I have been recently diagnosed with gluten intolerance and I also LOVE brownies, I decided I would give it a try.I WAS NOT DISAPPOINTED!!I followed the directions to the T but also added in some chocolate chunks (about half a bags worth - I LOVE chocolate too!! and some Madegascar vanilla bean paste about 1/4 tsp) and I made this mix in a mini cup cake tray that had about 24 mini cupcakes in it.  The entire batter made the 24 mini cupcakes.The texture was on point - it was moist, tender, decadent and the small mini cupcake servings were just the right portion sizes - two mini cupcake were enough to sate my sweet cravings.  And the remaining brownies freeze well.Betty Crocker has done an awesome job.

column9: YUM-better than regular gluten filled brownies!
column10: I was diagnosed Celiac 6 weeks ago and just started trying to bake gluten free treats the past week (I am a chef so I figured I would be able to make something decent!). I tried the Betty Crocker yellow cake mix and was not successful. Next, I baked some tollhouse chocolate chip cookies with Domata Flour (gluten free) and also was not successful. I was about to give up for a while but my boys asked me to make the gluten free Betty Crocker brownies I had in the pantry. I added some chocolate chips and waited.....not anticipating good results at all. I can tell you, I am in heaven! I have been taking little pieces from the corners before dinner (don't tell the boys!) and just cannot believe how great this is. If you want a brownie that tastes....yes....BETTER than what you have had in the past, try this. We have some birthdays later in the week and I plan on making another pan and serving with vanilla ice cream. I do not think my family will even know it is gluten free! Buy and enjoy, be happy!

column9: Better than the BC regular brownies!
column10: We have six in our fam and we all love, love, LOVE this recipe!  We undercook it a small bit to make the center a bit softer and they were gone by that night!  Right now we are in the beginning stages of cooking GF because our son was diagnosed with celiac, but this one is a HUGE hit here!  the only downside is the price and no coupons that I have found for it yet!  We like it better than the regular brown mixes by BC.Thanks BC for coming up with GF mixes!

These are some awesome tasting brownies when made when following the directions on the package.  I'm pretty sure no one can tell that they are Gluten Free, even my picky sister.  I like to substitute geletin for the eggs, and that worked well.  No real different in taste or texture.  When I tried to substitute applesauce for the butter like I do with other mixes it didn't bake correctly.  It got sticky and didn't want to come out of the pan.  The only draw back to this mix is that you need to use the butter which makes it high in saturated fat.

I personally think these brownies are amazing and would challenge anyone to tell the difference between these and a "regular" mix.  The only thing I noticed is that they may have dried out a tad faster than brownies with wheat in them, so next time I will make sure that I put them in an airtight container.  Even if I wasn't trying to follow a wheat free diet, I would make these brownies any day!
These brownies are very good!  They taste almost like the gluten version.  Definitely will be buying these again.  Anxious to see how the other Gluten Free products from Betty Crocker taste like.

The first time I made these brownies they were dry (I like cakey brownies).  The next time I made them I used olive oil instead of butter and added an additional egg.  Wow!  They are now my family's favorite brownie.  Thanks betty Crocker!

I used these for my son for his school instead of cake for cupcakes.  I put two heaping regular teaspoons, from your silver wear not measuring spoons, size in each paper cupcake liners and it ends up cooking level with paper cupcake liners. Then I cooked for 25 minutes.  Let them cool and frosted and decorated them. YUM they were good.  Makes 10 cupcakes.  I also used an extra egg on this batch and added around 1/2 to 3/4 cups chocolate chips.They were a hit.

I can't wait to try these. I have been longing for a *flaky* brownie!!! I'm so happy to see that a major brand has put their research teams to work on Gluten-Free recipes so that we can again enjoy convenient, quality products!! I can't wait to see these products on the grocery and health foods store shelves in Hilo, Hawaii.

I try to stick to a GF and dairy free diet b/c I have MS.  I bought this brownie mix hoping for the best b/c some GF stuff isn't also tasty.  I used a 1/4 cup of canola oil instead of butter and let me just say-these brownies are delicious.  Definitely has a dark chocolate taste, which I prefer.

column9: Only made them once, but very happy with result
column10: I've been GF about 1 year now, and to be honest don't miss cakes, brownies and the like that much. With that said, the novelty of these (buying GF items in a regular grocery store) meant I had to try them.The batter turns out VERY thick. It's okay, just spread it out very well. I used a 9x9 square pan. If I make these again I will cook them a few minutes less than the box recommended as the edges were a little tough. With that said, these turned out GREAT, just like regular brownies.I bought the chocolate chip cookies next - I can't wait to try them!

First, let me say that I can sympathize with the reviewer who gave this a low review because the first time I made these brownies, they were so hard they almost broke the knife when I tried to cut them!  The second time I made them, however, I added an extra egg and also waited a little longer for the melted butter to cool.  They turned out a little more cake-like and were thicker and easier to cut.  These brownies are the best of all the gluten free Betty Crocker mixes I have tried and are comparable in taste (and a little cheaper) to other gluten free brownie mixes I have bought in specialty and health food stores.  In fact, I always had to doctor those mixes a bit by adding extra chocolate chips, but, with this mix it is not necessary.  This mix is easy and quick, which is really nice when a yummy dessert is needed and time is of the essence.  Good job on this one, Betty!I keep experimenting with this mix to make it "just right."  My latest experiment worked out the best so far!  I sacrificed my last can of pumpkin for this one! (Pumpkin seems to have disappeared off store shelves this year!)  Use three eggs, 1/3 cup canola oil, and 1/2 cup of "sacrificial" pumpkin puree.  Beat together well before adding the mix.  Bake for 30 minutes at 350 degrees in a 9 X 9 pan sprayed with baking spray.  These turned out really moist, cake-like, and cut easily!

These brownies are simply amazing, especially considering that they're gluten-free. I've tried a few gluten-free brownie mixes and these stand out above the rest. The great thing about gluten-free brownies is the fact that the chocolate usually masks the fact that they're gluten free. So, taste wise, gluten-free brownies tend to be fairly comparable to regular brownies. These are rich, chocolaty, and delicious. As for texture, typical gluten-free brownies are dense and feel more like fudge than brownies. These brownies, though a little dense are a little lighter than most mixes and gives the feeling of a standard brownie. If you're eating gluten-free and looking for a dessert fix, then I'd suggest indulging in these.
These are so close to what I remember Betty Crocker's Fudge brownies tasting like!  They need to be eaten on the first day because they get crumbly on the second, but oh, they are SO good!

I've been eating Gluten Free for six years.  What did I miss?  Real brownies.  Gluten Free Pantry makes good brownies.  But these brownies by Betty Crocker are JUST LIKE "REAL" BROWNIES!  Everyone in my family likes them (I'm the only GF person in the house.)Oh, one other thing.  Try Betty Crockers Chocolate Cake.  AMAZING TOO!My wife did some research and found out that these mixes are made at a special GF plant in Canada.  So put all your fears of cross-contamination aside!THANK YOU BETTY CROCKER!

These brownies are awesome!  My family is GF, but often for events we go to I don't make GF things just because others aren't used to the taste/texture.  However, not with these!  I have fooled many people with these GF brownies!  They are very fudgy, but I love them!  5+ stars!  I hope they come out with even more GF products!
These brownies are so amazing! I was prepared to be disappointed in these brownies as I am in most gluten free products, but these were moist and delicious. You won't be disappointed!
Baked a batch last night and they were great!  These are the closest to gluten brownies in both taste and texture.  We had ours with a scoop of ice cream :)
These are a tasty, easy alternative to making GF brownies from scratch. I just wish they weren't so high in sugar. We subbed plain unsweetened applesauce for the oil and they came out very well.
Weve made this three times now, Everytime it has ben great. One batch came out a bit sticky but otherwise no worries. Definately worth buying/Trying.

column9: Very Comparable to the Real Thing but Costly
column10: I've had these brownie a couple of times and have found both times that they taste and look like regular brownies.  They do dry up quicker so need to keep them covered.  I'm glad that they are good because the price is pretty steep!!!  I'd buy again but not on a regular basis due to costs.
This is the BEST gluten free brownie mix out there.  Finally, a major company has taken notice and is providing really tasty GF dessert mixes!  Way to go, Betty and company!
Wonderful!!! They taste like regular brownies.  By far the best gluten free product I have tried yet.  Can't wait to try the cake mixes.

My neighborhood Kroger just started stocking the Betty Crocker GF mixes, so I bought 3 mixes on Friday, prepared the brownies this morning, and took them to a church event today.  There were 4 celiacs in attendance, plus one who has decided to eat wheat-free.  They all loved them, and two of the celiac women have been living gluten free for 20 years, so they've tried every mix and every recipe out there. Everyone declared these brownies to be the very best they have ever had anywhere.  All the husbands (who eat wheat) tried them, too, and the guys are anxious to have them again!  The batter is very stiff, but so easy to make (just add melted butter or margarine and 2 eggs, stir and bake).I also like Gluten Free Pantry Truffle Brownies, but it is so wonderful that another major name-brand manufacturer is coming into the gluten-free world (Chex paved the way!) with such an excellent product.  The availability of the Betty Crocker mixes will be a big plus, but the price on Amazon is certainly far better than my local store.  Oh, it is so nice to have delicious options!Thank you, Betty Crocker!

Easiest mix ever!!! Just like I remember the regular wheat filled mixes being, in 5 minutes or so the brownies are ready to go into the oven. And the results are delicious! These brownies were chewy and thick and really, really good.

These brownies are excellent!  I can't say enough good things about the flavor!  My husband has celiac disease and I was so excited to see Betty Crocker come out with these mixes.  These brownies were so good my husband and I were fighting over the last one...and I'm not even gluten free!!  I have never felt the need to write a review on Amazon, but these were just so good!  I hope Betty Crocker continues to make these and more gluten free products!

column9: WOW - the BEST gluten free brownies out there
column10: WOW was all I could say when I tasted these.  They're the closest thing to "real" brownies that I've had since having to go GF 10 years ago.  I do like other brands but none have tasted like real brownies to me - with the chewy texture and flaky top - until I tasted these.  My whole family devoured them and some of my family didn't even suspect they were gluten-free.Many, many kudos to General Mills for offering gluten-free options (Chex is now GF too!!) thus raising awareness of GF among a wider audience.  Hopefully this will be the start of many more GF options from mainstream companies!  Now if they'd make GF Cocoa Puffs...
My kids and husband got SOOO sick from this product!!!  Shocking it was!  This is SO not GF.  I won't touch Betty Crocker with a 10 foot pole now.

column9: Beware of gluten in this product
column10: The brownies are delicious but my boyfriend (who has celiac disease) had a sudden and severe gluten reaction within 15 minutes of eating the first brownie.  He hadn't eaten anything else for several hours so we know it had to be the brownies.  Celiacs, eat at your own risk!!
I cant seem to get this to cook properly. It is either overcooked and hard as a rock or runny & way to sticky.

column9: not the same GF brownie mix
column10: The first time I made this mix it was outstanding, to the point I doubted it was actually gluten free.  Today made mix and it was totally different in making it and had totally different taste/texture.  Totally lacked any chocolate taste or smell.  Soon after eating it I developed the same sharp stomach pains that happened with the chocolate chip cookie mix I made the week before. Very disgusting products, sadly!
If you have to substitute eggs in the recipe, this mix is not for you.  The brownies turned out to be a sludge which became as hard as a rock.

Firstly this is NOT gluten free. Secondly the mix is terrible, very very dry as batter, and very dry and crumbly and rock hard around the edges when cooked. Ate 1 and threw the rest away. NOT WORTH BUYING!

Fabulous brownies!If you're like me, you want to know the ingredients before you buy.  Here they are:Sugar, semi-sweet chocolate chips (sugar, chocolate liquor, cocoa butter, soy lecithin, vanilla), cocoa processed with alkali, rice flour, potato starch, corn starch, xanthan gum, salt.  Contains soy ingredients.It tells you to add: 1/4 cup butter melted and 2 eggs.Happy GF Baking!!

If you have missed the ease and familiar taste of a boxed brownie mix try these!  Betty Crocker's GF brownies are an amazingly close contender to their original brownies.  They smell the same, look the same, and taste pretty darn close.  It was lovely to add butter and eggs and have yummy familiar brownies in under a half an hour. We are thrilled that a major brand has jumped on the gluten free band wagon, we hope many more companies follow!
These are without a doubt, the absolute BEST Gluten Free brownies EVER!!  AMAZING!!!  Even flaky on top!!  I can't wait to try the other new GF mixes by Betty Crocker!

I recently went gluten free and I tried another brownie mix that cost $7 or $8 and wasn't impressed. I learned about the new Betty Crocker mixes right at the beginning of June before they were available, and kept checking in the grocery stores around here to see if they had them. I found them at Price Chopper last Friday and made them today, and the batter tastes like regular batter, even though it's a lot thicker. Once I baked them, the whole house smelled like chocolate, which didn't happen with the other mix. They taste SO good. They're really chocolatey, and a little bit chewy and are just like regular brownies. The Amazon price is a deal - I paid $4.49 at the store, and I would pay that much again, but with the Amazon price SO much lower... I'd rather buy them here. DEFINITELY worth the money.

I regard this as a good starter for something more.  By itself, it makes good brownies, with a regular consistency that's neither cake-like nor brittle.  But there's nothing distinguished about the product.  Indeed, if you make it according to the package directions, it runs a bit dry (add about a tablespoon of oil to keep it from getting crispy).Instead, use this as a foundation and build on it.  I've had success turning this into something special by mixing in a few spoons of mint or raspberry jelly.  Or add a quarter cup of dark instant coffee for a special kick.  With either of those, consider adding in a pinch of cayenne pepper.  I'm not kidding: cayenne really brings out chocolate's hidden qualities.If you simply make these brownies according to the package direction, they'll be okay.  Nothing much stands out about them, but theyre better than bad.  But if you grab this opportunity to get adventurous and play with your food, you can really turn this adequate mix into a fun dessert that will keep your family coming back for more.

I've baked for several restaurants over the past 15 years, and now that I have to live a gluten-free lifestyle, I've tried many recipes. This mix is even better than any recipes I have tried. They are terrific!

These make delicious brownies.  SO easy to mix and bake.  I made mini brownie muffins and baked for only 15 minutes and they turned out PERFECT.They were soft, moist, chewey and SO chocolatey.  Really good.

I make these for my daughter, the only member of our family that needs to be GF.  These brownies are EXCELLENT!  Even my husband and I can't help but have a few ourselves--they are really quite indistinguishable from the "real" thing.  My daughter also has allergies to casein (milk protein) and I've had no troubles substituting a casein-free margarine for the butter called for in the recipe.The only downside to these brownies is that they don't hold up very well after a few days (they get quite hard).  This isn't usually a problem and we manage to eat them pretty quickly (the recipe makes a 9x9 pan, which we cut into 9 brownies).  I have not tried freezing them to preserve them longer but that has worked well with other gluten free brownie recipes in the past so you may want to give it a try if longer term storage is necessary for you.

column9: Made me very sick!!!NOT Gluten free
column10: Just like some of the other posts, its made me and my 3 yr old daughter very sick. I cant handle small amounts of gluten. Were 100% gluten free. We ate these for our bedtime snack and both of us felt so bad in the morning we went back to bed and slept 2 1/2 hours and had all the other symptoms of eating a large amount of gluten! the chocolate cake from Betty CRocker did the same thing!General mills cereals that says GF do the same thing to us! Beware! Make your brownies from scratch!

column9: Very good, but there is better
column10: These were good, but tasted comparable to regular gluten brownies.  Gluten-Free Pantry Truffle Brownie Mix, on the other hand, is moister, has more flavor, and is hands down the very best brownies (gluten-free or not) we have ever tasted.  The Gluten-Free Pantry Brownies always receive raves wherever we bring them, and our non-celiac friends are willing to go out of their way to find them.  It's a shame to think new celiacs will purchase these because they are more conveniently found in grocery stores, rather than experiencing the best in gluten-free baking.They're good, but not the best.

My husband is a long-time celiac, and we manage just fine by being careful.  He can tolerate trace amounts of gluten -- in soy sauce, for example. But this Betty Crocker brownie mix gave him the tell-tale gut-ache that says -- IT'S NOT TOTALLY GLUTEN FREE.  Celiacs beware.

Thank you Betty Crocker for a product that is simple to prepare and one that might soon be available in mainstream markets.  Received mine through Amazon yesterday and promptly made them up as directed.  Super easy to prepare, directions clear, but flavor was just okay and thought there was a slight chemical taste (thinking maybe it is the cocoa used in the mix).  There was also mini chips in the mix which I am not sure really improves the flavor.  In the future for a better result, I will still reach for my standard brownie recipe using "Pamela's Gluten Free Baking and Pancake Mix", unsweetened chocolate baking bars, and "Pamela's Products" Brownie recipe (found on their website).  But, for friends who wish to mix up a batch of brownies for my child without a lot of fuss, this Betty Crocker Gluten Free Brownie Mix would be just the right product.

We are new to the Gluten Free world as my daughter was diagnosed with Celiac about a month ago.  After several disappointing products, we pretty much decided just to stick with foods that are naturally gluten free.  The breads and baked goods had been just awful!  I bought these with subscribe and save thinking I would need something gluten free and quick just to have on hand.  I made the first "test" batch tonight.My changes:Used 3 eggs instead of 2 (there wasn't enough liquid to incorporate the powdery mix otherwise).I baked for only about 25 minutes (checked at 20 and again at 25 and toothpick came out clean the 2nd time).I am thrilled...about 1/2 the price of the other mixes we have tried and they taste great!  No stomach issues either and since the the mix is made in a gluten free facility and advertised as gluten free by a reputable company, I highly doubt it actually contains gluten as other reviewers had suggested.Now we can't wait to try the cookies and cakes!Hopefully as gf becomes more mainstream more delicious and inexpensive products will become available.

Kudo's to Betty Crocker for taking on gluten free!  This is a fabulous formulation, much better than what I've  tried to duplicate from scratch, and maybe the best gf brownie mix yet...  I've converted the box recipe to make chewy chocolate cookies, which is even better than the brownies!  My family prefers these cookies to any other regular cookies they can have.  WOW.Make up the recipe as directed on the box, but let the batter sit for 15-30 minutes to dissolve the sugar granules.  Preheat oven to 350.  Line cookie sheets with parchment paper.Use a cookie scoop to drop dough onto lined cookie sheets, leaving plenty of room to spread out--about 2" between cookies.  (A small scoop will make about 20 cookies, a medium scoop will make about 12 cookies)Bake 1 sheet at a time in 350 oven for about 12-13 minutes for small size, 15 minutes for medium size  The cookies will be flat and shiny, but set.Remove from oven and cool for several minutes on cookie sheet so the cookie can harden and set up, and not fall apart when removed with a spatula.  They will retain their shape if left to cool on a flat surface.These make rich chocolate cookies that are crisp around the edges, but incredibly chewy and soft in the centers.  I've tried chilling the dough to see if it will bake up more "fluffy", but they still flatten out quite a bit.*The cookie can be used as the cookie in ice cream sandwiches as well, but I think they are better assembled and eaten immediately, unfrozen, rather than made up in advance and frozen to firm up the ice cream.

Love this product and I'm not even gluten-free! I saw it and wondered if it tasted as good as regular brownie mix and wonder of wonders-- it tastes better. Trader Joe's gf brownies don't compare. I also LOVE that it doesn't have a lanudry list of ingredients. Betty Crocker keeps it simple and keeps it good, which is a nice surprise. Stock up, chocoholics!

Delighted to have found a GF brownie mix - only it got us sick as you get with a typical gluten allergic reaction.  Ate a brownie at 10 am, was sick at 11, bloated, gut pain.  Didn't realize it was the brownies - ate another and the same thing until i had a full blown colitis attack on top of the pain.  My husband who is NOT allergic to gluten had the same reaction.  There is something seriously wrong with this product.

Put this in an 8" square pan and you'll have 9 perfectly sized brownies to eat and NOT SHARE with normal people.  This is for US.  We know who we are, and we're not gonna let those normals eat our brownies!!!!  MINE!I need to do some experimenting with thinner brownies, maybe to cut out more pieces... smaller... but to make it last longer?  Really, one box makes only one serving, but you have to trick yourself into splitting it up into "servings" hahah...  servings.  It's your time to eat some brownies, dig in, and don't let them have any!

column4: BettyBoop "Andre Gide says: It is better to b...
column10: I loved the Brownies!I'm the only one in my family who has become sensitive to gluten, so I tested the brownies out on them to see how good they really are...my family devoured them! They said that they taste like "normal" food lol. So I got the thumbs up and made more. I added peppermint extract to one batch and it tasted like thin mint cookies. Delicious. I will definitely buy these again because they are the best gluten free brownies I've had so far. They don't even have that funny after taste like a lot of gluten free foods. So I think Betty Crocker is on to something here. And I like it! I suggest that you buy these whether you are gluten free or not.{{{By the way, it states on the box that it's made in a gluten-free processing factory, so I'm not sure if the people complaining about stomach aches actually had a gluten reaction or a reaction to another ingredient. I was fine after eating the brownies, but it usually depends on how much I eat for gluten to affect my stomach. It always affects my skin, and I didn't break out after eating these...so I guess just know your body and eat the brownies accordingly.}}}

I've tried every GF brownie mix I've come across in the last 5 years, and this is the best.  They bake up with the same flakey, shiny top that regular brownies have.  I've made them for gluten-eating people and they can't tell the difference. So glad a mainstream company is now offering GF options.Some reviews say this isn't 100% GF, but my daughter eats these with no problem and she is very sensitive.  If her food is prepared with even a contaminated utensil, she will become sick within an hour.  Betty Crocker makes all their GF mixes in a dedicated GF facility.

These brownies are delicious! They blow the other store bought brands out of the water. You would think they would taste a little funky, but that's not the case with these. They not only taste great, but they're gluten free. Without any flakey tops or dry insides, everything's great. If it's brownies you're looking for, give Betty Crocker a shot. I think you'll be glad you did.

I was so grateful when Betty Crocker put out some gluten free alternatives.  The brownies are absolutely perfect.  There is nothing missing at all, not in taste or texture.  In fact I think I like them better than brownies full of gluten.  Even my husband who has no issues with gluten found them to be delicious.

I'm in a house with 3 celiacs that love some dessert.  We have tried every brownie we can find.  This mix is the BEST GF brownie we have had to date.  I have baked them when we had friends over and the enjoyed the brownies and would not have guessed they were GF.  You can add extra items such as nuts, chocolate chips, etc if you like extras.  The sugar content is quite high for these.  So if you watch sugar grams, you should be aware of this.  Serve this warm with some vanilla ice cream and you have a great GF dessert.Also, the price for the box of six that I bought was great.  In the grocery store, these can be $3.50 - $5.00 a box.
Finally, a product that is as easy to make as the old style. Easy. Great tasting.  Love them.  After 9 years without a brownie, it was a little overkill on my part.  Thank you Betty Crocker.

Taste good, easy to make.  However for the price, I expected a full 9x13 pan, not an 8x8 pan. So I'll stick to making them from scratch. I am thrilled though, that a well known company is taking on gluten free items.  Who knows? Maybe it wont be long until we can buy little debbie snacks too. :)

My mom made this brownie mix for me during a visit.  The taste and texture are great and it's wonderful that they stuck to pretty natural ingredients.  However, I have my doubts as to how "GF" it really is, because it gave me my usual gluten stomachache.  I ate the brownies a couple of times over the next few days and each time I got that characteristic stomachache.  Hate to post a negative review because I'm so supportive of mainstream efforts to make GF foods available, but the truly gluten intolerant and celiac crowd should watch their reactions to this product carefully.

column9: Thanks Betty Crocker for a Superior Product!
column10: I was diagnosed with Celiac disease in April 2011, and this brownie mix has been the best thing that I ever stumbled upon.  The brownies are downright DELICIOUS.  They bake very nicely...and the flaky crust that forms on top is delectable. Most of my pans of brownies mysteriously lose four corner pieces moments after leaving the oven...I dont know why :)The cost is steep when compared to normal non-GF mixes, but if you think about it, gathering all of the necessary GF flours, xanthan gum, etc. to make your own, costs much much more than getting this mix...plus it wouldn't taste nearly as good.Thank you Betty Crocker for your GF efforts.  I will be a customer of yours for life so long as you keep making these delicious GF products.

What's the worst part of eating gluten free?  The sandpaper feel when biting into those GF brownie mixes.  This mix from Betty Crocker breaks that mold.  The brownies from this mix a moist and just sooooo good.  The fact that I can buy a case from Amazon is even better.

column9: The best brownee mix you can find.
column10: We purchased this product because we are gluten intolerant.  Our expectation was that it might be almost as good as regular brownee mix.  The truth is that this mix is better than any other brand we have tried even before becoming gluten intolerant.  Be sure to add walnuts to the mix.  It's just a spectacular product.  Thank you Betty Crocker for designing this one.

I just made these today, and I have to say that I'm pleasantly surprised.  These will definitely go on my list of guilty pleasures.  The taste and consistency are such that you wouldn't be able to tell that these are gluten-free if you hadn't seen the box and made them yourself.Just a note for those who might try to veganize these.  I'm not vegan, but I have done some vegan baking, and I've also taken a food science class or two.  Trying to do your standard vegan substitutions for this mix probably won't work.  The non-glutinous flours and starches in this won't react the same as if there were regular all purpose flour in it.  That's one of the main reasons that this mix calls for the use of butter instead of oil, like a regular box brownie mix.  It's the saturated fat in the butter that's helping to hold these gluten-free flours and starches together.  Saturated fat is solid at room temperature.  Oil is not.  It's that saturated fat that's helping to give these brownies their structure.  Using Earth Balance margarine might help, because it does have saturated fat.  However, it doesn't have as much of it as butter.  You might need to get a bit creative by using half Earth Balance and half coconut butter.  Coconut butter has almost twice the saturated fat of butter, but Earth Balance is a bit more solid at higher temps.  The combination of the two might achieve the desired effect.  Also, using Ener-G egg won't provide enough emollients for this mix.  I would recommend using some flax goo (Google flax egg if not sure) in addition to the Ener-G egg.  The Ener-G egg will give the brownies some rise and the flax goo will add more moisture and additional cohesion to make sure that these things don't just crumble when you cut them.I haven't tried the above recommendations yet, so I can't give a 100% guarantee on the results, but it's a decent starting point to experiment.  The end result, done properly, is definitely worth the effort.

This Betty Crocker Gluten Free Brownie Mix is the best brownie mix, it is just as good and maybe better than "regular" brownie mixes!  This price is just a little less expensive (when you add in shipping) than in the local grocery store but it can be hard to find sometimes in the grocery stores.A great product!

I am gluten intolorent and love these brownies, my husband is not and loves these more! My husband has been sweet and headed to the store a few times and purchased these for me, he has also baked them, and by the time I have gone to get one out of the pan they are almost all gone! We have 4 and 6 year old picky girls that also are big fans! I love that our small town grocery store carrys these.

Account holders wife here.  If you can eat them all before the day is over they are fine. The next day they will be hard and that is in a covered pan that I make other things in and nothing else turns into a hockey puck. I was diappointed.

Finally, something easy and tasty that's gluten free for dessert! THANK YOU BETTY CROCKER!!! Turns out PERFECT, every time! I like my brownies a bit fudgey, so I double the amount of butter in the recipe (and totally lie to myself about the calories and cholesterol). Worth it for the taste, as an occasional treat.  :o)
Pretty tasty, but of course doesn't taste like homemade.  Be sure you grease the pan well, or you'll be fighting to get the brownies out!
These are awesome. The batter was so thick I could barely spread it and I was worried. They came out fudgy and dense with a great top with a little crunch. You wouldn't know these were gluten free.

column9: JUST LIKE THE REAL THING! AWESOME!
column10: I first saw these GF brownies here on Amazon. I was skeptical and did not want to buy a whole case and end up not liking them. I found them in my local grocery store (almost $5 per box) and got a box. The first time I made them was for just my husband and I. He did NOT know they were gluten free and talked about how GREAT they were! Then I made them when we had people over......AFTER they ate them and complimented them I let them know they were gluten free.....ALL were shocked. These are moist and so good. Not gritty, grainy or the other weird textures you get in some other brands. There are little chocolate chips in the mix that when baked make little pockets of chocolate explosion. I am verrrrrry impressed with this and will keep buying! ---- I also mixed in nuts and that was GREAT! One time I decided to up the chocolate and added some Enjoy Life allergen free choco chips......that was super good! But not really needed as these are yummy enough on their own!

column9: Finally, a GF everyone wil eat!
column10: I'm not GF myself, and this is the first GF brownie mix I've tried that wasn't either weird in texture or downright gross. These taste like...brownies! They're a little bit different in texture than brownies made with wheat flour, but I suspect if they were served to me without note, I wouldn't notice the difference. I think they're  just as good as the homemade GF brownies I've made. I have GF friends & customers, and I hate making two separate batches of desserts, but I also hate serving something that's only appealing to someone who never gets to eat wheat. This is a great solution.They make a normal sized pan and the price is right. Yay!

Good brownies! Only wish Amazon had listing of ingredients for all BC Gluten Free Mixes!!! Had to find in store first because BC didn't have ingredient list either... Made for a pot luck dinner and no one knew they were gluten free. Husband enjoyed having dessert w/ his friends.

I spotted these in the grocery store (a lady had five boxes in her cart).  How perfect for a thank you gift for a neighbor who has gluten intolerance!  I made up the mix and was a little concerned to see how stiff the batter was, almost the consistency of thick mud pies.  The box warned that the dough would be heavy, so I restrained my desire to add more liquid.  Putting it in the baking pan required forcibly pushing it around with the spoon to reach the sides.It came out of the oven looking like brownies, but I was still worried.  When I gave them to my neighbor, he was ecstatic to have gluten-free brownies.  His dessert options had been severely curtailed.Later when he returned the baking dish, he raved about the brownies and how good they were.  He froze some of them for later (and didn't share even with his wife).He's going to be searching the stores looking for more Betty Crocker gluten-free dessert mixes.

These brownies were so delicious. I added the cookie mix to the batter and made cookie-brownie swirls. For Father's Day my mom made the wheat kind, and I made the g-f kind, and everyone there said the g-f ones were better. I also made a plate of just g-f brownies, and I added a handful of chocolate chips to it just in case it wasn't moist enough, and I ate almost all of them myself. They were crinkly on top, just like regular brownies. I have missed that. They are perfect.

These Brownies are so good. I have been Gluten Free for over 3 years and i have tried many different kinds of GF treats. I feel that these Brownies are way better than Pamela's Brownies and cheaper which is very nice on the wallet. These taste so close to Gluten Brownies, i think that these brownies would be easy to give to someone not on a GF diet and they would not be able to tell the difference.I am very excited to try the other treats that Betty Crocker came out with:)

I am new to the GF world and was very excited when a friend told me she saw Gluten Free Betty Crocker mixes at the store.  I bought the Brownie mix and gave it a try yesterday.  I would be shocked of this mix is truly GF.  That was the most miserable I have been since I went Gluten free.  Although there is no wheat flour in the mix, I am guessing that the cocoa powder is milled in a plant that processes wheat.

These were loved by everyone that tried them!  I co-host a holiday tea every year and we were looking for foods that were gluten-free that everyone would enjoy.  During our experimentation in the months leading up to Christmas, I found these on the shelf and gave them a try.  Wonderful!  They don't "rise" as high as regular brownies, and the batter seems particularly thick if you're not used to it, but they are equally tasty.  Everyone that had them had no idea they were gluten-free.  Added bonus: they're also dairy free, so lactose intolerant folks enjoyed them as well.
this product is easy to fix and tastes really good if you eat it the same day.  it seems to dry out easily if kept longer, even if refrigerated.

I'm glad a mainstream company (Betty Crocker) has some GF products available. That said, this mix is pretty dull. I am a professionally trained baker. Now that I'm GF, I'm lazy too, and don't keep a bunch of different flours around to create baking mixes, so I rely on prepared mixes a lot to make baked goods at home.I've made 2 boxes of this product.  It tends to be dry, hard, and not especially flavorful despite the chocolate chips in the mix. Brownies are one of those things that are easy to make GF with basic ingredients, so I'll keep doing that.

I made these Brownies for a function I was attending and didn't mention they were Gluten Free. I made two batches and they all went! I'm not too crazy over most GF items, but this is one of the best. The price on Amazon is much less then the price in supermarkets.

column9: OMG- I almost cried when I tried these!
column10: My fiance was diagnosed w/ celiac two months ago, and it has been really difficult for the both of us.  I normally would bake cookies, brownies, or cupcakes once a week for him (he has a big sweet tooth!), but since the gluten-free diet started, I haven't made any g-free treats- the ingredients are expensive, and rarely available at our small-town grocery store. When I saw this mix for a little over $4, I grabbed it. I undercooked them a little (as I always do with brownies) and they were gooey deliciousness! I could barely tell the difference between these and the regular Betty Crocker brownies. I can't wait to try the cake and cookie mixes!

This is a great gluten free product which can definitely pass for a gluten product.  Make it for your gluten eating friends and shock them when you tell them it's gluten free.I made it with dairy free earth balance "butter" and it was still great.  I did use eggs, but next time I'm going to try it with an egg replacer and see what happens.Best of all,  I got this at my regular grocery store.

column9: Another sick customer says NOT GLUTEN FREE
column10: Oh, convenience.  You bring me back time and again to products that I should probably know better than to try. Like the other dozen or so one-star reviewers, I picked up this mix for some quick brownies and wound up with a full-blown gluten reaction - bloating, pain, nausea, the whole deal. I know this was the source of the problem because I haven't had anything new, different, or strange in a week or so. It couldn't have been the xantham gum because I had a very small portion - if the laxative effect is that strong in what would normally be considered a very, very small brownie (1.5" by 1.5",) then too much xantham gum is being used. The sad thing is, I used my brand new non-stick baking pan for this and now have to replace it (for the unaware, gluten can hang on in plastic, silicone, and non-stick coatings.) I'm just glad I had these after my anaphylacticly allergic child went to bed!

Have to add my voice to the minority, I tried these brownies and had the one of the quickest and most severe gluten reactions I have ever had.  This is especially disturbing because I am not even extremely gluten-sensitive and can tolerate small amounts.  All the ingredients listed on the package are things I normally consume without ill effects.  According to General Mills, some of their GF products are manufactured on the same equipment as their regular wheat products, they just clean them in between.  Maybe some GF lots are getting through with contamination?  I don't know, but there is definitely something wrong here.On the up side, they tasted great!

These are really, really good!The pros:-They taste just like the Betty Crocker box-mix-brownies you remember from your gluten days, the ones your kids might remember, too.  And they're a snap to mix up and bake.-You don't have to add chocolate chips, nuts, cream cheese, or frosting on top to make them taste good. But you can if you want to!-They're readily available at your local store, or here for a better price!  Mainstream and GF, yay!-They have that dense, chewy, fudgy texture most of us love in a brownie.  These aren't cakey or crumbly.The cons:-The mix only makes an 8x8 inch pan.  Bob's Red Mill GF brownie mix makes a 9x13 inch pan for roughly the same price, which might be better if you have a large family or are taking them to a party.-These don't make a good brownie sundae with ice cream (they'll get hard) and they aren't good for crumbling up to layer in a trifle or parfait (they'll get hard and icky).  I'd recommend the Bob's Red Mill GF brownie mix again for that, or just a scratch recipe.A great find for someone who's got a celiac kid at home with a sweet tooth or maybe a just a celiac "kid at heart!"

This product goes for $1  a package in Walmart. At this price it's over quadrupled the cost. From the list of ingredients it does not look gluten free. I'm glad the bigger corporations are addressing the gluten free issue. But this is NOT gluten free.

LOVE this mix. I use it for basic brownies (make sure to dust the pan with cocoa powder before baking for a better result), and for other recipes on the Betty Crocker website. I am celiac, but my husband isn't, and he begs me to make these all the time! I also love the bulk packaging because I end up saving about $1-2 per box as opposed to buying them individually at the grocery store.
These are great. I think they might even be better than regular brownies! So so good and so happy I found them.

column9: Too Good! Can't tell they are GF!
column10: Wow! We made these last night and also made a pan of "real" brownies. Can't tell thedifference...may actually be better! Rich, dense, fudgy, chocolaty heaven! The batter is gritty and grainy before baking, so I was worried, but they baked up great! No "GF" after taste.
Best gluten free brownies ever! They're fudgy, chewy, and flaky on top. SO, so much better than the kinds I have found in specialty stores like Trader Joe's. Yum!

I made these three hours ago and the pan is half empty! They are so,so,so good! I bought the mix at my local store for 5.60 a box,needless to say I will be buying then on amazon from now on. I will be making a huge batch of these for my son's fourth birthday. :)

column9: Best Gluten Free Brownies in a box!
column10: Just wanted to get my 5 stars in :) Wonderful brownies worth the buy! I think the price in stores is $4.60ish a box.. a little pricey that is gluten free for you.

These brownies are SO GOOD. I made them for a gluten-intolerant friend expecting them to be mediocre. I was amazed. So flavorful! The batter makes you think they are going to be hard and not very good. Wrong! GREAT brownies!!

I love these brownies. The mix has little chocolate chips in it, and I always put in loads of walnuts. Mmmmmmmmmm! Only problem is my family is afraid to try them because they are gluten free, and I end up eating the whole batch myself. Oh, well..............
Every member of my family loves these brownies.  The pan is gone before they even cool.  Be sure to spray the pan before adding the batter.

Holy Cow! The Betty Crocker cake and brownie mixes are amazing! I haven't tried the cookie mix yet, but have high hopes for it too. I wish it wasn't so expensive - about $10 to make a 2-layer cake (two boxes of mix), but alas this seems to be the life of a celiac.

It was recently determined that I have a gluten intolerance, so I've been missing all of my favorite baked goods. I wasn't expecting much from this mix, but I splurged and bought a box. These taste just like 'normal' brownies. I did replace the melted butter with applesauce because my partner is allergic to butter and oils. We couldn't even taste the applesauce because of how chocolately these are. (:

column9: Betty's Best GF Brownie Mix (w/dairy free recipe)
column10: Yum.  I have been GF for over 5 years and this is the very best GF mix that I have tried so far, tastes like scratch! A couple notes on how I made them vs the box instructions.  I added the following: 1 tsp apple cider vinegar, 1 Tbs (decaf)instant coffee 'grounds', 2 eggs, 2 Tbs vegan(Earth Balance)butter substitute, 3 Tbs coconut oil (melted).  IF you prefer a fudgy, gooey-in-the-middle brownie...then the key is to UNDER bake! And yes, the edges will still be crispy.  I baked mine in a lightly oiled, parchment-lined 9x9 pan for 16-18 minutes (rotate pan at the 8 minute mark)  After they have cooled, I cut and wrap each brownie in wax paper, slip them into a gallon zip bag and freeze.  GF baked goodies keep very well in the freezer, when tightly wrapped.  They thaw in minutes.  Subscribe-and-Save is the only way to go!
You can't find a better gluten-free brownie. These are sinfully rich and chocolaty. If you are not allergic to nuts - add a handful of walnuts to the mix. You won't be disappointed.

This is the ONLY good gf brownie I've found in 7 years and it is wonderful! Good texture, not grainy like the others. I leave mine slightly undercooked so they're nice and gooey.Just don't top with ice cream, they turn to stone!
I use these and make them egg-free.  Have not made them with the recipe on the box...but they are probably even better that way.  These are a nice treat for kids with food allergies!

Some gluten free mixes leave a lot to be desired, but this one is a winner!  You would never know they are gluten free, and the taste and consistancy is perfect.  I don't think I could do any better from scratch.
I love this brownie mix. Easy to make and taste like wheat brownies too.Thank you for this mix.

Betty Crocker met my high expectations with their chocolate brownie mix. The ingredients are minimal, just butter and eggs and the baking directions couldn't be more simple. I love that this brownie mix has chocolate chips mixed in, I think it helps make the final product more moist when you have melted chocolate throughout each bite. The ONLY reason I gave these four stars instead of five is because they are so high in calories because of all the butter and eggs. I know this is part of why they taste so good but its also hard to justify making them very often because I feel guilty eating so much saturated fat!
Watched my nephew for a month, he's GFree and we had these every week. My daughter and I loved them too! I lightened the recipe by adding milk in for 1/2 the butter. Still wonderful!

Love, Love, this GF WF Brownie Mix.  I serve these to guests and eat one myself!  They are shocked and ask me why I am eating something with Wheat and Gluten..my husband was so shocked as was my entire family.  Each time I have them taste test WF GF food, they say they want to gag.  The joke was on them this time when they told me how great and moist the BC Brownies were.  It was then I told them they were Wheat Free and Gluten Free!  It was great fun, and the brownies are amazing!We need more products like this that make WF GF NORMAL!!Thanks Betty Crocker!  You ROCK MY WORLD!Betty Crocker Gluten Free Brownie Mix, 16-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)

It has been a long time since I have had any sweets so  I am in gear and I can't stop.  These are wonderful.  I made them in my Redi Set Go grill and it worked out fine.What I love most is the mini chips.  These are very chewy and moist, I believe it will taste good with some pecans or walnuts but that is not necessary, they  are fine just the way they are.In a blind test I am not sure I could tell which ones are gluten free and which are not.  I cannot wait to test her other gluten free products.  But first I have to get over eating to much of this one.

column9: Betty Crocker Brownie Mixes Easy As 1-2-3 & Your'e Done
column10: I found this Betty Crocker brownie mix to be a breeze to throw together and bake. The brownies came out moist and chewy just like you'd want a chocolate brownie to taste. Having them be gluten free on top of that is just an added bonus for us all. It's nice companies are making products geared more towards health that still rock.

My 8 year-old son was diagnosed with Celiac Disease a week ago and this past week has been a flurry of buying, trying and tossing many various gluten free products.  These brownies are NOT one of the products we tossed.  We ate them up, they are delicious!  My son was so happy when he took a bite of these delicious brownies.  Even my hubby - a dessert aficionado who would probably curl up and die if he had to give up gluten - loved them and had to be chased away from the pan!  Thank goodness a giant like Betty Crocker is finally paying attention to the plight of gluten intolerant people and putting out quality gluten free products!

column9: Great Brownies, Skeptics Need To Read The Label!
column10: I just found these brownies the other day in the store. I haven't had much luck with many gluten free baking products so far but these are really REALLY good. They taste just like regular brownies and weren't like hockey pucks when I took them out of the oven.For those of you who believe that they may not be gluten free because you had stomach upset and bloating, READ THE LABEL. This product, like many gluten free baking products contains xanthan gum which is considered a highly effective laxative. It can cause stomach pains, bloating, and diarrhea when ANYONE consumes it. So moderation is really important. Also the xanthan gum can contain traces wheat so if you have a wheat allergy which is NOT the same as celiac disease you may have a reaction to this product...Eating them in moderation has left me(and my family) with no ill effects. They taste great and I look forward to trying the other Betty Crocker gluten free products!

After recently going gluten free as a family, this is so far the best instant mix we have found.  The brownies taste exactly like a "normal" brownie should taste.  They are chewy, fudgy and cakey all at the same time.  I did have to let them cook about an extra 5 minutes for the 9X9 pan, but they really came out wonderfully.  I can highly recommend this mix and was so happy to find a mainstream company that made something for our special circumstances.

Betty Crocker Gluten Free Brownies are unbelievable!!!!!  My son was diagnosed 3 years ago with Celiac Disease and the gluten free cake and brownie products were all so dry and also very expensive.  Betty Crocker's products are all delicious. I make them for him weekly.  Thanks Betty Crocker!!!!!
The brownies are easy to make and taste great! Everyone enjoyed them, even those that do not have to eat gluten free food.

I've tried quite a few different brands of gluten-free brownie mixes, and this has got to be my favorite!  I find that some GF foods tend to be a bit more dry (compared to wheat-based), but this brownie mix makes a great, very moist and fudgy brownie.  Instead of the oil, I often use a small cup of applesauce (I like the stuff without added sugar) and 1/2 cup of Eggbeaters.  The taste is still great and it's a bit lower in fat.

I made these for my gluten-allergic girl, and she loved them. I can make them from scratch, but sometimes they come out slimy in the center. (If you've baked gluten-free, you know what I mean!) These came out GREAT, just like the regular ones. I can't say if they're totally gluten-free, but they work for us!

The kids really like these and they are 14 and 11.  The 14 year old has hated nearly every gf baked item thus far.  Serve with a little Ben and Jerry's vanilla ice cream (which is also gf) and you have a wonderful treat.  I do think that the batter is a bit tough to scrape out of the bowl into the baking pan, but I have purchased several of these in the past couple of weeks since becoming gf and will keep purchasing.
These are super delicious! Can't tell much of a difference between regular brownies. My husband and 2 boys (3 and 6) love them and can't tell it is g free!

My partner is a celiac so we have been trying all kinds of new foods and recipes. Gluten free baking never lasts as long as the regular version, but if you eat these within a day of baking them these are the best we have found.

Betty Crocker has done a great job with the 3 items I have tried, the Choc.Chip Cookies, the Brownie mix and the Choc. Cake mix.  I can't believe anyone wouldn't love the taste and the convenience and ease of using these products.  At Thanksgiving, I used 2 boxes of the Cake mix to make a Choc. Sheet cake.  Everyone thought it was my sister's sheet cake that she usually brings.  Our entire meal was gluten free, from the Dressing & gravy to the desserts.
These are just as good as regular brownies.  We are new to a gluten free diet and these are our first gluten free desert.  Very yummy!  Now if we can only find a good pizza crust ;)
These brownies are absolutely wonderful. My family likes them better than the original Betty Crocker brownies. They are moist and really satisfying to that chocolate craving.

These brownies are addicting.  The flavor is unbelievably good.  They taste rich without being too rich.  They are a chocolate-lover's dream.  They're also very easy to make - I don't even use the mixer.  If I had to list a negative, it would be that they start to dry out after a few days, but that's only on the top.  The lower 9/10 stays moist and delicious.

I had high hopes for this product and was not let down! I made them for my son's birthday and shared them with non-gluten-free relatives. No one could believe they were gluten-free! They were very moist, with chocolate chunks throughout. They were gooey, therefore a little messy, but all part of the fun. I'll undoubtedly be making these again.

These brownies are AWESOME!  I found out I have a wheat allergy about a month ago.  My first GF brownie mix I tried was Pamela's.  They were "gritty" and just not like the brownies I was used to.  I only ate one and threw the rest of the pan out.  I saw the good reviews of the Betty Crocker brownies on Amazon, so I took a risk on a pack of 6.  I am THRILLED to report these brownies are easy to make (add 1/2 stick butter and 2 eggs) -- and most importantly they are delicious!  I can definitely bring these to family gatherings and other events without others suspecting a thing!!  I'm so thrilled.  And the price is a lot better than the other gluten-free brownie mixes out there.
Smooth, flavorful and savory.  No acidic after-taste. I'm a coffee fanatic and this has to be my favorite brand. I first tried it when I was in Germany so I'm glad it's available for shipment.
This is the best Tchibo coffee with my Krups 468 Coffee Maker.  My cousin in Germany recommended this "exclusive mild roast" and I love it.

You have adopted the word "balance" on your product.  This word is generally used for a true balance of decaf and regular coffee.  This misleads people purposely to think that they are using a coffee that is a mix of both. I have always mixed the two and was happy to see that you have a "balance" and believed that it truly was such.  That was quite a disappointment.

I love this Tahini! To me, Tahini is all about the same, but the price is super cheap for 4, 16-ounce jars! It's more that half of what I was paying in the local grocery store. I used to have to skimp because Tahini was so expense, but now I can use it how I like, without going broke. I've had the subscription for 3 months now and have been eating very well as a result!

I didn't know from different brands so I got this because it was a bargain on Amazon.  When it arrived I opened the first jar and was surprised because it was mainly a viscuous liquid, and I wondered if I had gotten a defective product or if the bargain was because it was inferior...boy, was I naive!I had always gotten my tahini from the grocer, paid double this price, and it was mostly a solid brick of stuff I had to deal with.  I like this so much better...it still has the flavor and it's actually able to be measured and used in recipes so I find many more opportunities to use tahini now that I have it.  It will take me a while to use all four jars (only into my second one now after a few months) but I do intend to buy it here again...

column9: Very light roast, very thin consistency
column10: This is the lightest roast I've ever seen, and the thinnest consistency (high fraction of oil) as well.  Maybe that's what you want, maybe it isn't.  It's fine for hummus but too thin to be used a standalone dip.

column9: Bought it for the price - Won't reorder for the taste
column10: I use tahini frequently for homemade hummus. There are some fine brands and good deals on bulk quantities from time to time.  I was willing to try this product since it was such a good deal price-wise.  The flavor was lacking.  The consistency was a little thin, not sure it being something called "light roast" adds anything to this brand appeal.
I love it... it's my wake up tea every morning. I make it with boiling water and microwave 30 s with milk. Just great!

column9: Love these tiny little tea leaves
column10: I always go back to this tea as my standby after sampling MANY others. The bags make great iced or hot tea.

We have been drinking PG Tips (also from Amazon), but my wife prefers this blend so I guess we will stick with it.  I have called it "English Style" as in small print on the boxes it says it was packaged in India for the USA.  That does not detract from the product in any way as all this sort of tea comes from India or Sri Lanka.

I use this to make a batch of our favorite ice cream. I use a package of vanilla Junket and follow directions on it, add the bubble gum flavoring and put it in the ice cream maker. Really couldn't be any easier. Really good! Much better than boughten ice cream.  :-)
These salmon jerky were terrible tasting.  I suppose a grizly bear might like them, but for human consumption---oh no.  To much salt and not enough flavoring other than fish.

column9: The best salmon jerky I've had
column10: This is easily the best salmon jerky I've had yet (I had the teriyaki flavor) -- delicious salmon flavor, just the right amount of smoke and salt, and it flakes like real fish (which, of course, it is). Could eat this stuff all day!

This product is delicious.  I bought a few bags while in Alaska just to try it, and now that I am home and just ate my last bag, I have come here to order some more.  Unlike the other reviewer, I love these precisely because they are salty and taste like fish.  Great snack for Weight Watchers too as they are also packed with protein and low in carbs/fat (1 oz is only two points!).  Good product.

It takes alot of this to TASTE it in tea or in food.  If you put it right on TOP of the food and don't mix it in then you can taste more of it.  Also, look up Agave Plant online.  You will find it high in oxalate acid and well, "the juice" of this plant on my hands did leave me with contact dermatitis.  The other problem was the oxalate level.  I happen to have to watch mine, and this is too high because the amount you have to use is well, alot to really get a sweet taste/as sweet as sugar.  Right, it doesn't raise blood sugar - but considering there is no real nutritional benefit this is one dietary "extra" I'm passing up.  I'm not diabetic so I can't speak for that situation, but I suppose if you were diabetic without a weightproblem (this is not low calorie) and no oxalate issues (kidney stone), then you might consider this product.  If not diabetic, don't bother.  Too pricey when a teasp of sugar is only 16 calories and sweetens much more easily.

column9: Tastes GREAT, doesn't raise blood sugar
column10: This stuff is fantastic.  It tastes better than honey, but is vegan.  I am sending some to my diabetic mother because it doesn't raise my blood sugar at all.
I love this sweetener! I take it with me everywhere, because I will never use sugar or any other sweetener in my coffee or tea ever again!
I've tried them all..this is the best Organic Sweetner...no after tasteThree times sweeter than refined sugar and it's good for you, unlikeregular sweeters.  Try it You'll love it

Great sweetner, great taste, use in tea, coffee, baking, anywhere you would use sugar, plus since it is a liquid it stirs into foods and drinks without any effort. Try it you will like it!!!  I add it to my unsweetened cocoa!!!

I tried a a good number of incense by HEM and I really enjoy the Precious Rose scent. I am 98% sure that the oil that the sticks were soaked in was synthetic; because I smelled organic rose essence and oil 2 different rose synthetic oils and this scent smells very similar to the synthetics. I also think that the scent is synthetic because natural/organic rose oil is very expensive and I do not see how it could be used for such inexpensive product as the incense sticks. Nevertheless, the scent is very pleasant. At first I wanted to give this product 4 stars because of my suspicion of the synthetic oil and no identifier of it on the packaging, but the I decided to give it 5 stars because I honestly enjoy it a lot. If I could I would give it 4 and 1/2 stars.

A friend of mine gave me a pack of this for Christmas last year, and I've been hooked ever since!  This is my absolute favorite incense now.  I've tried other rose incenses in the past, and though they smelled nice and vaguely smelled of roses, nothing can compare to HEM's Precious Rose.  This stuff is strong and smells exactly like roses.  I mean it when I say "strong" - if you aren't ready for it, this stuff might knock you over...with awesomeness.

HEM's Precious Rose incense is a pleasure lover's delight. Intense and deeply evocative, it conjures the intoxicating scent of times long past, of the best roses at the height of their power.  Perfect for summer afternoons - the heat of the day enhances and is entranced by the pungent billowing profusion of this incense.  I burn this and most incense outdoors usually and it wafts into the house creating a sense of expectation and relaxation.  There's something quite powerful about this Precious Rose, making it one of my very favorites.  It's scent is definite and potent and may not be for everyone, but a sybarite may be smitten.
These smell wonderful, not to overpowering, smell stays long after burnt, I love these, and will never be with out them again!!

column9: good but some burned out before it got to the end of the stick
column10: The smell is just what i was looking for smells just like rose water and roses but it did burn out when it got to the end of the stick i was almost done with the box so i dont know if that was the reason or not. But the smell is really good

This is the incense for those who wrinkle their nose and blink when they encounter a strong fragrance."Scented" is a word that usually makes me cringe.  I am very sensitive to manufactured fragrances.  Things meant to fragrance a room, like "Yankee Candles" make me feel nauseous.  The smell is like an overabundance of fake concentrated scent attempting to mask a strong chemical fume.  I do not understand how anyone can stand to be in the same room.The majority of popular scented items have this strong chemical smell to me.I don't mind the scent of certain varieties of incense, but they are often too strong and overpowering to use in a room without the window open.I've tried a tonne of different incense, from numerous manufacturers.  I've even tried at least 5 or 6 different "rose" incense over the years.HEM "Precious Rose" incense is perfect.  It is a light, natural rose scent. Lovely and subtle. It does not overpower the room, it is truly like sitting outside near a few rose bushes in bloom.  I now buy it in bulk at a great price from XTREMEK, here on Amazon.The HEM lavender is lovely as well, and the scent is very similar to being near wild English Lavender, but of course lavender has a stronger scent than roses, so I do not use it nearly as often.note:HEM also make a "sandal rose" and a "musk rose". I don't care for either of those.
Buen precio, buen aroma, no dura mucho se consume muy rapido, si quieres inundar el espacio debes usar varias, en varios puntos, el aroma permanece por una hora.

FIVE STARS AND A SALUTE! Their very best incense! It's my very favorite of them all. It has a romantic aroma that is pleasing and tingles the senses. I order by the biggest box and I'm never out of it!!! It makes a great air freshener.

This is a nice but unspectacular rose incense; I'm pretty sure the scent is synthetic, not that I care much. It's potent enough to be noticeable but not overpowering, and lingers for a while after done burning, which is nice.It doesn't compare to the pure Rose Absolute incense I had been using, but it's also a fraction of the price, so you don't have to worry about using it whenever you want. If you like rose and use it often, this is a very good choice. If you don't use it often, try the Rose Absolute 20 Stick Box - Rare Essence Incense-- it's heavenly.

It's not often that I review purchases,.... but HEM precious rose incense is AMAZING! It actually smells like roses! Strong scent, yet not overpowering. The scent lingers in my drafty home for at least an hour. After 20 years of burning various incenses,...... from cheap store-bought sticks, to the hand-rolled craft-fair sticks,.... I can say without a doubt that THIS is my absolute favorite!

column9: The saltiest club soda ever--kind gross
column10: We purchased a Prime membership so we could get cat litter delivered. I had been hoping that I could also get seltzer delivered, as we go through about a bottle day. Yes, we should get that seltzer making kit and be done with it, but we're pretty sure someone has purchased that as a gift for our upcoming wedding.Sadly, there is no actual seltzer available that is Prime eligible (do you hear me, Amazon? You'll make a bundle off of us if you add some seltzer to the Prime ranks) so I tried out this 12-pack of club soda. It was kinda gross. It took us almost 3 weeks to go through it all. I know club soda usually has some sodium added--that's why it is different from seltzer, which is just carbonated water, potentially with added citric acid. This White Rock club soda, however, is way saltier than most of the ones I've tried before. It was almost like drinking brackish water. I will not be ordering this again.

Now, I like Fresca as much as the next person (which is to say, I'm fairly indifferent to it), but there's no reason this should cost $80.  Is there some kind of Fresca speculation going on where, like, people are driving up the price of Fresca in anticipation of it disappearing?  Has science recently discovered that it can be used as an alternative fuel source?  I understand that you get 6 of these bottles for a grand total of 12 liters, but GAS is cheaper than that, folks.  Friends don't let friends buy $80 Fresca.
This is $1.xx per bottle at most grocery stores. They want to charge $80? REALLY? What is going on?! The world is falling apart...
The shipping was unbelievably fast and I was pleased to receive it so soon after placing my order.

I make this for my husband every morning. I keep telling him I will teach him how to use our espresso machine, but of course it tastes better if I make it.  It is delicious or he won't care whether I make it while he reads the newspaper.  this is ese compatible

I love a good latte, but it has to be right - strong and rich (two or three shots per 12 ounce glass.)  I can't stand bitter coffee, and can't even drink most coffee from drip makers.  I have an espresso maker and I use the Lavazza decaf pods when I don't want as much caffeine as a regular cup, sometimes mixing one or two decaf with regular so I get the flavor without as much kick, or all decaf if it's in the afternoon.  If you "subscribe and save" it's very reasonably priced.The pods make it easy to make multiple shots back-to-back, because there's no cleaning needed, you just knock out the pod and put another one right in.Some things I've noticed:1) You get better results if you carefully center the pod, and use a tamper as you would loose coffee (even though they're not supposed to need it.)2) The Decaf espresso loses color earlier in the extraction process than the regular.  Since I use the "watch carefully until it turns blonde" method of knowing when a shot is done, I've had to go a little longer with decaf.3) This is about all pods:  If the espresso is watery or clear from the first drip, pull the cup away and stop.  The pod is not centered and you're passing water around it.
Trying to reduce caffeine intake and my wife likes LavAzza best. High quality, fresh and makes a terrific home latte...

I love Stash teas and that's mostly what I drink. Organic premium green and organic earl grey are my standards, with several other things here and there for variety. (I really miss the organic sampler package!)When I couldn't get the sampler any longer, I deliberated about which Stash mint tea to get for the family and picked this one. Meh. We all think it tastes strangely like toothpaste. Which is to say that there's something off about the mix of mints and/or the sweetness of it. I'll go back to the Organic Cascade Mint.

Although billed as "Festive blend of organic green tea and lively spearmint and peppermint", I'm reviewing this product mainly to let people know that the wintergreen taste is dominant in this tea.  I really dislike wintergreen, but hoped as the last ingredient on the label, that the wintergreen component of the flavor wouldn't be noticeable.  However, wintergreen oil is powerful stuff, and it really overwhelms the green tea and peppermint/spearmint components.  Honestly, I think I'd prefer a more straightforward mix of green tea and peppermint and/or spearmint leaves, without additional ingredients like lemongrass, ginger, and especially wintergreen.

This tea would be perfect if the amount wintergreen oil was reduced.  The predominate flavor is wintergreen even though it is the last ingredient on the list.  I like wintergreen, so I will continue to drink this, but probably won't order it again.  The Moroccan Mint is much better if you're looking for a tea with a spearmint flavor.

column9: If not toothpaste, then breath mints
column10: Should've believed the "toothpaste" review.  The wintergreen oil overpowers any mint that might be hiding in there.  Much prefer St. Dalfour's Spring Mint.
Delicious tea, so good I bought 6 packages at once (also because it was a great, low price at Amazon).  Minty, subtle, no bitter tea flavor.
I am on the auto delivery plan for this flavor which is one of my favorites.  Stash tea is superb.  Highly recommended.
I am unable to buy most flavors Stash teas that I like in my city, so it's great to get it through Amazon.

It's an ok product.  I got it for my kitten to teeth on.  Because it's a stick, he had a hard time getting his mouth around it to pick it up when it's on a flat surface like the kitchen floor so he would just swat it around until he lost it under the refridgerator.  So I decided to put it in the microwave for eight seconds until it became soft and then held it in a spiral shape until it cooled off and became hard again.  This gave it some dimension and was then easier for my kitten to get a hold of and chew on.  He loved it after that.  It helped him greatly with his teeth growing in.

I've seen these at my local Petco where I looked over the ingredient list.  Soy or Soy protein is either the first or second ingredient.  Soy is something I avoid in anything I give my cat.  Soy isn't very digestible by cats and is often a common food allergen.  Also soy is also considered bad for your cat's thyroid gland.  In addition soy may also impact the amount of Taurine your cat absorbs; a lack of Taurine can cause blindness in cats.
My cat loves these and it keeps her from chewing the wrong things.  I wish it was available in pet food stores rather than just over theinternet.

AT first my cat was not really sure what to do with them other than play with them but he figured out really quickly that they where treats. Also having these around has kept him from chewing on everything so much. This was a really awesome buy and I plan on keeping these on hand at all times.

My kitten( 11 months) who likes to chew on everything loves these treats.  They are sort of like kitty raw hides. She knows where I keep them and goes to look for them. The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is I wish they lasted longer, she can chew and eat one in just a couple of minutes.

Warning - do not buy these for your cat. They are a major choking hazard. I narrowly averted disaster when my cat chewed off an eraser sized piece about 30 seconds into gnawing on this stick. The piece was hard and not easily chewed or ground up. In other words, it's not like food, but more like the consistency of a hard piece of wax. He would have choked on it if I hadn't quickly taken it out of his mouth. I threw the rest of the package away.I thought these were chew toys and they dissolved like rawhide (or not at all). I did not expect them to break off into pieces that could be choked on. I am horrified that these are being marketed and sold for pets. Amazon shame on you for carrying this product.

column9: Great Chew Treats for Dental Cleaning!
column10: These chew treats are great and my cat loves them. I have not been able to find them at any retail locations and get them exclusively with KV VetSupply.  The problem most cats have is the size. I find it is best to hold one end and let your cat knaw on the other end.  I would not leave with them unsupervised.  My cat really chews on them like a dog and scrapes his back teeth good with them.  I would buy them by the case if I could afford it.

Strange smooth, plastic-like texture that my cats didn't care for. My oldest cat likes to chew on my Beagle's bones and rawhides so hardness isn't an issue & both my male cats will eat just about anything. Even fruits and veggies. I'm thinking that the flavor/smell (or lack there of) wasn't enticing to them. Oh well, at least the dog will eat them so they won't go to waste. If your cat likes electrical cords or other similar tasteless, yet firm items-these chews just might be for you!

I didn't mind my kitten teething on my finger when she was smaller, but she's 9 months old now and hasn't lost her urge to chew on things.  She was constantly after a certain consistency - something firm, but not completely hard, like a pencil topper, electrical cord. etc.  This chew treat is perfect - firm enough for her, but still something she can sink her teeth into.  I'm thrilled, and will definitely be getting more.  The suggestion to heat it up and re-shape it by another reviewer was really helpful and made it much easier for my kitten to play with independently (vs. me holding it).  Also, I wouldn't recommend it for small kittens, as pieces will break off and your kitten/cat needs to be able to chew it up before swallowing.  My kitten is a small 9-month old and doesn't have any problems with these.

My cat is the most food oriented animal I have ever had.  He was a scavenger before we adopted him; eating out of dumpsters and who knows what else.  It took us months and many rolls of duct tape to train him to stay out of our kitchen trash.  He will eat anything except for salsa, peanut butter, chocolate, and food with too much cinnamon.  Notice that jalapeno potato chips, bread of any type (through the plastic bag), carrots, and bird seed were not mentioned in the list of food he won't eat?  Well add these cat chew treats to list of things he won't eat.  He won't even touch them.  He shows absolutely no interest in these once he sniffs them.  They may help with tartar, but only if the cat eats them.  Will not purchase again.

My cat is just over a year old and loves to chew. He was chewing on the hose from the toilet and a lot of other inappropriate things. He really likes these. We got them at Petco. It's hard to find chew toys/treats for cats. He didn't like the rubbery/plastic dog toys. These are a perfect solution and keep his teeth healthy.

N-Bone Cat Chew Treats have solved the problem of my cat wanting to chew on my fingers first thing in the morning . . . substitute nursing?  She is delighted (can cats be delighted?) to accept my holding the treat while she bites off bits.  Then we can both get up satisfied and intact.  Great product!  Great company!  Many thanks!

column9: Cat doesnt like, and he's not particuliar at all.
column10: Could be my cat, but too hard for him to chew, and doesnt like taste. Other products from this seller are great though. HAS NOTHING TO DO WITJH SELLER, IT'S THE PRODUCT.*I'm a STICKLER on *DELIVERY! "Great job, A+  "

We have two cats from the same litter.  One is inclined to chew on things, like telephone and electric cords, and the other doesn't.  The one that chews, loves these treats and the other one just sniffs and walks away.  If your cat tends to chew things, try these.
