And this continues that trend. . .it just doesn't taste real.I'm more of a processed cookie needs to be non-chewy or if you want chewy make homemade.Kids are definitely not particular, they just want a sweet item. My kids did like them, but agree that homemade cookies will always win out. Even with all their praise, they didn't come chase me down the following day for more cookies, they wanted other sweets. So, it was a fleeting impression on them too.Go with the original in my opinion, you could pass on these unless you really want something you don't have to cook and isn't a hard cookie cookie.

These cookies are great if you also love Chewy Chips Ahoy cookies. The extra heavy layer of fudge in the middle it too much for some, but for others in our family it was just right.That said; some of us feel that Chips Ahoy original cookies are the one and only. For us this cookie offers very little. They are not the cookie for those looking for that crisp crunchy perfectly balanced chocolate chip cookie that is the original Chips Ahoy.Simple math: Love Chewy Chips Ahoy = Like or Love these cookies / Love original Chips Ahoy = Not likely to love these cookies.

column9: An acquired taste, so say the least
column10: While I love Chips Ahoy cookies, I can't say these "Chewy Gooey Chocofudge" cookies would ever win me over. They are slightly reminiscent of the Chewy Chips Ahoy cookies, but filled with fudge in the middle. If you like the chewy CA cookies, you'll like this. If you're on the fence about the chewy version (like me), then this definitely will not sway you to their side. Oh man, these are bad. I've tried eating a couple of them at different times of the day just to give my taste buds a chance to try a second opinion, but it's always pretty much the same. Think I'll go back to my old favorites, the original brand.

Small cookie with chocolate chips and gooey chocolate in the middle. It was soft and chewy which I like. Overall it was a little too sweet for me. As my teenager said after eating one "eh" Not bad, but not great,

column9: I hope I got a bad batch...
column10: First: I wanted to like these cookies.  I really did.  The concept is good, they look awesome on the outside of the package.  I like the regular chewy Chips Ahoy (like them, not love them) so I figured the addition of more chocolate would be a plus.Before opening the package, I checked the ingredients.  To my VERY pleasant surprise, no HFCS, but real sugar.  Doesn't say cane or beet, so I'll probably never know, but it isn't HFCS.  I'm sensitive to HFCS, so this was a BIG positive for me - and the only reason the cookies got two stars instead of one.Now for the bad:  The cookies are small.  A little smaller than standard crispy Chips Ahoy.  That's not a bad thing, except a serving is two cookies and that serving comes to 150 calories.  For the calorie content of approximately 3 cookies, I could've had a Snickers bar (or similar) - and I would have been happier.Finally, to touch on the title of my review: I hope I got a bad batch.  These cookies were awful. They tasted like plastic.  I'm not talking about a plastic texture, but taste.  They honestly tasted like melting/burnt plastic.  My wife tried one and noticed the same thing (without any coaching from me).  I'd love to try another batch, in hopes of having received defective cookies, but I'm not going to take the chance.If you're considering buying a pre-packaged cookie, stick with the standard Chips Ahoy varieties - crispy or chewy.  But stay away from these.

Words cannot describe the nasty aftertaste in my mouth right now after just having finished one of these cookies. I am currently wracking my brain thinking what I have in the house that might get rid of this taste (other than brushing my teeth). Ugh. Basically, these are the regular soft Chips Ahoy cookies with a chocolate filling. It's not a gooey filling that spreads out of the cookie when broken open like the picture on the package implies. The filling just sticks inside the cookie and stays there when you break it in half. Not gooey at all (though I'm not even sure that would have helped). The flavor is totally artificial and sickeningly sweet with, as I have already mentioned, a very nasty aftertaste that lingers. My husband had pretty much the same response as I did when he tried the cookies. My 12 yr. old kids are away for a few weeks, but when they get home I'm going to let them try them and see what they say. Personally, I would stay far, far away from these.

column9: There are Tastier Things Out There
column10: The soft cookies are oddly flavorless, with a chemicalish undertone.  The filling is an OK texture (though not particularly gooey) and proportion, but not particularly tasty.  They weren't even very good dipped in milk.  I ate them, but I'm not sure why...I think it was just because they were there.  I wouldn't get them again, but a die-hard Chips Ahoy fan might like them alright.

As a big fan of Chips Ahoy chocolate chip cookies, both the original and the chewy, I was prepared to love these as well. But it was just a big glob of mushy chocolate, barely held together with a tiny bit of cookie. Now, like most people, I'm pretty enthusiastic about chocolate, and theoretically, there is simply no such thing as "too much." But it just didn't taste right here. I really wish there had been more cookie involved, to break up the taste a bit; maybe that would've helped. But whatever went wrong here, it definitely did.Overall, it was a rather disappointing experience. I won't be buying these anytime soon.

column9: Not as good as a bakery cookie
column10: I normally eat cookies from bakeries, rather than supermarket cookies, as  provided by my workplace at lunches and events, so I'm comparing them with what I'm familiar with, not against other industrially produced cookies.These are very sweet, without much real chocolate flavor.  While the gooey chocolate filling is much better than just the dry little chips, it needed to have more flavor. The texture of the cookie itself was what really lost me.  Instead of being soft and chewy, it had a sandy, gritty quality.  I'll stick with just the bakery cookies.

Adding extra chocolate to something already chocolaty is usually a spectacular idea. Unfortunately, the end result of adding a gooey, fudge center to Chewy Chips Ahoy! cookies is something that looks like a mushy cookie and tastes like a mouthful of chemicals.The taste of these cookies is strange. They look and smell like your average Chewy Chips Ahoy! if left out in the sun for a bit. The appearance doesn't do anything to indicate the taste though. The initial bite is of a salty, sweet cookie, but there is a biting aftertaste that points to way too much in the way of processing and preservatives.The fudge used to fill these cookies isn't gooey. The picture on the package in no way accurately represents the consistency of the filling. The fudge is thicker and drier than expected and doesn't seem to have any flavor at all.Chocofudge Chips Ahoy! are a disappointment. A better choice would be to just stick with the original Chewy Chips Ahoy! cookies.

This rating is as much for the state of delivery as the cookies themselves.  The cookies were delivered in a box with air pillows but were totally crunched.  Because they are "gooey," you'd think crunched meant just smooshed, but, no, actually crumbly as well. There wasn't a whole cookie in the package.Still, being a fan of the normal chewy Chips Ahoy, I figured my cookie crumbs would at least be tasty.  The taste is different, though, more bitter and almost metallic.Maybe there was a chemical reaction going on here, exposure to higher humidity or air that caused the crumbs, thus impacting the taste, too.  Regardless, these were literally dead on arrival.I love amazon.com, but cookies and crackers seem to be total waste of money purchases.  I don't know if the fault rests with UPS, but cookies and crackers are the only amazon shipping fails I've experienced in 10 years.

column9: Okay for me, but the kids loved them
column10: Chips Ahoy! Chewy Gooey Chocofudge is very soft and chewy as advertised.  I found the chocolate filling inside a little overpowering though.  The cookie was smaller than the average chocolate chip cookie, but a little thicker.  I really liked the way the package opened and could be resealed.  It would be nice if all cookie packages were like this one.  I might have liked the cookies a little more if I could have warmed them, but the kids loved them and they disappeared too quickly for me to get the chance.  I prefer the Chips Ahoy chocolate chunk cookies, so my rating for these would be 3 stars, but the kids would rate them 5 stars.  I set my actual rating at 4 which is smack in the middle of what I thought and what the kids thought.  I think that's fair

column9: Run of the mill and pretty small
column10: Basically, these are very soft chocolate chip cookie with a fudge filled center. This is pretty much what is advertised, and thus there can't be any complaints on that end. However, I just don't particularly see the value in this compared to many other options -- they don't particularly taste special (average....maybe even a bit worse than that compared to more expensive options), and each cookie is pretty small. Sure you can just eat more, but I find a single larger item more satisfying than two smaller ones, especially when it there's a filling such as in here. And the fudge somewhat overwhelms the fact they are chocolate chip cookies on the outside.Three stars, on account of the fact that they ARE still good enough that, were I presented with a plate of these and no worries about health, I would still chow down -- but at the same time, I'd choose many more options first were I given a choice.

When Chips Ahoy! first came on the scene when I was young, I thought they were a good cookie that was always soft and a good balance of cookie to chocolate chip ratio. Since then, they have come up with variants on the initial blend to keep people interested and aware of the Chips Ahoy! brand line. Now they introduce Chips Ahoy! Chewey Gooey Chocofudge. Do I like it? Not really. Maybe its with age or refined taste or my lack of interest in snacks and sweet foods in my older years, but I found this cookie very sweet. Not just in the chocolate chips, but the cookie itself seemed very sugary. Also, in addition to the many chocolate chips, it looks like they baked one giant chip smack in the middle to ensure every bite gets a chocolaty taste. So it seems overkill on the sweetness factor. And because this is a cookie that is manufactured by food scientists to ensure sameness in every cookie, it ended up tasting on the artifical side. Perhaps these would taste better fresh out of an oven and have a warm taste, but that is a preference for the individul to determine. But they are not sold that way, so I am taking it as it is given. So will I buy these? No. I dont buy the ones I grew up with, so I definitely will not get these either.

column9: Not as much of a hit as the Megafudge Style
column10: These seemed a little overly sweet, the flavor was "off" (had a funny after-taste to us), and the texture just didn't mesh as well as with the Megafudge style.My kids didn't even finish the sample I gave them. They were "deep sixed" after one bite. One of the kids went so far as to spit out the one bite they took.If you want to purchase them in bulk from Amazon, we recommend that you purchase one pack from your grocery store for a taste/texture test first. Just because we didn't like them doesn't mean you won't.ETA: I forgot to mention that the center is creamy, not gooey and there is a wafer type texture just above the creamy center.

column9: a glass of milk won't make it go down better
column10: Cookies are one of my four food groups, and it really pains me to give a cookie a bad rap. However, these cookies do not taste good! They smell sort of good, and they are fresh and soft. They taste awful! They do not taste like Chips Ahoy cookies or just plain old chocolate chip cookies. The soft "chocolate" filling has a very unpleasant artificial taste. The cookies do not taste like chocolate. They taste like a cheap, imitation food product. I had such high hopes : (

I love the softness of Chops Ahoy! cookies so I like to buy them often, but I'm not all that fond of this particular Chewey Gooey kind. The inside is filled with gooey chocofudge, which I like as far as texture goes, but the chocofudge is really, really rich, too rich for my taste (had to break out the milk after one bite) so I can't have more than one cookie at a time.For intense chocolate lovers, this would be just the thing, but if you're not an addict of chocolate then this'll probably be a bit much for you.

To say the actual product bears no resemblance to the gorgeous cookie on the package would be a huge understatement. The cookies are tiny and do not 'ooze chocolately goodness' as the picture indicates, although they do have something resembling a chocolate center. The cookies are tooth-achingly sweet and otherwise flavorless. The product looks interesting but the execution is very poor. I don't even have any suggestions for tweaks that would improve this -- Nabisco needs to throw this out and start over. I'm surprised it made it past what I'm sure must have been many testers and focus groups.

I am on a quest for a satisfying grocery store chocolate chip cookie. Unfortunately, Chips Ahoy Chewy Gooey didn't get me any closer to my goal. For context, I like regular Chips Ahoy, but don't consider them great; I prefer a softer texture. Chewy Gooeys are not hard, but also not really soft. More mushy, or squishy. Also, the fudge filling isn't gooey, more like pasty. The overall mouth feel is too oily for my taste. Finally, I couldn't get the resealable package to open correctly and had to put the remaining cookies in another container.When I gave one to my husband telling him that I didn't care for it, he popped it in his mouth and disagreed with me saying, "I don't know, they're OK." We won't be buying any of these to stock our pantry.PS. A quick warm up in the microwave helped the texture of both the cookie and filling, but not enough to change my mind about future purchases.

These are small, soft, cake-like cookies with a fudgey center. Yes, they're chewy and gooey and boy are they sweet. A bit too sweet for my taste, but my husband, who still has the taste buds of a kid, gives them two thumbs up. Pretty good for a store-bought cookie, and a little bit of an upgrade from regular Chips Ahoy.

column9: Not Bad but Not Really Good Either
column10: Chips Ahoy! Chewy Gooey Chocofudge cookies are a chocolate chip cookie stuffed with soft chocolate.  They're good but they don't really take the basic chocolate chip cookie in significantly new or interesting directions.  This is nothing much more than a soft cookie with a layer of frosting on the inside. Ultimately not so exciting that they inspired much more than a shrug.  Not bad but really not a big deal.  And one of us who tried them said we'd rather just eat freshly baked cookies because these tasted a bit fake.

It isn't really chewy or gooey but if chocofudge is concoction that is neither truly chocolate of fudge then the description is one third correct.  These cookies aren't as overly sweet as many new entries on the market but the smaller size does indicate that they are pushing the limits on how much sugar and fat can be stuffed into a single serving.  While the outside isn't as crumbly as the texture and taste would predict, it seems to be little more than a coating for the center portion of semisolid fudge.  This stuff is more sugar than anything else, with a bit of texture to it and a slight chocolate flavor.  The cookie itself isn't very good although there is only enough of it to cover the fudge center. Overall, none of the parts of these cookie come together well and the result is a letdown.
I ate way too many when they first arrived.  Like most chocolate chip cookies, I can't eat just one. For my personal taste they are way too rich & I probably won't buy them again.

I like the regular Chips Ahoy cookies. They are crunchy. The outside of these Gooey gookies are crumbly like a dry cake. The inside is similar to the filling in a Keebler double stuffed fudge cookie, but the taste doesn't work well with the crummy cookie.Even a glass of cold milk couldn't save these cookies. I had another adult try one, but it went into the trash after one bite.

column9: Soft and chewy, but not gooey
column10: I couldn't resist getting a pack of these cookies to give them a try. As I opened the package the wonderful aroma of rich chocolaty cookies filled my nostrils. I picked up my first cookie and immediately noticed the soft texture and fresh feel. I was a little surprised when I gently broke open this chocolate chip cookie to expose the fudge center. The fudge center was not gooey like the picture on the packaging had suggested. The center was more like soft chocolate rather than gooey fudge. My wife decided to put one in the microwave in an attempt to make it gooey, yet that didn't work either.As for the taste, I felt the cookies tasted pretty good. I still prefer homemade chocolate chip cookies and I suppose I shouldn't expect packaged cookies to come close to homemade cookies. All in all these cookies are some of the better grocery store cookies you can buy. I recommend them, but I wish the fudge lived up to the advertising. Don't expect gooey fudge on the inside, but rather soft chocolate and you won't be disappointed.This item would get 4 stars if the fudge was actually gooey by the time it reaches consumers. I would be willing to give a perfect 5 stars if the fudge was gooey and the flavor profile tasted even more like homemade chocolate chip cookies.

(See the image gallery for my three photos that accompany this review)I hadn't eaten a Chips Ahoy in a while, but was kind of looking forward to these new "Gooey" chocolate chip cookies. But, from the moment I opened the package I knew I was going to be disappointed! First off, the cookies were a crumbled and jumbled heap of a few cookies in overly large packaging... the same as regular Chips Ahoy packaging that would hold two or three times as many cookies. Not the most appetizing first impression. So... is this really what Nabisco wants us to see when we open the package?? a jumble of cookies in an overly large package for the few cookies you get? A total turnoff from the beginning. I didn't expect the cookie to be as big as the photo on the package, but I did expect it to at least kind of look like the photo (which looks like a standard Chips Ahoy with the goo inside). This cookie was dark and mottled and misshapen and kind a gross to look at.Okay, presentation stinks, but maybe the cookies are really good nonetheless? Um... no... they kind of suck. And, Gooey?? Not even close... it is a wedge of grainy and dry chocolate-like stuff in the middle. The most distinct flavor (or really after-taste)? That is an overly sugary and heavily preserved food-like substance. After one cookie, I tossed the rest out.Bottom line... just plain gross.

These are chewy chips ahoy cookies (not the crunchy ones), with a chocolate fudge baked into them. What could there possibly be not to like? ;-) The fudge is uniformly and well distributed throughout the cookie and it complements the cookie part well. The overall taste is very rich and very delicious. The soft chewy cookie complements the texture of the soft fudge very well. My only gripe is that the chocolate chips and the chocolate fudge create too many somewhat clashing textures. I think the cookie would be better if it had just the fudge inside the cookie without the chocolate chips.

column9: Taste fine...get them in the store, not through Amazon.
column10: The cookies are fine. A bit too sweet for my taste, but I really had to force myself to try one. Getting cookies shipped to you is NOT the way to go. Let's just say it was a cookie LOAF not individual cookies. Everything had melted together by the time they got to me in the mail. They were probably sitting in some mail truck for six hours re-baking. I don't think I can give a proper review for this one.

I must confess that I do not like Chips Ahoy cookies to begin with. Their recipe changed sometime in the past decade, and now they are just 100% pure nastiness. Adding a gross chocolate center makes them 125% nastiness. Seriously, I would not give these cookies to my worst enemy. DO NOT PURCHASE!!!!

Chips Ahoy Chewy Gooey Chocofudge cookies are delicious! They can be a bit messy in regards to getting chocolate on your fingers, but as far as flavor and texture goes for store-bought cookies, they're about as good as they can be. They're soft and moist. Each one is like a gooey, quarter-sized chocolate disk wrapped up in a soft chocolate chip cookie.They're not nutritious nor are they supposed to be. The easy open and seal package contains three stacks of a few [10 oz. worth of] cookies which probably will not last too long in a casual goodies-munching environment. A few seconds at a low-power setting in the microwave makes for a wonderfully fudgy melted treat.
Cookies were chewy with a fudge center, they didn't even last a day in my house.  Very yummy.  Reminds me of soft batch cookies.
These cookies are really good tasting. The Gooey Chocolate is flavored just right to my taste.  Sweet but not overly sweet.  Some of the best cookies to come along in years.

The Chips Ahoy! Chewy Chocofudge cookies are just that. They are chewy with a gooey center of fudge, and taste delicious. They are really rich, and a perfect snack if you have the will power to eat only one or two. And, you better just eat one or two, or the package will be gone before you know it. Like all products, Nabisco is shrinking the amount of product they put in a package while still charging the same price.  You'll get around 21 cookies in a package (3 rows of 7).
These are soft chocolate chip cookies that also have a fudge filling.  Very good, although I slightly prefer the Megafudge version, as these are just a tiny bit sweeter than I prefer.

column9: Taste is great for summer...shipping not so much
column10: Because the box didnt fit in my mailbox it was dropped off at my door and as soon as i opened the package the cookies were in crumbles...but i wanted a cookie so i tried them anyways and they are yummy addictive...ooey gooey goodness thats great with a large glass of milk...enjoyashEdit:I'm not really sure why people thought that I didn't eat this product from Vine but when I recieved the product the cookies were in crumbles. Besides that I really did try them an share them with my kids who are the ones that said they were gooey. The cookies really are good an if your looking for something that has the chocolate chip original with a new spin these are for you. An now that the seasons are changing these would be great warmed up with a glass of milk...hope you enjoy them as much as my family am I did...:)

These cookies are very soft, chewable, and delicious!  The only problem I had with them is that each cookie is pretty tiny, so I kept eating them.  I don't know if they're quite "gooey" as the label claims, but they are quite good.

column9: Not very good and kind of pricey
column10: I did not find either the cookie part or the chocolate part of Chips Ahoy! Chewy Gooey Chocofudge appealing to my palate. There are only 18 cookies in this large package. If I feel a craving for a small expensive cookie with chocolate, I''ll stick with Pepperidge Farm or something from a local baker. This is not a knock on Nabisco, by the way; their Nilla wafers, Ginger Snaps, and Fig Newtons® are the supermarket cookies I buy most frequently; I've just never found their chocolate products (other than some Snackwells) very enticing. Chips Ahoy! Chewy Gooey Chocofudge did not change that.

First, let me say I'm an adult, so maybe that affects my tastes.  On the other hand, though, I have not one but 32 sweet teeth.  With that being said, I'm going to be bold and assert that the Chewy Gooey Chocofudge cookies are going to be too sweet for anyone over the age of 11.  Unless you're drinking really black coffee with them.  The kind of black coffee that is so dark and strong, you wouldn't be able to see ANY light through it if it were in a clear cup. Besides that, if you're looking at these cookies here on Amazon with intent to order a bunch, you should note that they don't travel well.  My package arrived looking like most of the cookies went through a rock tumbler (on the bright side, I guess they're ready to be made into a cookie-crumb crust?).  They ARE chewy.  Gooey?  I wouldn't go that far.  Maybe on a really hot day, or if you put some on a plate and microwaved a few seconds.  Finally, they have sort of a Play-Doh aftertaste if Play-Doh were made with lots and lots of sugar.  Chips Ahoy has a good thing going with their original cookies.  I think these are an abomination and should be skipped right over with no regrets.

column9: Chalky, salty, just below-par for choc chip cookies
column10: These are definitely below average cookies.  They don't even try to look homemade, and are kind of small and processed-looking.  For taste, they are passable but I thought there was something powdery and definitely salty about them.  In my little tasting party of seven people in my immediate family  I was hearing words like  chalky, boring, stale, and "has that low-fat taste without the low-fat benefit."  They are certainly edible--but it's not a product I would seek out.

column9: Not what I expected but I wouln't throw them out
column10: The package of the cookies shows a VERY gooey cookie but the cookies fell well short of that. I liked the soft texture and there was a lot of chocolate even though not it wasn't quite gooey. I wouldn't seek this cookie out especially but I would eat them if someone served them to me. Chips Ahoy has plenty of delicious cookies that I would eat first.

I usually like Chips Ahoy, so was eager to try these; they were, unfortunately, a disappointment.  To start, the portion size is incredibly small: two mini cookies equal 150 calories.  And there was just something artificial about the taste.  The chocolate was only okay and the surrounding cookie was fairly blah.  They are, however, chewy so at least that part of the description is accurate.

Anyone who has eaten a real chocolate chip cookie would not bite twice at a Chips Ahoy Chewy Gooey Chocofudge creation.  The chocolate center makes up the largest part of this small cookie and while it is soft, it is not what I would call gooey. It does taste pretty much like semi-sweet chocolate which is about all this product has going for it. The pastry part is chewy in a dry sort of way with a strange taste going down and a bitter, unpleasant back bite afterwards.  The 2 piece serving has 150 empty, off-flavored calories that could be wasted on something far tastier.  The lift resealable packaging must be less expensive than the original. It may or may not be effective but it is hard to imagine that a stale chocofudge would be any worse than a fresh one.

column9: Tastes different than original Chips Ahoy!
column10: The Chips Ahoy! Chewy Gooey Chocofudge tastes a lot like chocolate with the cookie "breading" of a Fig Newton.  I doesn't taste a lot like the original Chips Ahoy!  It was soft, with a log of chocolate (though not particularly soft or gooey chocolate).  Personally, as someone who likes Chips Ahoy! and who's not a fan of Fig Newtons, it was not a tasty cookie.  If a chocolate Newton sounds good to you, then you'd probably enjoy these.
I'm not usually a fan of chips ahoy, but these changed my mind! These cookies are tasty! Chocolate stuffed and chewy! I foresee myself taking trips to the market and sneaking these home!
Anyone who loves chocolate would like these cookies.They're chewy, gooey and delicious!Thanks Amazon for letting us try them.We like them too much.

I was very interested in what Chips Ahoy! would do with a soft cookie and these do not disappoint. Like most soft cookies, they use a lot of brown sugar (or at least it tastes like brown sugar) in the flavoring to keep them soft. As I understand it, there is a variation in taste bud which causes some people to taste this type of flavor as very bitter and objectionable - luckily I'm not in that group but if you have had that experience with soft cookies this might not be a great purchase for you. The chocolate flavor is very bittersweet, which I like as well. For me, the resealable package is a blessing and a curse - it works so well that I find myself returning for more and more cookies whereas a more challenging-to-open container might serve to slow down my vacuum-like consumption.All in all, this is a recommended product for those that like soft cookies with bittersweet chocolate. I actually prefer the original Chips Ahoy!, however.

These cookies seemed a little on the small side, but they're chock full of soft, melted chocolate - not too sweet (especially with a strong, black cup of coffee) but satisfying enough to the sweet tooth within the serving size (2 cookies). I like to microwave my cookies to soften them up and make the chips melt, but this wasn't necessary with these Chips Ahoy Gooey (no, they weren't particularly gooey but I was glad - the chocolate was melted but not messy - perfect). Very soft cookies that amazingly did not crumble.

I always liked Chips Ahoy cookies and was glad to try this new variety where cookies are still thin looking and yet loaded with chocolate.  They were delivered on a sunny Florida day and cookies braved the heat until I come home from work.  They probably spent at least five hours in the hot weather, in the mailbox.  When I opened them so I can treat myself to a desert after dinner, they were still intact.  Bag comes in resealable package, so one does not have to worry abot keeping cookies fresh.  Cookies were medium size and loaded with chocolate both on the inside and outside.  I liked cookies very much and I took them with me to work, so I can nibble on them when I feel like having a desert after lunch; or in a late afternoon with my last cup of coffee.

column9: Chips Ahoy version of Soft Batch?
column10: These Chips Ahoy Chewy Gooey Chocofudge cookies are very similar to Keebler Soft Batch Cookies.  They are about the same size and softness.  I am not sure if Soft Batch has the fudge center these do, which in my opinion, give them the advantage.  They are small, about 2" each, and come about 18 to a 10oz package. Stats are not great but not unexpected for cookies: 2 cookies 150 cal, 7g fat, 3.5 sat. fat, 13g sugar.  They are tasty little guys and my whole family liked them.  I recommend the Megafudge version if you like all chocolate cookies.  Those were tastier but you really have to like chocolate (like I do).

column9: "Gooey" Is Not The Word I Would Use
column10: They are definitely chewy, but the fudge inside is far from "gooey". Unless their definition of "gooey" is something far different from my own. I tried putting them in the microwave to see if it would at least get melty, and, yeah, not a good idea, definitely didn't improve the taste.And honestly they're just unappetizing to look at. Either they used too much brown sugar or they just plain burnt them.And the flavor itself, they're not sweet. They just taste bland. HUGELY disappointed in this product. Gonna stick to the original from now on.

I love chocolate chip cookies.  I love Chips Ahoy! chocolate chip cookies.  So, CHIPS AHOY! CHEWY GOOEY CHOCOFUDGE chocolate chip cookies should be just about perfect, right?WRONG!!!  CHIPS AHOY! CHEWY GOOEY CHOCOFUDGE chocolate chip cookies truly could not be more disgusting.  The cookie is mushy not chewy, the taste is like cardboard, and the chocolate fudge smells and tastes medicinal.  They are not at all sweet.  They are tiny, highly caloric, and have a strong, weird aftertaste.I've offered samples of CHIPS AHOY! CHEWY GOOEY CHOCOFUDGE chocolate chip cookies to just about everyone who has entered my house in the past few days, just to see if it was me or if it was really the cookies.  It really IS the cookies.  My family (husband and kids ages 6 and 14) were not impressed.  Friends and neighbors were equally disappointed.  The best thing my kids said about CHIPS AHOY! CHEWY GOOEY CHOCOFUDGE chocolate chip cookies was that they tasted like Kellogg's Nutri-Grain Cereal Bars.  Now, that may very well be, but I ask you:  who wants their chocolate chip cookies to taste like dry, low cal cereal bars?  Not me, that's for sure!It is possible that the packaging and shipment may have contributed to the disastrous taste and texture of these CHIPS AHOY! CHEWY GOOEY CHOCOFUDGE chocolate chip cookies.  These cookies were shipped to me, cross country in 100 degree weather.  They sat in my broiling mailbox for most of the afternoon.  But, come on, if you are going to offer a product that you ship nationwide or worldwide, then it needs to be able to  stand up to any and all possible conditions.  Hey, Nabisco, you need to seriously rethink this product.  NOT RECOMMENDED.

column9: Addictive, a bit on the sweet side though
column10: If you're a Chips Ahoy! fan, you'll probably understand when I say these taste like the red bag Chips Ahoy Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookies, not the regular blue-bag Chips Ahoy!. They're a slight bit sweeter, a lot softer, and the cookie part doesn't have that (to me at least) distinctive Chips Ahoy! flavor. It's like they took a Chewy Chips Ahoy! cookie and shoved a large chocolate fudge chip in the middle (which I guess really is what they did).They don't taste bad - far from it. If you're a fan of Chips Ahoy! cookies in general you won't be disappointed. They're addictive and will hit your sweet spot sugar craving without much effort. To me they were a bit on the over sweet side of the fence which was probably the only thing that kept me from eating the whole bag at once. Kids?  Kids will probably inhale these.It should be noted that even at room temperature (78-80 degrees) these things are falling-apart soft and the chips are melty. On the day they arrived, they were literally destroyed (and it was a cool day - only reaching 94 instead of 104). You opened up the package and it was just a giant clump of cookies and chocolate. Attempting to pull out a single cookie resulted in "cookie bits". After a while in the AC they did firm up a bit and had their shape somewhat restored. However I would call these cookies overly-soft.Oddly enough, the ingredient list was a lot easier to understand than I would have guessed. There aren't a ton of artificial ingredients (comparatively to other snacks on the market) - I'm not saying these are an organic, all-natural wonder, but other than a few specific additives, you could probably make these at home from scratch.IngredientsUnbleached Enriched Flour (Wheat Flour, Niacin, Reduced Iron, Thiamin Mononitrate {Vitamin B1}, Riboflavin {Vitamin B2}, Folic Acid), Sugar, Semisweet Chocolate Chips (Sugar, Chocolate, Cocoa Butter, Dextrose, Soy Lecithin), Palm Oil, Invert Sugar, Coconut Oil, Dextrose, Soybean Oil, Cocoa (Natural and Processed with Alkali), Cornstarch, Whey (from Milk), Leavening (Baking Soda and/or Ammonium Phosphate), Salt, Molasses, Nonfat Milk Solids, Caramel Color, Soy Lecithin, Natural and Artificial Flavor.Serving Size: 2 cookiesServings Per Container: 9Calories 150  Calories from Fat 60Amount Per Serving and/or % Daily Value*Total Fat 7 g (11%)  Saturated Fat 3.5 g (18%)  Polyunsaturated Fat 1 g  Monounsaturated Fat 2 g  Trans Fat 0 gCholesterol 0 mg (0%)Sodium 110 mg (5%)Potassium 60 mg (2%)Total Carbohydrate 21 g (7%)  Dietary Fiber <1 g (3%)  Sugars 13 gProtein 1 gVitamin A 0%Vitamin C 0%Calcium 0%Iron 4%

There is only one word for "Chips Ahoy! Chewy Gooey Chocofudge": Yummy!I open a pack of 4, and all of them are gone in no time. The pack was shared by one adult and four kids, everyone loves it.The pack of 4 actually contains more than 4 pieces: it has probably 12 regular cookie size pieces. Sorry, I cannot get an accurate count of the number becausee they are all gone before I can count them. Enjoy it!

These are good, but the chocolate gooeyness is still somewhat subtle.  I had expected more intense.  These cookies are actually better when they're a little bit beaten up in the package.  For whatever reason, the crumbliness makes the flavor stand out more.  (A weird thing I discovered between my first and second box of these).

column9: Loved by all, curse my luck
column10: I can't review these cookies completely honestly: my family ate them all before I even got home on the day they arrived. On the other hand, that's a pretty strong recommendation, don't you think?By all accounts -- there were three greedy family members (not including me!) who got to eat these fudgy, chewy cookies -- they were entirely satisfying and quite tasty, and I have to believe them.But I don't think I'll ever have cookies sent by mail to an insecure location again.

column9: These chewy Chips ahoy cookies are actually quite good!
column10: I thought this Chips Ahoy Chewy Gooey "Chocofudge" product was pretty darn good. I prefer this one over the other Chewy Gooey flavor "MegaFudge" because it has a better balance of fudge and cookie. The Megafudge tasted too much like a hot cocoa flavor on the outside dough instead of a traditional cookie dough flavor. That's why I say that I prefer this one. Other than that, the two flavors are very similar.  A few other minor complaints is that the dough on the cookie crumbles a bit easily... especially around the edges. I would've liked it more cohesive. Also, the "fudge" core wasn't quite creamy enough, as far as the texture is concerned. The fudge also would've been better if it tasted more like "dark chocolate", but instead it tastes more like hot cocoa. Despite these observations, I think these are pretty delicious cookies and definitely worth a try. If you like the chewy variety of chocolate chip cookies, I would definitely recommend these for you to try out.

column9: Chips ahoy has done it again
column10: The kids loved them, I loved them and they were definitely gooey. Warmed up in the oven they were the best. Soft, not crispy, with chocolate oozing out of the middle. Excellent and a tasty treat. Taking it one step further I also put ice cream between two of these cookies, stuck it i the freezer or 20 mins and it came out to be the best ice cream sandwich. Chip Ahoy is definitely missing out on a potential gold mine in the ice cream sandwich department.

column9: It's a gooey, fudgy Chips Ahoy - what's not to love?
column10: This is a Chips Ahoy flavor called "Ooey Gooey Chocofudge," so it should already be pretty clear from the get-go who is going to love this and who isn't.  The cookies are soft, but don't fall apart or dissolve in your mouth.  They are definitely gooey, but not overly messy.Obviously they aren't going to beat homemade fudge cookies fresh out of the oven, but for a packaged treat in the goodie aisle of the supermarket, these are pretty tasty and well worth the purchase.  Add a little milk and you're in for a seriously good time.

column9: They got it right! Chocolatey and delicious!
column10: I am a fan of Chips Ahoy. I love them. I am not, however, a fan of the Chewy Chips Ahoy. Those are too soft. the flavor is very different. I like the original and even the low-fat. Yummy.So i was a bit skeptical about the Chewy Gooey Chips Ahoy. but Nabisco nailed it: they found a great balance between gooeyness, chocoloateyness, and cookieness. Magic, if you will. These are yummy cookies, not too sweet, not to soft. Delicious. Sorry, I have to go... I'll get myself another cookie....

column9: Not as good as regular Chips Ahoy
column10: This product was chewy and had plenty of fudge in it, as the name suggests.  The flavor, however, falls short of regular Chips Ahoy.  The taste seemed a little unnatural.  My kids were not very excited about them and both liked the regular Chips Ahoy much better.

These sounded like such a great idea.  Of course gooey chewy chocolate fudge cookies will be wonderful, right ?  Sadly, no.  There is a strong artificial chemical taste and the texture is neither chewy nor gooey but only soggy.  They were surprisingly edible after having been left to get stale for a month.  I would never buy them at a grocery store.

column9: Kids Love Them, I Prefer Original
column10: My kids absolutely loved these cookies, which have a chocolate filling that is sort of like commercial chocolate frosting. I thought they were good (they are Chips Ahoy, after all!) but I prefer the original Chips Ahoy or Chunky Chips Ahoy. It's a fun and different cookie but for everyday cookies, I think I will stick to the original types.

I've always loved Chips Ahoy cookies, so I was excited to try the new Chips Ahoy! Chewy Gooey Chocofudge......In retrospect, the operative word is "Chocofudge" which conjures up images of something that is not quite a food, more like a chemically created psuedo-edible.....thing. The fudge in the middle of the crumbly, dry cookie is neither chewy OR gooey, more like a piece of old jerky that's been sitting in a hot car for a few days. I cannot imagine ever having any occasion to eat one of these cookies again.......

The Chips Ahoy! Chewey Gooey Chocofudge cookies are good for a packaged cookie. They were soft like homemade cookies but the taste was off and tasted like a typical packaged cookie. They were fudgy and full of chips, but to me they did not taste homemade. Overall they are good for a packaged cookie.

I like these better than the Chips Ahoy Chewy Gooey Megafudge cookies.  There's still a slight aftetaste to these cookies, though.  Yes, the cookies are soft, but they really aren't as "gooey" as the name implies.  The packaging, with its resealeable flap, is a good idea.  It will keep the cookies fresher longer.  If you like Chips Ahoy cookies, you will likely enjoy these too.  For me, they were just okay.

column4: Tracy Foote "College Savings Plan Author, Pho...
column9: A little too gooey for me
column10: These were a little too gooey for me. Parents should have napkins readily available for young children as there may be quite a mess, especially if it was hot weather. Also, having been through the shipping system, many of the cookies were broken. Of course if you can find these in the store, you probably won't have this issue. One thing you could do is refrigerate them and then you will have a nice soft cookie that doesn't seem to melt on your finders. My recommendation is to purchase these in winter months only.

column9: Didn't care for them at all!
column10: Yuck.That's the one word I would use to describe the taste of these.But, before we get to taste, let's talk about how these were so smooshed and crumbled inside the package when I opened it. Many of them stuck together, and then fell apart when you tried to pull them apart. They're WAY too mushy and soft, so much so that they lose their form and come apart into pieces.The taste, to me, was awful. I can't even describe it, but let's just say that my reaction was "Ugh!! Yuck!!" after a few chews. It almost had a medicinal taste to it (to me, anyway). I also found that they leave a bit of an after taste in my mouth. I LOVE cookies, baked goods, and almost all sweets, but I couldn't tolerate these. I ended up throwing most of them out because I didn't want to eat them.Good try, Chips Ahoy, but not your best work.

This is the first cookie I've ever eaten which *almost* had too much chocolate in it -- but not quite!I got these in the mail and had a pal with me at the time -- we're both trying to count calories a little but this was a bad time to do it. So I had him open the package and I said we'd just try a couple apiece. We arrived at my house in about 20 minutes and they were all gone. Diet blown but, man, those were good cookies. Somewhat chewy and very rich.Highly recommended if you're splurging.

My family and I loved these cookies a little bit too much. I think they only lasted 24 hours in my house with a family of 5 that is not good. They tasted yummy. I liked the gooey middle. They are Chips Ahoy goodness with a bit of an extra bit of goodness.

Fudge flavored chocolate chips? Soft cookie? Sounds good, huh?Well, it's on OK cookie, not a great one. The "soft" style of cookie just doesn't have the taste of the harder original style and the fudge chip tends to overpower the cookie as well. In fact, I am more fond of the original Chips Ahoy than these.That being said, I ate the whole package because, let's face it - an OK cookie is better than no cookie at all.

column9: not as delicous as it sounds
column10: It did have a fudge center but it was too much chocolate and not enough cookie,  and the cookie was all damp and soft as a consequence.  I think gooey is the perfect word - but it translates to soft and not very interesting,  as well as having a bad chocolate cookie ratio.  Too much of a good thing can overwhelm the flavors, and unbalance the baked good...We all ate 2 (some may have eaten 3) but we all agreed that the while regular chocolate chip chips ahoy are terrific,  these are not.  I will not buy them again.

These are all right.  I probably liked chips ahoy! cookies more as a child than I do now.  They taste fake, look kind of gross and just aren't very good overall.  The chewy fudge in the middle is pretty lacking, but it does make the cookies softer than your normal chips ahoy! cookie.  They are slightly better warmed up, but I can't say I'd recommend them.  There are so many better cookies out there worth buying.  Not to even get into the ingredient list, which contains nothing decent for you.  I'll pass.

These should be amazing.  Really, just look at that picture!  A chocolate chip cookie that is chewy on the outside and full of creamy fudge.  Good glory, I could go into a happy coma just thinking about it.Unfortunately, they are not so good.  The fudgey middle is actually just a bigger chocolate chip, and the cookie is more crumbly and dry than chewy.  The taste is heavily dominated by all of that chocolate, and the chocolate, while not bad, is not good enough to stand on its own.Don't break your heart by buying these.  Just look at the picture and dream.

column4: Lonnie E. Holder "The Review's the Thing"
column9: The taste and texture were okay, but is this the best option?
column10: I tried this cookie at the same time I tried Chips Ahoy Chewy Gooey Megafudge cookies.  These cookies are better than Chips Ahoy Chewy Gooey Megafudge cookies, but they still fall short of what I expect from Chips Ahoy Chewy cookies.I have given up expecting products to look like their packages.  I suppose there is a bit of artistic license in making food look as though your mom and grandmother whipped it out of a bunch of basic ingredients.  The problem, of course, is that the cookies bear little resemblance to the picture on the package.  Things seem to go downhill from there.Try putting one of these cookies on a napkin next to the package.  The picture on the package is beautiful, with chocolate chips on the outside and gooey chocolate in the middle.  I could barely see the chocolate chips on the cookie itself because something, crumbs I think, covered the chocolate chips.  None of my cookies were lovely and round like the one of the package.  Instead, my cookies were mostly broken and I had a difficult time removing more than fragments from the package.Well, beauty is only chip deep, I suppose.  The important features are the taste and the texture.The texture was okay.  The cookie seemed chewy and moist to me.  In general, I thought the texture of these cookies compared favorably with regular Chips Ahoy Chewy cookies.The taste was okay.  The taste was hardly great, but okay.  I tasted cookie dough and then a chocolate hit, about what I expected for chewy chocolate chip cookies.  What I missed was the creamy chocolate in the center of the cookie.  I tried several of these cookies, trying to taste the creamy chocolate in the middle.  My taste buds could not separate the taste of the supposedly creamy chocolate from the other flavors in the cookie.These cookies need to compete with regular Chips Ahoy Chewy cookies along with dozens of other varieties.  In order to do that, a new cookie should be phenomenally good to convince customers to change brands.  However, this cookie is hardly phenomenally good.  In my opinion, this cookie is just average.  I believe there are many better options available, particularly given the price of these cookies.  My prediction is that either this variety will disappear from store shelves or its formula will change.  Meanwhile, you have plenty of other, better choices.Good luck!

column9: Okay but a little strong of a taste
column10: These are okay cookies, and they keep well, but the chocolate taste is a little overwhelming for me. I'm not sure if there's some bitterness there, too. Anyway, each cookie is a nice small size.

column9: An Odd Mixture of Tastes Not Quite Ready for Shipping
column10: Chips Ahoy! Chewy Gooey Chocofudge cookies are billed as soft-baked cookies with a fudge center.  The cookie part is pretty good - definitely chewy if that's your thing.  However, the fudge center has a strange, almost bitter taste that is at odds with the rest of the cookie.  It also has a thick, gooey (can't say they didn't warn us) consistency that makes each cookie way too rich and heavy.  Even though the cookies are small, you'd be hard-pressed to eat two of them because of the heaviness and strange flavor combination.  Make sure you've got plenty of milk on hand when you bust these ones open.Also be aware that due to the small size of the cookies themselves, there was a lot of shifting during transit.  As a result, several of the cookies were already bent if not bashed into mush by the time the shipment arrived.If it sounds like the Chips Ahoy! Chewy Gooey Chocofudge cookies were saddled with a name that only a kid would love, it's likely no coincidence.  Only a kid would (probably) enjoy the cookies as well.  Anyone who puts much/any thought into their snacking would steer clear.

column9: Meh, Nothing To Go Out Of Your Way For...
column10: These cookies were certainly chocolatey, what with the gooey chocolate-flavored filling.  But, it was kind of a phony-tasting chocolate flavor, as opposed to the rich milk chocolate flavor of, say, Nestle Toll House morsels.  Furthermore, there was also a someone stale, wheat flour flavor that lingered on the palate after the chocolate flavor faded.  Plus, these cookies were somewhat soggy, not in the least little bit crunchy.  Neither my wife or I cared for them much, to be honest, and won't buy them again.  Kids might like 'em, but they didn't impress us in the least...

column9: Better than many, yet still disappointing
column10: We all can see that these are mass produced processed cookies destined to sit on grocery store shelves and occasionally find their way into one's basket and eventually tummy.  In that context, these are good enough, but they fair to excite or live up to the promises implied in the packaging.  That being said, you can do far worse in the cookie aisle, and these may do the trick for you, just don't expect more than these can offer.

column4: Meg "Livin la vida loca in Maine!"
column10: Nothing will ever beat the taste of a fresh warm homemade cookie. Chips Ahoy Chewy Gooey Chocofudge will help you satisfy your sweet tooth even if it isn't homemade. My husband loved these and ate the whole package (except for the two I managed to get!) They're soft (which I like) and the fudge inside replicates the gooey-ness of a cookie warm from the oven. Now this isn't to say that they taste like the "real thing" because they don't. But when you need a chocolate cookie fix, this will do!

I love chocolate chip cookies. I love fudge. So, when you combine the two, one could reasonably think that it would make for a perfect cookie right? Well, it very well may, but in this instance it doesn't.A couple things for starters.Based on the packaging and picture on the packaging I was expecting to bite into this cookie and have fudge ooze out. Not the case here. The fudge, and I use that term loosely, if really just a gob of something in the middle that does no oozing at all. I even tried to microwave a couple cookies to get the packaging effect and never did.The cookies also seem really dry and crumbly. I usually like the Chips Ahoy line because of the soft chewy nature of their cookies but these are just a crumbly mess.Just a side note the cookies in the package I received looked nothing like the cookies on the packaging. Several were reduced to crumbs, a couple were slightly burned, but none even resembled the picture on the package.Taste wise they were average at best. Nothing special about them, which left me disappointed. I was expecting a more full flavor and something different than the normal Chips Ahoy chocolate chip cookie. Didn't get that. If I see these at the store I will most likely skip these as they aren't anything special.

These cookies are moist and have a good chocolate taste. They are a chocolate chip cookie with fudge cream in the middle. They were really good after I warmed them in the microwave for about 12 seconds!The package has the pull flap on top that reseals. And it worked well. They didn't get stale after 4 days.I will buy this product.

I should have known when I selected these packaged treats what they would taste like--overprocessed, high sugar, high calorie discs of nothingness. To compare these to real home baked cookies is like comparing real life to THE REAL HOUSEWIVES OF NEW JERSEY. There may be something to occupy your time for a moment or two, but there's no substance, and certainly no love, underneath the veneer.

This is a good product, that my wife and I enjoyed, but the name of it doesn't match up with the actual product.  It really isn't gooey or that chewy.  It has a good dark chocolate fudge taste that isn't overly sweet, which we both liked.

This cookie is very similar to the Chewy Chips Ahoy except it has added chocolate chips on the outside.  It tastes okay but it's not going to earn raves.  Just like the Megafudge version, the cookies are very small and at 150 calories per serving (which is only a few cookies), it's not worth it. The taste isn't spectacular, cookie kind of dry, although the fudge center tasted good. It's a small package as well (10 oz) and at more than $3, I think I can find a better tasting and more satisfying cookie at my local grocer.

I love most things chocolate and these were quite tasty, although rather thin, with a soft center of chocolate.  My husband, the real cookie connoisseur, told me he prefers the original Chips Ahoy because they're crispier. So let that be your guide; if you're a fan of gooey centers, these are for you; if you're a fan of crispy, stick with the original.

column9: You will love them and keep buying them again and again
column10: These are delicious , ever since trying them i have recommended them to other people and they buy it and they tell people and they buy them too,,,,sooooo good!:)

column9: If you like fudge, you'll love this cookie
column10: These cookies, while they don't look like the one being broken on the package (maybe if heated?), have great taste, and stay chewy even if refrigerated.  I found them delicious and tried to hide the box from myself in order to try to make them last longer than a day (I was successful ... barely).  They are definitely a big step-up from standard chips ahoy (which I would rate as "OK").
Very moist and chewy. Shipping and temperatures left a little to be desired (a lot of them were stuck together) but tasty nonetheless. I would buy these!

....  but neither my husband nor I liked them.  After opening them (and trying a single cookie each), the package sat untouched for almost a month before my youngest son decided to try them.  He liked them enough to eat more than one, but even my boy hasn't finished the package after more than a week (very unusual for him).My husband prefers the crunch of original Chips Ahoy! cookies, and while I usually like my cookies chewy, I didn't like these.  Maybe if they had put the fudge center in their original cookies (instead of inside soft cookies), these might have more fans at my house.

Growing up in San Francisco, home of Mrs. Fields's cookies, I have a very healthy appreciation of soft cookies.  Couple this with the fact that many packaged cookies that you find at the super-market is pretty stiff and crumbly, I'm generally apprehensive when I hear about the words "gooey" and "soft" when describing such cookies.  Regular Chips Ahoy is no exception, unfortunately.  I do, however, appreciate their chunky chocolate cookies (Chips Ahoy! Chunky Chocolate Chunk cookies, 13-Ounce Packages (Pack of 6)), especially the peanut butter ones (don't see them on amazon, though).  Therefore, when I saw the new Chewy Gooey line of cookies, I had hope that this new generation of cookies would continue their improving trend!Sure enough, the cookies were soft.  I wouldn't say that the chocolate was able to stretch like on the main package, but there's definitely more chocolate in these new cookies than in your standard Chips Ahoy.  It's almost like a filling lay, and definitely not just chips being melted more during the baking process.  Honestly, they're strictly not even chocolate chips anymore, more like a fudge.And the big question, are they tasty?  Definitely.  Are they messier?  Yeah, so be even more careful giving them to little kids (or even my 10 year old, who happens to still eat with her hands when we aren't looking).Recommended.  If only they'd bump up the package size closer to the 12-14 ounce of the earlier packages (or even better, make them 16 ounces again!!!!!)  Then I'd give them 5 stars!

column9: I don't really like Chips Ahoy
column10: I'm a chocolate fan, and a cookie fan, and I like the idea of these cookies. The thing is, it turns out I just really don't like Chips Ahoy. If you do, but wish they had more chocolate, you'll probably like these.I don't eat many packaged cookies, but I was still surprised at how little I liked these. Honestly, they kind of taste like cardboard and chemicals. The chocolate is, of course, low quality as well, but that's to be expected.Lest I sound like an irrelevant snob, I will say that I do enjoy Oreos, and they're certainly made of cardboard and chemicals -- they just don't taste like it. But it would be hard for the local cookie man to recreate an Oreo, whereas he can do super chocolatey chocolate chip cookies no problem, so....if you want the latter, just go buy fresh made. Unless you really do like the regular Chips Ahoy, in which case these are even "better".(I'm gonna get blasted for this, aren't I?)

What's better than a chocolate chip cookie filled with fudge?  A WARM chocolate chip cookie filled with fudge!  I pop one of these cookies in the microwave for a few seconds (experiment to find your perfect temperature), then sit back with a warm cookie and a cool glass of milk.  Pure bliss!  Granted there are plenty of calories in this treat, so do consume in moderation.  It is a wonderfully decadent treat!Service size - 2 cookies, 150 calores, 7g fat, 0mg cholesterol, 110mg sodium, 60mg potassium, 21g carbohydrate (13g sugar, less than 1g fiber), 1g protein.Contains: wheat, milk, soy.

column9: What can you say about store-bought cookies?
column10: Yes, these Chips Ahoy cookies are better than their hard, crunchy counterpart, but they still taste very artificial. Also they are not terribly gooey, just very soft, with the chocolate in the middle seperating very easily. I've had worse and obviously much, much better, but I think some kids would like them regardless. I brought these into work and left them on the counter. They were all gone by lunchtime so I guess some adults who could care less about quality would like them too.

The downfall of these cookies are not the way they taste, but the way they are advertised. From the packaging, I expected a chewy cookie with a soft and, to use Nabisco's word, "gooey" chocolate center. Unfortunately, the cookies failed to meet my expectations.The actual cookie part was similar to what I expected. The outer portion tastes just like the normal chewy Chips Ahoy! cookies. However, I would not describe the center as gooey. Instead the chocolate center was closer to the consistency of chocolate that is just beginning to melt.While I would not say these cookies were necessarily bad, I certainly would not pick them over regular chewy Chips Ahoy!

column9: Cookie good -- chocolate not so much
column10: I couldn't wait to try these Chips Ahoy cookies. I mean, how do you make chocolate chip cookies better -- by putting more chocolate inside (yes, I'm a chocoholic).  The chocolate has a strange taste to it.  I definitely prefer the plain, soft batch chocolate chip cookies by Chips Ahoy.  However, they weren't so bad that I didn't finish the entire package!!!!!

Sorry Chips Ahoy, this was a miss. I'll preface this by saying I'm not a huge standard Chips Ahoy fan, but they're not bad dipped in milk in a pinch. But these just tasted weird to me.More than just gooey, they're extremely soft and fall apart easily; they actually felt a bit unpleasant and fake. There's an odd taste to them that I can't place as well, and I wasn't fond of it. Neither was my family. My wife: "I hated them." My son: "they were ok I guess, but they tasted weird. I like the crunchy ones." My daughter isn't here now, but she wasn't a fan either.Bottom line is this: I can see no reason to ever buy them again, and if they were on a platter at my kid's elementary school function I'd still skip 'em. Not exactly a ringing endorsement, I know.

I could't finish the first cookie I tried. It just tasted overly processed and chemical-laced. Ick. But I am giving the cookies two stars since my husband ate most of the package before I threw it away. When asked, he didn't really like them but he didn't find them as repulsive as I did, obviously. He didn't complain when I threw the rest away however. I wouldn't buy these even on sale and in desperation for a cookie. I can handle a regular Chips Ahoy or Keebler at times but these were just gross to me from appearance to consistency to taste which was the ultimate condemnation.

column9: A little dry, but tasty nontheless.
column10: Not a bad cookie. It is a tad dry, but the moist fudgey interior makes up for it. It has a rich taste of chocolate  and the interior is smooth and tasty. A nice cookie, especially nuked in the microwave for a few seconds or with a cold glass of milk.

column9: Nothing special, and high in calories to boot.
column10: These Chips Ahoy cookies are not very appealing nor appetizing.  When we first opened up the package, we noticed the majority of the cookies were broken or in crumbles.  One of them even looked like it had a bite taken out of it.  You can't always judge a cookie by its appearance, so we tried a few.  The exterior is soft and the fudge inside isn't bad.  But it just didn't mesh well together and it won't be a cookie you crave.The other negative is that each cookie is fairly small and contains 75 calories, which is pretty high considering the size.  You can get other chocolate desserts that will bring you more satisfaction at lower calories.

The Chips Ahoy! Chewy Gooey Chocofudge cookies were chewy and gooey as promised. They even included a good amount of chocolate making the Chocofudge moniker appropriate. The product itself I have no problem with. The cookies were delicious and are definitely something I would buy again and recommend to my friends, but the way they arrived? Smashed to bits! If I were to buy these cookies I'd save myself the hassle of eating crumbs and pick up a package at the grocery store.Maybe they were all crumbled because they're chewy cookies? I doubt it. I buy chewy cookies at the grocery store and have never seen so many smashed up cookies in one package. Maybe the UPS guy threw my package around because it was relatively light? I'm going to say that's doubtful because everything else I've received via UPS or from Amazon has arrived in tip-top perfect shape. (Including soft cookies from Mrs. Fields.)The Chips Ahoy! package just isn't made to endure the rigors of shipping in anything other than it's nice large case of cookies that arrives at the grocery store and then gets parceled out and placed on the shelf. The packaging wasn't sturdy enough to keep the cookies in place despite a plastic tray with individual slots for each cookie. In the entire package I had approximately four whole cookies. The rest were pieces. But at least they were delicious pieces!Like I said earlier, I'd definitely buy these cookies again but it'll be from my local grocery store, not from Amazon.

column9: Chips Ahoy with Pudding Goo Inside!
column10: I'm not a huge packaged cookie eater, but I like regular Chips Ahoy, so I thought I'd give these a shot.  I found them somewhat pleasant, but a bit unsettling.For starters, the cookies came with a resealable package.  That's cool and all, but my package had been opened, presumably by the workers who shipped the cookies, and a cookie or two eaten from each row!  A few of the remaining cookies were broken, and the majority were covered in black chocolate smears.  This was not the best presentation, and although I wouldn't expect packages to be open normally, the crumbs and smears I would expect are common.Taste was okay, close to a classic (non chewy) chips ahoy: not too sweet and somewhat cracker-like.The texture was a bit too crumbly, but similar to regular chips ahoy.  The gooey insides were not as gross as I expected.  More of a drier chocolate pudding.Ingredients were better than expected.  There's still a lot of sugar, but no hydrogenated oils or high fructose corn syrup. That's nice to see in a mass market product like this.Overall I found the cookies okay, but unimpressive.  Buy a single box before you go for the box of 4.

column9: Not as good as the "Megafudge," but still a tempting snack
column10: Chips Ahoy! is a mass-production outfit, so there's always going to be something a bit industrial about the cookies they turn out. These are definitely very edible and, if not exactly addictive, I could (and did) find myself putting away more of them than I should at one sitting. I didn't think these "Chocofudge" cookies were as good as the all-chocolate "Megafudge" variety, but still, the quality of the chocolate was, again, industrial at best. My wife, who knows her chocolate, said it tasted like they were trying to craft something darker than milk chocolate without the characteristic bitterness of true dark chocolate. She didn't think they succeeded. But if you're not looking for a connoisseur cookie experience and just need something for the snackin', these might not be bad to keep in the cabinet. If they make it there before you eat them all.

What can I say?  I love Chips Ahoy and this one with a nice fudgy filling was just what the doctor ordered.  I'm a chocoholic and proud of it!  The cookies are nice and soft with just the right amount of choco chips that are enough to satisfy even the pickiest of chocolate lovers.  Ahhhhh, these with a nice cup of ice coffee, YUMM!I do so like the softer cookies better I think even though if you are going to be dunking you might want the hard ones.  They are great with ice cream also.  I softened up some good chocolate ice cream and crumbled up pieces of these cookies and mixed together then refroze and oh my it made a nice sundae for the terrible heat we've been having.  You have got to try a few as I'm  sure you'll be hooked in no time.

We really liked these cookies!  While we were expecting them to be hard and crispy like the regular Chips Ahoy cookies, these were actually soft and chewy, just like a home baked cookie.  With the addition of the chocolate, gooey center, these cookies exceeded our expectations and will definitely be something we purchase again in the future.  These cookies will satisfy your sweet tooth and go great in milk.  Try some and you'll see that I'm right!

column9: Not as good as plain Chips Ahoy
column10: Basically these are Chips Ahoy chocolate chip cookies with a fudge center. When I first got them they were very gooey, as it was over 100 degrees that day. I put them in the fridge and that fixed that. But after trying them hot and gooey, room temperature and some-what gooey and cold and not-gooey from the fridge, I have to say, I liked the cold from the fridge ones the best.Overall though, the original Chips Ahoy chocolate chip cookies taste far better to me and the gooey factor just tasted gross. I'll stick with the Original from now on.

These cookies are chocolate deliciousness.  The title of Gooey might be a bit much and they don't really live up to the image.  The center has more chocolate (but not gooey and not like the photo).  If you chill these cookies there is really next to no gooey coming out of the center.  The flavor of these is really nice and they are soft!

I can understand the mixed reviews for these cookies.  The taste is what it is but that just means some folks will like them and some won't. I thought they were fine. I wouldn't buy them again mainly because I try to avoid eating cookies, but I didn't sense any chemical or plastic character as some reviewers mentioned.  Each cookie contains an abundance of gooey chocolate fudge that is definitely very sweet. The dough itself is also sweet and I thought it had a good texture to it. Not too crumbly, but soft and chewable.  I like these much better than the regular Chips Ahoy cookies which to me do taste artificial. The only drawback - each cookie has 70 calories and they are not very big. On the plus side, even one cookie gives you an overload of chocolate and sugar so I can see why such a small thing is so caloric.I would recommend just buying them for yourself and tasting them.  What is "too sweet" for some is "just right" for others. I found them to be very chocolately and sweet.

Chips Ahoy! Chewy Gooey Chocofudge are normal size cookies with a chocolate chip type dough with a fudge type layer within.  The dough itself is good and the fudge is tasty.  Although I enjoy these cookies I think that I like Chips Ahoy chocolate chip cookies better.

It's been a long time since I've purchased this sort of cookie, and I was surprised by how sweet they are.It's overpowering.  It doesn't even taste like chocolate.  I just get SWEET SWEET SWEET in my mouth, and there isn't any other data getting to my brain.  After I eat the cookie, the aftertaste is actually a bit noxious.I also requested a different flavor from this brand, and surprisingly, they taste great.  These simply don't.  I love chocolate chip cookies, but perhaps I'm spoiled because I bake a lot.  These are simply too processed and sweet for me.  And I'm no snob.  I love cheap junk food.They are chewy, and they are filled with some kind of super sweet frosting, but it's just too darn sweet.  Makes my teeth hurt just thinking about it.  Also, when I cleaned out my desk I discovered one of these cookies had fallen out of my lunch bag a few weeks before.  It probably spent five weeks in the open air, and yet it was identical to a fresh cookie from the original package.  No bugs had touched it.  It hadn't dried out.  Whatever they are using to preserve this product is potent.I realize prospective customers for this product are not looking for Martha Stewart's $100 chef inspired perfect cookie, but they probably want something that is reasonably wholesome and tastes less like chemicals and corn syrup.

You know those soft chips ahoy cookies that you so love? These are not those.These are smaller than those, stuffed with some plasticy-tasting 'fudge' that's actually pretty solid. Maybe like a brick of fudge but less yummy?It's 4 points plus for 2 cookies if you're doing Weight Watchers and TOTALLY not worth it.They also turn rock hard within a week and a half so chow down fast. Or just throw them out. That's probably a better option.Again, Ew.

It's ok- kids and young people will like it, but older people or those not into supersweet chemistry will find it too much. It's soft, chewy, and the one good thing is, after two cookies, you will want to share it because you won't be able to eat more!

column9: Excellent for store bought cookies... great for chocolate chip lovers!
column10: I received a package of both these and the Chewy Gooey Megafudge... so I will compare both of them.  These are excellent cookies for a store bought cookie. They are soft and have a great flavor.  Although I'm more of a brownie person (and thus loved the other variety), my husband is an avid chocolate chip lover and greatly preferred this version.  Lots of chocolate inside makes it an awesome cookie... no more plain cookie if you happen to be low on chips in each bite. EACH bit is guaranteed chocolate since it has a nice chocolate center. But it's not overbearing at all, it's really done quite nicely.  My only complaint is really towards store cookies in general: they all have a tendency to have that store bought chemical taste (I think it's the preservatives). Nothing quite like homemade in that regard!  So I took off a star for that. SOME expensive brands somehow mange this by having quick expiration dates, and if you want to spend the money on those it's worth it!

column9: about what you'd expect from a popular cookie
column10: Well, I can tell you, these didn't last long after I brought them to work.  Anything chocolate, of course, elicits immediate interest, but there were two of us working in the area when I opened the bag and a scant 3 hours later I discovered that only about 6 cookies remained. The fudgy center is certainly an added bonus to an already good cookie. The consistancy is good; not too soft, not too brittle - and overall flavor is excellent also. This would be another thumbs up.

Homemade cookies are the best in life, so I won't attempt to compare this to them.For a store-bought cookie, they are decent. I liked the MegaFudge better.They are soft and have a fudge "ribbon" in the middle that improves after having been microwaved. They do have that store-bought cookie after-taste, but they are a good cookie for an emergency treat or dessert on vacation.I feel like they could have included more in the package. The package seems disproportional to the amount of cookies you actually get. Also, they are quite fattening. The calorie and fat content is high per serving, but it is a cookie afterall.I may or may not get these again.

There must be a common ingredient that all "chewy" cookie makers use because they all taste the same. Be it Soft Chews, Chips Ahoy Chewy, or even Pepperidge Farm, whatever it is that keeps these cookies chewy also keeps them palpably homogeneous.  Chips Ahoy Gooey are no different.  Even the "fudge" on the inside tastes like "that flavor". Now don't get me wrong, "that flavor" is good and put me in the right mood, it's positively addicting.  Just know that's exactly what you're getting into here and don't expect a chocolate chip symphony in your mouth.

These cookies were good for a packaged cookie. Of course, with three kids, cookies of any sort are not long in the house. Here's the breakdown:1. Crumbled cookies: I didn't have the problems with crumbled cookies that other reviewers had. They held together nicely. However, getting baked goods shipped to you always has a risk, especially during times of temperature extremes like summer. So, that might be a problem in some cases.2. Taste: these cookies are no comparison to a homemade cookie, but what packaged cookie is? The taste is about the same as a regular Chips Ahoy Cookie if you added chocolate frosting to it. They do taste like a commercially processed food. Most likely because they are.The chocolate filling adds an additional flavor to the normal Chips Ahoy taste. It's good, but not super exciting.3. Gooey-ness: The picture and label hints that you're looking at a fudgy-gooey center. The package I had was good, but the chocolate was more a disc of chocolate. It was not hard, but it wasn't the runny-chewy that it looks like.4. Overall: these cookies weren't bad, but they also aren't something extremely exciting.These are ok if you want to keep a package of cookies laying around.

My 7 year old liked this cookie, but  she couldn't handle eating any more than 1 a day because it was overly sweet.Personally, I didn't care for the taste that was full of preservatives and was the furthest thing to the standard home or stored baked cookies. It's interesting that they were able to keep the chocolate soft inside the cookie, but it didn't add any value to the cookie. The cookie was indded soft, crumbly, w/ lots of chocolate inside but the overall taste was just too unnatural to enjoy.It's not something I'd recommend.

To me, despite the Chewy Gooey Chocofudge hype, these tasted pretty much like any other packaged soft chocolate chip cookie that I've had.  They are small enough that it just takes one bite to eat one.  It's very soft and so is the chocolate fudge in the middle and the chocolate chips.  They tended to already be broken or crumble pretty easily.  The chocolate is very sweet with little cocoa taste and the cookie itself is also very sweet.  You definitely need a glass of milk to go with these.Overall, it's a pretty basic packaged cookie experience - no surprises or anything special.  My kids of course liked them the most.  I don't think the package lasted more than half a day in our house.

I saw these in the store and wanted to try them because they looked like something so chocolatey and delicious. I couldn't wait to bite into one and have the chocolate just ooze out of it. Unfortunately, when I tried it there was no oozing or chocolate explosion or really any sort of different flavor from the soft chewy Chips Ahoy!So, I thought to myself, aha! If I warm them up in the microwave they'll get the texture and oozyness that I'm looking for. Again, big disappointment. It was just a warm cookie.I'd have to say that these are really no different then the chewy Chips Ahoy! There may be a slightly more chocolate filling flavor but not like what you'd expect from something that claims it's gooey. The cookie certainly doesn't look like the image on the cover. Even after the microwave it still pulled apart without any goozing of any sort.They're good cookies and all just not what I expected or hoped for.

My husband and I love chocolate chip cookies.  We enjoy especially ones that are warm and gooey.  So when I saw these we just had to try them - they are great.  I often make the refrigerated cookies and we eat them while they are still warm.  These cookies taste like they are fresh from the oven; pop them in the microwave for 20 seconds - warm cookies from the oven.  The package kept them fresh even after being opened for a about a week.  An added bonus the fudgy center.
