column9: OK stuff if used within reason.
column10: First, I'm not sure why it's called "oil": it's butter, not oil; it's solid w/o refrigeration. The consistency is translucent sorta clunky white, sorta like grated candle would look. Just like butter, it immediately melts in your hand or mouth, to say nothing of the frying pan. Smells great, tastes also nice: like, well, coconut. Supposedly it's great for cooking due to its supposedly higher heat-resistance something: it's supposed to keep its nutritional qualities when heated better than other common cooking oils. There's a rub though: with many foods you can mix and match and achieve some sort of mixed flavour -- not with this stuff! It's irrepressible: whatever you add it to -- veggies, cakes, meat, cardboard, or motor oil -- will then smell/taste like coconut and nothing beside. It overpowers every other flavour. So the only cooking variables you have left when using it is texture and sweetness (and looks, I guess). It goes very well with something that's sweet (probably because we're used to coconut being used in sweets). From what I've tried, it goes well with carrots, apples, sunflower seeds (anything nutty-tasting), stuff like that. Real good with sweet potatoes. But I would not recommed using it for cooking meat (unless you like your pork chops smelling and tasting like coconut). You can't kill this flavour, that's what I'm getting at. I'm using it carefully (not too much and in suitable combinations) and I'm happy with it so far. The product seems good, and so is the price (Added on 12/18/2010: that was the price at the time of purchase, $13.54 on Dec 2, 2010 -- and now, only two weeks later, the price on this page is $18.46, amazing, no? A 30% increase in two weeks, wow, these guys sure are optimistic about the value of their product).A bit of a warning: there's a megaton of unsubstantiated semi-literate BS online about miraculous powers of coconut oil. Be careful about it: coconut oil is pure saturated fat (a serving consists of 14 grams of fat, 13 of them saturated) -- and I've found no acceptable medical/scientific info in support of the healthfulness of saturated fat (while there's a lot on the opposite). What I did find was that it's not openly harmful when used in small doses: a healthy 200-lbs 40-sh male, not overweight and exercising regularly, is allowed 200 saturated-fat calories a day. A serving of coconut oil is 130 calories, but of course, you'll get saturated fats from other foods too. Another thing is that coconut oil contains no appreciable amounts of vitamins/minerals (unlike butter, which is _loaded_ with all kinds of goodies). So be careful: despite the squall of shilling on the net and in print, it's not health food. But it's tasty and not like lethally bad, so...-------Added on 12/18/2010: I'm half-way through the first jar, and I find myself using it less and less. It's too smelly, and I just don't have that much opportunity to use it for stuff where it's OK. Besides being food, it is supposedly also good for external use, for skin and hair; I haven't tried it this way (yet; maybe I will). But I have a feeling that _as food_ it doesn't have much of a future in this household: it's too overpowering, too particular.-----01/01/2011: Tried it for skin lotion: well, um, yes and no. No: it doesn't get absorbed into the skin, and the area of application stays greasy forever, so you can't do it before going out (even wiping with, say, paper towel, doesn't remove enough of it, so you'll stain the clothes with oil). Yes: it has a terrific staying power, hours and several hand washes after application there's still something remaining on the skin. And I work with my hands a lot, with the result that they tend to get real dirty, so I wash hands frequently and rather severely, the surgical way: very hot water, several soap-ups, brush. This causes severe dehydration of the skin, so I've always used hand lotion immediately after, but with coconut oil the skin remains slightly oiled, soft and moisturised even after a couple of such washes.So, finally: I'm not sure how (and whether) I'll continue to use coconut oil: I have definitely ceased to use it as food; as moisturiser we'll see... at least it's marginally cheaper than dry-skin cream so I'll give it a longer try. But the cream dries up in a minute, so it's more practicable, I must say. Doesn't smell of coconut either! :-) I must say I did not find the product as useful as it's hyped, so I'm taking one star off right now. I'll revisit in a month or two: if I discover by then that I've stopped using this thing altogether, I'll update the review to this effect.--------02/20/2011: Bottom line: I think I've settled into a two-sided routine with this oil: I use it, first, for light-frying/sauteing veggies (with yams or sweet potatoes as a basis; adding greens, like spinach, in the mix later on). I don't do this often though, 'cause I prefer to steam or eat raw, rather than fry anything; sauteing is quicker though, so when I'm pressed for time, this is workable. The other use is for skin: skin really loves this oil -- in addition to staying hydrated forever, it becomes very even in texture and colour; after shower I grease myself up, literally from head to toe, and it's just lovely (except for the clothes who get stained :-).

I've only used a few other types of coconut oil, but I find this one pleasing in taste (no weird or artificial taste) and consistency (not lumpy or grainy). It is also the most affordable one I've found.I use it to make popcorn (yummy) frequently, and eat a scoop or two each week unheated.  I just let it melt in my mouth.  I know about the risks of using plastic for storage, but at some point, a person has the draw the line.  My line has been drawn, and I've decided that coconut oil in plastic containers is A-OK by me.  If you have major concerns, I suppose that you could transfer it into a glass jar.  I scoop it out with a plastic utensil - something just tells me dipping metal in the jar is counter-productive, but I could be wrong.This oil is well-regarded in general, I believe, by many.

We have been using Nutiva Organic Extra Virgin Coconut Oil for several years now and the results we have experienced are excellent. Taking 2 tablespoons of oil daily greatly helped in raising low body temperature, enabling a sluggish metabolism to be stabilized and facilitating weight loss. We have also used it topically on acne with great success - both in healing the blemishes and removing the scars. It is not a panacea, but in combination with healthy diet and exercise it is a wonderful supplement.  Before we had been buying this in the 54 oz jars, but these 15 oz tubs are so much more convenient to use and for travel -- and the price was lower! Unbeatable combination!  The first shipment was damaged in transit, but one phone call to Amazon resolved the problem and they sent out the replacement shipment express at no charge.

Coconut oil is one of my favorite oils for cooking.  This particular brand has a mild flavor, at least compared to other brands I've tried, and is very reasonably priced.  It is also very stable (keeps well) and is cold pressed virgin.  I used to get this at Wild Oats in Denver, CO to use for stir fries and sautees.  It makes an INCREDIBLE Thai style curry -- you use this oil to fry the spices and vegetables, then simmer everything in coconut milk.  You get several layers of coconut flavor this way.  Plus, this is one of the best oils you can consume *period*.  It is so rich in HDL and other good fats it'll scrub your arteries clean in a month.  The coconut is a magical thing...there's a reason that coconut water can be used in an IV in place of saline for dehydration-- it's meant to be in your blood!

column9: So moisturizing it made my skin RUB OFF!
column10: This stuff is incredible. I had been using almond oil, jojoba oil, all different kinds of body lotions, and castor/olive oil. NONE came close to being as brilliant as coconut oil!About me:*I am 20 yrs old, white/half-russian. My skin is acne-prone and a BIT on the dry-side. My skin doesn't tan or burn easily, and I am obsessed with anti-aging (I want to write a book on what worked and what didn't when I am older :D). I live in California, so the weather is rather neutral year-round.*What coconut oil has done for me:Coconut oil smells sooo nice and has a great texture -- depending on the weather it is either creamy and solid or silky and liquid. Being as affordable as it is, I can smear this all-over my body after showers and it will absorb within 30 minutes to an hour. My skin feels sooo soft and hydrated afterwards and it even helps my sunless tanners last longer! This stuff made my skin so soft that one day I wore cotton shorts from Hollister (so you can imagine, slightly baggy). It was a hot day, and after walking around outside for only around 45 minutes my upper thighs/bikini line were KILLING ME. When I went home I noticed the first layer of skin had rubbed off because it was SO soft!!! This was a bit annoying, so I cut-down on the amount of coconut oil I use...but that was like *Wow*Also, my boyfriend constantly tells me how soft my skin is when I am using it *waiting for three more to arrive tomorrow!*Coconut oil is the best moisturizer EVER! I absolutely love this stuff and will continue using it forever! I still use castor oil every few weeks just for the healing properties (I think) and for my eyes/teeth/gums, but this stuff is sooo nice for my skin (and hair in small portions)!If you want a moisturizer that FINALLY gives the results you want, THIS IS IT!!! Five stars! :D

I've tried coconut oil before, but it was usually refined and unscented. In other words, horrible! Nutiva is great! It smells like fresh coconuts and has a very subtle coconut flavor. I use it to cook and as a body moisturizer. I don't do much deep frying, but I've sauteed shrimp and pan fried fish in this oil. Both turned out wonderfully with a slight coconut flavor which just made it all better for me. I have to agree with everyone that the plastic container is a let down, but I bought some small mason jars and put my oil in them. Works perfectly. That way I have a jar for the kitchen and one for the bath. Definitely try Nutiva if you're even a little curious about coconut oil. You won't be disappointed.

column9: Gives new meaning to:  eat it or wear it!
column10: While I ordered the Coconut Oil to cook with, I have found that it is absolutely incredible for other uses!  I suffer from psoriasis, and have been known to try anything to relieve it....well, you guessed it, the Coconut Oil was my next victim, and wow was I thrilled with the results.  It was soothing, moisturizing, and as a bonus, wonderfully aromatic.  After a couple weeks of continued use on my elbows, the results were really impressive.In addition to that, I have used it on my face, feet and hands as an overnight moisturizer, and it's doing wonders to my skin.  I also put some in a tiny tub to put on underneath lipstick (which can be so drying!).Finally, and perhaps most obviously, it is delicious and healthy for cooking.  The only caveat I'll put here is that you definitely have to know ahead of time that the coconut smell is there.  There are some meals I just don't want to smell like coconut, so those I use my good old canola oil on.  But for chicken, with a little soy sauce, it is downright tropical, and I love it!  Very very pleased with this purchase, and delighted with Amazon's pricing on it as well.

This coconut oil was great. I have been using it on my face every night after I wash. My skin tone is evening out and my pores look nice. I convinced my fiance to try it where he was chafing...ding! magic! no more chafing. :D he's pumped i'm pumped. This is good quality coconut oil. I do recommend it. It absorbs well, has a nice smell, and last a long time.

Don't even get me started on coconut oil!!! I love it so much. Great for baking, spreading, moisturizing, stirfry, has awesome cleansing properties and clears up baby's diaper rash!!! It's amazing! If you are new to coconut oil you will be intrigued as soon as you start experimenting too!! The taste is great and on the skin it goes along way. It smells nice too! Try it!!!!

This coconut oil (unrefined) is GREAT for baking.  Everyone loves my gluten-free, dairy-free brownies.  The oil is hard when refridgerated (cold brownies), but liquifies above 78 degrees F., so it literally melts in your mouth.  It also gives brownies a great extra sweetness.  You can use it in place of butter or lard in most baking recipes.  I also use it in the pancake pan and egg pan and to grease pans before baking.  This two-bottle version is actually less expensive per oz. than the large bottle version using the subsribe and save option.

Read so many reviews about this product that I just had to try it.  So far, I have used it in place of oil and butter, on toast, mixed in oatmeal, and on pancakes/waffles.  I sneak it into anything I can for my kids. It is great on my face, not greasy like I expected, it absorbs and really makes my skin glow.  I put it on my daughter's forehead where she was beginning to get little bumps, and they were gone in 2 days.  Let's see, what else?  I am happy to find a natural product that has so many uses.  I wish I had know about this last year when I had to go through Chemotherapy for breast cancer.  I have read all kinds of studies where coconut oil has been used to help patients after chemo.  I had terrible memory loss and "chemo fog".  Will definitely re-order, and send some to my Dad who has always worried about the possibility of getting Alzheimers.  (Google has great information about this.)  Hope this helps!

This product worked very good. I use it on my natural hair as a conditioner and a moisturizer and it has worked excellent for both of them. My niece who has very course kinky hair has used it and it has made her hair noticeably smoother and softer.
High quality product! I just wish that it didn't come in a cheap plastic container.. It was delivered to me on a hot day so the liquefied oil was all over my package! Eck.

column9: LOVE the Oil; Wish the Jar were Glass
column10: I love this coconut oil and I continue to order it regularly, but for health purposes, I wish it came in a glass jar.  If it did, I'd give it 5 stars.  I also wish it were cold pressed.Please consider glass?

I use the EVCO for a lot of things...I put a tablespoon in with my coffee, I have used a mixed of baking soda and the EVCO to brush my teeth and my teeth are whiter than they have ever been and they feel much cleaner after brushing, I also use it for my nightly moisturizer on my face and it helps get rid of any pimples I may have. I've also used it for cooking eggs,seasoning my veggies instead of butter.

column9: Smells great and so many uses
column10: Coconut oil is amazing, and a very versatile product.  This particular brand has a wonderful smell/taste to it.  Its way better than the LouAna brand from WalMart.  I've also noticed that this product stays liquid better than the LouAna brand.  There are also no granules or impurities.  And if you don't know, this can also be used as massage oil and personal lubricant.  I can't recommend this product highly enough.

I buy a half gallon of this every 6 months or so.  I don't worry about it spoiling because it has a much longer shelf life than other oils and a very high heat tolerance.  I use it for cooking mostly.  It is great on popcorn with sea salt, freshly baked bread, in stir frys and you can often use it in place of butter in many dishes.  I have a fabulous raw chocolate recipe that I make with it and give out as gifts.  After reading The Coconut Oil Miracle book by Bruce Fife I try to use coconut oil as much as I can.  It is anti-viral, anti-bacterial and anti-fungal.  Truly a miracle food that is so healthy for you.I also use it on my hair when it needs a deep conditioning treatment.  Just leave it in overnight and wash out the next day and my hair is so shiny and soft afterwards and even feels a bit thicker.  It is great for your skin, especially if you feel like you are getting sick.  Just slather it on and let its amazing healing properties absorb into your blood stream via your skin.  I use it in smoothies to help my immune system as well.  And if I feel like I am coming down with something I will mix it with orange juice like is recommended in the Coconut Oil Miracle book.I also oil pull with it.  If you haven't read about oil pulling with coconut oil, you should.  It is a great teeth whitener among many other things including healing mouth sores.I really like the Nutiva brand because it tastes fresher than most. Very clean coconut flavor. I like that it is organic and doesn't have any thing funky in it nor is it processed unhealthily like so many other brands.

I've been using this product for a week now and I cannot believe the difference in my skin. I have seborrheic dermatitis on my scalp, ears and near my eyebrows and I have put the coconut oil on and left it on overnight (using a towel on my pillow because it is greasy) and the difference is amazing! I was given an Rx from my dermatologist (Luxiq Mouse - which is a steroid), but I don't like the idea of putting that on daily, as it thins out your skin.I've tried lotions (cetaphil, eucerine, etc.) but I have never had an improvement like this.In addition to the seborrheic dermatitis, I have very dry skin. At the end of the day, if I'm wearing a dark-colored shirt, upon removal, the shirt is lined with skin flakes (gross, I know). But, since using this coconut oil, the flakes are GONE! It's truly unbelievable! Prior to receiving the coconut oil, I was washing with Cerave and using their lotion as well. While I noticed my skin didn't feel as "tight", I still had flakes. It wasn't until I mixed the coconut oil with the Cerave that the flakes disappeared.I also take 1 tbsp of coconut oil daily, with my breakfast. The flavor is amazing!I would 100% recommend this to anyone with dry skin or seborrheic dermatitis!

Use this for my very dry, scaly skin specially during winter time. Feels really great! Not a dry spot and it lingers for days i noticed.Use it on my face as well during night time. Use sparingly, a little goes a lot.

I have tried three different brands of coconut oil: Barlean's, Nutiva, and Tropical Traditions. The VIRGIN coconut oil has a nice, light coconut flavor.  The EXPELLER pressed coconut oil has no flavor. So, if you a buying virgin coconut oil here's my tip: Barlean's had the best flavor and smell...I wanted to eat it right out of the jar it smelled so good, tasted phenomenal!! Barlean's was the most expensive of the three but for the flavor worth it. Nutiva was a close second in taste & smell and is more economical. Tropical Traditional (which I have always loved their products in the past) did not measure up in flavor. In fact it had a strange, burnt taste and smell...something was off about it. If you want no coconut flavor at all, get the expeller pressed coconut oil. It is less expensive than virgin coconut oil...all three companies use proper, healthy, non-chemical practices to extract the oil, so I would go with the best buy for the expeller cold pressed oil but pay a little more for the flavored version.Barlean's Organic Oils Extra Virgin Coconut Oil, 16-Ounce JarNutiva Organic  Extra Virgin Coconut Oil, 15-Ounce Tubs (Pack of 2)32-oz glass - Gold Label Organic Virgin Coconut Oil - 1 quart

If you are going to eat this kind of stuff, then you might as well do it right. THIS is the only brand I buy for my cold pressed, extra virgin coconut oil. This is fantastic and at this price, I'm even happier. You will love this product.fyi - it can solidify pretty easily at temperatures below 65 degrees Fahrenheit. Just use your butter knife and kind of scrape a bit at a time. Enjoy. :)

Just started using coconut oil at home a few weeks ago. I started with a brand I purchased a local Hy-Vee because I wanted to try it out before I bought a more substantial amount. THe first buy was a refined coconut oil made by Spectrum. It worked well for what I used it for - nightly oil cleansing on my face, moisturizer and as an addition to my weekly deep conditioner for my hair...occasionally I'd spread some on toast. It worked out well, so i purchased ther Nutiva and was expecting a much better product than the Spectrum....it arrived yesterday and I was not disappointed. As soon as I opened it I could smell it - it smells and tastes AMAZING - just like fresh coconut. If you're not a fan of coconut, remember that this is not the smell/taste of sweetened, dried coconut or coconut fragrance...it smalls like actual coconut. I did my first oil cleanse with it last night and it seems slightly gritty at times, but nothing that is concerning to me. This is definitely a staple from now on!!

This is the only Coconut oil I have ever used so I can't compare it to others. But the fact that I love it so much that I've never considered switching should tell you about the quality of this oil. It's creamy, fragrant and tasty. I use it to cook and bake a variety of items from Thai, Indian foods, and Mexican foods to cookies and cakes. The subscribe and save price is excellent as well. I had previously purchased this brand of coconut oil from a local health food store and I'm now getting twice the oil for only a few dollars more from Amazon.

I've tried many different brands of coconut oil. So far, Nutiva beats all the other ones. I use it as an oil/shortening substitute for everything from frying to baking. It is also great to simply spread on toasted bagels or bread. If I'm not using in foods, then I'll eat a couple tablespoons daily as suggested by my doctor, the health/nutritional benefits are finally and increasingly being recognized and praised. You won't regret trying this product, and you'll be hooked on it!

Uses:-drizzle on toast, green salad-after bath oil to retain skin moisture-massage oilPros:-tub as pictured-pleasant, fresh coconut aroma-smooth, clean taste-pure white color-solid at room temperature below ~75 FCons:-one out of six tubs leaked during shipping-awkward container for pouring if room temp above ~80 F

column9: Great Stuff for a Number of Things
column10: I was almost put off using coconut oil entirely, after purchasing another brand (I think NOW was it, but different packaging). It came hard as a rock, yellow-looking and smelled pretty foul (almost sickly-sweet) - certainly nothing like coconut. I literally was chipping it out of the jar, and melting it was near impossible. Eventually, I realized that I was dealing with rancid oil, so it's pretty fortunate that I didn't use it all that often. Yuck.After watching a view Youtube videos for hair care, I noticed everyone's was white, creamy and you could easily scoop it out of the jar, so I decided to give it another shot and purchased Nutiva in February 2011. I'm so glad I did, too, because this stuff is great and for a number of things, some of which caught me off guard.- Cooking -I enjoy cooking with it now and then, especially with my quick-fix quesadillas when I don't have time to cook anything else. However, it doesn't work on everything due to the subtle yet nutty flavor it can give, but I do like it for frying. Your place will smell like coconut when you fry with it, as a warning. I do love how fast it heats up, though.- Hair -I originally intended to use this for hair and as a deep conditioning mask. I am biracial, with 3A/3b and a tinge of 3C hair. While I usually prefer to have it relaxed, I decided to give it a break due to lack of funds. The hard water we have here has been wreaking havoc on my hair and it's been in need of a trim for a while, but this stuff has greatly improved things, and it even can be used (lightly) to help tame frizz to some degree as a leave-in. My ringlets are back and the best-looking they've been since I can remember, and all I've been using since then is just Aphogee Green Tea spray, coconut oil and occasional argan oil.- Skin -I consistently use this on my body and at night as skin cream. For the face, you only need a tiny, tiny amount. It also helps to tame down blemishes, which is a bonus, and leaves skin glowy. Last year or the year before, I also developed what looked like flesh-colored moles, which I thought were blemishes at first, but I can't be certain. Nothing I did would get rid of them though, until I started using the oil, which I found odd, but at least it worked! All in all, my skin has dramatically improved using this, with the help of some other products, and I don't feel I have to wear foundation.- Pets -I give 1/2 tbls. to my cats and 1 tbls. to my dog a few times a week to help maintain their coats and keep their skin nice. It seems to be doing great and they've stopped driving me mental with scratching. I also tried it in hopes of helping my dog with her seizures. While it's not a drastic improvement, they have been fewer in between, which may or may not have a connection. I just mix it in their food maybe 2-3 days a week (ask your vet about how often, especially if they have health problems), and they love it. Even my female cat, who's picky about what she'll eat licks at the oil before she munches away.- Warts -Short of the suspicious-looking things on my face at one point, I don't get moles, warts, or even freckles. However, I did get one whopping wart on the top of my big toe last year, which nothing would get rid of. I tried apple cider vinegar, wart patches and gels - you name it; I tried it. Not only did it hurt like crazy and work slowly, but it never got rid of it. All I did get was a scar and a lot of grief, only for it to return a few weeks later.When I started using coconut oil on the skin, I realized one day, like with my face, that my wart that had grown back was getting smaller. I kept watching it and finally realized the connection. I started using bandaids and applied a glob of oil on the spot before bed and then really started noticing results. This wart was the size of a chick pea (sorry to be gross lol), but now you can't see anything.I finally looked things up and realized that it was the acid in the oil that attacks lipid-coated virus cells, such as what's associated with HPV (warts), so I guess it makes sense. I was surprised though! I can tell due to the texture of the skin that it's not 100% gone (roots), but it still getting better and I'm not embarrassed anymore. It took about a month, but the more painful options took just as long and this is pain-free. So, it's something to try!Love this stuff and can't stop raving about it. I'm going to purchase more soon in this size to keep one in my kitchen and one in my bathroom again, plus a larger one for the mutts. The bathroom one still has plenty in it, despite me using it near-daily.

I have had coconut oil before but none that compares to this.  It is sooooo good!  It looks good, smells good, and tastes good.  It is well worth the price.  It is very smooth and has a slightly sweet taste.  I use it in place of butter and shortening.  It is really good on toasted bread. I suppose it would be a really good skin moisturizer also.

I'd seen many suggestions for coconut products, including coconut oil, on the healthy living blogs I subscribe to, so I figured I'd see what the buzz was all about.  We searched at the local natural foods stores and weren't able to find it, so I turned to Amazon.  I swapped it in for the canola oil in a boxed brownie mix - delicious!  It had a slight coconut flavor (likely because of the amount it calls for), and the oil stays solid at room temperature, thus minimizing spillage.  Next, I'll be testing it with savory foods to see if the coconut flavor comes through in eggs/veggies/etc.  But for baked goods, I'd totally suggest the swap.(Oh yeah, and this product was eligible for Prime, so I had it within 3 days...nothing beats that!)

I use the small container strictly for my skin.  I never fear a heat rash or break outs.  This is great for Athletes Foot.  Any type fungus.  My son has dandruff and he rubs it in his scalp, no more dandruff.  This brand is the creamiest that I have found.  Good for skin and hair makes skin extremely soft. Melts good in the bath.

This is great stuff... it confers an open, airy flavor to things that calls out to be used (and eaten).Really makes me want to come up with more ways to integrate it and cook with it... I'm impressed.Mixes well with other oils (I keep a garlic-oil concoction at the ready at all times in case there are french loaves that need toasting or eggs that need scrambling)Very very good.

This is the best coconut oil around!--"Extra virgin" means it actually smells of coconut and is far less processed than the refined coconut oil that is next to it on the shelf.--It's a solid when left at room temperature but takes seconds to melt down in a pan and measure accurately into measuring spoons and cups if you're put off by its solid state. It should also be melted down before going into baked goods to be most effective, unless mixing it into something heated.--I use this coconut oil to toast pecans for my morning steel-cut oats as well as substituting all oils and butter for most of my baked goods!--It adds a subtle sweetness when replacing butter and any other oil.--If ever I happen to get this oil on my fingers, I simply rub it in as a moisturizer since it smells heavenly and trumps any other moisturizer I've used.--The wonderful thing about this oil is that, while high in saturated fat, it is broken down differently in the body and thus is not the bad sort of saturated fat you might normally be weary of (This is as I understand from my own personal research and there is still some debate on the topic).--So while you shouldn't go overboard and use this by the barral because it's healthier than butter, you can feel better about using it as a substitution.--I recommend Artisana Organic Raw Coconut Butter 16oz also if you like Nutiva's extra virgin coconut oil that can be added to steel-cut oats and any other food you can sneak it into if you're like me and need to force fat into your diet because you're an active vegetarian lacking consistent  source of fat and don't want to have to plan it into meals each day

You can read all the reviews for coconut oil, so there's no need to say it again, but this product has improved my life and the lives of my pets many times, many ways. I have tried several brands, and the Nutiva brand is my favorite for flavor, cost and effectivness.  I love it!  I would recommend this product for everyone, as it offers benefits for every type of problem, and for improvements in energy levels, weight loss, better skin and hair, fighting infections....the list is endless. Bravo Nutiva for offering a product that is reasonably priced of the highest quality, and bravo Amazon for offering this superior product at such a good price point.

I have been having problems with my skin. The moisturizer I was using felt kind of scummy on my face after I added my foundation and I was having troubles with facial redness and dry patches. I was also having heat rash problems in my underarm area. I started using just a little of the coconut oil on my face in place of my moisturizer, then applying my foundation and wow! What a difference! My skin has cleared up and I love the soft smooth way my face feels. My foundation spreads and blends much better.  Also, the coconut oil really helps with the heat rash, immediately soothing the discomfort. I like using this as a hand cream too. I look forward to seeing how well it works this winter when the air is much drier.I have done a little cooking with it, but not enough yet to have an opinion.Other folks have mentioned that the oil leaked during shipment. I was concerned about this since I ordered it during the summer. I ordered 4 tubs (2 pks of 2 tubs). The plastic containers arrived packed in plastic bags, 2 tubs/bag, within the box. Even though the lids felt pretty tight on the tubs, both of the plastic bags had some coconut oil that had leaked, but not enough to feel cheated. A little oil leaked out of the plastic bags into the box, but they were the only things packed in the box so nothing was ruined. I can see that if the lids had been any looser though, there would have been a mess. Oil is hard to keep in a container with a wide mouth like this.One more thing...I absolutely love the smell of this stuff. It has a light roasted coconut essence which isn't too strong and doesn't linger overly long, but long enough to enjoy for a short while while it is being absorbed by the skin. Yum!

column9: Nutiva Organic Extra Virgin Cocunut Oil
column10: I purchased this product to use with my other hair products.  I love the results!  After using it for just two days I noticed instant thickness in my hair.  I have it mixed with 3 parts EVCO, 2 parts EVOO, 1.5 part Vitamin E and 1.5 part hari oil with almond oils. I use it as a pre-shampoo treatment and twice daily.

Excellent! I use this in EVERYTHING I cook, I use it in plain rice, fried rice, pasta, frying eggs anything. The flavoring is great and my house is always filled with the delicious aroma. Not just food, but creates soft, healthy coat on dogs.  Just rub in while petting.

My daughter introduced me to this product. We both had bumper crops of tomatoes and needed to use  them up. She decided to make and can salsa. Texans are very particular about their salsa, so I was skeptical about using a packaged seasoning. I changed my mind when she let me taste what she had made. I ordered mine online, so now I don't have to go looking for it.

The best product on the market for making Salsa.  I have been using for years.  Just by giving my family and friends samples of the salsa, they have all been purchasing this product.  The only problem is it is hard to find in stores but ordering on line the pricing is much better.

column9: Probably the best I've ever made!
column10: This is the first year I've made this and have had to make 3 batches in 1 month because family and friends absolutely Love it!  Not too spicy - wonderful flavor.  I add black beans and corn and it's almost a meal in a jar!  I highly recommend this from beginner to expert!

Mrs. Wages is the best salsa mix around. It's great to be able to freeze it and not worry about canning and pantry space. Great product for reasonable cost! Also available in regular, medium, and hot varieties.

I have been using Mrs. Wages salsa mix for some time now.  I can my own salsa each summer when my tomatoes are taking over in my garden!This salsa mix is the best I've ever found.  My husband is the salsa lover and he LOVES it!  You won't be disappointed.

column9: All good but use less vinegar
column10: Have made two batches the first was good but had too much vinegar.  The second batch we put half the amount and it was great.  I went a purchased gallons of diced tomatoes.  It was very easy and good!

Mrs Wages salsa mix packages provide everything you need for good salsa except for your own home grown tomatoes. I prefer the mild over the medium, but the mild is difficult to find.  I like the mild because then I can add my own jalapenos to get the flavor I want. This product saves you from having to chop all those smelly onions and saves time too.  All in all a good product our family has enjoyed for years.

This is my favourite salsa-mix, ever.  When I didn't know enough about cooking and making salsa, it was perfect.  But now that I know more and can whip up one without a recipe, it's still perfect - I know the proportions, how many pounds of tomatoes to buy, and how many pint jars one packet will fill.  It's the best way to take advantage of delicious summertime tomatoes for salsa, especially when there are only hothouse tomatoes to be found and you're craving a great salsa that's not overly processed.

They shipped it after the last day that Amazon said I would have it.  Good thing I had other tomato canning to do while I was waiting for it.

G-Tox works great!  Be sure to follow the directions for it to fully work and don't try to take the bottle the morning after.  I have given the product to many of my friends and they all love it.  Every time I have taken a G=Tox, I wake up with no hangover.  Remember though, you may still be tired due to lack of sleep.  Your head will not be pounding in the morning!!!!

I just got back from a three day Bachelor Party in Montreal, which was epic.  I was the Bachelor, so in good form my buddies fed me plenty of drinks throughout the night.  Luckily my cousin was there and he gave me a GTOX each night before I passed out.  I felt one hundred times better the next than I expected after three long nights.  I was still tired from not sleeping well, but my head,stomach and body felt much better.  I would recommend this product to anyone and I just bought a case for my house.  I will let you know how it works out in a few weeks, as I have anoother Bachelor Party for a friend coming up in three weekends.Cheers,Joe

I thought this was a gimmick. It's not. I woke fully refreshed and feeling as if I had done nothing the night before...even though I had over-drank wine. It's truly something cool to have for the occasional event. Probably not a good idea for alcoholics who drink all day or those who drink super hard beverages by the gallon every night.  But for regular types, it seems to do the trick. You wont wake up groggy or with a headache, you simply wake up business as usual. Very cool.

column9: Great stuff I am amazed it works!
column10: I was not thinking this would work, but I drank 2 bottles of GTOX before bed after drinking a mix of shots, beers - I was tore up.  I work early and woke up feeling good.  I was amazed, I will be buying this again!

This product might work for someone else, but didn't seem to help me at all. I drank several bottles before going to bed after a heavy night of drinking and woke up feeling just as bad as I would have if I hadn't taken anything.

column9: money tree plant owner, glenn mifune
column10: Dear people at Amazon.  I recently made a purchase on Amazon for a large 5 braided money tree plant.  Well, that's what I received, butit looked like a Charley Brown Tree.  Who ever braided this tree, took 5 of the worst individual trees they could find, braided it, andsent it to me.  After complaining about this tree, I was told, Glenn be patient with me, and I will find another nicer looking 5 braidedmoney tree plant and ship it to you.  That was the last I heard.  When I sent another message, there was no response.  Never again willI make a purchase.

column9: Twice the price of the individual boxes
column10: Did the math. A square cardboard box of 8 of the SINGLE SERVING INDIVIDUAL pouches, each of which makes 16-20oz, costs between $1 and $1.50 at WallyWorld in the Tampa area. We rounded and say each BOX makes one gallon.In comparison, each of these 2.1oz canisters makes 3 gallons (12Qts) and there are 2 canister to an order for a total of 6 gallons for $12.75 plus S&H; average total $17 for 6 gallons.  The individual single serve pouches cost $6-$9 per 6 gallons from WallyWorld or the grocery store, almost half price.The wife LOVES the stuff though in every flavor but orange! I however LOVE the Orange and use it in smoothies with milk, banana and extra Splenda for an Orange Julius type drink.

This is not the same Adams Flea and Tick Dip of days gone by.  The old formula was quite effective and got rid of ticks after 2 dippings on my dog Maggie.  My grandson's dog King is plagued with ticks because of the surrounding area that we live in. He's taken for walks along the street with woods and a lake and gets re-infested quite quickly.  It has helped, but is not 100% effective. Now he scratches all the time and I have ordered some Stop Itch shampoo and conditioner to see if this helps. We even tried AdvanTix that did not help get rid of the ticks either. We shall go back to the Preventic collar. Maybe a bubble suit or space suit would be the solution.  "White American Eskimo Dog in a Bubble/space suit walks the outer perimeter of Miami Florida along the lake and woods to keep out ticks".  We use Advantage for fleas and he is flea free 100%.

The product works well and my dog did not have any adverse reaactions.  It would be nice if the company included something to reduce itching because of dry skin, and other reasons.  It is hard to tell if my pet's scratching is due to fleas or dry skin.
I am old-fashioned, so I love the fact that Charms offers a whole box of the original flavored Blow Pops.  This is one of the small things in life that make me very happy!

i drink starbucks as my choice of coffee. i decided to try something new. this coffee has become my favorite coffee ever. the taste is bold with a smooth nonbitter finish. the taste is like a combo of hints of very little dark chocolate. i now find myself ordering mycoffee from amazon on a reg bases. i never thought i would replace my starbucks, but i did.
by far the best! i cannot get enough of these! and bc they are small my 7y/o feels like he's getting a lot! LOVE THESE!

My growing kids and I all love these!  They satisfy a salty-snack craving, but they're made with good ingredients so you feel like you've eaten food, not junk.  Very satisfying!  I can't keep them in the house, so I'm glad to find a multi-pack and a better price here.  The subscribe and save price is definitely the best I've found.

Loved the idea of a healthy snack so gave these a try. Tasty treat but WAY too much salt. They are soooo salty they gave me a headache!  If you are watching your sodium intake, skip these little crackers.  It's too bad, too, because otherwise they were a nice snack.  Not going to purchase again.

column9: If you have to eat junk food, at least eat organic junk food!
column10: Since watching the movie Food, Inc., I have been taking even more care not to buy anything with HFCS or partially hydrogenated oil in it. When it comes to snack foods, that's really difficult. Graham crackers, soda crackers, and many bagged crunchy snacks have one or the other in the list of ingredients, not to mention that the ingredient list includes a lot of unrecognizable ingredients! I'd be okay not buying junk food, but my kids would revolt if we had NOTHING. So I bought some of these Late July mini crackers, both cheese and peanut butter. The kids gobbled them down in no time, and I have to admit, I ate a handful too. They're pretty pricey, but buying them in bulk definitely helps. Feeding them these crackers makes me feel a little bit better about allowing them to eat food that, let's face it, has little nutritional value.

column9: Late July Mini Cheddars the Best
column10: The crackers are the best. Great for lunches or a mid afternoon snack.
These sandwhich crackers are very good. The whole family loves them, and they are healthy compared to what is in the store.

I'd pass on purchasing these snack crackers again.  Amazon was out of the full sized Late July Organic Cheddar Cheese Sandwich crackers (which I liked) so I thought I would give these a try.  Most were broken and those that weren't were soooo "mini".  This might be OK for toddlers...  They also did not taste as good (cheesy or fresh) as the full size crackers.  Sorry Late July...  I wouldn't bother making these...
I love grape laces, but these are too hard and don't have much flavor to them.  The plastic bag they were in was so crisp and stiff that it ripped all the way open and the laces when everywhere.

I bought a box of these treats for my two picky little dogs with itchie paws (10lb each) from Costco several months ago.  I've now emptied the box - well the dogs emptied the box - and I went back to Costco for another go around.  Whoops - it was a one time thing for Costco.... darn! So off to the specialty puppy store for grain free/gluten free dog treats.  Tiny little bags of treats for $6 a bag! Sooo got home and checked the Amazon website .... Hello .... Here are the treats from Costco!  Wish I had found them before now!My dogs are kinda picky.  I feed them Fromm grain free foods which they eat well - but the Fromm treats are really expensive and kinda large.  These are nice and small for small dogs ... about 1.5 inches by .5 inches.  They look kinda plasticky rather than "home baked" but that didn't seem to bother my dogs - they still woofed them down.  As for flavor ... well I didn't eat them but my dogs both seemed to like them.The box I got at Costco lasted me about 4 1/2 months with three heavy treaters for the two dogs.  There are a LOT of treats in this box and they held well in a ziplock bag.

My dog, a 65 lb Aussie Dingo mix isn't finicky, but he seems to especially love these biscuits. I love that they're grain free with generally wholesome ingredients.The ingredients are not on the Amazon site nor on the company web site so as a service to fellow Amazon shoppers: the ingredients are Peas, Ground Peas, Turkey Meal, Potatoes, Pea Protein, Pumpkin, Chicken Fat, Blueberries, Cranberries, Pea Fiber, Ground Tapioca, Flax Seed, and Lecithin. While not perfect, Turkey Meat, for example, would be better quality than "Turkey Meal", and Sweet Potatoes would be better than "Potatoes" these are generally excellent and non-allergenic ingredients.I use these in my treat bag, about 7 or 8 a day and Rusty works very hard for them, which makes for a happy dog and owner. Healthwise, we feel comfortable giving him a few of these a day these instead of quality kibbles.

Korean seaweed snacks are very tasty. My local Chinese supermarket sells this brand, in addition to another favorite ChoripDong Korean Seaweed Snack (Kim Nori), Roasted w/Olive oil & Sea Salted, 0.17-Ounce Bags (Pack of 12). If you've tried Japanese seaweed snacks and didn't like them, you may like Korean ones. Korean seaweed snacks are typically roasted and flavored with salt and oil while Japanese ones are oil-less. This makes Korean seaweed sheets very light, flaky, and crispy. They just crumble in your mouth. Both are very nutritious and healthy, but Japanese seaweed strips are thicker and more chewy. The downside to the yumminess is that Korean seaweed snacks typically taste saltier, so it's best to eat them with a bowl of rice, though I've gone through several packs of them on their own. You also have to wipe your fingers afterward because of the oil.Inside each pouch is a plastic tray that holds 6 or 8 sheets of pre-cut seaweed to prevent crush damage. If you don't like seaweed at all, you might not like this. Seaweed snacks are not for everyone. But if you do, definitely give this a try.
great timing on delivery....tastes great...but the packs are so small, I guess that's why they are called snack packs.

This product is ok. Not as good as other brands that I have tried (such as assi brand premium seasoned seaweed). If you are looking for a seasoned seaweed that has less salt than the others, this product would be perfect for you. The quantity is pathetic for the price...that is its only true downfall.

These seasoned seaweed strips are crisp and maybe a little oily when compared to Japanese-style seasoned strips.  This is a very flavorful and refreshing change to my diet.Seaweed has iodine in it and is what I feel is a more natural way to add it to my diet.  Portion controlled as they come in little boxes.

I get these all the time from a local Asian market at about a third of this price. Costso is now selling a nearly identical product by the case! (36 (or 12 three-packs) for 9.95) Yay!! They don't weigh much at all, so I send them to my son at college. Yes, they are an acquired taste of you're not into Asian food, but also highly addictive!
This is probably the best tasting roasted seasoned seaweed on the market that I ever had. Taste great with plain white rice.Try them you will not be disappointed...
I bought these for my brother and though I gagged at the thought of eating roasted seaweed, he LOVED them, so of course I give them 5 stars.

column9: Not what I thought it was
column10: It was not the same product pictured. I was specifically looking for that product. I am slightly disappointed. It didn't taste as I had expected either.
With four labs, a golden and a pitty, we need to  purchase rawhide bones in bulk.  This was delivered on time, and the product was good.  You get lots of chews for your buck.
These are great bones that were delivered quickly.  Will order again.  My black lab loves them and they help keep her teeth clean.

I'm rating this product based on flavor. It has a somewhat subtle sweetness that doesn't make my face scrunch up if I eat it by the spoonful. When I first tried it I noted a slightly floral pungency, but I could no longer detect it after continued use. It is absolutely perfect for tea and one of the better honeys that I've used in my tea.It's a beautiful golden color that seems to swirl or glitter in the light unlike any honey I've seen before.This is definitely worth trying. The aroma alone is notably enjoyable.After trying several other honeys from New Zealand, I've decided that I prefer the flavor of this one in particular.This jar is made of #1 PETE plastic and is BPA free. The lid is made of polypropylene, so you won't have to worry about BPA or PVC in plastisol food liners touching your honey. There is no seal, and that's the major downfall of the packaging. I like when there's a seal even if the lid is considered relatively safe -- it makes me feel better about having the honey shipped during hot weather when certain plastics are more likely to leech into food. I'm not going to take a star away because of packaging, but if I could give it a separate vote the packaging would get a three or four star -- mostly for not having a seal.Other organic honey with BPA and PVC free packaging:Certified Organic ManukaReally Raw Honey, 1 X 16 OzWee Bee Naturally Raw Honey -- 1 lb EachHimalaya Herbal Healthcare - Soliga Forest Organic Honey, 8.8 oz gelWholesome Sweeteners Organic Raw Honey, 16oz

I've been searching for a product like this for a while now.  A business associate of mine brought me some "pepper spread" that his Italian mother makes and it was great.  So I started looking for a similar product in grocery stores and specialty shops.  This is the first one that I would buy again.  It's quite hot and delicious!  I love to spread this on crusty bread and eat it along with dinner.

column9: Tutto Calabria products are superior quality
column10: My family lives in the village where Tutto Calabria is based. In fact I just returned from there (they're 3 houses away from my family but that's another story LOL) All produce used by Tutto Calabria are organic and the recipies used are traditional to the region.  The Celli family are wonderful kind ethical people who look to produce a superb product at an  affordable price.  Explore and trust me you won't be disappointed!!
This hot spread can be used on bread (forget mayonnaise) or thinned down with olive oil and serve with linguini and  grated cheese.I bought 4 jars!

column9: Was hoping for a little more heat, but love the flavor
column10: I've been hooked on pepper spreads for a long time and especially since I was in Italy and brought home a few. I love the distinct Italian pepper flavors which are different than Mexican and Asian peppers. This spread is actually pretty mild but it does have a great, unique pepper spread flavor. it's also a lot of diced stuff, and reminds me of the texture of an olive tapenade. It is not super oily. there is oil that collects around the top when you first open it, but overall it's a pretty 'dry' spread as opposed to something that is soaked in olive oil and drips everywhere. That makes this very suitable for putting on crackers. It also works great for bread of course, though I'd want it more oily for breads. No problem though, just have some olive oil handy.Because of the cost, I would not bother using this a part of a sauce. It's best as a spread or maybe used as topping for stuffed peppers or pizza. All in all it is very high quality and an excellent appertiva/tapas addition.

We buy this in Italy, when we are there, at a small grocery store.  Actually we clean the shelves of it and bring it home to the States with us. It was great to find it on Amazon as no one in our area sells it; that I know of. It can be used on great bread as a spread or to cook with to liven up sauces or to marinate seafood, etc.

column9: Intense flavor for just a few calories.
column10: I love finding food items that add a lot of flavor without adding a lot of calories. At just 20 calories per tablespoon, this spread is amazing. Yes there are plenty of low-calorie spreads out there, but who would want to eat them? One tablespoon on a sandwich gives it a fiery bright flavor that makes the sandwich special. On a piece of fresh Italian bread, you have a gourmet treat. Yes, it is very spicy, so stay away if you don't love a little "burn" on the the tongue. But for those who seek out intense flavorful experiences, give this a try.

column9: Tutto Calabria Hot Spread is Very Good
column10: Just used this spread on crusty French bread.  Toasted it, then put this spread on.  Man o man, this stuff is yummy!!  This stuff is awesome.  Taste great and has a very nice "kick" to it.  I like it so much, I will now order other Tutto Calabria products.  If there other products are anything like this one, I can't wait to try them.  Very high quality indeed.
This stuff is good on just about anything! If you don't like high spicy, don't purchase this item. All the Tuto Calabria products are wonderful!

My dogs love the bacon/egg/cheese Becca's biscuits so I decided to give these a try also. They are perfect for my Chihuahuas but would also be great as a training treat for larger dogs. They are not insanely little like the Cloudstar itty bitty buddy biscuits- they measure about 1" each- and my dogs absolutely love them. Another great Becca's product.

column4: E. Bernardino "Addicted to the Gold Box"
column9: All natural; the dogs love it!
column10: I highly recommend Becca's Barkery! These itty Bitty C&PB Biscuits are just the right size for a smaller dog (I have Pugs), and all 3 of them love the taste! They are all natural (and the ingredients are as pure and basic as home made). The 6 bags are a fantastic buy when you "subscribe and save" (less than $4.00 per bag...); I've never seen these retail that low anywhere! Try them...I don't believe you or your dog will be disappointed!

My mastiff started eating Becca's treats when she was 8 weeks old and at 5 years old she is still eating them. She will spit out another company's biscuit for a Becca biscuit. I have recommended her biscuits and will continue to recommend Becca's biscuits.

column9: Good for training, but what about the calories?
column10: I bought these as a healthy, affordable training treat for my dog. I also hoped my dog would like them a little more than the traing treats he had been eating, Premier Liver Biscotti Dog Treats, 6-1/2-Ounce Wheat/ Egg Free Bow Wow Bites. My dog liked the biscotti, but I thought he might be getting tired of them. My dog likes these Becca's treats, but not more than the biscotti. I get the same response from my dog whichever I use.The ingredients are wholesome, but the calory information is not available, even on the company website. I struggle to keep my dog within his healthy weight range, so not knowing the calories is troublesome. The biscotti treats are 1 to 2 calories each. Each biscotti treat is smaller and less dense than each Becca's treat, so Becca's must be more caloric. I just wish I knew how much more caloric.One slight advantage to the biscotti for me is that they are very hard and can be carried in one's hip pocket on a walk without crumbling. Becca's bits are softer and need to be carried in a loose pocket. Their softer texture may be an advantage for small dogs or dogs who have trouble chewing.I personally won't buy these again and plan to give some bags as doggie gifts, but some dogs may really like the taste and respond best to these for training. I'd say to try them, especially if you are searching for a good traing treat for your dog.

This cornbread is perfect. You cannot tell it is missing anything and it is egg, nut, peanut, milk, and wheat free (and maybe more-that is all I check for). My hubby is from the south and when he commented on how great this cornbread was, I knew that we had a true winner!

This is a great cornbread mix!  I don't eat gluten products & it can be difficult to find good non-gluten muffin mixes.  This is so yummy, especially when you add honey (a variation of the recipe written on the package).  I eat it all of the time! : )

This stuff is so good it puts "regular" cornbread mixes to shame!  Even if we ever stop eating gluten-free, we'll continue to use this mix - it's that good!  I used it to try to duplicate my mother-in-laws cornbread dressing at Thanksgiving and it was amazing!

We use this for cornbread stuffing at Thanksgiving, and plain old cornbread other times, but my favorite use is to make pumpkin bread with it, or cheesy corn muffins (I can have dairy, though one of my kids can't.) I've done pesto sausage muffins for portable meals with this mix, so very tasty!

My family has used Knorr Bearnaise for years in the individual packets from the grocery store. This large size us great for those if us that prepare a little larger amount at once. We find this extremely convenient.  A great bargain.

I cannot eat a steak without Knorr Bearnaise Sauce.  I usually purchase the individual packages but they got way to expensive...then I found the restaurant size!!!!!!!!!!!!  Can't say enough about Knorr products.

can't beat the price on this compared to the little packets and even the cost for it at restaurant supplies stores. i use it for home use as a base for other sauces or made per the directions. consistent product, same delicious taste as the half ounce for $2 packs at the grocery store

The grandchildren really like them and so do the adults.  The bars are great snacks and healthy. They have a touch of sweetness and you can't go wrong with pecans. They make a good after school snack with a glass of milk.

column9: Better then the plain Nature Valley Bars
column10: My favorite Nature Valley bar flavor is peanutbutter. I saw the pecan and decided to try them. These are my second favorite flavor! They arrived fresh, crunchy and well packaged. If you like granola bars and pecans, you will LOVE these.

column9: Pecan Crunch reminds me of Old South
column10: Nature Valley Crunchy Pecan Crunch Granola Bars are very good. they have that delicate old southern pecan taste mixed with that legendary Nature Valley Crunch. I loved them.
I love this flavor and wish that it was available at a local supply for purchase as I absolutely love the taste of this pecan crunch bar

column9: Finally found them! Stores have stopped stocking these in my area.
column10: My husband loves the Pecan Crunch flavor but they become hard to find and then non-existent.  So glad I found them on line!  Yes I ordered a case and they are in date.  My husband was excited that I found his favorite treat again!

column9: Granola Bars - Nature Valley Pecan Crunch - My Favorite
column10: I am a fan of this product.  I may be incorrect, but I find these bars give me the taste satisfaction of eating a cookie with the nutrition and calorie content of a healthy snack. The Granola is reasonably healthy and the calories of 190 calories for 2 bars is very reasonable compared to other granola bars and particularly if compared with 2 cookies of comparable size (mostly sugar and butter). I have tried a number of other healthy snack bars and I like Nature Valley the best. Although I vary which flavors I purchase, Pecan Crunch is my favorite because it has a nutty pecan flavor.

They are sometimes hard to find in my local grocery store so I was so glad to be able to get them online.  I cannot eat peanuts that are added to so many granola bars, but I want a tad more protein than bars with no nuts.  So these pecan-filled bars are great.

column9: Nature Valley Pecan Crunchy Granola Bars, 12 Ct Boxes ( Pack of 12)
column10: These granola bars are delicious!  Since I prefer the pecan bar to all the others out there, I wanted a way to purchase them without buying the variety packs. I prefer not having to drive to my local grocery store (Publix) which was the only one in my neighborhood that carried the boxes with only the pecan crunch bars.  Using Amazon to buy the product in bulk is a much more convenient way to purchase this great tasting product in bulk..

column9: Better but not enough pecan taste for 5 stars.
column10: Pretty good relative to the plain oat and honey or the almond type.  Not great though.
Essential for baking for a gluten-free diet. Not easy to find in town. Ordering by mail is very convenient.

column9: There is a reason it is expensive....
column10: This xanthan gum is not corn derived, like the rest of them seem to be.  Consequently, it IS gold plated to a mom whose children are gluten free, lactose free, soy free, dye free and CORN free.  ;)  I don't care that it is more...things turn out much sturdier and nicer using it and my son doesn't have a reaction to it.  YES.
This stuff works okay in bread mixes and such.  It is rather expensive for such a small bottle though.

It's not "gold plated".  It's too expensive for 2 oz.  They want almost $10.00 for shipping to boot!  I bought 6 oz., 3 times that amount for less than what they want for 2 oz from Swanson's,  and they charge $5.00 for shipping total for all you want to buy on your order.

Actually is not the product, which is excellent.Is the service you, Amazon.com provides.By a stroke of bad luck, I called, I have ended up in an office chair, not able to go shopping for the bare necesities of life.Live alone, no help, and the Internet along with Amazon.com, has been my proverbial raft in the middle of the ocean.Very good prices, many, many of them below supermarket mark ups.And if provided by Amazon, the option of free shipping to your door.NOW AIN'T THIS A BLESSING?Keep up the good work, and God Bless.Pedro.

I bought these pickled onions along with several other items popular in the UK. I love them. They are pickled in malt vinegar that one uses on fish and chips, which I greatly enjoy. I have used these onions "sparingly" in several applications, including on top of a pizza! They are strongly flavored so I chop them up - a little goes a long way. This is also great since they are expensive, but worth the price. Recommended!

Absolutely love these pickled onions.  reminds me of my earlier youth, being half english.  hard to find, was so happy.  only problem was in shipping, one of the lids came loose and lost all the juice.  so I had to eat some realy fast  lol

I picked up the taste for pickled onions when i lived in England.  If they make you squint when placed in your mouth theyre just right.  These were pretty close to perfect for me but I like the London Pub ones better.  I also tried Judy's sour pickled onions but they were too sour for me.

column9: Best Onions, by far - But brutally expensive.
column10: I give these five stars, because there is, really, no substitute when celebrating the Christmas Holidays. Crisp, tart and delicious, these pickled onions are always a staple on our table for Christmas and Boxing Day.  My only complaint is that you really have to be in a "Price is no object" mindset when you order these, because the price is brutal.  If you have to pay shipping also, it becomes even more scary.  As always, I will continue to look for more reasonable suppliers for them.
We adore these and have gone a long distance to  buy them.  Thank you, Amazon.  Good choice and try them with French bread and English sharp cheese.  What a treat.

column9: Next best thing to the ones in the pubs!
column10: I love pickled onions, especially when they are served in a pub with a ploughman's lunch.  Haywards are the closest I've found to the English pub pickled onions.  They are crisp with just the right tartness. I have a jar in the fridge right now.  Luckily I can buy these at the local Publix grocery store here in South Florida for less than half the price of ordering them on line!  I like to serve them with a warm buttered hard roll, a couple of cherry tomatoes and a chunk of good quality cheese.  Branston Pickle goes well with it, too.

column9: I've always preferred the traditional onions to the non-traditional ones
column10: First of all, the non-traditional ones have that chocolate coating that somehow doesn't fit in with the overall theme of the onion, and when I hang them on my tree at Christmas, the coating melts from the heat of the lights.No, it's traditional onions or nothing for me.
This makes my homemade popcorn taste delicious. This and organic evoo are all I use when I cook chicken. Great quality for the price.

column9: OK--but not good value or extrodinary taste
column10: Item arrived after at very end of allotted shipping timeframe.  Product's unremarkable plastic bottles were packed in a twin-pak box that required considerably larger exterior packaging for secure delivery.  These 16.9 oz bottles are even smaller than expected--each of the two is about the size of a premium soft drink bottle.  What was more disappointing was the lackluster taste and flavor impact of the oil itself: although smooth and light, it is nothing special.  Its use imparted no enhancing flavor when used to pop corn in an electric popcorn popper and certainly offered nothing special when used to toss a fresh salad with balsamic vinegar.This BetterBody Foods organic oil may indeed have been processed in an ultra-fabulous unique manner, but I discern no real taste difference from the grocery chain's 48oz bottle of Crisco-brand canola oil (bought on sale locally today for $2.99) with its own light taste, cholesterol-free rating, and trans-fat free purity.  Save your dollars: use more distinctive coconut oil for your corn popping [you likely will have fewer unpopped kernels than was the case with the steeply-priced BetterBody Food's organic canola oil] and buy your cold-processed canola oil in larger containers  having a more favorable price per ounce.
Look closely - the HappyMelts have much more nutritional value (including calcium!) when you compare them to the Graduates.  Our OYO loves these in all flavors!
These are yummy, healthy little treats for my kids but I won't be buying them again due to the price. I can find them at Target for cheaper and without shipping and handling.

column9: Very small tin - not worth the price!
column10: I was very disappointed when my pack of cocoa tins arrived. They are a lot smaller than I thought they would be. I would never have paid $2 a tin for these, and that is half of the original price! I was buying these as Christmas gifts, but they are too small for individual gifts. Just thought I would give everyone a heads up. The cocoa does taste good. Also it is not eligible for returns.

I have been looking for an alternative to hot chocolate for years because I do not eat or drink chocolate.  I just happened to come across this product while on vacation and was ecstatic to discover that I could buy it in a larger size.  It tastes great and I love to have mine topped with Fluff.  If you are looking for an alternative to hot chocolate this may just be the drink for you.

McStevens Belgian White chocolate is the best. I have been using it in my coffee for years. Never fails. Also, you know those drinks we buy at the coffee shops? Well, hot or cold, all you need is a blender, some ice, some coffee and McStevens and your imagination,. Have fun, but hey, don't forget to buy the McStevens, (other brands do not work).

This was pretty good.  I used probably double the instructed amount to go with the hot water.  I suspect milk would have allowed it to be the correct instructed amount.  Nice tins.  I tad pricey for me personally so I'll only drink when I'm really craving it

column9: A delicious Christmas gift; perfect for care packages & distant friends
column10: McSteven's cocoa makes an excellent Christmas gift. We send a holiday care package to our friends living overseas each year. Each package includes an assortment of gifts and treats, which we try to buy from local companies here in the Northwest (McSteven's is based in Vancouver, Washington).The cocoa is rich and creamy. While you can make your hot chocolate with just hot water, we recommend using hot milk instead for a more decadent cup.McSteven's Olde English Toffee Cocoa is packaged in 14-ounce tins, a nostalgic metal canister with a pry top plug. The size is 3.2"W x 8"H. Each order includes three tins.Each tin holds 11 servings. The ingredients are: sugar, nonfat dry milk, whey (milk), cocoa powder (Dutch Process), canola oil, corn syrup solids, natural and artificial flavors, guar gum and salt. According to the company, no hydrogenated oils are used, so your cocoa is transfat free, too.The back of the canister also includes a number of recipes.In summary, this is delicious cocoa. We purchased both McSteven's Olde English Toffee Cocoa and McSteven's Jolly Blend Cocoa. The price is reasonable and the charming packaging makes these cocoa blends an attractive Christmas gift, one that is easy to ship to distant friends.BTW: In addition to these cocoas, we also purchased and recommend Chocolove Premium Chocolate Bars, Raspberries in Dark Chocolate as a Christmas gift.Last year, we bought truffle collections from Seattle Chocolates to send overseas. Each order -- Blackberry Crème Truffles, White Chocolate Orange Truffles and Pink Polka Dot Assorted Truffles - included three boxes of individually wrapped truffles. These chocolates are no longer available on Amazon but keep an eye out should they return.

I have an absolute passion for deep, dark hot chocolate. I want chocolate which tastes like *chocolate*, rich and flavorful, with a hint of a bite. You can savor chocolate like that.What I have an aversion to is hot sugar. And, most hot mixes taste just like that; you might as well suck on a cube of sugar with a sprinkling of coca on top than drink a cup.Regrettably, McSteven's Dark Chocolate European Coca Mix fell into the latter category. It had a bit more chocolate than, say, Nestles mini marshmallow or Swiss Miss Yodel, but all in all...sugar cube. Nicht goot.

column9: The best popcorn for an air popper!
column10: I have tried other brands and this is the best for my Presto brand airpopper.Others don't pop as large or as consistent for a batch.  Few kernels are left unpopped.Love it!

The Orville Redenbacher brand has meant premium quality for decades, and today is no different.  This popping corn is designed for use in air poppers, but can be used with oil as well.  Of course, the advantage of an air popper is that the popped corn leaves the heating chamber and can't burn - unlike popped corn trapped in a microwave bag or in an oiled popper or stovepot.With Orville, you get consistently large popcorn that stands up to whatever toppings you prefer.  You won't do better with off-brands, and you don't have to deal with the continually shrinking sizes of microwave bags (which cause you to burn the first bag or two until you figure out what time setting you really need every time the size changes).  Even if Orville costs more than what you can get elsewhere, it's worth it.

column9: Overpriced, with less flavor than some brands
column10: I've popped gallons of Orville Redenbacher popcorn both in oil and in my Presto PowerPop and it always comes up big and fluffy as expected with few unpopped kernels. One day, just for the heck of it I decided to buy a bag of Great Value (Walmart brand) popcorn and see if it could compare in the PowerPop. It took a little longer to pop, but after filling the PowerPop full and 2-3 minutes in the microwave I only had 6 unpopped kernels. What also struck me is the flavor was more like CORN! It makes me wonder if Orville is GMO and Great Value is not, and if genetic modification reduces the flavor. At any rate, I will definitely be looking at other brands, perhaps organic, etc. to bring back more of that old-time popcorn flavor.

This is the best popping corn ever. It pops up light and fluffy, and when properly made, you have few kernels. The popcorn tastes great, and the jar packages it so it stays fresh and has a long shelf life.Somewhere along the way, the art of making fine popcorn has been lost, and everyone just pops the popcorn in the microwave. When you make microwave popcorn, you lose the ability to assure the freshness and healthiness of the popping oil. So, here is the way to make good old fashioned stove top popping corn.Get a large sauce pan and lid. Place two tablespoons of heart healthy oil. Let the oil warm up (medium high), and then pour in 1/3 cup of Orville Redenbacher popcorn kernels. Put the lid on and shake vigorously. In a few moments the popcorn will begin to pop. Once the popping slows down to a trickle pour the popped corn into a bowl. Salt to taste with buttery movie popcorn salt.On the oils to use . . . I like to use Olive Oil because of the health benefits, but olive oil smokes at a lower temperature, so making the popcorn is tricky in olive oil. Start by using corn oil. When you have gotten good with corn oil, then try using the more heart healthy olive oil.Assure you this will be the best popcorn ever, and you will never go back to the microwave.

My dog loves to chew, doesn't yours? These rawhide dog chews are an all USA product. Some get so rotten looking they are bleached or dyed or sometimes painted with a whitening agent to cover this up.The Wholesome Hides are from US cattle and do not leave the country. They are rolled from a single piece of hide that also maintains its collagen. Cheaper rawhide chews can be made of multiple small pieces that are loosened as the dog chews and can become a choking hazard or are made from split hides creating such thin brittle pieces they can tear the gut.It's good to find something to make my dog happy that I can also feel good about.It would be nice if they were within the Prime program for shipping and if the middle size was offered here.

After reading the book throughly, I decided to go with the Chinese Elm, since it looks great and can stand the hard tap water in the area where I live. The tree also is capable of withstanding most pests, with the exception of spider mites, but I got a humidifying tray to aide with that. I literally just received this tree and it is just great! I've been a Bonsai hobbist for more than 10 years.  I have personally visted the Brussel's Bonsai Nursery in Alabama.  IT's about 40 minutes away from Memphis Tn and well worth the drive.  I've purchased LOTS of trees from Brussel's (at the nursery, by mail and at bonsai shows) and have always been satisfied.  You get great trees at really resonable prices.  Pay particular attention to if the tree is rated for indoor or outdoors.  Outdoor bonsais that are brought indoors for more than a few days will die.  I love the Chinese Elm variety.  It has tiny vergated leaves just like the mamouth elm trees that used to blanket Chicago neighborhoods.  The Chinese Elm can be kept inside during the winter. but ALL bonsai's will do much better if you let them enjoy the summer weather outside.  If you fertilize them, they will grow profusely, thickening the trunk and developing more character and allow to enjoy your had at shaping your tree to what you define as Cool.  Dive in and Enjoy!

I received the tree three or four days after I ordered it.  It arrived in perfect shape, with plastic over the soil which was still damp!  There was no way it was going to be damaged in shipping, but it was SO well packed I was worried about hurting it while taking it out of the box.  It seemed perfectly healthy, all of the leaves being green, anyway.  Its bent form was not identical but equivalent to that shown in the picture, and with that I was pleased.Never having dealt with bonsai before, I approached my caretaking with some trepidation.  I read a couple of books (101 Essential Tips- Harry Tomlinson, for one), and another one picked at random from Amazon's wide selection.  The most important thing I got out of the books was the importance of watering.  The soil must be kept damp.  It seemed like water just flowed through the soil into the evaporation tray without any staying in the pot, but there was nothing I could do about that.  Still, I water it daily (as directed) and so far (two months), somewhat to my surprise it has thrived.In fact, although it is Fall, there is actually new growth--tiny little leaves popping out at the end of some branches!  I guess whatever watering I am doing is sufficient.  It will be interesting to see how it will survive the Winter.  It is an outdoor tree (and it is important to know when you are considering getting a bonsai plant whether it is indoor or outdoor) and requires the dormant period of cold and short days.  It should be watered as often as possible even then (obviously if the soil is solid ice that won't be possible).If it dies anytime from here on out, it is on me; the plant itself as delivered was healthy and happy. I do not hesitate giving the tree five stars, and would buy bonsai from Amazon again.
