Strangely there is ZERO peppermint listed in the ingredients!!Even when I tried it with half serving (2 tsp), the peppermint stood out but the mocha/cocoa was very light.I mixed a full serving with a cup of black coffee and I felt like peppermint, cocoa and coffee all stood out better. When using a full serving with water, there is zero coffee taste to me.OVERALL:If you want a peppermint hot chocolate with a small amount of caffeine, then this is your product.If you want more of a mocha latte, then this will fall short.

I was surprised at at the taste of this instant peppermint mocha latte. I am a huge fan of Starbucks peppermint mocha and this instant mix does a decent job of creating it for me at home. It's definitely not the same as the coffee house version, but the peppermint isn't too overpowering and (always important to me) it dissolves well and doesn't leave clumps of the mix in the bottom of the cup. The only thing that I don't care for as much is a very, very slight aftertaste - which could just be the peppermint flavoring. If you need a peppermint mocha fix and are looking for a way to stretch your coffee dollars, this makes a pretty good substitute.

If you haven't tried any of the line of International Coffee flavors, the peppermint mocha is a great one to try. It's a delicious mint chocolate coffee that is great after dinner. The peppermint mocha is not too sweet or too minty, it was a nice sophisticated hot chocolatey coffee.The coffee is super easy to make: just add hot water. The directions also say you can add hot milk. I'll give you one of my favorite twists: add a scoop of peppermint mocha mix to your morning cup of Joe for a little treat. I keep several flavors on hand to flavor my coffee depending on my mood.I find a little less is more with these coffees. They can be a little too sweet if you use too much powder. But a few trials and I am sure you can find the flavor level that is best for you. Also the mix does contain powdered milk just in case dairy is an issue.I can easily recommend the peppermint mocha to anyone who likes mint, chocolate, or coffee.

column9: You'll like it if you don't want a strong peppermint taste
column10: I'm not much for flavored coffees but wanted to give this a shot.  I actually had to go higher than the recommended 4 teaspoons to 8 ounces of water because the flavor was just simply too weak.  Adding another couple teaspoons had it in the wheelhouse of the typically stronger coffee I like to drink.  The flavor is pleasant and not overly sweet, and the peppermint flavor is obvious but not as strong as I expected- a good thing, in my view.  Overall, it's a fine drink, but because I am a black coffee drinker, it's not for me.  Recommended for those who like sugar or creamer in their coffee, and who are looking for something Christmasy to drink for the holiday/winter season.

This is another example in this line of pleasant warm-drink mixes from Maxwell House. It is smooth and rich and good-tasting. You have to put rather a lot of it in the cup, and it is quite high in calories, but that is sometimes a price worth paying for something which tastes good. In any case, it is not something one would want to have every day; more for when one deserves a bit of a treat.

column9: WOW no artificial sweetener for a change YAY!
column10: I really enjoyed sipping a hot cup of this with some ginger snaps. It is very pleasant tasting just enough mint and coffee flavor but could have had a bit more cocoa so I added a little and it was better. This is a nice little now and then treat to look forward too. A bit high on sugar for my taste but I was so glad it was NOT ARTIFICIALLY SWEETENED! and adding extra cocoa down played the sweet perfectly. I really liked this product and I would buy it and recommend it.

this from my wife:"I enjoy my coffee and my hot chocolate.  Put those together and add a peppermint stick, and that's about what you get with this latte.  It's delicious.  However, I regard the value of this product as a mere packaging convenience.  It's something you could put together yourself at home, but would you?  File this under 'indulgence'.Speaking of packaging, I appreciate that the plastic packaging is recyclable but would've preferred tin.  To their credit, Maxwell House have marked the package as top-rack dishwasher safe and the size and shape of the package mean that I might actually reuse rather than recycle."

I usually purchase the Vanilla and love it, I did not care for this at all. I put in the normal amount, sipped and found that I inhaled peppermint with barely any taste of chocolate or coffee, I put in 2 more spoonfuls and tried it again..... it tastes a little like chocolate, but it definitely can't replace a trip to your local coffee store. I did like that they have repackaged this and replaced the old tin canisters that it's been in forever.This flavor needs to be worked on

A real TREAT!!  Peppermint Mocha Latte is so smooth and invigorating with the hint of peppermint flavor and aroma.  A most enjoyable treat any time of day or evening and especially if you want to serve your guest something a bit different from a plain old cup of coffee.  WOW this is good will be heard all around and all you did was add a few teaspoons of powdered mix and add hot water.This came from Amazon on a windy rainy day when I was looking to serve a dear friend something different and it sure hit the spot!!Maxwell House International Cafe Cafe-Style Beverage Mix, Peppermint Mocha Latte 7.1 oz (202 g)

Let me tell you all a secret: I don't actually like coffee that much.  There I said it.  I ordered this product anyway because it sounded really good from the description.  So, now that you know what perspective I'm coming from, let me describe my impression of this drink.Well, it's more like hot chocolate than coffee.  Seriously, my impression is that this tastes very little like coffee and much more like a Peppermint Dark Chocolate Hot Cocoa.  That's fine with me, as since I mentioned earlier I don't really care that much for coffee.  So, really, what you've got here is "latte" that tastes like hot chocolate.There are some other issues I should mention, it's very pepperminty - in fact, it may be too strongly peppermint for some people's tastes.  The other issue is that it takes a TON of teaspoons of powder to make a normal average-sized mug.  I think I used like six on one mug.  That's not efficient at all compared to a normal-sized packet of hot chocolate.  Speaking of hot chocolate, since this tastes like hot chocolate, you really should just buy hot chocolate instead because it's a much cheaper, better value per ounce than this stuff.  So, given the things I've mentioned, I can't really recommend this "latte" drink mix to fans of coffee at all, or to fans of hot chocolate just based on price alone.  So really, I guess that means it's just not recommended!

column9: Nothing better on an Autumn day
column10: Maxwell House has done us all a favor by releasing this awesome blend. Smooth , calming flavor that continually resonates through the taste buds. Best when served piping hot. For even more flavor , I dropped a peppermint candy piece in the cup , and let it melt. Reasonable price for great coffee.

I made this with a few ounces of steamed milk, water, and a little heavy cream. I won't say that it taste bad but I much prefer french vanilla. Also, I'll reiterate what a couple of reviewers have already said: this is not really a latte-especially if you are making with just powder and water.After I tasted it, I tried adding a little instant Folgers to help it along. That, however, did not work. I just hate that I wasted the milk. As a side note, let me say that it wasn't really the peppermint flavor that turned me off. I drink peppermint tea all of the time. I just think adding peppermint to a coffee-type beverage is a bad idea. It reminded me of an Andes mint.

I have always seen this item in the coffee section of my local market so I assumed it was coffee based. After trying it several times it certainly tasted to me like a malty hot chocolate drink. The ingredient lists "instant coffee" and no chocolate so it is coffee after all - I was fooled.  I found the taste overly sweet. The item could of used more of the bitterness of the coffee to tone down the sweetness. Nonetheless the item was a pleasant drink on a cold day but nothing out of the ordinary.

column9: Maxwell House Has Always Been Our Favorite Brand
column10: This combination of tastes and smells is great, truly seductive of course.  Maxwell House is an established brand of great reputation, which is why we favor it whenever possible, even without regard to price differentials.For this particular product, there is a tiny bit of unexpected surprise or disappointment of course, since it contains a "hydrogenated" ingredient, which we avoid always.  With more attention to the natural side for this ingredient list, this product could have been a first-class, even preferred item.

I can definitely taste the mint flavor and the latte does come out foamy like the box says. The mint seems stronger than the usual peppermint lattes that I've gotten at Starbucks before. It's not super sweet but is still sweet enough, unlike the dark mayan chocolate flavor that I've had before. The new packaging is also an improvement since they got rid of the metal rim that used to make it difficult to get out the last bit of powder when the tin is almost empty.

I am an adamant lover of coffeehouse peppermint mochas.  It doesn't need to be cold out for me to want a nice, hot cup of chocolate with a cool edge of peppermint in it.  I look for packages of peppermint cocoa, have syrups and adore York's Peppermint patties.  That said, I have expectations of anything that says it is peppermint and chocolate.International Coffees are something I also buy on occasion as an added shot to my normal brewed coffee at home.  I like that it adds flavor and also seems to spike plain brew with a bit more energy; almost like adding a shot of espresso without having to douse the cup with sugar or cream, first.  I like my coffee smooth and sweet.Having my normal use in mind and that of someone who might purchase this item to try as a stand-alone, I did two tests:1) I put a couple of spoonfuls of the powder in the bottom of my cup before adding my brewed coffee2) I heated milk to pour over the powder (I wouldn't use hot water for cocoa, I'm sure not going to use it here)The brewed coffee mix, had a nice strong (but sweet) peppermint taste with a dark edge to the chocolate flavor.  I know the brewed coffee brings out the chocolate a bit more, so I was happy to see that I didn't lose the peppermint in the mix.  The smell didn't carry a lot of the mint, so that was a little disappointing as I was hoping for a full scent and taste experience for the peppermint mocha spike.The heated milk produced a very sweet cup that lost most of the coffee flavor.  Honestly, it ended up tasting like a decent cup of peppermint hot cocoa instead of a mocha.  I started off with only 3/4 of the recommended powder and even that didn't have the hint of coffee while being a bit thin-tasting.  Putting the recommended amount of powder in created a more full-bodied drink, but still wasn't very coffee-esque.So, as an add to my brewed cup, I will definitely keep it.  I honestly think this is the best way to use this product.  For powder mixed with milk or water (gak!), I'll probably skip it because it was a little too sweet.  Though, if I'm out of cocoa, I may consider it as an alternative.

This drink mix was good but really nothing special.  Its basically just a strongly peppermint flavored hot chocolate.  Calling it peppermint mocha latte is somewhat of an exaggeration.  Its a fine drink but I wouldn't necessarily go out of my way to find it again.If you like hot water with just a touch of flavor... you'll like this drink.WEAK WEAK WEAK (when mixed according to pkg directions (which i'm sure are to keep the calories looking low))you really need more than twice as much mix as called for (of course I also put two cocoa packets in one cup for hot cocoa and like strong coffee so perhaps my tastebuds are sensorially challenged)makes a disturbing crackling noise when mix and water meet (like pop rocks candy...very strange)but does have a nice little foam on top for a brief momentWhen mixed per directions:Peppermint: just right!Mocha: definitely some chocolatyness...but coffee flavor is barely detectable to totally absent(I personally wouldn't want peppermint in my mocha anyway...cocoa definitely...but not in mocha latte which SHOULD have coffee flavor in it)more like a lightly chocolaty mint tea!When mixed 2x strong:Hmm. Still weak-ish. Strongly mint and somewhat chocolatey and no coffee overtones.Should be called Cocoa-infused Mint Tea.Or Peppermint Cocoa at least. Not Mocha.

I had a cough and sore throat when I tried the peppermint mocha latte. I didn't know if it was such a great idea to try it when I didn't feel well, but the mint appealed to me.I followed the directions and mixed 4 tsp. with about 8 ounces of steaming hot water. I was happy to see that it mixed well - I didn't come across any lumps of unmixed granules while drinking or at the bottom when I was done. There's a nice frothiness to it. And I was right: The peppermint is very soothing. I felt a bit revived after the first few sips. The peppermint is not strong or overwhelming, but it does linger, which I liked. The mocha is very subtle; what stands out is the peppermint. It's just a really nice mix of hot drink with a gentle, chocolate-tinged minty coolness.I don't really have any gripes, because I'm the one who made the drink, but I do think the next time I make a mug of peppermint mocha, I will add another half teaspoon or so - it's not that the drink I made was bad, but I found I wanted it just a touch stronger. The flavor is that good. With 9 carbs and 7 sugars per mug, I felt better health-wise about enjoying it, too. Easy to recommend!

I was excited to try this product because I thought it was going to be the perfect drink on my cold night.  When I tried it, however, I was disappointed.  The drink was just extremely too minty for me.  It was a menthol overload.  There was too much peppermint and not enough mocha.If you like York Peppermint Patties, you might like this drink.  It is like the liquid version of a peppermint patty.  I didn't enjoy it, but maybe other people will.

Some similar kinds of flavored coffees have a subtle mint flavor. This is powerful stuff.  In a good way, of course.  It had a very powerful taste of chocolate mint, very fulfilling.  Much better tasting than similar products.  I highly recommend this.

The package is very appealing and the aroma from the drink is divine, but the flavor was mediocre.  I added a little bit more mix to water and added a little bit of coffee to add flavor.I think it will be perfect for my college student in dorm room because it's something a little different but for myself, I'd rather drink coffee or tea.

I am not a big coffee drinker but I had two cups of Peppermint Mocha flavor this morning and it was so good. It is the perfect flavor for chilly fall and winter mornings. The peppermint flavor is light and not at all overpowering, you can still taste the mocha. Very good and I would definitly purchase

Although I carefully followed the directions, what I got was a thin, watery disappointment.  I'm sorry to give a bad review but I'm sure this isn't a cheap product and I would have been very unhappy if I had paid for it.Maybe I expected too much.

This stuff is super yummy. It took me a little while to figure out how to get the water / powder mixture just right, but that is not a problem. The taste has just the right amount of peppermint for me,too much peppermint (like some other drinks) is a turn off for me. IMHO the peppermint should be a nice accent, no the main "star" of the coffee.Well worth a try, and perfect to have on hand in the winter months for when friends stop by.

This stuff is so good!! I am huge an of Starbucks Peppermint Mocha lattes during the holidays, so I was a little skeptical of this instant drink...but it was delicious!! I'm a real coffee snob, and this one met my standards. It's a great drink for a cold day. This scent is wonderful and inviting and it has the perfect amount of sweet.

Maxwell House International Coffee Peppermint Mocha Latte is great coffee. I was a little hesitant to try it being I don,t eat sugar, I thought it might be too sweet. This is really good; not too sweet at all. It has a nice mild peppermint taste but the choclate latte still comes thru strong. It is really good especially as we are heading into the holiday season . Its a treat for big kids!! I made it with just the hot water to see how it performed. It was frothy & did'nt rquire milk or anything else. It was good all on its own. Try it I think you will like it !

We're pretty rabid coffee and hot chocolate drinkers at my house.  The Maxwell House International products aren't something we normally buy, but I figured this could be a really nice alternative to the coffee pods in hurry.  Sadly, the Peppermint Mocha Latte experiences left us a bit wanting.First and foremost, the flavor of the Maxwell House Peppermint Mocha Latte isn't bad; however, at the recommended amount of powder to water (4 tsp per 8 oz of water) the flavor is really, really subtle.  I would not recommmend using their recommended amount of powder unless you're looking for something more akin to a tea.When we upped the ratio of powder to water, the product was much better.  The flavors of the peppermint weren't overpowering, and you still get the flavor of the latte coming through just fine.Overall, it's a middling product.  It isn't bad at all, but I think there are better mixes out there if you're really looking for a nice flavor experience.

I am a coffee lover, and in general coffee lovers do not like instant coffee.  But Maxwell House's International coffees are not like normal instant coffee.  Their instant coffee is smooth tasting, and their are many varieties to choose from.  The Peppermint Mocha brand that I received can be enjoyed as a latte coffee, or as a hot chocolate type beverage.All you need to do is add one cup of hot (not boiling) water to 4 teaspoonfulls of this latte coffee in a cup.  It is instantly enjoyable.  Initially I felt the flavor was a bit bland, so I added some sugar to mine.  My Husband however enjoyed his cup without sugar and felt it tasted fine without it.It advertised that it could also be used as a hot chocolate type beverage, that all you needed to do to serve it this way was to add the teaspoonfulls of the latte to hot milk instead of hot water.  I asked my son to try it this way, and he did.  My 10 year old did like it, but we did have to add some sugar to make it sweeter. Both my son and I must have a huge sweet tooth.Enjoy this coffee as the nights grow chillier!

column9: There's a picture of this next to "Meh" in the dictionary
column10: With fancy sippin' coffees in general you expect a rich, complicated taste.  This coffee, with PEPPERMINT MOCHA flavor, you expect even more something that knocks you back.  You get... Meh.There's a peppermint flavor.  Not very strong.  I get more flavor by adding small amounts of flavor syrups from the 99cent store.The preparation is a bit touchy.  Directions say add between 6-8oz of boiling water.  I tried 7oz and got hardly any flavor.  With 6oz. it was noticeable but bland.  A bit less than 6oz and a dash of milk was ok.The back of the box says "The New Look of Decadence".  I want DECADENT.  I got mildly flavored coffee or ... "Meh".This is not terrible coffee, just not worth the trouble.

Although this coffee, like all the International Coffees, is too sweet for me, the mint/mocha flavor is decidedly the best of these products that I've ever tried. It tastes and smells like Christmas! I almost always tone down the sweetness and up the coffee flavor by adding a spoonful of instant coffee to the mix before pouring in boiling water, but I use less of the instant with this flavor because it's so pungent. If you like mint and chocolate, you'll like this one. I'll bet it would taste great iced, too -- it's a seasonal flavor, so this would be one to stock up on if you like it.

column9: Very minty. Very sweet. Nice chocolate flavor.
column10: I'm assuming if you're reading this review that you realize that it's instant coffee, and you know what that means (easy to prepare; often weak; lacks the bold flavor of real coffee). Some of us, like me, prefer the ease and variability of instant coffee - I can make it as strong or as weak as I like! The mint chocolate does a good job of masking the fact that this is instant coffee. My one potentially negative comment would be that the mint is very, hm, fresh (almost bordering on toothpaste) and is the strongest of the flavors.

Cuddle up with your favorite book,throw and a cup of this chocolately mint flavored coffee.A refreshing way to relax after a hectic day or a good morning warm up drink to start a cold day.Cheaper and quicker than you local  coffee house.4.25*rating.

column9: Lovely smell, tastes pretty good overall, REAL sugar
column10: I love peppermint and chocolate as a rule. I was a little wary of this canned coffee mix at first. Opening it the first time and the dry mix smells like chocolate cake mix with a faint hint of peppermint. Adding the hot water to the mug with the dry mix in the bottom was wonderful. The bright smell of peppermint wafted up followed by a weaker scent of chocolate. I did the four teaspoons to 7 ounces of hot water per the instructions and the flavor was weak. Adding a bit more mix fixed the problem. The flavor overall is mild and smooth - no funky after taste of any kind. There is a tingle of peppermint on the tongue after you swallow and I really like that. One thing I really like is no artificial sweeteners - just sugar. I truly detest the flavor & aftertaste of the artificial sweeteners, so a product like this with just regular, natural sugar is always welcome.The only reason for removing a single star is due to the need to add more mix - otherwise it's sort of watery. This is a product I will keep on hand - we have a Dolce Gusto machine for traditional coffee & lattes with the real deal foam etc. However, they don't make a peppermint flavor, so this Maxwell House International mix is a decent option.

Maxwell House Internationals Peppermint Mocha Latte has a great peppermint flavor - not chemically at all like some other products. Nice taste, easy to make - really liked it a lot as did those with whom I shared it!

For me nothing says the holidays like peppermint lattes @ Starbucks. But who can pay $4+ for their smallest size? And if you are like me, you want to enjoy your coffee while sitting at your desk 1st thing in the morning when you get to work. Who has the time to wait in 15min morning rush lines at your local coffee house? I don't have $4 a day or an extra 15min even to rush over for some coffee so that is where Maxwell House Peppermint Mocha Latte comes in hand. Make your own holiday classic out of the convenience of your own home, at work, or even in your car on the way to work as long as your aren't driving. It's that simple, and you can adjust the flavor to meet your needs instead of having to wait an extra 10min to send your drink back for them to fix it for you. All you need to do is boil water, or heat milk, and then add 4-5 teaspoons of latte, stir and you are done! That's it who knew a latte would be so simple to make. I prefer to make mine with milk with about 6 teaspoons (I prefer a stronger peppermint taste, but overall I would rate the peppermint flavor mild with only 4 teaspoons and the mocha very slight.) and add a little bit of caramel drizzle to go along with it. Takes me only 1 min to get my latte ready in the morning and I am out of the door, and the best part about the whole thing is that it didn't cost me $4 for a single cup.Other than convenience, I love the fact that you get foam on the top of your latte. I know lattes are supposed to have foam, but I can't tell you how many times I have bought make-it-yourself-lattes and their excuse for foam has been this pasty layer at the top. Maxwell House lattes have had a generous amount of foam on the top, much more than you would expect from something that you are just stirring into a cup.If your just like me and love your holiday coffee but don't have time and don't want to pay your coffee house prices I highly suggest you try Maxwell House Peppermint Mocha Latte. And if you want an extra treat add a little bit of caramel to your drink, you can thank me later.

I enjoyed the Pumpkin Spice version of this same product, but I was far less impressed with this Peppermint Mocha.  My wife, who loves all things minty and chocolate flavored, didn't even like it.Simply put, its too bland.  Its sweet, sure, but there's not much peppermint and not much mocha.  It goes okay (but not great) in coffee, but in water I just felt like I was drinking hot sugar water.The Pumpkin Spice stuff is great, but don't bother with this.

I am sitting here sipping this delicious drink as I write, and this is NOT my first cup.  It has been a while since I have had an International Latte and I'm wondering why. Talk about a drink that just makes your insides happy, this is it. At first I thought  perphaps the peppermint flavor would be over-powering but it is not.  Just the right amount, the flavor of the entire drink is rich and very satisfying, although I had to add some sugar, but I want everything sweet. I made my granddaughter one, she wanted it cold, and she loves it.  I myself think it tastes better hot and is perfect for the upcoming nights of sitting around the Christmas tree with friends and family and sharing this drink.  Very good, a tasty treat  and I would recommend it.

Maxwell House Peppermint Mocha is a wonderful cold season treat.  From the initial opening of the can with its burst of scent to your first taste, this is what starts the holiday season for me.For an extra indulgence, I love to add it to Maxwell House's Orange Café and the combined flavors remind me of a special treat from an old coffee house that is no longer in business.  So for something special, combine these two great tastes for an amazing holiday delight.

Delicious taste. I love peppermint, so I was incredibly excited to try this product. Unfortunately, the ingredients are not so delicious. Hydrogenated oil, corn syrup... two big no-no's for me. While this was great to try (and this was definitely a treat drink for me), I try to keep the not-so-good for you ingredients out of my diet, which means the remains of this went into the trash.When it comes to taste, this is amazing. If you don't take issue with the ingredients, then by all means, buy it. If, however, you are like me--and are mindful of what you consume--then I would say to avoid the temptation with this and make your own peppermint latte.

After mixing and remixing this, I finally found the correct ratio of product to liquid.  The peppermint flavor is bold while the chocolate is not quite rich enough, being masked by the initial mint burst.  However, when mixed with milk, the flavors come out a bit more evenly than with water, which tends to make this seem really watered down if there isn't enough flavor mix added.  I like it as a change from just chocolate or vanilla coffee flavor since the peppermint is refreshing without being overly powerful.  Just takes some fiddling to get the mixture right.  Overall, a good instant product.

column9: Too sweet... but you can work with that.
column10: This coffee was just tooo chocolatey, and minty.  Which is a matter of opinion, I know.  When I used less than the recommended 4 tsp, it tasted watery.  I ended up using 2 scoops of this with 2 scoops of regular Maxwell House Cafe Francais for the perfect drink.  I gave it 5 stars because the flavor is good, the value is good, the convenience is excellent.

column9: Maxwell House International Coffee Peppermint Mocha Latte
column10: This is a lovely balance between peppermint and mocha.  It is my observation that that the peppermint is more prominent than the mocha.  This does not take away from the drink, as I found it completely refreshing and appropriate for "my time".  It is also a great idea for the coming holidays and cooler weather.

Being the oral type, I associate food with holidays and chocolate and peppermint are definitely Christmas flavors.  Add coffee to that and you've got a satisfying jolt of caffeine with some holiday flavor.  The flavor is light and not overwhelming and mixes well with hot water.  Be sure to use hot water and stir generously as these coffees sometimes leave a dredge at the bottom of the cup if not mixed thoroughly.  Overall this is a nice pick me up anytime of day and excellent to sip while reading or watching tv.  And it's a lot cheaper to make a cup of it at home than go to you-know-where and try to remember that tall means small and grande means medium and have to choose between numerous milk options.

Many folks are scaling back on the cost of gift-giving this year, and I highly recommend a gift basket or gift bag including an inexpensive Christmas mug plus a can of this Maxwell House International Coffee in the Peppermint Mocha Latte flavor. Remember that Amazon sells a pack of 4 for the price! It makes a smooth, creamy instant cup of coffee with rich chocolate and cool peppermint notes... sinfully delicious!You can bake with this, too. I stirred two rounded tablespoons into dry packaged brownie mix (9 X 11 inch pan size) before adding wet ingredients, then folded in chocolate chips and broken peppermint candy pieces. You could skip the fold in part, frost your brownies with chocolate frosting and top with broken pieces of peppermint candy as a special dessert or treat for holiday potlucks. Consider stirring a tablespoon or two of the dry mix into your chocolate sugar cookie recipe for a hint of coffee and peppermint flavors.In summary, this instant coffee is a yummy, affordable splurge for the upcoming holidays. Enjoy!

Everyone is offering a peppermint mocha today.  Just take a drive down the road at all the major chain coffee shops and even the local ones.  You can't miss it this time of year.  Well now Maxwell House wants to bring that popular holiday flavor to your home.  First off, the recommended serving size is too small of a serving.  Your going to have to double it.  Mixing is easy, add powder to water.  The end result is a very weak latte or a strong hot cocoa.  The peppermint flavor over powers any chocolate or coffee taste.  It's nice to have the ability to make something like this at home, but I think it's a concoction best left for the experts.

column9: No Coffee, No Mocha, Just Peppermint
column10: I adore the Christmastime Peppermint Mocha drinks from Starbucks. While I never assumed this would be anywhere near AS good, I figured it would at least be GOOD. Mixed with hot water, all this tastes like is peppermint. There is a faint mocha taste, and no discernable coffee taste at all. This is better used as a flavoring for real coffee or mixed in milk to make a peppermint hot chocolate drink.

I'm a tea drinker, not a coffee drinker but I find these little tins make a nice change and a peppermint  coffee sounds good for the holidays. Unfortunately the delivery didn't live up to the promise.It smells wonderful. A Christmassy peppermint smell with a thick froth of foam on top. Sitting on a table top perfuming the air it's like a commercial for Christmas. The problem is that the flavor is too weak. After all the promise it just sort of falls flat. I tried to make it with more powder, same effect. It looks and smells wonderful but in the end it just disappoints. Not really worth the money.

Very Watery - and no latte flavor in sight here.I received one 7oz tin and the instructions said to add 4 teaspoons into a mug with hot water (6-8 oz). Fairly easy, and it dissolved with no problems but very heavy on the peppermint and not much else there. The ingredient list isn't terribly encouraging either with sugar right at the top, followed by the *cream* with a list of things you'd rather not know, with the "instant coffee" well towards the bottom of the list. From looking at the Nutrition facts its seems rather high on the carb content.I really didn't find much in this product that I could recommend it at all, and not one I'd try again.

column9: Too much mint, not enough mocha.
column10: To this day my mom still loves her International Coffee, which is why I decided to give this new flavor a shot. Peppermint Mocha sounded good for cold, holiday-type weather. Sadly, I still don't see what my mom loves about it. First, the packaging is "new." No longer does it come in a cute, sturdy tin can; but rather a flexible plastic packaging. Second, I used approximately 7 ounces of hot water (calls for 6-8) and added 4 heaping teaspoons of powder. A pleasant fizzing ensued, creating what I assume is supposed to be the "foam" of the latte. After I let it cool a bit, and stirred it plenty to dissolve those annoying chunks of powder, I took a sip and was hit in the face with peppermint. Way, way to much peppermint. After letting it cool some more I took another sip and it was actually worse than the first. Perhaps I used too much water and not enough coffee, but I tasted no mocha flavoring in this beverage. I can't imagine using less water though, as the peppermint was insanely strong with the amount I had.Overall, the convenience is not worth it, unless watery-peppermint-with coffee undertones is your thing.

Peppermint mocha is a favorite holiday tradition in our family.  There is just something about that flavor that gets you in the spirit.  This has a smooth, velvety taste and is easy to make.  This is not coffee though so it is not like McDonald's Peppermint Mocha drink.  More like their Peppermint Chocolate Milk.  The only thing wrong with this product was ours came with the foil seal open at the corner.  I would figure that was an anomaly and not the norm, however.

column9: Weak on mocha, watery, extra minty
column10: I made a cup according to instructions - a cup of water to the number of teaspoons mentioned. It did say adjust to taste. I found it watery, no real flavor of rich chocolate, no coffee flavor and the mint tingled the mouth and overpowered any other flavor.  I would not recommend this at all. I had hoped to use it over a cold winter so I wouldn't have to make it from scratch but this was not very drinkable. I will stick to making hot chocolate with real milk and adding mint flavoring.

Having been a fan of the Maxwell House International "coffee" mixes for years, I looked forward to trying the peppermint mocha flavor and anticipated a chocolate peppermint blend. One of my favorites in the series is the International Orange mix.It appears that Maxwell House has changed the design of the packaging, the names, and the size, for I remember buying these in a larger, metal container.A look at the ingredients shows that the first ones listed are: sugar, non dairy creamer, multiple multi-syllabled concoctions, and far down the list cocoa and instant coffee. Mixing the powdered blend with water produces a somewhat tasty drink with a litle bit of a foam on top. There's a hint of chocolate in there, but the only way to know coffee is in the blend is to read the ingredient list. For me, the peppermint taste is too pronounced, but that's my personal preference.I like making my drink with at least half milk to produce a tastier, richer experience. Using the International Latte as a creamer/flavorer in my morning coffee is also a preference of mine. That way I get the coffee and the subdued peppermint kick.Though I'm enjoying this sampling of International Latte, were I to purchase another it would be a different flavor, the International Orange or something more chocolatey.

I really like the Peppermint Mocha, but if I look at a calorie, it jumps on me. So, I mix a teaspoon of the Peppermint Mocha with a sugar-free coffee mix like French Vanilla or Mocha. You can get the full taste of the Peppermint Mocha with the mixed in sugar free versions. The 100% Peppermint Mocha with no sugar-free is super rich and tastes like a desert. To knock yourself out, get some peppermint ice cream (the kind with the little chunks of candy cane) mix 2-3 tablespoons of Peppermint Mocha into just a little water--until it's dissolved and pour it on the ice cream. Knocked my socks off!

Normally I don't go for instant coffees, but this was delicious.  The instructions suggest 4 teaspoons in 6-8oz of hot water.  I used 5 teaspoons in 12oz of water with a dollop of Silk soy creamer.  It made for a delicious peppermint mocha low in fat and high in taste.  Starbucks' peppermint mochas are too sweet and sharp for me.  Too much peppermint, too much chocolate.  This powder is the perfect mix - you get a much lighter drink.  My only complaint is that it doesn't pack much of a caffeine wallop.  Starbucks has Maxwell House beat there.
Very delish, but a little better made with milk instead of water.  Of course, I feel that way about pretty much all hot chocolate/mocha mixes.

column9: maybe they should omit the coffee
column10: I am a senior citizen, and I served this drink to friends in my age group.  They all agreed that it had a pleasant flavor, but many of us do not want caffeine in the evenings when one is more likely to wish for a minty chocolate drink.  So several of them thought the company should make a companion drink WITHOUT the coffee that would be suitable for evening time -- and also for children.all agreed that the mint was a very fresh overlay on the mocha -- a pleasing flavor combination.

column9: Time Saver:  Morning Coffee & Mouthwash All In One
column10: Anyone who has enjoyed dipping a candy cane into a mug of cocoa and savoring that hint of minty goodness that blends so perfectly with chocolate is going to be really, really disappointed by this brew. The harsh artificial peppermint flavor tastes exactly like mouthwash.  The coffee flavor is very faint, there isn't much sweetness either.  This is a perfectly horrible beverage.  I tried adding a little sugar, hoping more sweetness would cut the medicinal peppermint assault. It didn't.Forget TV commercials that depict women sighing with delight over their steaming mugs of International Coffee.  If those women can drink this stuff without shuddering, it can only mean one thing: they had the foresight to lace it with a double shot of bourbon.If coffee/chocolate/mint appeals to you, there's a really easy way satisfy the craving:  Make a cup of real coffee and toss in a Peppermint Patty.  No kidding. It's easy and yummy. You get a lovely, rich, chocolaty, minty blend (and you can still add that shot of bourbon if no one is looking). And when you finish the cup, there's this delicious chocolate-mint sludge at the bottom of the cup waiting to be spooned up.

column9: Needed to tweak recipe to taste good
column10: I've tried many flavors of Maxwell House's instant coffee drinks. They all do better with four "well-rounded" teaspoons instead of the flat four teaspoons the instructions suggest is all you should need for 6-8 oz water. i.e. Use 5-6 teaspoons per 6-8 oz water if you want a drink at all worth the time/money. It's a shame the packaging is not more honest with how much mix is really needed for a decent drink in order to fool customers into thinking they're getting more for their money than they really are. I tried one drink following the packaging directions just to make sure since it's a different flavor than what I've had before (6 oz water + 4 tsp mix). The result was a muddy looking pool of peppermint water.. no good mocha taste except what you might expect when you put some water in a dirty coffee cup and pick up the remnants of coffee - that's the only trace of "taste" other than peppermint I picked up.After adding an extra teaspoon (6 oz water + 5 tsp mix), I had a drink that was acceptable, but still not something I would favor enough to buy this mix over other flavors. The mocha taste is lighter than what you get from other flavored coffee mixes. I prefer stronger. At least I didn't find the mint or sweetness overpowering even with the extra teaspoon of mix.The best way I found to take this mix is adding in some extra instant coffee granules (6 oz water + 4 tsp this mix + 1 tsp other instant coffee mix + 1/4-1/2 tsp sugar). I added the sugar to counter the extra bitterness added by the regular coffee granules. This combination gave me a much more satisfying, flavorful drink, and I will continue drinking it this way until the powder is gone.I'm not happy with the fact I have to do so much tweaking on my end to get a good drink out of this. The whole point of these mixes is everything should already be in good proportion with proper instructions given on how much is needed to make it. If you don't mind the extra hassle, get this, otherwise, you might try other flavors that come with a better balance of tastes.

I am sorry to say that I was disappointed in Maxwell House International Coffee Peppermint Mocha Latte. If Teddy Roosevelt had been served this coffee at the Maxwell House hotel, Maxwell House may never have earned their colophon ("Good to the last drop.") This beverage boasts of two flavors; peppermint and mocha. Peppermint flavor has a strong beginning and a weak ending. Also the peppermint flavor does not linger. The mocha flavor is weak to non-existent throughout. I tried following the package directions; four teaspoons per six to eight ounces of water. I then kept adding more and more mix. Unfortunately, I could not find an acceptable ratio. This has to be the worst Maxwell House product I have tried. I do not think it is worth the money. It is very expensive. For the same cost, you could buy coffee beans, peppermint candy, cocoa and milk and create a much better home-made concoction. For the price of one canister, you could probably buy two cups of latte at Starbucks and enjoy it much more.

column9: Didn't Really Taste Like a Latte
column10: I tried this product and it really didn't taste much like latte or even any kind of coffee.  I had to look up latte on the Internet to make sure I wasn't missing something.  The generally accepted definition of latte seems to be strong coffee with steamed milk.  When I checked the ingredients on this package the first ingredient was sugar, followed by nondairy creamer.  The first ingredient in the non dairy creamer was corn syrup solids.  The third ingredient was partially hydrogenated coconut oil. Coffee was actually the ninth ingredient, listed behind dipotassium phosphate, artificial flavor, and maloxdextrin, which explains why it didn't taste much like coffee.  I do think it is a misnomer to have latte on the front of this package.  I guess in smaller print they have the words "naturally and artificially flavored cafe-style beverage" so technically that is how they are defining their product. But in larger letters are the words Maxwell House and International Latte so I was really expecting something coffee tasting. Anyway the product doesn't really taste like latte or coffee at all.  It really just mainly tasted like hot sugar water with a few other kind of odd flavors thrown in.I think for the money I would stick with something more healthy and natural like black or green tea or even just real coffee with real milk added in.

It is peppermint and mocha flavored, but after years of drinking richer, bolder coffee, International Coffee's flavor is just not strong enough.  This might be a good addition to coffee, a la Nestle Coffeemate Peppermint Mocha Coffee Creamer 15 oz, but is far too watery when directly added to water as per the directions.

column9: Not Bad for an instant coffee
column10: It didn't pack a lot of punch taste-wise but it smelled glorious and really warmed up some cold days.  All in all, easy, convenient, and a great match with peppermint schnapps!

I'm not much of a coffee drinker so if I drink a cup I prefer to have a mocha.  The chocolate flavor is good, the coffee flavor isn't overwhelming and the mint adds nicely to the overall taste.  Not a substitute for those who like a strong cup of black coffee but a good pick for someone looking for a good-tasting, milder, flavored coffee drink.

I grew up with these coffees as a little kid, not sure if I just remembered those old commercials or if my parents really liked them.  The Maxwell House International Coffee extends from the original General Foods International line, that is why the tin may be familiar to some and yet slightly different at the same time.I received this just as I experienced my first winter in the new town I would live in and it was such a welcome arrival.  Peppermint and mocha, together served hot in -10 F or more temperatures in a gloomy town with no ambition or progress is such a savior.  I loved and savored it, enjoying it with my lovely wife as she too endured this backwoods town (town name is witheld for now of course).I noticed some of the reviews about a lack of flavor or a serving size too small and just shake my head.  To each our own, but I am one of those that eats healthy and exercises regularly and can't help but feel somewhat saddened at so many of us who indulge in and grow blind to oversized proportions and our foods and drinks have to be bursting with insane amounts of sugars and fats.  But at around $8-9 a tin, those of us that need excess can use the entire tin for our single serving and sated...or perhaps even make it 2 servings to be a little bit more healthy (sarcasm hinted just in case).

column9: Coffee, chocolate, and peppermint flavors in one handy little can... what's not to like?
column10: I'm more of a basic coffee person, but my wife enjoys flavored coffees so I ordered this for her.  She really liked it, pointing out how the rich chocolate flavor and underlying peppermint zing really complemented each other.  The sample can was gone in about a week and a half.And, hey, I even made a cup for myself, and quite enjoyed it.  It would likely be a big hit with me on a cold winter day... it's like a cup of hot chocolate with a little sophistication stirred in.I'm still more of a "normal cup of coffee" type of person, but one would be a cad to totally turn away from an occasional sweet indulgence like the one Maxwell House offers here.

This drink tastes great - like a sticky sweet peppermint hot chocolate. But a coffee drink? No way. I kept adding more product to the hot water hoping for coffee but all I got was an extreme sugar rush. The price is outrageous as well. I won't be buying this.

I'm not a huge fan of instant coffee, but the Maxwell House International Coffee Peppermint Mocha Latte was quite enjoyable. The peppermint flavor was not overpowering and the hint of chocolate gave it another layer of richness that is often lacking in other instant mixes.
Sweet Mocha with a hint of peppermint. What I like is it has a strong taste of mocha that isn't overpowered by the chocolate or the minty-ness. I love it (great in a milk shake.)
The Maxwell House Peppermint Mocha is delicious and easy to prepare.  My husband and I were both big fans of this drink.  A cross between hot chocolate and coffee.

for it being from a mix/can, this is a very good quality latte. peppermint mocha is one of my favorite seasonal flavors and maxwell house does it just right. very easy to use. just mix with water or milk and instant satisfaction!

column4: Glenda Boozer "Live, live, live! Life is a ba...
column10: The first coffee I ever remember drinking (more than a sip, anyway) was Maxwell House International Coffee. I have enjoyed watching the new flavors come out and trying the various dietary options, and I'm also a big fan of peppermint, so this one was a natural for me. Even though it is not sugar-free or fat-free, one serving (4 teaspoons of the powder) is 50 calories, which is really not bad compared to having a pastry or something else when the sweet tooth hits. The peppermint flavor is strong, and then you taste the same old mocha that was probably your first favorite flavor of this stuff - a bit thinner than the coffee my mom makes, but pleasant. Like all of the International Coffee flavors (and all instant hot cocoa powders, for that matter), it mixes much better if you add hot (not cold) water to the powder instead of adding powder to water. If you like to use the microwave, you can heat the water in a measuring cup, use a single-cup coffee pot, or even use hot tap water. It's nice to have on hand for quick and easy enjoyment.

column9: Lots a mint, a little cocoa, but where's the Coffee?
column10: Well folks, I'm not sure what this is supposed to taste like but all I get out of it is watery cocoa with lots of peppermint in it. Or is it lots of Peppermint with watered down cocoa? Its got so much peppermint its to the point of overdoing it. WAY overdoing it!  My first try of it I used my big 12 oz. glass mug that I use for Latte's. Mixed it with approximately 3 parts milk to one part water & 7 heaping spoons of the mix. It was kinda watery so I added another three more heaping spoons of the mix. Even with 10 heaping spoons of the mix & that much milk, its still kinda thin. If you like a hot drink with a lot of Peppermint to it, and I mean a LOT, then you will probably like this one. I didn't realize it until I drank about half a mug full but my sinuses had been about half closed up and this stuff with all that Peppermint in it opened them right up! There is some chocolate flavor to it too but its mostly overpowered with the Peppermint and I cant tell if there's any coffee in it at all.  I'm still not sure if I really like this very much. Maybe if I cut it with regular cocoa mix and make it half and half, or 2 parts cocoa to one part of this, it will be better. Or mix it with the cocoa @ 2 to 1 and use more milk than I did or add some half & half to the milk. It makes a richer latte if I use 3 parts milk to 1 part Half & Half in my Mr Coffee Cafe Latte machine so maybe it would improve the results with this mix.But right now I'll have to wait to experiment with it 'till after I make a trip to the store since I used the last of my milk on it. But, to be honest I don't think I'd like it any which way that I could think of to mix it because it just has way too much Peppermint in it. It's been half an hour since I finished the mug full that I made and I still have a very strong aftertaste of Peppermint in my mouth.

I like mint, so I decided to try this product.  I am not willing to spend the big bucks on fancy latte drinks at restaurants, so this is a compromise.  It's not "too" minty, and it's quick to fix and satisfying when I want a little sweet pick-up.  Probably not as rich and decadent as "store bought, but then it doesn't cost $2 to $3 a serving.  My kind of treat.

column4: Julie A. Dawson "Bards and Sages Publishing"
column10: I've always enjoyed the International Coffee line.  Made for a nice treat over the holidays when I wanted a cup of coffee but didn't want to brew a whole pot.  Just the right amount of peppermint flavor so it didn't overwhelm the coffee.

Let's be honest, peppermint mocha is a great winter treat. The warmth of the liquid with the refreshing peppermint is delicious. Being a fan of peppermint mocha, I was excited to try this. Overall, I thought it was a good drink mix. It was a nice change from my usual coffee or hot chocolate. Also, I am a huge fan of anything peppermint.Having said that, there are some things to know when purchasing this product. First of all, this is sweet, so if you are not a fan of overly sweet drinks, you may not want this. Also, the coffee and mocha flavor was subtle. I didn't find it an issue, but do not buy this if you are looking for a rich decadent treat; you will be disappointed.

I fell in love! Rarely do I come across a flavored coffee that I like but with one sip of the Peppermint Mocha Latte, I knew I had found a coffee that was destined to become my favorite. The peppermint taste is perfect and does not leave an overwhelming flavor. It mingles nicely with the mocha that provides a satisfying taste. I had researched the Maxwell House website to find out where the product was sold. After running from store to store without any luck, my husband discovered the coffee here on Amazon (of course!) He promptly ordered eight cans of the coffee so that I could have enough to get through winter.

I have enjoyed all of Maxwell House International Coffees so far, and this is no exception.  Although great on its own, my new favorite treat at the workplace is a Nestle hot chocolate packet mixed with a large spoonful of the Maxwell. Try it!

column9: Subtle taste works for this tea drinker
column10: I'm more of a tea drinker and was surprised I actually liked this coffee.  It wasn't too heavy on the peppermint or chocolate flavors.  I would buy this coffee again as it's a pleasant change for me and doesn't upset my stomach like some flavored coffees tend to do.

column9: Yummy.. but has a good amount of sugar in it.
column10: This coffee is flavorful, creamy and it tasted a lot like a latte that you would purchase at a coffee house.  I was pleasantly surprised by this coffee and didn't think I would like it as much as I did.  There is a good amount of sugar in it which is why I gave it 4 stars instead of 5.  I loved how frothy the coffee was, I anticipated it to be flat and not creamy which is just the opposite of what I experienced.  I wish it had less sugar in it but that is just me.  It is definitely tasty!

I have always loved Maxwell House International Coffees and this one does not disappoint.  It is chocolatey and minty with just a touch of froth on the top.  As you add water, it starts to foam and the coffee dissolves.  You do have to stir quite a it to get all the lumps dissolved but not as much as you do most hot chocolate mixes.  It has just the right amount of sweetness for my taste and makes a nice afternoon treat.  I wish they made a sugar free decaf version.
I've always enjoyed the International Coffees.  This is a cozy and warming flavor, perfect for winter.  A nice blend of chocolate and mint.

column9: It is ok, but nothing special
column10: Comparing to Starbucks Peppermint Mocha, this one tastes like mud. If you never tried Starbucks one: this one is too watery when prepared as directed, if you up the dosage of mix per ounce there is still not enough richness or decadence in it. It is simply not good enough. I did find a use for it though: if you add a teaspoonful to Swiss Miss Dark Chocolate sensation mix, which is perfectly divine by itself, it brings a bit of minty coffee flavor to dark chocolate and tastes great, but only mixed into Swiss Miss.

Peppermint mocha coffee...that's just what this is!  A wonderful rich mocha flavor with a fresh, cool mint aftertaste.  I would recommend using milk rather than water for a richer drink.  What a great way to celebrate the winter season.

I doubt it's much different than it was prior, if any.  They said it's only a changed label.  For what it's worth, I liked the old label better, but that's of no real substance here.I didn't think the coffee flavor was strong enough, even with double the dose.  The peppermint was a nice addition to the coffee, but neither was strong enough.  I wouldn't get it again for only that reason: strength.The idea is good, and the flavor is good...just not enough of it.  I guess there's no reason to up the peppermint, since it's only supposed to be a hint of flavor, but the coffee needs some work.  If the old Cafe au Lait appeals to you, i.e. weaker coffee flavor, but still not tasting like 'instant', then this might be just your thing.  It certainly has that holiday aroma, and I'm just sorry it didn't offer enough "coffee" for me.

I always need my coffee in the morning, and this made for a nice change of pace. It has a smooth, rich chocolate flavor with hints of fresh peppermint. It would make for a great treat during the holidays.However, it does have its flaws. Depending on how you mix it, it can have almost no flavor or be too sweet. It also uses corn syrup, non-dairy creamer, and artificial flavors that aren't particularly good for your diet. In addition, the package is rather small, so the coffee goes quickly.Overall, I'd say that this is more for fans of hot chocolate than coffee drinkers, but makes for a sweet winter treat for anyone.

column9: Rich Taste and a Refreshing Change!
column10: A nice change from regular coffee, it has a nice rich taste depending how you prepare it, I made it with water and also tried it with milk, I found I preferred it with water. Asides from the taste, I got quite a pick-up from it and  found it a very enjoyable drink. It is quite sweet, something you cannot compromise on or else it will be on the thin side.The package itself is a little on the small side, It did not last long in our house, and was empty by the next day....though this does mean that everyone liked it!I would compare it to a high end hot chocolate drink with a nice peppermint taste. If you enjoy flavored coffee's or hot chocolate hot drinks, this will please your taste buds. However, if you don't like sweet drinks...it may not suit you.

The Maxwell House International Latte is easy to make, and does taste good. You must use a lot of the mix to get a full-bodied cup of the peppermint mocha. In my opinion, the peppermint flavor overpowers the mocha... And it really seems more like a cup of peppermint hot chocolate than a coffee drink. Keep in mind, it's made mostly of sugar, nondairy creamer, corn syrup, and a host of artificial favors. That said, if you like peppermint hot chocolate that's easy to make with hot water, this is for you.

column9: Tasty but certainly not the best
column10: This tastes like a weak hot chocolate with peppermint in it. It does get a little foamy on top which makes you think it is like a capachino but the flavor isn't strong enough and I really couldn't taste any coffee flavor in it. You need to put more than it calls for to get a strong enough flavor but it still doesn't have a coffee flavor to it. The mint makes it a nice change of pace and really does add to the flavor but this is not something I would buy often, for the price and the extra you need to use, plus the fact that the flavor isn't as good as the real thing it really isn't worth the price and is not what I would consider gourmet or special.

This drink can be made with water or milk, and I chose milk.  The directions suggest 6-8 ounces of milk or water with 4 teaspoons of the drink mix.  I used 6 ounces of hot milk and 4 teaspoons of mix as suggested, and it tatsed bland so I added about 3 more teaspoons.  I like FLAVOR and wanted to taste something!  With this addition, the mocha flavor was subtle but detectable, but I noticed an enjoyable peppermint flavor.

column9: A tasty treat for the family
column10: My kids and I have always loved hot chocolate and splurging on the occasional International Coffee.  This one was a hit with all of us, a faint taste of peppermint, although I thought it tasted more hot chocolately that mocha-ey.  Not complaining though.  I would say if you like the International Coffee flavors in general, then you will like this one.  Perfect for the holidays, so I would enjoy it while it is around.

I love Peppermint Mocha and eagerly await it's arrival at Starbucks every winter, as well as the Coffeemate Creamer in the grocery store.  So I was excited to see this product.  The first cup I made tasted weak, so I decided I hadn't used enough.  Next cup, two heaping teaspoons.  Still a tad weak in the flavor department.  So, although you taste the mint and the mocha, you just don't taste it enough in my estimation.  Also, they've now changed the containers from tin (recyclable) to #5 plastic, so into the landfill it goes.

I am a huge peppermint lover!  I am also a bit of a picky person when it comes to drink mixes.  For me, many end up being powdery and not as creamy and tasty as I would like.  That was not the case with Maxwell House International Coffee Peppermint Mocha Latte mix.  Once you find just the right mixture of powder and hot water, you are good to go.  The container states 4 tsp to 6 - 8 oz of boiling water.  Well, I always have a big mug when I drink, which is about double this.  Not a problem - I usually use 8 tsp for my 16 oz. mug and it turns out great.  The peppermint flavor is amazingly refreshing and so delicious.  It is not overpowering, yet is strong enough that the drinker knows it is peppermint flavored.  For me, this is one of the perfect ways to treat myself after a crazy or hectic day.  Curling up with a mug of this peppermint mocha latte and a great book makes a blissful evening!  I highly recommend this mix to anyone who enjoys peppermint and chocolate.

The mint is not overpowering or overly fake.  I don't like it mixed with water so much as I do mixed in with my own coffee or mixed in with milk.  It gives it a festive zip.  I certainly wouldn't mind finding some of this in my stocking come St. Nick's day.

column4: Tracy Foote "College Savings Plan Author, Pho...
column9: Perfect for non-coffee drinker on a cold day
column10: I'm not a big coffee drinker so I worried that this would be a cup of coffee with a hint of mocha and peppermit. Instead, it's a cup of hot cocoa with a hint of coffee and mocha, and this is perfect for me. I saw others mentioned that it is not too sweet and I agree. But, I actually prefer this. This type of product is the perfect alternative to a warm cup of tea. I'm interested in checking out the other flavors. ~Highly recommend for hot cocoa fans.

column9: Festive flavor for the holidays, but I think I'll stick with "real" coffee
column10: To save calories and all the artificial ingredients, I really wish I could drink plain black coffee, but I just don't like it.  I usually have brewed coffee with flavored non-dairy creamer.  When I saw this product (and the Pumpkin Spice variety) available through the Vine program, I thought I would give it a try.  It's okay, but nothing great.  It's sweet and has a slight peppermint flavor (fun for the holidays), but really no coffee flavor to speak of.  It's certainly not the quality of a latte drink you would get at a coffee shop.  On the plus side, it is super easy to make plus costs much less than a latte drink from a coffee shop.  The product does not contain much actual coffee, so it certainly won't give the morning pick-me-up that I have come to expect from my morning coffee.  So I think I will stick with my usual brewed coffee with flavored non-dairy creamer in the mornings and the occasional latte or similar drink at the local coffee shop.

column9: Good at home peppermint mocha mix
column10: I like mocha, and I like peppermint.  I think I especially like these drinks around the holiday season.  A little sweet, a little decadent, but why not?  The Peppermint Mocha flavored International Latte by Maxwell House is a convenient and cheaper way to have a peppermint mocha at home.  Is it the same as those made by your favorite coffee shop?  No.  But it is a nice instant drink when you are in the mood for something hot and flavorful at the house.It mixes well, but I use a larger than 8 oz mug, so I have to put more than the recommended serving to get the taste I want.  That's another nice thing about doing it at home, you can make it as strong or weak as you like.  If you want more coffee, try mixing this peppermint mocha powder with coffee rather than water.  I like it that way too, just as I like the liquid peppermint mocha creamers being sold this time of year.  However, most of the time I just mix this powder with water.There is more sugar and other ingredients than coffee by reading the list on the package.  That means it is not a strong cup of coffee, which may suit some people better.  Because it is high in sugar, with a touch of fat, it is high in calories for what it is.  But it is not nearly as calorie laden as those from a coffee shop.So, for a nice, flavorful, quick, mix-it-at-home, powdered beverage that mixes with water, Maxwell House's Peppermint Mocha is nice to have in the cupboard for when you want a cup of peppermint mocha at home.

column9: It's the moooost won-der-ful tiiiime of the year!
column10: ...and Maxwell House's Peppermint Mocha mix will help set the tone at your house.  I'm not sure what sort of magic Maxwell House has captured here, but this product completely surpassed my and my wife's expectations.  (It probably helps to have somewhat low expectations!)  We weren't hoping for anything close to coffee house quality, but I dare say that when mixed correctly, this mocha surpasses the beverages one gets out of the machine at the local gas station.  That's pretty darn good, considering this comes out of a can.  That considered, I'm very happy with this sweet concoction.  It's got a lovely peppermint flavor that balances the coffee nicely.  Not too sweet, certainly not bitter.  It's a nice cold-weather combo.  The peppermint aroma will have the family wandering by to see what you're brewing.If you're looking for a remarkably easy coffee treat at home, this is a nearly fool proof way to go.  I recommend it without reservation.

Maxwell House's International Coffee Peppermint Mocha is something that I'd only think of picking up around the holidays. As it is a simple, home mixed Latte, you have to keep that in mind when you compare it to Latte's you get in coffee houses and restaurants. Each can is just 7.1 ounces and the amount that it takes to make a good cup of Peppermint Mocha is about 1 1/2 times what the directions call for.  The peppermint flavor is stronger but you do get the taste of the mocha (particularly if you increase the amount used). It is good with both water and when you use milk and it is delightful as a "holiday extra" or on a cold night. We did mix some in with a pre-packaged cake mix and the peppermint flavor is primarily what came through, so I'm not sure that using it to bake with is more cost effective than just using some peppermint extract. I'd classify this more as a "treat" or impulse purchase but one you'll be satisfied with if you keep in mind that it isn't replacing a trip to the coffee house.

As with many cocoa mixes, the quantity of powder needed to make a satisfying cup of hot chocolate is surprising. I followed the instructions on the box and felt that the taste was a little thin. I will add more powder next time. The peppermint flavor is tasty. Not much mocha taste, though.

The Peppermint Mocha flavor of this instant coffee is amazing!  I have tried other flavors, but this is my very most favorite!! The taste is wonderful and it mixes well whether I used a lot of the mix or just a bit in a brewed cup of coffee!! The aroma of this beverage is wonderful.  The peppermint enhances the taste rather than overwhelming it.  Try this coffee and you will be hooked!! I only hope it is not just available for the holidays!

Well, I have to say that I never would have bought this product on my own.  I got this on Vine to test, and I am sold.  I would actually buy it again.  I'm a coffee snob, so I would have walked past it in the supermarket.  But seriously, it's delicious!  It's not for the hard core coffee drinker - it almost tastes like a peppermint hot chocolate, maybe a mocha.  But it is easy and tasty, and I totally recommend it if you want something yummy once in awhile.
This stuff is great, Can definitely taste the peppermint and mocha and it's a wonderful holiday treat! I do suggest doubling the recipe though so it is more rich and creamy!

It's crazy stormy outside on this November day in Oregon and my cup of peppermint Mocha Latte hits the spot wonderfully. It's the perfect blend of mocha and peppermint to make a steaming cup of pleasure on such a yucky day.Another reviewer said she added a few t-spoons of this to her brownie batter and it turned out fantastic. So next time I'm going to have a cup and a brownie. Hello sugar high!I'm ordering more right now.

Holiday season here means peppermint coffee.  It's really hard to find for our main coffee machine (a Keurig) so I was thrilled to see this mix.  I've used the whole thing by mixing with hot water and it is quite delicious.  It really did not last very long at the house.

One thing for certain, you really can not go wrong when choosing Maxwell House. For years their products have been top quality in taste and always at a reasonable price. But the Peppermint Mocha Latte is by far their best creation, especially during the Holidays. It has such a rich flavor! Our main concern was that the peppermint would overpower the taste but I have to say it was perfectly blended. To us it's the best way to wind down a day; sit by the fireplace sipping a peppermint mocha latte and just relaxing. Very highly recommended!

Ummm...I'll admit that I'm in love with a lot of Starbuck's drinks, so I compare all coffee to theirs. However, as I sit here sipping on a cup of Maxwell House International "Peppermint Mocha Latte" Coffee, I must admit that I am pleased. This chocolaty with a hint of peppermint drink is slightly reminiscent of a certain Peppermint Mocha. All that's missing is the whipped cream and chocolate shavings. I must admit that this is my first time trying a Maxwell House International Coffee and I think that I'm a fan. Very satisfying except that I had to add a little sugar. Other than that, I would recommend this drink.

column9: Save yourself the trip to Starbucks...and save your money
column10: I got these for my wife since she loves peppermint-flavored coffee especially for the holidays.  She is pretty particular about her coffees, especially the flavored ones, but she loves these.  And as I said in the title, they've said us a few trips and quite a few dollars we'd have otherwise spent going to Starbucks for a similar hot, liquid treat.

This beverage has been a huge hit with my family. We all agree, it's flavorful without being overpowering, the perfect warm beverage on a cold winter day. It's easy to make, we have time for a cup before we have to head out the door in the morning. I'm definitely going to pick up more for the holiday season, perhaps even stick them in some stockings.

column9: Not bad if you keep in mind it's instant coffee
column10: A "latte in a box" is really instant coffee, and in setting expectations for this product, you've got to keep that in mind. There's no fancy milk steamer, no fresh coffee grounds, no barista to pull a shot and stir in the milk.You just boil water, put a tablespoon or so of the coffee mix in a cup, pour on the water and stir. There's nothing at all to add, not even milk. Easy? You bet. That's the good part.The bad part is that something has to be compromised in the process, and like all instant coffees, this one can't, and doesn't, measure up to the real thing.So then we have to ask, how close does it come? Is enough flavor and quality delivered to make it at least a decent drink, if not a great drink?I thought so when I tried this product, and I got one unexpectedly pleasant surprise: a nice frothy layer of foam appeared at the top of my cup, nicely mimicking a "real" latte. I haven't seen that before in an instant coffee.The flavor wasn't fantastic, but neither was it unacceptable. The mocha and peppermint, especially the latter, were somewhat overdone and detracted from the coffee taste, which came across as a little weak and thin (despite following the package directions as to quantity of powder to use). You might want to mix yours a little stronger, although that might make the peppermint even more dominant.I would call this something of a "mood" drink; something you'd need to be in the mood for, as opposed to a regular, everyday sort of thing.Nutritionally, you might think this would be a brewing disaster, but the stats per serving are really quite good: 50 calories, 9 grams of carbs (7g of that is sugar), and 40mg of sodium. That's a lot better than a can of sugary soda even if it isn't quite the same as plain black coffee.I give this four stars out of five because I think it does quite well for an instant coffee product. It isn't something I'll drink very often, but I was quite surprised at how far the instant coffee "art" has come.

Ok, this was not gone that quickly, but we loved it so much, it lasted only a few days in our house. Peppermint Mocha is my favorite flavor at other big-name coffee places, but it's so expensive, I don't treat myself often. This Maxwell House Instant version is so close, and so much more economical, that I'm going to be able to indulge more often. That makes me happy.

I was utterly excited when I saw this item and it certainly did not disappoint. It's not too sweet and the the mint undertones were perfect. The chocolate taste was also not overpowering, but you could certainly taste it.I added around 4 teaspoons to a cup of heated soymilk that I had heated in the microwave. It was delicious and I personally think that the soymilk helps compliments the flavors. I haven't tried regular milk since we don't usually have that in our fridge.I also attempted to mix this with milo, with soymilk of course. Two teaspoons of milo and two of this product had a richer chocolate taste, but the peppermint taste was still there. I prefer this one versus just the 4 teaspoons of peppermint mocha latte.Oh and did I mention the wonderful foam? It's absolutely splendid and it doesn't disappear after a few minutes.I have yet to add this to coffee, but I definitely plan to once I start drinking coffee again. I'm sure that a teaspoon or two will help brighten my day up in the morning.As for the cost, it's on the pricier side for me, especially since one 7.1 oz can doesn't seem to last a long time if you only use this mixed with water/milk. With 4 teaspoons per cup, I can maybe manage about 10 cups. It has a much higher value if you simply mix a teaspoon or two to hot chocolate or coffee since I can still get the same flavor, but enhanced with the taste of coffee or more chocolate. I might pick this up at my local store, but I can't see myself buying 4 cans of this at this price. While it can go a long way, I'd rather buy one can to last me during the holidays.

I am a bit of a coffee snob, so to call this "coffee" is a little hard for me to swallow.  However, it is a great holiday beverage -- more along the line of a gourmet hot chocolate.  The mint is good and strong- the choclate flavor is creamy - but the coffee flavor is non existent.  I thought it took more than package recommendation of the product (powder) to make my beverage falvorful enough. The mix had a tendency to sink to the bottom, so be sure to over-stir.  My favorite way to use it to add the mix to warm milk -- very rich and flavorful.

I was expecting this Maxwell House Peppermint Mocha Latte mix to be a thin, watery-tasting mess but I was happy to find that the flavor was decent.  The flavor really increased when I decided to use milk in place of water.  Wow.....it made a big difference in the flavor and the richness!  I highly recommend skipping the water and going with warm milk.  Here is what I did...I heated some whole milk in a saucepan over low heat until the milk was lukewarm. I then added the Peppermint Mocha Latte mix. (Waiting until the milk is WARM helps the powder to dissolve and creates a smoother drink.) I then continued to heat this mixture until it was hot - about the temperature of hot coffee or cocoa.  Yum!If you are expecting a coffee tasting drink (as the Latte in the name implies) then you will be disappointed.  I would describe this more as a hot chocolate or cocoa type beverage.  The taste was really nice and the minty flavor was refreshing. There was a good balance of mocha and peppermint which resulted in a smooth, rich flavor.

column9: Yum...Can't go wrong with this one
column10: I love anything Peppermint Mocha, so I was excited when I came across this.  I typically add Peppermint Mocha creamer to my hot chocolate and my coffee.  This is gives you the same feel when you don't have time to brew a pot of coffee.  I like it at work since all you really need is hot water.  I would recommend it.  The only sad part is that it probably won't be around once the holidays pass.  Peppermint Mocha seems to be a holiday trend and gone.  Get it while you can find it...for you, for the coffee lover in your life, to pair with a cute mug in a gift basket...Five stars from me for Peppermint Mocha International Latte by Maxwell House.  Yum!

If you like hot chocolate with mint, you will likely enjoy this new holiday flavor by Maxwell House.  There isn't much coffee flavor, so this is literally like drinking hot chocolate with mint.  My mug holds about 2 cups of hot water and it takes 2 heaping tablespoons to get full flavor from this mix.  The mix is also a bit powdery and needs to be stirred very well before it blends into the hot water.  The container is made of some sort of reinforced cardboard. I preferred the tins.  But I suppose this is one way for the company to save money.  All in all, though, this is a nice treat for the holidays.

column9: Short on coffee, long on tastiness . . . and sunnies up a winter day.
column10: Don't count on this to keep you awake because of its caffeine content.  If anything, you might get a sugar high.  "Instant coffee" is the fifth ingredient after "sugar," "non-dairy creamer," "maltodextrin" and "cocoa."  In fact, it tastes much more like a specialty cocoa than it does a coffee.  Nice blend of peppermint and mocha flavors.  Certainly won't win any "healthy food" awards, but you probably know that already.  Fifty calories per serving, fifteen of which come from fat.  Nine grams of sugar.As with many hot-mix-type beverages, recommends 6 oz of milk or water per 4 tsp of product.  I used 4 tbsp (that's tablespoons) instead and was impressed with the intensity of taste.  Glad I tried it.

column9: Good for the money, but way too sweet.
column10: Okay, so if they didn't master the problem with the pumpkin latte, well, they certainly made it all the worse with this one.  So, you've got a veritable guaranteed combo to sate the pate.  Trouble is, the sugar content is way too high.  When you take your first sip, it's a cavity enclosing sweetness surge.  So, if you like sugary confections in your steamy mug...rock it.  If not, you should stay away.

I have always been a fan of peppermint ANYTHING, so I just had to have this coffee. It has a delightful blend of peppermint and mocha that tastes just right. I love how it's not too minty to overpower the other flavors. It tastes rich and premium, too. This is very much a holiday kind of flavor that is good for warming up with on cold nights. I am thinking this is a good Christmas morning coffee too. Something to wake you up while tearing into the presents! :) I highly recommend this and also the Pumpkin Spice flavor I reviewed as well! These are great!!

This is like drinking candy in a cup -- almost like sweet hot cocoa with peppermint.  The cocoa and peppermint flavors are heavy and can't be missed and the drink creates a nice foam.
