After a long battle with a strange rash around my son's mouth, we and our dermatologist finally realized that my son has an allergy to dyes. Even though I feed him healthy food, his toothpaste and the ocassional iced tea mix were causing it. After going completely dye free and giving up candy, these lollipops have been a very welcomed treat for him. They taste great and he loves to pass them out to other kids at little league games or at the playground, and I feel good that he's sharing something that is natural. We are eager to try other YummyEarth products!

column9: Tart, but flavorful. Nice alternative to artificially flavored & colored lollipops.
column10: Very tasty, although they are on the tart side, some more than others. My favorites are the pomegranate and watermelon. The blueberry is a little too sour and the mango has a slight bitter taste to me, but I still ate them. I don't feel as guilty eating these since they are all-natural and with cabbage and carrots for coloring, it's almost like eating health food! :-)

We got these because both of our sons have a sensitivity (or allergy) to the artificial colors in most hard candies.  It's really nice to be able to give them a candy that won't make them sick later.  Plus they really taste great, so we like them too.  I recommend these to friends too.

We have to go dye-free because of my son's allergy.  These lollipops are wonderfully tasty, and he never complains when I substitute "our lollipops" for other candy that he's been given.  They are small (about half-dollar size, or slightly smaller), but seem to last a while.They are worth the cost, and I will definitely buy these again!!
These lollipops are fantastic. My son has an allergy to food dyes and these were his treat. Now all the other kids are begging to eat them too because they are soo good. Thanks Yummy Earth!
Very tasty.  Some better than others.  They are quite small but that is not necessarily a bad thing.

I ordered these for my son's band teacher to give to him as a treat.  We do our best to avoid food coloring and these help ease the blow of going natural.  He and anyone who has gotten one loves them!
They are low calorie organic lollies that the kids love and I don't feel so bad because they are only consuming 20 calories and not 60-120 like most others. Plus they are natural!!!

If you too are gluten intolerant, you have become aware how much food you can not eat.  I missed having cookies.  When I saw this on Amazon.com, I thought could it really taste good.  The answer is yes!  Finally, I can have cookies again.  Try them, I believe they'll become a regular with you.

column9: It's too good.....but it IS true!!
column10: I actually found this product at my local grocery store (Weis).  It was a bit more expensive than amazon at 4.29 a box but I figured what the heck, I MUST find out if this is a good mix or not.  I have a wheat allergy but not all gluten bothers me so I have more options than some people.  I have tried many mixes and recipes, just wheat free and totally gluten free.  I am VERY happy to say that these cookies taste just like a "regular" chocolate chip cookies.  They are the best I have come across from a mix or a recipe.  They are not gritty or funny tasting.  They are divine.  If you live wheat or gluten free I"m sure you have said at one time or another "that's not bad for being wheat/gluten free".  There is no need to say such a thing about these cookies.  I doubt most people would be able to tell you that it was not a regular old pilsbury or tollhouse cookie.  They are slightly more crumbly than a traditional cookie but it does not affect the quality or flavor of the cookies.  Try them! You will like them for sure!!!!

column9: Not my favorite, but the wheat lovers liked it
column10: I have Celiac disease and cannot eat gluten at all or I get terribly ill. This cookie mix DID NOT make me sick at all.  It is 100% gluten free and safe for Celiacs! That is a great thing for all of us on gluten-free diets.Unfortunately, thought the cookies did not make me ill, I will not be buying them again. Frankly, I did not enjoy these cookies. What I like are fluffy soft, cookies, that have no greasy residue. Betty Crockers cookies come out chewy in the middle, crispy on the edges, and a little greasy.  Therefore, I prefer Cause You're So Special's chocolate chip cookies and will be buying those instead.On the positive side though, all the wheat lovers in the house ate the cookies up and loved them.  So, even though I do not like them, the cookies were close enough to the original that the wheat lovers were delighted.

column9: Best gluten free cookies I've had!
column10: Like most of the reviewers already pointed out, these cookies rock!  All of my friends and family have tolerated my attempts at making gluten-free baked goods, and they were extremely pleasantly surprised by these cookies.  They said they couldn't even tell they were gluten-free (and they are brutally honest).The Betty Crocker website has a product locator, which I don't think is working for this product, since I did buy them at the store, and no stores actually appeared after I searched using my address.  If you don't want to use butter, there are alternative recipes on the website that use oil.
Easy to mix, tastes great! Non-Celiac husband loves these!For those that need ingredient lists, go to the actual Betty Crocker site before submitting negative reviews...sheesh.

These cookies are abaolutely unbelievably good - taste just like the real thing.  The price on Amazon, especially with the subscription service, which you will definitely want to do once you tast these, is the best price around!

These cookies are buttery and delicious! Just like the old tollhouse ones...maybe a little more buttery tasting. I would definitely recommend buying this product. Its wonderful to have on hand to whip up a quick batch of GF cookies and the dough freezes well if you don't want all the cookies at once. Try mixing in a little shredded coconut for something different. Delicious!

These are incredibly easy and oh so good!  Best of all, our 13 yr old daughter can bake them herself.  She uses a sheet of parchment paper on the bottom of the cookie pan and allows the pan to cool completely after baking.  The result is a perfectly shaped cookie that stores well without crumbling.  These are every bit as good as traditional choc chip cookies and worth buying again. Thank you Betty Crocker!

column9: Great cookies, thank you Betty Crocker
column10: These cookies are good, chewy and have great flavor.  Next time I may try baking a slightly shorter time than recommended, as mine were a little too brown around the edges but otherwise, perfect.  My son (who does not have celiac) thought that they were fantastic and was disappointed the day after I made them when I had finished them off!  I just couldn't stop after missing good, fresh from the over cookies for years.I noticed a few negative reviews here from people who have not tried the products!  Shockingly, there is even one from someone plugging her own gluten free bakery and then hypocritically criticizing others for getting on the "gluten free bandwagon" since there are "bucks to be made"! Well, it turns out that perhaps the larger manufacturer has the research money and testing facilities to get the taste RIGHT.  This mix (along with the yellow cake mix) is better than nearly all of the specialty mixes I have tried.  It is sad how many pans of cakes, brownies, blondies and cookies I have tossed in the garbage because they were inedible.Thank you Betty Crocker (General Mills) for making a very high-quality gluten free mix available in my regular grocery store!

column9: Woo hoo! Gluten free Betty Crocker!
column10: I am so thrilled to see these products! As a person who lives with celiac, thank you Betty Crocker for mainstreaming gluten free products! I would like to see a mixed group of the 4 products available, such as 1 of each of the cake mixes, 2 brownie mixes, and 2 cookie mixes.

I give these cookies 5 stars because the recipe was so easy, compared to many other gluten free mixes that have lots of additions and many steps, this recipe basically has 2 steps, mix the wet ingredients then add the mix.The flavor was good, the rice flour does give it a bit of a gritty texture but it's not much. I think this mix would benefit from refrigerating the dough for an hour or so because the cookies were a bit flat, I have some in the fridge that I will try and see if the refrigeration makes a difference.

These cookies turned out great!They didn't crumble the next morning either!  I used Fleishman's unsalted for the butter it called for making it gfcf and they still came out perfect. They seriously tastes like regular cookies.  Next time, I am trying it with coconut oil.  Good price if you sign up for auto ship.  These will come in handy during the holidays.

column9: Really good cookie, takes a little practice to get them just right.
column10: When making these cookies, I would change the directions given on the box by adding "Wait until cookies are cool to the touch before removing from the cookie sheet"  Two minutes was not long enough to wait, and the first batch of cookies that I made crumbled into a tasty pile of crumbs.  Cookies tasted great, and had only mild aftertaste (a bit powdery, but not unpleasant).  Might be better with a glass of milk to chase them down :)
Great taste & texture!!! They were gobbled up by my hubby & kids who are not on a GF diet. Thanks Betty!

As the husband of a Celiac, I've been subjected to a WIDE array of gluten-free products in the never-ending quest to find food that tastes like "normal" food. Let me tell you, these cookies are indistinguishable from cookies made with regular flour! Wow!They have all the great characteristics of a tried-and-true, classic chocolate chip cookie... chewy not brittle, moist not dry, smooth not gritty, flexible not crumbly, and plenty of chocolate chips!!If Betty Crocker can do the same magic with other products as they've done with these, they will REVOLUTIONIZE the gluten-free industry!!These should get 6 stars out of 5!!!

I just made and tried Betty Crocker's Gluten Free Chocolate Chip Cookie mix.  (I used butter as directed.) The cookies turned out chewy on the middle and crispy on the edges.  Perfect. The amount of chocolate chips in the mix seemed just right.  I often make Nestle Toll House cookies for my family.  These Betty Crocker cookies tasted and looked just like the Toll House ones which my family has always loved. The gluten free cookies were delicious-no  bad odor or after taste like many gluten-free mixes have.  I can't wait to try the other gluten free products by Betty Crocker.  If you love chocolate chip cookies, you won't be disappointed.  Very easy to make and great to eat!!

Way to go Betty Crocker!!! Just made these this morning and they are yummy. Complaints have been made about the grainy texture. Well come on, how picky can you be when it's gluten free. When you have celiac, you are greatful for such a yummy tasting product! Two thumbs up from my children and I :-)

I love Betty Crocker GF mixes, so I had high hopes for this one. Unfortunately, I found it to have kind of an odd aftertaste, and the cookies just didn't hold together for me at all. I tried it using crisco grease, then again tried it using butter, then even tried it using cooking oil, but the cookies just spread out too thin no matter what I did. I tried removing them from the parchment paper warm and removing them completely cooled -- no difference. They just fall apart.  Makes a good ice cream topping, or great for using as a creative decoration on top of a birthday cake, though.

column9: Didn't get this one right BC!
column10: I have tried the GF cc cookies-very dissappointed!  I followed the recipe, used real butter, baked on a cooled cookie sheet, but my cookies came out flat, thin and super sweet.  I have made several different GF cookies that taste great and resemble a cookie, but this recipe isn't the one Betty Crocker!  I will have to keep making mine from scratch!  GF Brownies are awesome though!

These cookies are not gluten free. I made them hoping that I would be able to enjoy some cookies,but I ended up in severe pain, having to go to bed early that night! Some people with just a slight gluten intollerance may be able to handle but if you are a true Celiac watch out.

Made these for my son who is two years old who has to be GF due to a birth defect. He had one and won't eat another. What two year old passes up a chocolate chip cookie. Will not buy again. Something is missing for sure. HORRIBLE>>>>

I bought this after trying the brownie mix which was outstanding.  The dark brown blob that is supposed to be a chocolate chip, tasted rancid and not in any way chocolate.  Utterly disgusting product.  I suffered from stomach issues later that night

On the Amazon page, the product information contains only the brand name and the quantity. For the sake of those who may be allergic to wheat (rather than suffering from celiac disease), the contents of the mixes should be listed.I haven't used the product, because I can't tell from the description whether I would be able to use it or not. I rated it a "3" only because I couldn't submit the review without a rating.
I would love to purchase this product along with the others but won't because there aren't ingredient lists. It is extremely irresponsible to sell these products without the ingredient lists.

Before I would buy this product I would need to read the label completely.  No information is given.  Just because the product is gluten free does not mean that it doesn't contain other objectionable ingredients.I hope someone at Amazon reads this.

column9: Let me know when you post the ingredients list!
column10: Like others, I cannot order this product w/o an ingredients list.  Amazon, people with food allergies, intolerances, or other dietary restrictions need complete information!  Thank you and please resend the G-F for Betty Crocker notice when ingredients lists are included.

I totally agree with those expressing their requests for more ingredient information.  There are so many gluten-free products on the market now because it's "popular" to do so and bucks can be made.  I recently opened a wheat-free, gluten-free bakery because most commercial products take short-cuts and include ingredients which should not be combined, even if they are wheat-free & gluten-free.  Also, most commercial gluten-free products contain a ton of sugar.  Please be very selective and pay attention to how your body responds - you can learn to do that even before you eat something.

These make great cookies.  I think they have the right amount of chocolate chips and they taste fabulous.Be sure to use real butter.  In GF cooking, margarine doesn't work as a substitute...I tested it too and margarine cookies tasted terrible, looked even worse and crumbled into a million pieces.  Butter (as box calls for) were perfect and delicious.These will definitely be my go-to for chocolate chip cookies!  I hope Betty Crocker begins to make other Gluten Free items as well!

These cookies are by far the best GF cookies I've had.  The Ingredient list is as follows:  Rice Flour, Semi sweet Choc chips (sugar, chocolate liquor, cocoa butter, soy lecithin, vanilla#,Brown sugar, Sugar, Potato starch, potato flour, Leavening#baking soda,sodium acid pyrophosphate, monocalcium phosphate) salt.  Contains Soy ingredients.Try them, you wont be let down!

These cookies taste just like I remember the wheat-flour recipe tastes!  I like my cookies a little crisper and these came out perfect!!  Highly recommended for those who "remember when" and want that great Betty Crocker taste.

For those that are looking for the ingredient list check out the Betty Crocker website - they have a great gluten free section for the new products.When mixing the ingredients don't be alarmed that the batter is very crumbly.  We used a round ice cream scoop when putting on the baking sheet - worked fabulously!  The result is a buttery, chewy delicious cookie!  My daughter made them with her friend and her friend brought some home to share with her family...they had no clue they were gluten free.  I would buy this over and over again!

Thank you Betty Crocker for a product that is simple to prepare and one that might soon be available in mainstream markets.  Received mine through Amazon yesterday and promptly made them up as directed.  Super easy to prepare, directions clear, but flavor was just average and texture grainy (the rice flour used in the mix is not a very fine grind).  Must say that my standard GF chocolate chip cookies using Karen Robertson's "Cooking Gluten Free" recipe, page 184, and "Wendy Wark's Gluten Free flour mix", is in my opinion far superior.  But, for friends who wish to mix up a batch of cookies for my child without a lot of fuss, this Betty Crocker Chip Cookie Mix would be just the right product.

Some reviews have given low scores to this product because Amazon is not listing ingredients. In 2 minutes I was able to go to the product website[...]and find out that the line of products are "Celiac Disease Foundation and the Celiac Sprue Association" approved.My advice to the reviewers that gave this a 1 star because no ingredient information was listed, I hate lazy people!,next time do an Internet search (it's easy, ever hear of Google),go to the product website to get the information,stop bashing a product for information Amazon does not have andkeep your thoughts to yourself until you actually try the product.I give 5 stars to Betty Crocker for stepping up and giving a minority population a product in mainstream grocery stores at a reasonable price. I searched the Betty Crocker website and found that these are not avaiable anywhere in my zip code yet.[...]I have ordered all 4 Gluten-Free products from Amazon and look forward to baking!

column9: Add a few extra ingrediants and then....YUM
column10: Try adding some GF smooth peanut butter and about 2 T of heavy cream....let the dough sit in the fridge for 30 minutes, then bake as directed.  The wait time lets the dry rice flour absorb moisture and the cookies won't be as grainy.  You can also bake in a brownie pan for GF "Peanut Butter Chocolate Chip" brownies - very tasty.

column9: Yummy out of the oven, but crumble after cooling
column10: I purchased Betty Crocker's Gluten Free Chocolate Chip Cookie Mix from my local Wal-Mart and was super excited to try them, as I just recently went gluten free and haven't found a good cookie yet.They were easy to make, just like "normal" cookies, and the house smelled wonderful while they were cooking. I almost cried when I took the first bite because they were SO GOOD!! They were perfect, warm, and soft in the middle with a little crispy around the edges. I couldn't have asked for a better cookie!However, when I pulled one out the next day to have another cookie, I was so sad to see it crumble in my hand. I had to pick up the crumbs and throw most of them away as they were so dry I couldn't eat them. They just kind of dissolved when I picked them up and didn't hold together.All in all, these cookies are WONDERFUL straight out of the oven, but they seem to really dry out when they cool and are pretty useless as decent cookies afterward. I may buy this mix again, only if I have enough people to eat all of them straight out of the oven. I won't make them for myself, though, as I'll end up throwing away 75% of the cookies after they cool.
This is a great mainstream GF product, they taste just like normal BC cookies. The dough looked like normal dough. They turned out great.The product does contain soy for those that are intolerant.

column9: No negative reviews about actual product!
column10: Has anyone noticed that none of the Betty Crocker Gluten Free mixes have gotten any negative feedback from anyone who has actually TRIED the product? Just a lot of whining from people who complain about how hard it is to research a gluten free diet but then don't even know enough to call Betty Crocker if they have a question. I have Celiac disease too and am just thankful the disease is getting enough attention that a mainstream manufacturer will invest huge $$$ in developing products for us. Pick up a phone if you have any questions for pete's sake!

column9: finally an easy to get &  make gf option
column10: I read the reviews and purchased a couple of boxes yesterday. My daughters had friends over so I  made them. They were delicious and no ill effects (for those of you giving bad ratings w/o trying). The ingredients ARE listed on the box and you can also visit the web site. I am so happy and grateful that a "Mainstream" company is getting into the gf market. Waistlines aside, we should all be supporting them.

The best thing about this mix is it's fast and easy. Everything you need to know is on the back of the box. You don't have to measure anything. All it takes is 1 stick of butter, 1 egg, and a splash of vanilla extract. And you can actually go without the vanilla if you don't have any handy. With a bit of quick kitchen maneuvering (preheat the oven and get cookie sheets ready before you mix the dough), you can have the first batch of gluten free cookies in 15 minutes. That's not bad considering it will take at least 15 minutes to go pick up a box at the local store (if you have one down the street) when a craving hits and there is absolutely nothing to snack on in the house.The taste is not completely homemade. Maybe it's mental, but I think all boxed stuff has a "BOXED" taste. But it is warm and freshly baked and you get that nice sweet aroma in the house. I don't recommend eating the cookies directly out of the oven because the GF dough needs to cool and set a bit longer than regular wheat dough. Instructions on the box indicate that a 2 minute cooling period is required. I think it's wise to follow those orders. I let mine sit a little longer.The raw dough doesn't taste as good as regular cookie dough. The rice/potato flour mix is quite grainy and the dough itself is crumbly. I would not attempt to add it to my ice cream.The recipe calls for butter. You CAN substitute with margarine but butter tastes a lot better.I just made a box this afternoon. I followed the directions. I made 24 (3-inch) cookies and baked them for 10 minutes because I like my cookies brown and toasty with crispy edges. You don't have to brown them as much. The recipe say 8-10 minutes. I let them cool for 5 minutes then ate 3 with milk. Yum!

column9: They will do in a pinch, but I really wanted to love them.
column10: I was diagnosed with Celiac less than two months ago, so I have been without chocoalte chip cookies for a little while.  I was craving them and these were on the grocery shelf (with 'mainstream' baking mixes...hurray for Betty Crocker putting itself out there with gluten-free products!)next to the brownies etc.,  I wish I had eaten more when they were warm.  They don't hold up for long after they have cooled down and you let them sit.  A good idea would be to use only enough dough for the cookies you can eat right away and freeze the rest; then use the rest as you would like to satisfy a craving of your own.  They should be eaten while still warm....when they are at their best.  After they cooled down; the slightly overly sweetness comes through.  Even later, the sweetness has a synthetic taste to it and a grainy texture to it.All-in-all better than others out there, but room for improvement too.

column9: They were a let down for me...
column10: I had tried the Betty Crocker GF Brownie mix and loved it, so I bought these without testing them first. Silly me... They must be eaten while still warm. If you wait too long, they develop a sandy texture and loose much of their flavor.Just the two of us, so I mix up a batch and roll them into balls. I refrigerate the balls until we feel like warm out of the oven cookies. Then I only bake as many as I know we will eat for that one treat time.

You can produce a picture perfect cookie that will crumble on you with the slightest touch.  Eating the cookie is like eating gritty cookie crumbs with chocolate chips.  Adding milk to the mixture only helps a little.  I still have 4 boxes left to use and I'm experimenting to make a better cookie.

column9: Hard to believe these are gluten free!
column10: These cookies are terrific!  When I first ordered the mixes, I made a batch to take on a trip so I would have a gluten free snack item.  The whole family loved them!  I had to keep hiding them so I would have some for myself.  We have a 'from scratch' gluten free chocolate chip recipe that we really like, but these are better and easier to make.I did have to make an adjustment on the baking time, as they took longer to bake than the instructions said they would, but that was not a problem at all.Our local stores are starting to carry some of the Betty Crocker gluten free mixes, but the prices are MUCH better at Amazon.

I was very happy to find the Betty Crocker Gluten Free mixes at the local grocery store.  I've recently formed a gluten intolerance, but I do have a sweet tooth.  I have to be careful with soy protein, so many gluten free products are not usable for me as they use soy flour.  These however, do not.  The ingredients from the box are as follows:Rice Flour, Semi-Sweet Chocolate Chips (sugar, chocolate liquor, cocoa butter, soy lecithin vanilla), Brown Sugar, Sugar, Potato Starch, Potato Flour, Leavening (baking soda, sodium acid pyrophosphate, monocalcium phosphate), Salt.I made the cookies per the directions on the box.  Due to the dryness of the mix once everything is together, I found it much easier to mix with my hands rather than with a whisk or a spoon.  Once that was done, I formed the dough in to 18 even sized portions, baked 6, and threw the rest in the freezer so I can pull out a cookie when I feel like having one.The flavor of these cookies is very good.  In fact, my two year old who does not like cookies gobbled these up.  I am giving it a 4 out of 5 though, because the texture is a bit grainy, which means the people in my house that have food texture issues thought they tasted nice, but had problems with the graininess.I think I will definitely buy again just so it is something to have on hand when in need of a sweet treat, especially if the frozen dough comes out nicely.

This was my first time making these cookies and the mix was really crumbly. I cooked one sheet of cookies and before I put rest of the cookie dough on the cookie sheet the 2nd time, I added some apple sauce (cinnamon flavored) until there were no more crumbs. The mix was a little sticky and I cooked them a little longer, but they turned out nice and moist. I will keep using the apple sauce in mine.

I switched over to a gluten-free lifestyle many months ago to alleviate some health problems, and it's been quite a challenge. My body feels healthier, more alive, and no more digestive issues- but buying gluten-free mixes and prepared items are really hit or miss. You could end up with something that tastes almost exactly like it's wheat flour equivalent, or you could end up with something rubbery or super grainy.I've been experimenting with making all my gluten-free items from scratch with my wide array of starches and flours, but I was suffering from a sweet craving and just did not feel like playing around with recipes to get something yummy. So, I bought this mix. I cannot believe how amazing it tastes! It tastes almost identical to regular chocolate chip cookies! It has a very *slight* grainy texture, but nothing worth complaining about. I love that they don't skimp out on the chocolate chips either! The chips are a bit harder, but It tastes the same as anything else. I'm not sure why another reviewer said they tastes rancid. He/she might have gotten a bad box?Very sweet, moist cookies. I recommend only eating one at a time due to the sugar content. Also, I find this easier to mix with your hands! It worked better than my electric hand beater.This contains soy, which might be an additional issue for people with food intolerance. The mix itself does not contain dairy, but the finished product will. I bet you can find a clever butter substitute that works with mixes like this,though!

As with many gluten-free packaged items, they are adequate out of the box, but with a little modification, they can be great.  Here is what I have come to do after several different iterations. Add:1. 1 tsp potato flour (not starch)2. 1 Tbsp tapioca flour/starch3. 1 Tbsp waterYou end up with cookie dough and cookies that are nearly identical to their gluten counter-parts and have a longer shelf-life without becoming so dry and crumbly. I often add another 1/2c or so of chips as well. I have a hard time keeping them in the house after I make them. Take 2 and put some frosting or ice cream between them and...you may have to make more. I hope that helps.  Enjoy.

column9: You have to really be in a pinch.
column10: Good, but not good enough.  The people developing these either are producting for those that do not need to be Gfree the rest of their lives and obviously have never tasted Gfree foods.  Chocolate Chip Cookies should not have an aftertaste from the flour blend used.  Do yourself a favor and invest in the book Cooking for Isaiah (found on Amazon).  There is the most awesome recipe for your own Gfree All Purpose Flour and from there you can make the most awesome chocolate chip cookies of your life.  My non-gfree family members will eat down my gfree cookies before they will finish off a bag of Chips Ahoy.

These cookies are great right out of the oven but left to sit for more than a day or 2 they tend to get this sandy, crumbly texture.  The Betty Crocker brownies taste great and keep much better.  Might I also suggest that if you don't know how some of the gluten free products taste to begin with and to save money and probably waste, see if you can find it at your local store.  If you like it enough then buy it in the bulk that Amazon sells.  I have read a few reviews of customers who have purchased in bulk, don't like the item(s) and have been left with a product they don't want to use at all.  Buy one package (if possible and if it is available in your area) and then decide to buy more.  I hope that helps!  And donate the rest of the unwanted product to the food pantry etc.  Thanks!

I was so surprised that the cookies were as good as they are.  If you like crisp, crunchy cookies that taste great, these cookies are what you are looking for.  They stay nice and crunchy for several days.  I put them in a tupperware container and keep the container in the refrigerator and the cookies stay as fresh as the day they were baked.  I don't like chocolate chips and will sift them out next and add walnuts instead.  Great going Betty Crocker, it's nice for gluten sensitive people to be able to eat cookies again.

Thank you,  Betty Crocker...  It's nice to know that a well known company cares about people that have to make special choices in foods.  My 14 yr old grandson can make these cookies.  Everyone in his household loves them.  My one thing special that I do is use parchment paper. The cookies slide right off to the cooling rack, no sticking, and no mess.

I am definitely going to buy these again.  The taste was on par for non-gluten boxed cookie mixes, if a bit crumbly in texture.  My very picky gluten eating kids loved the cookies and said they would eat them again.A couple of notes on making them.  First, I added about a 1/2 teaspoon extra of vanilla, about a 1/2 tsp of additional water.  The extra fluid made the cookie dough more pliable and allowed me to use my cookie scoop.  The vanilla flavor was excellent in the baked cookies.  I ended up with about 2 dozen cookies using my larger cookie scoop.  I made the 1st dozen using my silpat - and the cookies did NOT turn out at all. They were not cooked properly and they didn't brown up at the edges.  I made the 2nd dozen using parchment paper and they turned out great!  They spread nicely and browned up beautifully at the edges.  So, next time, no silpat - parchment paper only!

If I was just judging these as gluten-free chocolate chip cookies I'd give them no more than 3 stars, but going against other mixes they are easy to make (even by children), and are relatively inexpensive, making them a 4 star product as long as people aren't comparing them to homemade.  They are slightly gritty from the rice flour and they don't hold together exceptionally well, plus they fall apart the next day.  But they do well when eaten partially frozen and actually make a decent cookie for a GF ice cream sandwich.  For slightly less spreading use Spectrum shortening instead of butter.

Thank you Betty Crocker.  These are by far the best GF cookies from a mix we have tried.  The taste is very similar to its wheat counterpart.  They are just a little bit crumbly, and the cookie dough isn't nearly as good as the end product. The convenience factor is great. This is a must for our pantry and once you try them, yours as well.

column9: A nice treat, but a bit sweet
column10: I was so pleased that these cookies were good tasting and soft.  They were extremely crumbly, but stayed fresh in a plastic airtight container for a week (yes, they lasted that long because my kids didn't love them).  As an adult, I found them to be a bit too sweet.  If I were baking from scratch (as I always did before I went GF), I would have given them a bit more complexity with brown sugar and less sweetener overall.

Though I have no issue with gluten, I do have a dairy allergy. The mix had no dairy and it has more natural ingredients than many commercial mixes.  I had good results w/minor modifications to substitute butter  I used 1 egg, 1/2 cup of vanilla soy yogurt instead of butter, a couple tablespoons of extra flour (to compensate from the extra moisture of the yogurt), and a bit of vanilla.  They came out puffy, light, and very tasty.  Not chewy or dense like some cookies, but still good.  The mix has a pretty generous portion of chocolate chips too.

These are quite grainy and not at all like the real thing even when using butter.  They also have an odd flavor to them.  The crumble so badly that a co-worker saw them in a bag and thought it was rice from about 5 ft away.
I really like all the other Betty Crocker GF products but I didn't like these so much. Too crumbly and too sweet. They are fine hot but really not good the next day.

column9: Taste like the cookies my mom made when I was a kid
column10: These are unbelievably good gluten free cookies, and quite easy to make. They taste very much like the cookies my mother made when I was kid: thin, chocolatey and sweet. Unlike some other gluten free baked goods, these don't taste gritty. They certainly don't taste like they come from a box mix.

I had initially given this a so so rating. I have since found out the secret to making good cookies from this mix. It take 2 EGGS - not ONE.I had noticed that most of my gluten free recipes called for 2 eggs.If you add the extra egg, they are delicious and do not crumble so easy. They taste very much like the Toll House cookies that come in the tub or roll.So I am giving it a much higher rating - enjoy!

column9: Betty Crocker Gluten Free Chocolate chip cookie mix
column10: The Betty Crocker Gluten Free chocolate chip cookie mixes are delicious and easy. When buying these particular mixes here in bulk of 6 boxes they came out to be so much cheaper than buying them in my stores in my area. So delicious sweet treat and cheaper price is a steal!!! The Chocolate cake mix and brownie mix are definately NOT cheaper to puchase this way here for some reason.

Rather stingy chocolate-chip to cookie ratio. 2 of my finished cookies had fewer than 3 chips in them. The texture is dry and crumbly, and the flavor is bland, thanks to rice flour. It could be that I'm still mourning my old chocolate chip cookies, which were dense and chewy, thanks to high-gluten (lol) flour. I just can't get into these, sadly. Things that help: (a) gently brown half the butter in a skillet, then add the rest of the butter to cool the browned butter, so it doesn't overcook; (b) vanilla.

We find these GF cookies to be quite yummy.  I am not Gf but my son is, and he gets mad at me because I will eat his cookies...The mix is a little crumbly, but overall they are easy and fast to make.  I make sure the butter is extremely soft before adding the rest of the ingredients.  It is definitely nice to be able to have freshly baked chocolate chip cookies that taste good.

column9: IF your Vegan like me, this may help...
column10: I make GF cookies the vegan way, with apple sauce and baking powder in replace of the egg, and smart balance instead of butter. Now I have made this same vegan variation with King Arthur's brand. The Betty Crocker version has the similar crumbly grain texture as King Arthur, but King Arthur brand has a nice sweet taste along with spreading out in the oven, neither of which this brand does. I tried adding a tad bit of water and it does help to make a more "dough" texture, these still aren't as good as KA brand of flour.

These are really great cookies.  I originally made them for a relative who requires a gluten free diet, but I intend to keep making them for myself.  As suggested by another reviewer, I added an extra half teaspoon of vanilla extract and a half teaspoon of water to the batter.

I add walnuts and chocolate chunks to this mix and no one can tell they are Gluten Free. I have been asked for the recipe. I do suggest kneading the dough in the bowl as it makes the cookies less grainy. Buy it by the 6 pack as it is much less expensive that way.

column9: If you're eating these, you have fogotten what good cookies are.
column10: I just made up a batch of these cookies and I think I'm going to throw them all out. I bought a box, only because it was on sale. I thought it would make a quick fix for when I crave a cookie (I'm gluten free) and I know now I should just spend the extra time making my own. I know you can have wonderful gluten free cookies, so something is wrong with the mix. It's horrible. The texture is bad, they are gritty, the taste isn't good and the dough is gross. That should be the first clue. The dough is nasty.Don't waste your time, don't waste your money. Make them from scratch, look and find for yourself a decent recipe and use asian rice powder.Yuck, yuck, yuck.

This is a fabulous mix. I made a slight modification and they turned out very moist and were not at all crumbly. I did 1/4cup vegan "butter" spread, 2 mashed bananas, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1 egg, and 1 tsp vanilla. I baked them at 350 for about 12 minutes-14 minutes. They puffed up nicely, did not spread out into thin cookies. I did let the batter sit for about 20 minutes at room temp before baking. I modified a recipe I saw on the Betty Crocker site that used 3/4 cup pumpkin in place of the 2 mashed bananas. Adding the pumpkin or banana makes the dough much more like a traditional cookie dough, thick and sticky. This is a good base to give your own homemade flair. The cookies were not grainy like many other mixes I've tried. The recipe I used gave them a very nice texture. They did turn out slightly cake-like, so if you don't like your cookies like that, I would not recommend my version.

These will be the best cookies ever with a few simple additions. Add one extra egg ( 2 total) and a 3.4 oz packet of instant vanilla pudding mix. Follow the directions on package. Mix until a soft dough forms( not a crumbly one).I mix with a spatula and then use my hands. No one will know they are gluten free.  I have been trying to adapt this mix for one year and I think I finally have it right.

I was excited to try these but did not like them once I did.  As one review says, use real butter.  Maybe that was my problem - since along with a wheat allergy we have a dairy allergy in the family so I used my fake butter for this mix.  The cookie was crumbly and the flavor was just lacking something.... like a real honest to goodness cookie taste.  I won't be buying this again unfortunately.

I had a box of these cookies on the self and decided tonight to do some baking.These cookies were delicious and I couldn't tell any difference from a non-GF chocolate chip cookie. They were a little flat (probably my cooking abilities at fault)but I read that if you refrigerate them for 2-3 hours it should help. Cookies & milk hit the spot.

column9: Delicious, though crumble when warmed up
column10: I made these cookies and found the product a bit too dry at first, so I added a little touch of water to help the dough stick together. I made the first half of the batch as they were originally, and then added in chopped nuts to have some variety in half of the cookies.All four of my children loved these, and I love them myself.I was disappointed in the fact that when I warmed them up for a few minutes via the microwave (I love warmed up cookies...) that they fell into little crumbles. Yet when I ate them still slightly warm from the oven they didn't have such a problem.I am happy that I bought this mix to try out, and the kids are asking for these again for their lunches!
They are okay for GF I guess... I wouldn't buy them again though. They taste alright but they are really dry and crumbley-like.
THESE COOKIES ARE VERY EASY TO MAKE, COME OUT GREAT AND ARE AT THE BEST PRICE YOU CAN FIND ANT WHERE.

column9: The best GF cookies I've tasted, even including the fresh made variety!
column10: I found these initially at Target and even though they were over $5 a box, decided to try them.  Because when you're desperate for a chocolate chip cookie, you'll pay over $5 for a box, I discovered.  I'm also dairy and egg free so I substituted with egg substitute (flax and regular egg subs both work but the flax is a little heavier) and they worked well.  I also had to use Smart Balance butter subs or Earth Balance subs and those work well also.  I love these cookies and though I've been scouring my Targets and other stores for more of them, they're just not carrying them anymore.  Well, guess what??  Found them tonight on Amazon for waaaay cheaper...more like $3.50 a box, which is much more reasonable.  Try them, I promise you won't be disappointed!
Flavor is great, but I had to add about 4 tablespoons of milk to keep the mixture moist enough to work with.

column9: Easy to make and my children love them
column10: Being that I have a son with celiac disease, I love having this mix available to buy.  They turn out better than my gluten free cookies made by scratch, they aren't painfully expensive and are easy to prepare.That being said, they are lacking something.  I'm not quite sure what it is.  They are a little gritty and taste slightly too sugary.  It might just be me though because my children (and hubby) LOVE these and I've never heard a single complaint from any of them.  Because I'm so grateful to have this product available, I don't feel right taking any stars away on my review.  My children and I would be extremely disappointed if this product were discontinued.  These are better than nearly all the other gluten free cookie mixes and definitely better than any GF boxed ones.

column9: Betty Crocker Gluten Free Chocolate Cook Mix
column10: This cookie mix was very easy to use and the cookies came out fantastic! The recipe calls for the addition of one egg, one stick of butter and 1 t of vanilla. In addition, I added 4T of creamy peanut butter and some chopped peanuts. The dough held together nicely. I baked them on parchment paper and let them cool completely before moving them - as they are very fragile when they are hot. They were moist and perfectly sweet - very difficult to tell the difference between these and regular (wheat)cookies. I recommend this mix highly!!!

column9: Love this mix - great price too
column10: This is a great mix and very convenient.  Makes great cookies in a hurry, especially when I am out of the base ingredients.  Buying 6 boxes on Amazon is much cheaper than buying in the grocery store.  The only downside is that I eat more cookies when I always have the mix on-hand.

column9: Great cookies- we just add more chocolate chips!
column10: My whole family loves these cookies including my 2 and 8 yr old! My teen daughter loves them too. That are easy to bake and EVERYONE loves them!

I was skeptical of these, since I tried the brownies and thought those were disgusting!! However, I was very happy at the taste of these.  I don't think anyone would guess they are gluten-free.  Besides having the slightest grainy texture (hardly noticable)they tasted like "normal" chocolate chip cookies.  I love, love these cookies!! Thank you Betty Crocker!

I just recently went on a gluten free diet due to thyroid issues. I made these cookies the other day and didn't tell my kids or husband they were the gluten free variety. The cookies were gone by the next day! Of course I eventually told them :)Maybe I should have told them earlier and there would have been some left for me!

My Dad has celiac and I've tried a couple of chocolate chip cookie mixes before, but these are the best! He likes his chocolate chip cookies frozen-- don't ask me why, tho I agree that when they are frozen they are delicious! The first time I made these, I put white chocolate chips in as well and he fell in love. the white chocolate chips actually make the cookies more moist and adds alot to the flavor. I was going to make these again for Thanksgiving, but I couldn't find the betty crocker mix (or any chocolate chip cookie mix the was GF) anywhere in the Giant we went to down here in Maryland so later my Grandpa took me to Whole foods and we picked up a pack of Pamela's mix. Hopefully they are just as good! They will of course have the white chocolate chips in them as well! Need to hope that these mixes just keep getting better and better because I refuse to make GF cookies from scratch! WAYYYY TOO much work!!! (Although Macarons are totally on my list!!)

column9: Great cookies mix - even better with alteration to box recipe!
column10: This is a very delicious GF chocolate chip cookie mix but I have found that I like it even better when I add an extra egg - it gives them more hold.Also tastes great if you add that extra egg PLUS add 1/2-3/4 cup peanut butter.I definitely recomment this product! I have it on Amazon auto-ship :)

column9: I can eat cookies that taste like cookies again!
column10: These will be the death of me, now that I can have my cookies and eat them too. They taste great, I use plenty of coconut oil to make mine.  Buying it here in bulk is a mch better deal than getting it in the stores.  I keep the ratio of ingredient the same, and cooking time/temp is just right too.Perfect amount of chocolate chips.I hope they make more gluten free desserts!

Fantastic favor, and they are easy to make correctly. I use a cooking stone to make them and they come out even better.The only downside is they still probably have GMO ingredients in them.Your almost there Betty!

column9: I kids could not tell these wee GF!
column10: We are very new to the GF lifestyle and LOVED these cookies.  I bought a single box at Walmart to see how they tasted.  We came home baked them up and all 4 of my children scarfed them down.  They had no idea they were GF!  It's good to know we can still have some tasty treats :D  I just ordered these on Subscribe and Save for a full $1 less per box that WALMART!!  Can't beat that!
I have been gluten free for approximately 1-1/2 years and this is the best cookie mix for chocolate chip cookies.  My children even love it and they are not gluten free.

These are the only GF cookies I have tried so far, but they were fabulous!  My friends even tried them and said they taste like normal cookies.  I am convinced that adding enough butter and sugar to anything makes it yummy though.  lol  These looked exactly like the picture, and after being in the freezer for a few weeks taste just as good as the day they were made!

column9: *****Just like Grammy used to bake!  Yummy!*****
column10: I am grateful to Betty Crocker for producing several gluten free mixes!  The brownies rock too!!  Even if you dont have to eat gluten free like me, you will enjoy these cookies!!  I've made them for a ladies church event and for contractors working at my home.  No one could taste the difference, and they disappeared quickly!!!  These are easy to prepare too!  Suggest using parchment paper on the pan and to slightly underbake bya minute so they crisp up nicely onthe outside and remain chewy on the inside. Why not make yourself a scrumptious little treat today!  Happy gluten free baking!!!  :-)

With the picture on the front you think you're going to get wonderful chocolate chip cookies!  Didn't happen.  Crumbly, bland flavor, grainy texture.  Don't waste your time on these.  Quite surprised as I do like their gluten free cake & brownie mixes - but the coookies are not worth it.

column9: Surprisingly good - make sure to add another egg!
column10: Just started a GF diet a week ago and wanted to try this mix to assure myself cookies were still an option for me.  I was thrilled to see the mixes by Betty Crocker and immediately went in search of this.These turned out really well.  I followed 2 different reviewers' advice, one said to add a 2nd egg and another said to let the dough sit for a bit to let the flour soak up the moisture.  The cookies are delicious and moist, no crumbling the day after here.  The texture is slightly off but it really doesn't take away from the cookie at all.  Very very close to the wheat version.  Give it a try.

I never use cookie mixes for baking but a Celiac/GF diagnosis in the family made me look twice at a Boxed Mix.  Glad I did.  The are tasty and one can make adjustments, such as flavorings, add more chocolate chips, etc.  Make them "by the book" first so you know what the consistency is...baking GF is different and it takes some getting used to.  I hope that Betty Crocker continues to expand the line of Gluten Free.  This makes life sooooooooooooo much easier.  The cookies crisp up in a cookie jar, but if you like them soft, microwave briefly and they taste fresh out of the oven.  Best GF boxed mix I have tried for cookies so far.

column9: Chocolate Chip Cookies You'll Love To Bake Up With Your Kids Anytime
column10: This cookie mix from Betty Crocker does indeed make some delightful cookies. They have just a little too much chocolate in them but other than that they are great. They are certainly a better choice than their normal cookie mixes since they are gluten free. Your kids will have fun whipping up these cookie treats with you anytime.
This cookie mix is awesome! Everyone loved them and I couldn't get them to last more than one day before they were all gone:) I will definitely be buying more.

These cookies are awesome!  Even my husband liked them (He ate more than I did).  Yes, the consistancy is a little different from wheat-based cookies, but rolling the dough between your palms into tight balls makes them hold together better after they're baked.  For people trying to live GF it's great to have this mix in your pantry when you feel the need for a treat.

column9: So good! and dairy free, too!
column10: I LOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOVED these cookies!  I made them with non-dairy margarine and they turned out fine. They are delicate, but so many gluten-free things are.  But they have a great texture and delicious cookie scent and flavor.  Didn't feel like I was giving up anything. THank you Betty Crocker! (her GF cake mix is awesome, too!)

column9: Exactly what I want from a chocolate chip cookie
column10: I tried these yesterday for the first time, and I am thrilled with them! They are made in a dedicated facility and exactly what I want in a cookie - crispy around the edges, and chewy in the middle, and lots of chips. These, along with the other BC GF products, require that you add your own GF vanilla. I'm not sure if they left the vanilla out to keep costs down, or if it's because the mix needs just that little bit of liquid, or both. The advantage is that you could use any GF flavoring you wanted - banana, coconut, etc. I might try cutting some of the butter next time and replacing that with peanut butter and see how it goes.Unlike other reviewers, mine held up beautifully the next day after being sealed in an air tight container once they completely cooled.  I baked them on parchment, which may have made the difference. Held together nicely, still chewy in the middle and slightly crispy around the edges. Because it's just me, I only made a partial batch and refrigerated the rest of the dough. I'll update once I've baked some from that batch. If that works, I'll roll it out into a thin roll and freeze, then just slice off a few lumps so I can make a fresh cookie without the temptation of eating the whole pan!If you like a soft cakey cookie, this won't be your thing. If you want a classic "tollhouse" style crispy-chewy cookie - this is it! If you want a crispy cookie, try baking this for a little longer, possibly add some extra butter, and/or not using parchment. Great to have a real cookie fresh out of the oven!

I thought these were REALLY good, especially since they are gluten free. They are great just out of the oven, and the next day. However, I would not keep them much past that, as they start to get crumbly. My non-gluten free friends even enjoyed these.

I have close friends that have celiac disease & they have introduced me to a plethora of gluten free foods. I have grown to prefer some gluten free foods over their "regular" counterparts! I absolutely love the Betty Crocker GF Chocolate chip cookies. They are a little more crumbly compared to wheat flour cookies but I'm ok with this as the flavor is spot on! I rather prefer the texture of GF cookies.

These cookies are an answer to a Celiacs dream! Remember what cookies tasted like? This is it! And they don't cost a small fortune like most gluten free products do. The dough is a little crumbly but don't worry, the cookie are great and they are not dry or crumbly. Enjoy!

column9: Betty Crocker GF Chocolate Chip cookie mix
column10: My son loved these!  His siblings without wheat allergy would have consumed them all if I didn't restrict them.  Even my father-in-law was seen taking a few by my children, not realizing that they were special GF treats for my allergic son. I'm trying the brownies for the first time now...they're in the oven.  Hope they are as successful as these cookies were.

I loved these cookies.  They were the first gluten free thing I have ever had.  They are more grainy than normal cookies, and probably have lots of sugar.  But if you want a cookie that is to be expected.  Delicious!

I've tried alot of gluten free cookies, recipes and bakeries. . . this is by far the best of them all. It just taste like a regular cookie. I like to add nuts and eveyone loves them. Plus you can't beat the Amazon price. I've tried.

I can bake almost anything I want to gluten-free with good results. I have made many GF cookie recipes from scratch and loved them. However, these are awesome!! If you bake them according to the package directions, they are perfect. Your butter (and use real butter) MUST be softened (and not melted!). They are really really good. They will stay soft and chewy or you can bake them longer for a more crisp cookie. And the convenience rocks! Grateful for these.

column9: Good and Fast Choc Chip cookies
column10: I love these chocolate chip cookies!  I was so thrilled when Betty Crocker came out with chocolate chip cookies,yellow and choc cake and brownies! I have made these cookies many times.I got a great price on Amazon; all of us who are gluten free can attest that most GF products are more expensive than mainstream products! The cookies can be made so quickly and are great for unexpected company but mostly for me !  This is just one more product that my non-gluten free family enjoys with me. I have already sent Betty Crocker a thank you note for creating a good product especially for us who must eat gluten-free!
These are wonderful Gluten Free cookies.  Taste just like non gluten free cookies.Very hard to find in stores.

remember those great "other" chocolate chip cookies from your pre-celiac days? These cookies are just as good and as easy to make as that "other" kind....cookies were gone within 24 hours and people were begging for more!
This is the best gluten free cookie mix I have found. Well as of today 02/15/2010 who knows, I may find a better cookie mix?

column9: Awesome cookies - even with no egg!
column10: We made these cookies with 1/8 cup ghee, 1/8 cup SunButter and 1/4 cup of water - no egg.  I was skeptical about how they would turn out given these modifications but they were delicious.  After they cooled, we honestly couldn't tell they were gluten free.

While I agree that homemade chocolate chip cookies, gluten-free or not, are the best, this is my favorite gluten-free cookie mix so far. I do a lot of gluten-free baking, and I am completely satisfied with these cookies. They exceeded my expectations. My gluten-eating husband ate so many that he got a stomach ache.After making this mix twice, I do have three comments about making the cookies.*I added walnut pieces to the second batch (I love nuts in baked goods), and it made for a more fulfilling cookie.*I doubled the vanilla, because I love vanilla. It worked well.*Use completely softened butter--especially if your egg is straight out of the fridge. The first time the butter was only semi-soft and when I added the cold egg--the butter hardened too much to mix well with the egg. The second time I used butter that had been out of the fridge for about eight hours. Perfect cookies.
These cookies are so good!!  They are just like toll house chocolate chip cookies.  I do add a little water to the batter as it  can be too crumbly.
These are by far, hands down, THE BEST gluten free cookies on the market. Betty Crocker is awesome and I am a loyal customer for life!

Since going Gluten Free, I haven't had a decent chocolate chip cookie.  Most are downright nasty.  Betty Crocker perfected the GF cookie!  OMG these are just wonderful. Crispy, crunchy, chewy in the middle, great choco chips.  Yummy! Be sure to try the brownies too!  The GF yellow cake mix is not so good though.
These cookies are the best gluten free cookies we have had. Not as crumbly as most gluten free cookies.

I don't buy a lot of GF mixes because I like to bake and just do my own GF recipes, but these were recommended by a friend.  I have to say they came out very tasty and my daughter who does not have to eat GF loved them and said she would eat those instead of the "regular" ones if I just wanted to make those.  They are a little on the grainy side from the rice flour, but that happens with most GF baking.  My son has Autism and we follow the Gluten free/Casein free diet, so I did make the modification of using Spectrum non-hydrogenated shortening in place of the butter.  They came out just fine and I can't tell a difference.  Watch your baking times VERY carefully, and the second the edges turn brown take them out.  They will still look puffy and underbaked, but they will continue to cook on the cookie sheet once you take them out.  They made about 35 cookies using the Pampered Chef small size cookie scoop.

column9: Pretty good for Gluten Free baking mix
column10: This is actually pretty good for a gluten free baking mix.  The texture is a bit off, but most gluten free things are.  Tasted great!!

column9: The best chips in the world
column10: These are my favorite chips, I am from southern California but live in Texas so I can only get these chips via mail.  Chips are healthy, fresh and delicious.I've got my whole office hooked!!
Just like the other reviews - chips were stale and hard as rocks.  Like the taste when my teeth weren't pulverized, but very disappointed.Have'as are way better.

This is my first time to ever write a review.  Too busy to take the time, but this time, after ordering this product online for the past 1 1/2 yrs., it's time to let you all know how outstanding these chips are.  I have turned so many people on to these chips after I first tried them in Cabo San Lucas.  Sadly, they are not sold in KY, so I found them here.  All 6 of my kiddos and my hubby love them.  They are light, with a unique flavor that only causes that yearning for more.  Never have they arrived stale; however, you need to keep the bag sealed when not in use, like any other chip.  Outstanding by themselves, with guacamole or with salsa.  We are SOLD on these chips.

Cabo Chips have a unique taste because everything is all natural. A lot of the tortilla chips out there taste fake but with Cabo Chips, they taste real.  They have a solid crunch but that's what I'm looking for in a Tortilla Chip. I don't want a soft tortilla chip.  Another good part about the chip is that they are thin and crispy. Usually with the crunch you get out of them you'd expect a thick chip, but these have the perfect size.I've given chips to my roommates and parents and all agree that they are delicious. You can taste hints of the flavor although it is not overpowering which for me, is important. I hate getting a flavored chip and you forget that you're eating a tortilla chip.I would definitely get again (and am going to)

column9: Fast Shipping But Disappointed by Lack of Freshness
column10: I normally think Amazon is a great way to purchase some of the high end products I like for a reduced price but these Cabo Chips, which I really love, were not fresh. I had already given several of them to my son who is a college student so I could not return them. The sell by date wasn't until Nov. 2010 but they were semi stale, edible, but not fresh or as good as when bought in the store.
Terrible, stale, awful. They were purchased to go in a gift. Had to scrap that idea after I opened one.

I first discovered Cabo Chips this January when we vacationed in Maui - found them at Mana Foods in Paia. After we got home I looked them up on the Web & ordered them from Amazon (where I found the best price for a box of 12). I like them even more now! Next to Mexi-Snax (a local brand here in the San Francisco Bay Area), Cabo is my favorite tortilla chip. They are very similar to Hav'a Corn Chips - same size bag, and both are seasoned with soy sauce, not salt. But I now prefer Cabo Chips, which are a bit thinner & less oily than Hav'a and, IMO, have a finer flavor. You guys really know how to make a gourmet tortilla chip! I hope your fame spreads far and wide, so that I can buy Cabo Chips in my local supermarkets (Whole Foods and Safeway).
We've been obsessed with Cabo Chips since our honeymoon in Los Cabos San Lucas, Mexico this summer! I'm so happy we can order them through Amazon anytime!
Cabo chips are excellent, buying from Amazon is not.  The bottom 1/3 of every bag was crushed in shipping.

I've yet to find store-bought chips that can truly accent my homemade salsa. The typical variety just tastes store-bought; perhaps it's the added preservatives and such, or the processing, or whatever--they just don't taste like fresh chips and they add too much sweetness to the salsa.Cabo Chips, on the other hand, are much lighter and fresher, and although they have a twist of lime, they don't overpower the salsa. I'm certainly happy that Amazon carries them, because they're might hard to find, even here in the San Fernando Valley.

Great taste with the flavors of soy sauce and lime. Not as greasy as other chips. My bad experience is mishandling my order. All eight 24oz bags were crushed.....two-thirds of the chips were broken into crumbs. It was either the shipping or delivery service. A "negative" five stars for mishandling my order.
Great tortilla chips, love the taste. Would highly recommend. Tastes better than any chip I've had. Very healthy too.

Theses are fantastic, and  agreat deal to boot.  I love the tamari flavor, hard to describe of you've never had a tamari flavored tortilla chip before.  Very suttle, thin, crispy chip.  I've orderd several and cases and all have arrived perfectly.  I haven't been able to find these at all locally...I gambled ordering them for the fisrt time, definitely glad that i did.  Please keep stocking these and the other sizes regularly, Amazon!  Thanks!!!

I love these chips!  We've ordered them twice now from amazon on different occasions, and BOTH shipments arrived stale.  24 bags of stale chips = A LOT of stale chips to eat!  I gave them the benefit of the doubt after the first shipment, but I doubt I'll be giving them a third chance.

I thought these were great for the price. I used a coupon. I can see where alot of people could be turned off as it has a distinctive taste, but I loved them. These blow those regular store brand quaker oats type bars out of the water!

column9: Great bars but who typed the ingredient list??
column10: These bars are obviously for the health-minded.  My favorite are the trail mix but all have been wonderful so far.  They are chewy and satisfying.  I always want to know first thing what is on the ingredients list and I cut and paste this from the Amazon page:"Organic Whole Oats, Almond Mutter, Brown Facestrup, Organicevaporatedcanejijce, Rpjgns, Water, Dried Apples, Oatbran, Walnuts, Ricebr4n Fiber, Almond I-lxlves, Sijnflowerseeds, Sesameseeds, Natural - Vanilla Extract, Natural Flavor, Spices, Natural Plant Gums (Guar Gum, Gum Arabici, Sea Salt."Ummm....?

column9: Once a favorite - now far too sweet
column10: This apple ginger bar was once a favorite - it tasted like an apple & oatmeal cookie with just a bit of zing (from the ginger). Unfortunately this latest batch is excessively and disgustingly sweet. It's lost the punch from the ginger and seems to be super soft with fewer oats and the addition of sweetened apple bits.The bar changed once before, having become smaller (from 61g to 54g). Now it seems to me that the recipe has changed too. From a somewhat nutritional snack to a brown sugar cookie.The Earnest bars (formerly Honest bars) were once a favorite snack item. Not any more. I just made my last purchase.
Very tasty and a nice balance of protein, calories, and sugar.Most of the Clif brands now have way too much sugar for my taste or diet. Earnest hits it right on the spot.

column9: Not as tasty as other Earnest Bars
column10: I've fallen in love with other Earnest Eats Food Bars so I was excited to try out this flavor.  However, I was kind of disappointed - the taste is okay but not for me.  I found it to be too heavy on the cinnamon and while I couldn't really taste the ginger when eating the bar - it definitely left a funny aftertaste.

I thought it was the morning coffee throwing off the flavor of this quick bite to eat, but actually it was the apple ginger flavor that wasn't quite right.  There's too much ginger maybe or some other flavor that overpowers the apple.  I would not recommend them.

Very sweet and hardly a trace of flavor of apples or ginger.  The main flavor coming through is cinnamon.  There are so many natural food snack bars out there that the competition is fierce.  This is not one I will get again.
These bars are awesome! They are so filling and are made with healthy ingredients. I definitely recommend them!

I bought the gum for a habitual chewer. The price alone makes this a great deal in compared to buying a stick a time at a gas station.  The flavor is delicious but does dissipate way too quickly for my taste.  Since this is a problem shared by gum in general it isn't a deal breaker.  Regardless it is a unique taste that is reminiscent of cotton candy.

I ordered this gum for a game (and the prize) of "guess how many" at my son's circus themed birthday party.  The colors of the gumballs are soooo bright and pretty...You will feel like a kid again when you open the box. It's enough gum for a lifetime!!! The gumballs where the star of the party!!!

column4: Lonnie E. Holder "The Review's the Thing"
column10: There are so many different kinds of bubble gum on the market today that I would be clueless as to how to list them all.  On the other hand, with a bubble gum such as Dubble Bubble, who cares?Dubble Bubble has a long and glorious history.  The gum traces its history back to a bubble gum called Blibber-Blubber developed by Frank Fleer in 1906.  That gum was never marketed.  Other people at Fleer's company continued to work on the bubble gum, with the formula finished by 1928.Perhaps the biggest change from the original Dubble Bubble to today's Dubble Bubble are the variations in flavor.  Double Bubble retains the original flavor along with a variety of other flavors, though the flavors are relatively mild.Dubble Bubble has two features that make it one of the superior bubble gums.  First, the gum gets softer as you chew it (more on that in a moment).  Second, the gum makes excellent bubbles.  I like the fact that the gum gets softer as you chew it, though it can be quite hard initially.  There are other brands that begin soft, but seem to get chewier and stiffer the longer you chew it.  I suppose the goal with those brands is to chew the flavor out and then toss the gum.  However, with Dubble Bubble you can chew the gum for a long time and the gum remains soft.I have made bubbles with Double Bubble gum a long time after I started chewing the gum.  Thus, the gum maintains its softness as well as its cohesiveness for making bubbles.  For even larger bubbles you can add a second gumball once the first one has been chewed for a while.  However, I recommend you abstain from a third gumball; the size of the gum becomes cumbersome at that point.In spite of the huge array of bubble gums on the market today, I continue to choose Dubble Bubble Gumballs as one of my favorites.  I suspect that I always will.Enjoy!

This product is a bulk size of about 800 gumballs which are 1 inch in size. These are the size that you find in the commercial gumball machines. My kids love them and they taste pretty good. The flavor doesn't last too long but that is typical for gum balls. We will have gum balls for our machine forever.

I actually bought this product, because I am having a carnival themed wedding. I got these gumballs to use as fillers for my center pieces. I can't wait to put them to use! This is a MUCH better deal than ordering gumballs from any other website, where you only get a pound at time! The box was in great shape too.
Great gum balls.  Came on time, fresh with the typical gumball flavor and flavor lasting ability.  I'll get them again.
Bought a big gumball machine and have 3 boxes of these in so far.  Will probably take two more to fill it.  Tasty treat and the neighbor kids love it.

Product good value and seller. Double Bubble only brand in my opinion. Seller slow on delivery but did finally receive as ordered.
