column9: A great way to wake up
column10: After kicking a caffeine addiction I had nurtured for nearly 40 years, I was ready to find a tea that would not upset my stomach and that would help break through that groggy morning feeling.  Most teas make me a little nauseous or seem to fire up my heartburn not to mention their wake-up power was in caffeine still.  Doing some research I discovered the healthy aspects of yerba mate and decided to give it a try.  It does help to break through and give me a quick awake that lasts much longer than caffeine without the jitters and heartburn.  I do not think I would go so far as to say it is better than coffee at bringing me out of that groggy feeling - but it is certainly a different, milder and calmer kind of alert.  A cup of this in the morning and occasionally in the afternoon is all I generally need to keep me going and never once has heartburn or nausea set in afterwards.There are many other coffee substitutes out there, some do a fair job of matching coffee flavor, this is not a good choice for coffee flavor but it is the one best for the morning wake up.  Very good product.  Do some research because overuse of yerba mate has been linked with some health concerns but I would not worry with just a cup or two a day.

"Smokey" is a good description, I would go with root-like or woody... kinda like thai tea, for anyone who's tried that.  Even so, I thought it was great and conveniently wrapped.  I like the tea bag style and the bag lasts me longer then I originally expected.  Also, this company, which is grass-roots, no pun intended, truly seems to walk the walk when it comes to environmental issues (11th Hour anyone?) - as such, I would whole-heartedly support them, their products and the communities they serve.
Im not a tea lover, but this Tastes better than I thought! I'm looking forward to trying other Yerba mate  flavors....like chocolate! Sounds delicious!!

column10: because the ones at TJ's don't have strings.  These are individually packaged with strings.  TJ's are not separately wrapped and don't have strings.  While that saves on packaging, I find that having a string saves me from having to use a plastic spoon to dip and retrieve the tea bag.
This tea is great... it is all it is advertised to be and taste great too.  I have noticed an increased energy level and feel better after just a week.
IT IS ONE OF THE BEST TEAS I'VE EVER HAD. I WILL CONTINUE TO BUT THIS PRODUCT.

I thought that I could trust Amazon to protect us from vendors who were out to rape and pillage their customer base.  Not so!!!  I just found this identical item at Traders Joe's for $4.99!!!!  I better smoke a cigarette, because I've just been screwed!!!

But we first learned about Mate in Argentina where EVERYbody walks around with the stuff and we tried it after learning of the metabolism boosting benefits it brings. So you not only get good tea but your weight gets a hit also! Double bonus! tip: we drink ours with Stevia and not sugar or dangerous sweetners.

I totally love Yerba Mate.  Too much probably.  But some studies have shown that there is a connection between regular mate use and several types of cancers.  Another study found that mate has high concentrations of molecules associated with smoke that are known carcinogens.  Inference: it's most likely the smoking process that causes mate to be carcinogenic.  I know the smoked version takes better, but the unsmoked version ain't bad at all if you like the mate taste.  So do yourself a favor and find an unsmoked mate (I don't want to advertise --they're easy enough to find).  After a couple of pounds of unsmoked mate, you won't miss it.  But to be more safe, alternate mate with strong green tea like I do.

I was expecting the kind of Yerba Mate that when you drink it you feel like you could kill a polar bear with your "bear" hands (get it?)!  This didn't pack the energizing punch I had with other yerba mate teas, nor some of the other delightful effects.  It was in easy to use tea bags, which was handy dandy.

before trying this know this:your going to want milk and honey to put in it!!!!i'm not trying to air all my dirty laundry, but ive done a lot of drugs in my day and am just now getting clean and healthy and even during my druggie days this stuff got me toastedits like drinking a really good tea that almost gets you stoned - to me it was like a mild opiate high after drinking a few cupsbut yeah, u need milk and honey for best results

column10: I have had mate in South America, the gourds packed full of leaves, but this was my first trial in the US. Guayaki's flavored mate's warrant some consideration if you want the health benefits, but I would stay away from the original unless you really are a mate fan.

I haven't heard from her if she's tried it, but my son says she keeps it in the dorm (as opposed to his apartment) so I guess she wants to have it more often!  That's a good sign, right?  I'd never heard of it until he mentioned that he bought her the "pot" (cooker/cup) for Christmas.  She's a Kinestheology Major, so maybe she's onto something...I might have to try it when we go visit them the next time.
an old woody flavor I used to buy in another brand tea....always liked it.not bad in coffee either.

This tea isn't too bad ... it tastes a little bit like hay.  The stuff I've gotten in the local Espresso Royale puts this tea to shame.  This could be a more traditional/real deal tea but I wouldn't know.  It just tastes a little bit off.

First, these crispy treats are good to eat right out of the bag. To my astonishment (and delight) there is some heat that comes with the jalapeno flavoring. Oftentimes, products are "de-heated" so as not to bother people who don't like a nice heat. But this product is different--and delightful.Second, there are a n umber of uses for this--as crunch for salads, as a topping for casseroles, with macaroni and cheese, and so on. The package suggests a number of different uses.It is also low in bad fats and cholesterol and carbohydrates.Anyhow, a nice addition to the kitchen when one wants a little spiciness and crunch in a dish.

I love jalapenos on everything, but the first time I found this little jewel in the grocery, I knew I had to try them.  LOVE!  I mean this has to be my newest addiction.  If Amazon will carry, I will sign up for auto ship!  Please, please carry this wonderful treat.  Not too salty, not too heavy, just right!  The perfect little addition to salads, green beans, or really any entree.  Seriously that good!

America NEEDS these, they're fantastic! I've put them on burgers, sandwiches, salads, enchilada casseroles, etc.. WHY, Fresh Gourmet, are you depriving us of these? I live in Northeast Ohio and our Giant Eagle (in North Canton)  carried these ever too briefly. At least let Amazon sell them! Thanks, Fresh Gourmet!

I LOVE these and the red pepper ones, but can't find either! PLEASE get them. I do not like croutons, but much prefer these natural jalapeno pepper and red pepper ones. I like to eat them right out of the bag with pumpkin seeds and they are great on salads also!  Thanks!

Having said that...these are the BEST! I eat them like potato chips. They are spicy for people who like that kind of thing but they aren't too spicy. Also, the jalapeno-y flavor wasn't too strong which was something I was concerned about. I just wish they sold them in a big potato chip sized bag. :)

column10: These are amazing and I am starting to worry that I may have a hard time finding them again.  They are flavorful, crispy, and addictive.  I came here to buy these on Amazon and am sad that I can't.  I hope they are available soon.

This cinnamon snack has just the right amount of sweetness....just the right amount of cinnamon also. The six ounce package reseals to ensure freshness and avoid crumbs in the bottom of your purse.  The snacks are quite filling, surprisingly so.  If esthetics is important to you, they do look like a little clump of dirt, but you'll forget that impression when you take a bite.  I used these as a dessert with a glass of milk one night and they hit the spot.

column9: Tasty, healthy and great for dieting!
column10: These are extremely healthy, low calorie, low fat, high fiber and protein, morsels to cary you over between meals! I like these and the sea salt versions and find them the perfect snack to take away the edge between meals and even replace a meal if you are in a hurry. Highly recommended. The price was better than purchasing individual sacks at my local supermarket. I'll encourage my local market to bring their prices down a bit so I can support local shopping, but we also have to look after the old pocketbook sometimes! By the way, everyone in the house likes them, even my teen.

Somersaults Cinnamon Crunch have great flavor and are a tasty snack for anytime. I like that they come in a resealable pack to keep them fresh and crunchy. These would be great for a friend of mine who can't really eat nuts often. I'll definitely buy these in the future!

This is a great size to be able to grab a handful and munch away.  The package is resealable so you don't have to worry about searching for a clip after you get your portion.  The crunch and sweet flavor are a great combination and makes you forget you are eating a healthy snack that your whole family will enjoy.  These are a great alternative to candy or other sweets.

As the package states, it definitely twirled my taste buds. I brought this package into work to share the cinnamon treat with my co-workers and it was a true hit! The sunflower seeds enhance the flavor and the nutrition! I was happy to find that a serving includes 14 bites! Yum! ;) A definite MUST-try snack!

I shared this snack with my friends. We all love the sunflower seed combined with cinnamon taste and the crunchiness of this snack. we also agreed that it satisfies sweets cravings without getting too much calories.

These snacks remind me of cinnamon cereal and I want to eat them for breakfast.The cinnamon flavor is very good but not at all overpowering.  It goes well with the nutty flavor of the sunflower seeds.I love how portable these are--I am thinking breakfast-to-go!

Having already tried the cocoa somersaults, I thought it couldn't get any better for a healthy snack.  I was surprised to learn I liked these even better, so did my 4 year old.  Hard to believe considering I didn't expect to like any of them.  I'm not typically a 'healthy snack' kind of person and, in looking at the ingredients, I fully expected to dislike these snacks. Impressive - and you get the added benefit of feeling good about your snacking!  Can't wait to try the sea salt somersaults!

This is by far my favorite blend, bold enough to get you started in the morning, but light enough that it doesn't punch you in the face (I drink my coffee black).  It's a little more expensive than your normal brands, but I'd say it's worth it every single day.

column9: One of the best, but now pricing itself out of the market
column10: After trying many different K-cups looking for a delicious bold cup of coffee I found this brand. When first purchasing this (and others) I was paying roughly $0.43 per cup. Now it's up to $0.92 per cup.Keurig's marketing strategy worked.....create interest with a new and unique product.....and a good product at that.It's sad that now I and many people that I know are saying, "I'm going back to my drip coffee pot!"Exactly what I am saying.Goodbye Keurig!

I attened the allergy expo locally and was able to sample the product.  Ever since then I have continued buying this product.  Being a gluten free vegan its hard to find good snacks that are healthy and taste good.  This is the perfect snack and low calories so you have no guilt when you have them.  I hope they come out with more flavors in future.

I love this snack because the barbque flavor makes me feel like I'm eating junk food, but I'm not! I can pronounce every ingredient on the list. However there are a few iffy ingredients, which knocked my rating down a star.

column9: What a fantastic snack this is....
column10: I love them.  They are tastey but not loaded with sugar and salt at all.  Authentic tastes of cayene, onion and garlic.  My little nieces and nephews love them.  Why aren't they avaialable everywhere??Thank you Amazon.

Best tasting protien!!!!  Tastes and is as filling as a milkshake!!!!  Low calorie, low fat, with high protien! I don't like the tastes of most proteins (whey...soy...ect..) but CNP dessert protien pudding is like having "dessert" after every workout and even as a meal supplement!

While I agree the taste isn't the greatest, neither is the fat on a body. This is not a product I would recommend switching to if you were simply looking for a jello pudding alternative. You will shock your taste buds! The product is geared for bodybuilders or people used to protein supplements.Another problem is almost as soon as the powder and water merge, it begins to congeal, making it difficult to scrape out of the blender or off the mixer paddles. In other words, you lose a lot of the pudding. However, the powder mix is cheaper than the can contained (premixed) protein puddings I have seen.As far as nutritional value, it is a worthwhile product. (145 cal, 3g fat, 4g carbs, 25g protein) The sodium is a bit high at 550 mg per serving. I usually have one serving if I find my protein is a bit short for the day, so it is not a staple in my diet. I don't think I would be able to eat one every meal or day! I'm leaning more toward obtaining an unflavored protein powder for my low protein days and eat the pudding only once a month or so.

After finding some user reviews on other sites, I was hopeful that this would be a decent dessert.  Unfortunately the sucralose taste is way too strong for me.  I had the aftertaste in mouth for a full day.  After trying a pack, the rest of the box went in the trash.

Sodastream lemonade is the perfect drink for summer, alone or as a mixer for cocktails (this + iced tea vodka and a mint leaf = the perfect summer cookout drink!).  Those expecting traditional lemonade will be confused but if you love the slightly fizzy and tart (not sweet) lemonade you can get in parts of Europe, this is just the thing.I love our Sodastream so much that I got another to keep at my office.  Now I drink plenty of fluids throughout the day without popping $1 each time into a vending machine.  The fact that this is only 35 calories per 8 oz. serving is a giant plus.

column9: snacks you feel about giving your kids
column10: I bought these at the grocery store last week along with the Annie's Cheddar Bunnies.  They're both great.  The whole wheat bunnies are healthy without having that overwhelming "wheaty" taste some people aren't so fond of.  You won't think you're eating a plain goldfish, but my 8, 5, and 1 year old gobble them up and THEY are tough customers.  They have 3g of fiber per serving and with being whole wheat I feel like they're good enough to count as part of my toddler's meal.

It is ridiculous that Annie's markets itself as a healthy company for kids and then fills their products with insane amounts of sodium and food additives. Please research all the ingredients before giving these to your children, they are not as healthy as they would have you think.

Whole Wheat Bunnies are so tasty and we eat them non-stop.  Buying one box at a time at our local grocery store just wasn't enough. We eat multiple boxes a week and our store was often out of stock.  Now we buy them a case at a time online

I really love the whole wheat bunnies.  They are light and crispy, and they are stored in a foil bag inside the box so they tend to keep a long time before you open them.  It's a good product.  I'm not too fond of Annie's chocolate graham snacks, but these are a good healthier substitute for products like Goldfish and Cheeze Its.

My three kids love these (infant to 9 years old), but they are also a huge hit with their friends as well.  Even the kids who have been raised on white bread and white flour crackers scarf these up.  I've watched kids choose these over the refined flour, artificially orange goldfish crackers when both were available side by side!

column9: Healthy, tasty, one box treat for kids and adults
column10: My kids aged 4 and 2 love it, my husband who is the pickiest loves it too(took 2 boxes to keep at work). I dont like cheesy crackers but I eat this by the handful. I think we will use up the 12 pack fairly quickly. We are going at the rate of one box a day. It has been a good mid morning snack or on the go-snack for my kids. I am happy to have come across this brand and the snack.It certainly is guilt-free(whole wheat, no added sugar, real cheese)

I'm a 60+ male who never outgrew his love of animal crackers.  Problem was that my favorites contained trans fat that I (nor anyone else, for that matter) don't need.  I found these, and they are a great alternative - sort of a grown-up's animal cracker.  One 12 box case is a three month supply, and the price is well under what I find them for in the supermarket, on those rare occasions when I can find them.  If they ever get the salt down, I'll give them 5 stars.

It's not always easy finding fast and healthy snack foods but this certainly fits the bill. I personally don't find them very tasty, but if I had nothing else I would eat them. I prefer the cheddar bunnies.

column9: beware of carrageenan in this product
column10: I'm wondering about the carrageenan in this product. Scientific research indicates carrageenan may be risky. For example drweil.com states: "Carrageenan is a common food additive that comes from red seaweed also known as Irish Moss or Chondrus Crispus. Carrageen has long been used as a thickener and emulsifier in ice cream, yogurt, cottage cheese and other processed food products, including soy milk."Dr Weil cites research indicating that "a study published in October 2001 suggest that carrageenan may not be as safe as once thought. Findings from animal studies and a review of the scientific literature showed that degraded forms of carrageenan can cause ulcerations and cancers of the gastrointestinal tract...Dr. Tobacman thinks that undegraded carrageenan - the kind most widely used as a food additive - might also be associated with malignancies and other stomach problems. She suggests that such factors as bacterial action, stomach acid and food preparation may transform undegraded carrageenan into the more dangerous degraded type.

Information about the availability of your product was given to me.  Hooray! column9: Only gum on the planet I could find w/o aspartame - YAY
column10: So this gum is wonderful because it doesn't have aspartame (which = headaches for migraine sufferers). But as far as comparing to other gums, don't chew it unless you have to, like I do. :-)  The taste lasts for about 10 seconds (literally) and the gum tends to stick to your teeth.But to me the health benefits of a gum w/o aspartame (or sugar, as in the case of the sugar-free glee gum) is far beyond the minor disadvantages of the quality of the gum. I particularly chew it for aiding digestion after meals and to quench my need to snack.Also, I recommend chewing two pieces at once. The pieces are the size of Chiclets, so two at a time is really best.

I was happy to find there are natural chewing gum out there and just bought 12-packs of these.  The ingredients say Titanium Dioxide is also used.  Titanium Dioxide is one of the top 50 chemicals produced worldwide!  Google it and you find that it is "a white, opaque and naturally-occurring mineral found in two main forms: rutile and anatase. Both forms contain pure titanium dioxide that is bound to impurities. Titanium dioxide is chemically processed to remove these impurities, leaving the pure, white pigment available for use."  Titanium Dioxide, especially in ultrafine form, could be carcinogen or disease causing, and we currently still have limited knowledge about its health effects, but does that means we should take the risk?  If Glee Gum added Titanium Dioxide to their gums just because it makes the gums LOOK white and 'pretty', it is a VERY BAD decision.  People choose to buy 'healthier' gum absolutely would not mind how the gums look as long as they are truly natural. I am very disappointed. I really hope Glee Gum removes this chemical from their gum and make truly natural gums.

I am one of those people who has an artificial sugar sensitivity. It drives me nuts knowing that I cannot chew my favorite kinds of gums--primarily because when I chew gum, I'll have about five pieces throughout the day. Apparently, five pieces was enough to start giving me stomach aches and headaches from the aspartame and sucralose exposure.Thus began my search for a stevia (which I freaking LOVE!!) sweetened gum. When I saw Glee Gum, I was excited; not only does the package have a cute design, but I loved what my money was going towards.Unfortunately, my excitement died away upon chewing two pieces of this. In less than a minute, the peppermint flavor faded away and I was stuck chewing on a piece of rubber. Not very appetizing. I've gone through the entire pack (you'd need to chew like 8 pieces to be satisfied), but I will not be purchasing this item again.

In my quest for aspartame-free chewing gum, I decided to try Glee Peppermint gum.  Ho-hum.... it is a tiny bit minty (but not really peppermint) and very sweet.  The sweet and slight mint flavor only last for a minute.  I am okay if the flavor doesn't last too long as long as I have a cool, minty mouth.  There isn't enough mint in this gum.  Additionally, the gum is soft and sticks to my teeth.Nothing objectionable, but nothing remarkable, either.

column9: A loveable upstart of a biscuit
column10: The "Hobnob" is a Johnny-come-lately member of the upper echelons of the British biscuit market. Introduced only in 1984, this young upstart has nevertheless firmly established itself in the hearts (and mouths!) of the British biscuit-buying public, alongside the more traditional classics like the 300-odd-year old "Rich Tea" and the 130-year old "Digestive".  It is sweeter and chewier than many other British biscuits, made from a mix of rolled and jumbo oats, in many ways presenting itself as something of a hybrid between a digestive biscuit and a flapjack. It may seem very dry to anyone brought up with cookies (rather than biscuits) and -- like most British biscuits -- "Hobnobs" are best eaten with a cup of tea.  Needless to say, they make excellent dunking biscuits (although being quite flaky, they have a rather messy tendency to shed oat crumbs into the drink)."Hobnobs" are decidedly more addictive than traditional British biscuits (no doubt due to their sweetness) and there is nothing truer than McVitie's original advertising line for this product: "one nibble and you're nobbled". A multipack may therefore be worth considering, unless, of course, you're dieting, in which case you would do well to avoid them entirely!

Having eaten these first in Spain, I leapt at the chance to buy them here.  Full flavored, not overly sweet, they have a rich full grain taste and very satisfying texture. This is a cookie one must chew and savor.  They're a regular for me now.  Also great dunked in tea or coffee.

column9: Pu'erh Tuo Cha From Teas Etc
column10: Length:: 4:34 Mins

This was my first experience with Pu-erh Tea, also known as the "champagne of teas." It was fairly easy to steep and produced a dark liquid, even darker than my longest brewed Ceylon tea. I found that steeping for 3 minutes allowed me to get 3 to 4 pots (about 18 oz per pot) of full flavored Pu-erh. It has an excellent earthy taste with a scent that is reminiscent of oak wood and something sweet. I have read some books about tea and watched a couple documentaries that focus on what makes good tea. Some of that literature discusses what characterizes quality Pu-erh tea and this product seems to fit the bill. It's now definitely among my favorite teas, a list that includes Darjeeling and Oolong. The only difficulty I had was breaking apart the cake, which is very hard and held together extremely firmly. I ended up sawing off pieces with a serrated knife - once I got some pieces broken off, some of it would break away and crumble more easily by hand. I expect this cake hardness is common to all Pu-erh teas since the fermentation and cake drying process is the standard for this type of tea.

I've looked around a lot for a decent introduction to this style of tea. Teas Etc's video about how to brew it and flavor description was encouraging and helpful. I felt like I knew what to expect taking that first sip, and it was perfect. Light, mellow, smooth and woody. This is a great tea and now one of my favorites. One 3g tou-cha is perfect for my 32oz teapot. So the entire 3oz bag will last me approximately 28 pots of tea. I am very happy.

column9: Unhealthy Ingredients Missing In Product Description
column10: Because of the unhealthy ingredients in this product I would have rated this a ZERO, but that wasn't an option.I bought this product thinking it would be of the same caliber as Mariani cherries, which contains "dried cherries and sugar."  I'm not a fan of white sugar, nor do I buy or use it in my home, but at least it's the only other ingredient.After I received my delivery I read the ingredients for this product- "Mariani Berries 'N Cherries, 6-Ounce Units (Pack of 12)", as I have done with everthing food item have purchased over the past 25+ years, and I found the following quite disturbing!In addition to the fruit there are the following ingredients:  1)"Sugar" (who knows what kind. I can only assume it's refinded white sugar, but it's not as bad as the following 3), 2) "High Fructose Corn Syrup" (Nasty stuff this is!), 3) "Corn Syrup" (More nasty stuff and also useless), and 4) "Sucrose" (also known as "Splenda" with the Blueberries, and linked to health problems more than the previous 3 ingredients).ALL 4 of these are unhealthy and should be baned from all foods!I was looking for something natural and healthy. There's 'nothing' natural and healthy about white "Sugar", "High Fructose Corn Syrup", "Corn Syrup", and especially "Sucrose" (better know as "Splenda")There is quite a bit of information available that proves these 4 ingredients are unhealthy.  Search each one, or search "artificial sweeteners", and you will be surprised at the negative effects these have on the health and well being of both humans and animals, despite what the manufacturers claim.If 'all' of the ingredients had been listed in the Amazon product derscription I would NEVER have bought this product!I will NEVER by this product again, nor will I ever buy Mariani "Wild Blueberries" again!  They contain the same 4 NASTY ingredients as the "Berries 'N Cherries" product does!  And they taste awful!  NOTHING like real wild blueberries!Mariani:  You should have left nature alone, not tampered with the taste of fresh fruit, and only added some sunflower oil or Vitamin E.P.S.  I wonder if "High Fructose Corn Syrup", "Corn Syrup", and "Sucrose" are Kosher?
These were the most moist, delicious and flavorful brownies I've ever tasted.Only negative was there is no information on the nutritional values (fat, calories) of the brownies.

column9: Made in the US version, not the same recipe as Imported from Austrailia version
column10: I thought, wow, bulk Lucky Country Red Licorice, sweet, but alas no, it is a mass produced Americanized version from Lucky Country's new US manufacturing plant.  The recipe is completely different from the Lucky Country Red Licorice (same brand, same name) that is Imported from Australia.  The original recipe has more real licorice despite being a red licorice, and is much softer.  The Made in US version is your typical chewy waxy candy licorice with barely a hint of licorice, just pure sweet.  Shame on Lucky Country for taking a high end sophisticated product and watering it down like every licorice sold in every drug store in the US.  I'm heading back to Target or Trader Joe's for the real thing.

column9: FIVE stars for this as iced latte; TWO stars as a cup of hot joe
column10: I tried VIA when it first came out. I tried it the traditional route--as a hot cup o' java. I did not like it. Not this roast and not the Columbian (which was so weak, why bother).So, it's hot. It's summer. I normally hit Starbucks after the gym for my fave iced sugar free vanilla latte. I saw the ad for the iced coffee VIA, but it has sugar. I don't want sugar. So, it hit me, why not try making iced coffee from the regular VIA. (duh, should have thought of that sooner). I bought a 3-packer (like this one shown in image).It was amazing. 2% milk (about a cup), ice, Starbucks sugar free vanilla syrup (I buy it at my local Starbucks), in a blender bottle and shake, shake, shake. It comes out frothy and delicious. FOr me, I like it BETTER than my habitual 2 to 3x a week fix of it at the store. Because you add the VIA to the milk and the milk is cold and the instant coffee is not hot (like espresso), there is NO DILUTION. It makes for a much more flavorful, less watery, iced latte. OH MY GOSH SOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO good.Now, my problem is not having three lattes a day, instead of three a week. Seriously. I'm a junkie now. (And I have coffee everyday, but my homebrew is so much better than Starbuck's that I don't get hot coffee there, I just used to like the convenience--still do--of grabbing a fast latte after exercising. I have a great coffee set-up at home with Paradise Roasters and Terroir gourmet single origins and a Technivorm and a Barratza burr grinder and filtered water pitcher, so really, now that I can make a fast latte at home and take it with me to the Pilates studio and put in the fridge there until I'm done, I may not be visiting the Starbucks as much, except to get my fave protein plate now and then and stock up on VIA.)The product is crazy overpriced. What...more than five bucks for what's 3 servings? How sick is that? Buy it at the store unless the price is dropped. That's crazy.But, nummy latte.So, if iced lattes are you vice of choice, might wanna consider this. And if you don't want sugar, skip the one they're pushing now in the blue packaging and buy the unsweetened.And I just slurped one after dinner (latte that is). Addictive. (Er, literally, I guess.) But at least I'm getting my calcium. :DThis price is much better than the other one I reviewed on Amazon (by another supplier). But I still think it's overpriced. Once you pour out all those servings, it's just a few teaspoons of instant coffee. Amazon would move tons of this if they priced it more reasonably.
This is the best instant coffee that I have ever tasted. The price is a bit steep at just a little less that $1 a cup but for anyone who cares about taste, it's worth it.

I bought this to try for camping since I normally do Starbucks drip coffee at home but wasn't sure what access I'd have to coffee and didn't want to drive to a town to get it.  It was great!  Nothing like other instant coffees.  I saved my extra packets after my trip and have used them when I ran out of ground coffee at home for my "backup" plan.  It's expensive for instant but so much better than driving in to a coffee shop on a Sunday morning when I'm out!  For camping/travel it can't be beat.  We are the type who road trips with a camp stove, tent, cooler etc and stop where we are ready to stop, hotel or campground or what we may find.  Heat up some water in a hotel microwave or over a camp stove, it doesn't matter with this stuff.  Love it!

I've recently switched to drinking instant coffee due to time constraints and other reasons I won't get into on here. Let's just say I've drank hundreds of cups of instant over the last few months. Before drinking instant, I drank tea almost exclusively. Aside from being a former tea addict, I've had an appreciation of well brewed coffee in the past. My favorite coffee is Melitta's Sun & Moon organic. It's simply the best coffee I've ever had with perfect balance of rich taste and complexity. Formerly, when living in San Francisco, I really had no reason to ever go into Starbucks because there was always a Peet's near by, or a local coffee house. So I think I know a good cup of coffee.Alright, now I'll get onto the instant coffees I've tried. I've drank Folgers instant, which has an awful chemical taste but it's tolerable for instant, I've drank Fred Meyer's organic select, which is actually quite good and doesn't have much of a nauseating aftertaste. I've had nescafe, which also has the awful instant chemical aftertaste. How does Starbucks VIA compare to these brands? It has the same nauseating checmical aftertaste of Folgers and Nescafe.Starbucks VIA can be described as having sweet acrid bloom when it first hits your mouth that turns into chemical sweetness nauseating finish that makes you want to pour the whole thing out. There's no denying this is an instant. It's also a mediocre instant compared to generic organic select I've tried (which surprises me, honestly). I have no idea why someone would pay a premium for this, except they're very gullible and easily manipulated through brand loyalty and corporate marketing. Strange to me people would spend so much on an instant that comes in very environmentally unconscious packaging, costs almost 10x as much as any other instant, and tastes mediocre and only review it highly because it has Starbucks familiarity to naive and gullible consumers.Next to try is Jacobs Krunung instant coffee, and I'm hoping for better results. Which shouldn't be too hard considering Starbucks VIA is one of the worst instants I've tried so far.Thanks for taking the time to read my review and I strongly urge you to try purchasing Organic instant or perhaps Jacobs Krunung instead.

column9: comparable to most any home brew
column10: I am a plebeian as far as home-brewed coffee is concerned. My first coffeemaker deposited itself at the kitchen counter less than 12 months ago, after 30+ years of ground bean indifference. And it's a mini Mr. Coffee, to boot. So, I do not consider my coffee buds in any way honed or refined by home schooling. However, I do indulge in professionally prepared coffee at the many excellent outlets NYC provides and must say that the Starbucks instant comes close to a cup of coffee sold by a local Java parlor. The little packet is also a whole lot more potent than a cup of average Joe at the local deli -- I'd love to see what the actual caffeine content of the single portion is. Having said that, I can hardly justify the price of this new instant variant. The best deals on these are generally offered by Starbucks site itself and god forbid, one decides to check out prices at the local Target -- it's actually more expensive to buy Starbucks instant there than anywhere else!

This last summer we had an extended trip from Missouri, across Kansas, and then to Denver. As a Seattle area native, I'm used to great coffee on practically every corner and daily lattes are my favorite splurge. (Hey, I also give 10% of my income to good causes, so I'm not TOTALLY decadent.)I'm sure someone on here can tell me they exist in the midwest, but I didn't find a place for over a week with a decent cup of coffee, and while I know on a scale with world peace that isn't a tragedy, I LOVE coffee.From the freeway as we came into the Denver area, I spotted a Starbuck's sign and begged that we leave the freeway and find it. When I told the barista at Starbuck's about no good coffee for a week, she introduced me to Via packets I could carry in my luggage or even purse.I was totally sceptical that instant coffee would be drinkable, and then completely won over when I tried it. I don't know how Starbuck's managed it, but Via smells good, tastes good, and is incredibly convenient and easy to use. It goes with me everywhere I travel now.On mornings when I don't head for my neighborhood latte stand, I add Via straight to hot milk and get a very (relatively) inexpensive treat. I seem to be doing this more and more, and saving a lot of money doing this. If you thought instant couldn't be good, suggest you try Via.Added: I travel quite a bit -- both nationally and internationally -- and one of the first things to go in my suitcase when I pack are VIA packets. They are tiny, and guarantee I'll have decent coffee wherever I go, at a very minimal price per cup.

I'm not much of a coffee drinker but I like the taste of Starbucks coffee. I never have the time to stop by their shops and wait in line with all the cool and hip people, so this comes handy. I bought some DaVinci syrup to go with it and it makes it taste almost as good as the real thing.

A friend recommended Starbuck Via coffee, and now I can never go back to Maxwellhouse coffee singles again. I can now have a rich, delicious cup of coffee at work even without a coffee maker.  This coffee tastes just as good (to me) as brewed coffee, but is so much more accessible and and energy-efficient than running a coffee maker for just one person, since I work with a bunch of non-coffee drinkers.Ran out the other day and pulled out one of my old coffee singles and it tasted horrible -- can't believe I used to drink that stuff.  Highly recommended if you can't get to a Starbucks or a decent coffee brewing apparatus.

column9: Great coffee.  Better than Pikes.  Save the trip to the store.
column10: Rich tasting.In the afternoon my Starbucks Store only service Pikes.I can have a richer coffee from home.
It wasn't the best stuff I ever had, but it was worth buying to take overseas with me where all they had was nasty Nescafe.

I love coffee. I love it's taste, smell, texture - I love it all. What I love most about coffee now is how easy it is to make. There is literally nothing more simple than VIA. You simply heat water and pour. Up to this point, I was going to Starbucks everyday for my morning cup of joe. Well, not anymore. In fact, I love VIA so much that I no longer enjoy the taste of Starbucks morning brew. My favorite type of coffee has always been french pressed but it takes time. But then VIA came out and literally rocked my world. The best part is I can have great coffee anytime. When I travel or visit friends or family, I don't have to worry about whether or not they have a coffee machine or lug my french press with me.Also, for those of you who don't like the taste of Starbucks, no worries. My mother detests Starbucks and I asked her if she'd like a cup of coffee without telling her what it was. I made her cup of VIA and drank with her. She looked at me and said, "This is really good. Can I have another?"I know it may seem expensive to buy, roughly 83 cents a cup, but I found that I don't drink more than one cup and I used to drink around 24-30 oz every day. In truth, it's cut down on coffee consumption, not increased it.Also, you can vary the strength depending on how much water you add. I like mine strong, the way it was intended, so I'm adamant about only pouring 8 oz. of water into a mug. Actually, I bought the VIA mug too because it just made life easier.So, don't question your decision anymore. Buy it and love it.

column9: Not bad, not bad at all
column10: For an instant coffee, it's good. For a coffee that is supposed to compare to brewed, it's not living up to that claim. But, I do enjoy it and will buy it again. it is hard to believe the instant coffee can have the same taste as brewed one.

I drink 2-4 cups of coffee spread out over the first 8 eight hours of the day. I start with a travel mug on the trip to work, an occasional mid-morning refresher and a cup of coffee after lunch. My early morning coffee is almost always half-caff drip coffee and my lunch coffee is almost always instant. I drink coffee black with no sweetener.I like the convenience of instant coffee because it allows me to indulge in one of my favorite brews at odd times in the day. It is simple to make and there is very little waste or mess. If no one else drinking coffee then I can still have a nice hot cup with very little bother.How does the Starbuck's instant stand up for me? I like the no-mess packaging and the flavor is excellent - it would be hard to distinguish this from drip coffee. The quality is everything Starbuck's has advertised.What do I dislike? The only thing I don't like is the cost. I think it's way too expensive.Would I buy this on a regular basis? Probably not. For the price of an instant cup of coffee I could make a whole pot of coffee and thow out the extra.Would I buy this again? Absolutely. It really was very good.

column9: Hate to admit that I like this coffee
column10: I hate to admit when I'm wrong, but I was wrong. I received a box of these in a coffee raffle basket, and I immediately stuck them in the back of the pantry, with no intent on using them. I prejudged it because:- I hate instant coffee- Starbucks coffee is good, but I prefer to support local coffee houses whenever possible, rather than the "McDonaldization" of coffee that Starbucks is after. So, I'm one of those superficial "Friends don't let friends drink Starbucks" pseudo-snobs. Nothing against the product quality. Just against the idea and presenation (I still say "small," "medium," or "large" whenever I go there. Sometimes they're the only game in town. Can't bring myself to use the Startalk names)Today, I tried one because I was too tired to grind and drip. Surprisingly, this stuff tastes pretty good for instant coffee. Naturally, not as good as fresh ground, but still pretty good. After reading up on it, I suppose the difference is between the microgrind and the traditional freeze-drying.So, yes, I'd drink this coffee again. But at the price, I'm not likely to buy it often. Or ever. Trader Joe's has a similar type of instant coffee for much less. Maybe for camping trips, but I'll try others before buying the Starbucks brand.Five stars for the product quality, as far as instant coffee goes. Lose a star because of the high price, which is probably due to the brand than anything else. Good product overall.

column9: I expected to like it... instead, "yucky" and "owie"

column4: Bill Your 'Free Form FM Print DJ "bill nicholas"

It is heavenly, but he lives far away now and I don't get it anymore.  So, when I saw this VIA and that is was not processed like an 'instant' coffee, but the real beans ground into a fine powder I thought of the Armenian coffee.  Well, I was comparing apples and oranges.  VIA, however they say they process it, tastes instant coffee and that's not a good thing.  It is convenient, but so is every other instant coffee.  It's a decent substitute when I'm too lazy to grind and brew, but so are the other instant coffees.  Basically, it's okay, nothing out of the ordinary.

column9: Can't believe people actually buy this stuff...
column10: This is such a scam! All they do is grind up coffee beans extra small so you don't notice you're drinking grounds! Maybe it tastes ok if you swallow it down right away, but let it sit for a while and tell me you don't notice that nice burned bitter flavor like you left the french press sit too long. Let alone the acid stomach ache. Strong does not equal bitter. This isn't "instant coffee". If you're stuck on drinking grounds, just go to the store, grind up some beans on the finest setting, and put a spoonful in your cup. Just don't drink the last .5 inch. Or you could buy some of those hand-fillable tea bags, fill them with medium or coarse grind, and steep for 30 sec. They decompose and are near free. These little packets (just like everything Starbucks) are a huge waste of packaging and money.

I have a large Golden Retriever who loves to chew.  Rawhide chews are great for dogs because it takes quite a lot of chewing to finish them.  But they can also be dangerous because the rawhide gets soft and slippery.  If the dog bites off a large chunk it can get caught in the throat and is almost impossible to retrieve.  The directions always say to monitor the dog while they are chewing rawhide.  Another thing to consider when choosing a rawhide treat is the calories.  Dogs eat rawhide and too much of it will pile on the pounds.  Dingo makes the best rawhide toys, and they come in a variety of sizes and shapes.  The larger ones, particularly the ones shaped in a knot, are dangerous for my dog because the pieces she breaks off are too large and sometimes get caught in her throat.  But these sticks are perfect.  After a couple of really serious bites the red flavor strip in the center starts to fall out and that occupies her for quite a while.  When that's gone she returns to the rawhide.  They are large enough to keep her happy but small enough so that she can have a couple of these each week without compromising her diet.  I think Dingo may rate them for smaller dogs, but they work well for my Golden.  The only problem is availability.  My local pet stores have stopped carrying this size, for some reason, so I had to buy through Amazon.

column9: tastes good but could have wheat in it
column10: I ate these pretzels for years and loved them and YES they are a great value.  I am wheat sensitive so spelt products are what I use for a substitute.  A law was passed a few years ago that requires companies to label their spelt products in the ingredients section as:  Spelt flour (wheat flour).  (I'm not going to get into why they do this here).  BUT this allows the companies to cut the spelt flour with 50% or less wheat flour and still call it spelt.  This was a nightmare for me, and after attempting to contact Vitaspelt to ask if they did cut the product with wheat flour, they never answered me so I don't eat their product for fear it will make me sick.  If you aren't wheat sensitive it's a great product, if you are BEWARE.  There is another great alternative, Newmans Spelt pretzels.  They do not have the wheat label on them and I switched to eating those years ago...very tasty!

very nice subtle flavor came packaged well none leaked I thought it would be a stronger flavor but it was nice. The color is not as vivid as it looks in the pictures.

I love the Tassimo coffeemaker which also makes tea and hot chocolate.  I love the Twinings Chai Tea Latte and drink a cup or two every evening.  I love getting it from Amazon every month.  It seems to come at the right time.  It's so convenient that Amazon has so much of what I need or want.  I also get books, CD's, purses and other things.  The prices are great too.  It saves me time and gas for the car to be able to shop at home.

This is by far my favorite t-disc.  The flavor of the Chai Tea is wonderful.  I'll often run the tea just a bit longer to get a stronger taste.  I'm sure I'll go back to it over and over again in the future.

i love this company we are never without coffee and tea from this company,  great service fast and reliable.

I love this tea. I have ordered it a lot of this tea. I am not to sure about getting the wrong product though. column10: York peppermint patties, stand aside - this is the real thing.  And you can once again purchase the British chocolate maker Bendick's wonderful product in the US of A. Made from just a few choice ingredients and pure as the driven snow, this is real mint fondant encased in bittersweet chocolate. Worth every penny! These are the official mints of Queen Elizabeth herself. You'll never go back to ordinary mint patties! Enjoy.

The Brits have it down when it comes to candy making.  These peppermint patties are unlike any others you've had.  The center is firm, not gooey with an intense peppermint flavor.  Good dark chocolate encases!  Sublime.

column9: Great mints.  The power is worth the price!
column10: Bendicks bittermints are delicious, and the combination of chocolate and mint is amazing.  Highly recommended!  Also, anyone who has been to the UK will appreciate having a little taste of England.

These are simply the best mints made.  I buy them when I'm in Scotland, and often have my daughter send them to me from Edinburgh.  I am so pleased to be able to purchase them through Amazon.  Please continue to have tem available.
One of the strongest mint flavours in a candy out there, contrasts nicely with the chocolate not too much sugar. All together- delish!!!

These delicious mints were delivered from England to Connecticut in no time, but still, they sent a follow-up message to make sure the mints had arrived. They were concerned about delays due to the "frightful" snowstorms, but they needn't have been.

Bendicks Bitter Mints are an excellent English product. Too bad they don't have an American distibuter. I found out too late. The product is distributed from the UK and "posted" from the UK by the Royal Mail at International Postal rate. The product is priced in the UK in Pounds Sterling, charged to my credit card in US$ and after paying the exchange rate and surcharge on my credit card, the 8 or 10 mints I received cost me nearly a king's ransom. I'll wait until they are available in the USA. Meanwhile I will have to put up with a domestic mint patty.

While I'll have to give credit to Justin for his creative interpretation of this items flavor, I will also have to disagree. I love these crunchy little treats! Have only tried the chipotle tomato flavor as this is whats offered at my base commissary. As good as they are the problem is the price $$ hence only 4 stars. The commissary normally has the lowest prices, but the Amazon 12 pack box with auto reorder option is by far the best option around (plus you can share them with friends). I figure one order every 6mo should do. And yes, gluten free is the way to go for many of us regardless of your present health. I'm in the medical health field and all the studies are leaning this way.

This has got definite crunch if that's what you are looking for.  I would say that if you don't have good strong teeth don't attempt to eat this.  There are tiny little crunchy pieces that can break a filling.  The Tomato Chipotle flavor has a little chipotle warmth but no real heat, I wasn't crazy about the flavors or lack of it.  I did keep chewing away for the definite crunch factor.  If you are looking for a healthier snack I would recommend trying Newmans Own Organic Pretzels, Spelt.

New item for us. We saw the word  Chipotle and had to try them. The pretzel has an unique flavor and a great "crunch" factor. They are Organic, gluten-free and the ingredients is brown rice, flax, quinoa, sesame, amaranth, millet, and chia seeds. These sticks are hollow in the middle and come in different flavors,  chipotle tomato,  sea salt, and curry.  We have only tried the Chipotle tomato. We  liked them a lot but  I can't remember which store I bought them at. I have gone out of my way for a couple of months now to every store I shop at to find these again, that's how much we enjoyed them,  but no luck. It seems the Internet is the only way to purchase the product right now for me. I have never bought a case of any snack but since we thought they were so good it is worth it to us.

Read the ingredients - the three items used to flavor these are sea salt, tomato paste, and chipotle powder.  I would say the tomato is barely noticeable.  If you like smoky chipotle chili powder - this is a deeply enjoyable alternative to most other snacks on the market today.These are a snack I want to keep available at all times.  It is a crunchy (very, very crunchy to be clear), satisfying, noticeably spicy, nutritious alternative to basically any other snack.  I was surprised by the spice (as in spicy spice).  This definitely is not a flavor that has been tamed - and I am grateful for Mary's boldness.

We love these cracker sticks! We're happy that this flavor (and the curry one) are soy free too. They are nice and sturdy like pretzels and have an excellent crunch. This is our favorite flavor-Chipotle Tomato. The flavor is not overpowering, but a nice additon. They are excellent for munching on as they are and dipping in hummus or salsa and other dips too.

The crunch and texture are pleasant, but (wow) the flavor is terrible.  These taste like burnt hair, shaved from a sweaty homeless man on a humid summer day.  While there is a slight hint of heat, which I guess is the chipotle flavor coming through, the inclusion of "tomato" on the packaging is misleading to say the least.  In summary, I would rather eat extremely stale, unseasoned rye chips over these "sticks & twigs."

Every now and then a product will come along that seems so perfectly unsuccessful that I marvel it actually went into production. I love to cook, and as such, in my experimentation, I've had a few misses along with my hits, but there is something valuable to acknowledging the misses. These have a weird bitter (almost burnt) taste which merges most unharmoniously with the (vague) dry, smoky chipotle note. There is no tomato flavor whatsoever. The previous jocular review which cited the flavor of "human hair" is, sadly, not far off. When I dislike a cracker's taste, I'll try to make the best of it by slathering cream cheese on it. These are beyond cream cheese's redemptive powers. They're the first cracker ever that I've thrown in the garbage. Mary, you really have gone crackers by bringing these to market. They totally suck.

This Scotch was a mystery to me; I always thought that Johnnie Walker only came in colors. Turns out, they have this little quiet Scotch called Swing.Swing is a soft, delicate, smooth Scotch. There is a lot of honey flavor along with an incredible smoothness. This Scotch is very easy to drink. There is no smoky flavor at all.So where does it fit in the color scheme of things, someplace close to Gold. The price point is slightly more expensive than Gold. Where Red, Black, Double Black, and Green make a wonderful smoky progression, culminating with Blue, Swing stands almost alone. Its cousin is Gold, but Swing is much more refined and maybe a little bit sweeter.I love this Scotch, and I am a died in the wool smoke fan - Green is one of my favorite every day drinking Scotch. I really dislike Gold, it is too thick and the edges are too sharp and unfinished. Swing hits a very happy medium with those edges smoothed off. There are no really sharp flavors in this Scotch, just a lovely sweet honey flavor.From the Johnnie Walker website, Swing was supposed to be made for sailing ships, to take to the new worlds and sell. The shape of the bottle was supposed to keep it upright in a ship. Frankly, I'm not a big fan of the bottle. The maritime story is nice, but I much prefer Johnnie Walker's square bottle. The sad thing, this looks like a Crown Royal or Pinch bottle, and frankly was the reason I'd never bought it before. Don't judge a book by its cover; the contents are far better than Crown Royal or Pinch.If you like smooth Scotch, this is a winner.

Roll edges of pastry inward to make a large tart.  Bake 30 minutes at 400.  Travels well.

column9: Juice Plus+ Orchard and Garden Blend capsules
column10: There is a lot of controversy surrounding this dietary supplement. The manufacturer claims that their product is the next best thing to eating fruits and vegetables, and that it picks its fruit and veggies at their peak ripeness, and then they use a proprietary process to reduce them to a powder containing much of the original vitamins and nutrients, while maintaining high bio-availability (which means that your body is able to use and take advantage of the nutrients instead of excreting most of it as waste).Many scientific studies, however, claim to disprove, or have produced conflicting results to, many of the manufacturer's claims about the product (see the "Product Research" section on Juice Plus' Wikipedia page: [...]. It doesn't help that the main product distribution process is through the use of multi-level marketing (aka pyramid scheme), and that many reviewers/commenters giving it 5 stars are also re-sellers of this product who always seem to want to send you to their personal website for more information about the product. FYI: I, personally, have not, do not, and do not plan to sell Juice Plus+.Before I knew any of this information, though, our Lamaze coach recommended it as a convenient way for my pregnant wife to make sure that the fetus (and my wife) would get as many vital nutrients as possible. Of course, nothing compares to eating fresh fruits and vegetables, but it's not always possible to eat as many as JuicePlus claims to contain.I have personally used Juice Plus off and on over the past couple years, and I've found that, when I take it regularly for a couple weeks (morning and night, not all 4 capsules at once), most of the tension in my neck and shoulders disappears, which is amazing. So, what's the main catch? At just over $160 for a 4-month supply (per person), it's not exactly a purchase you shrug off. Until I'm able to find something that is as natural, convenient, and doesn't have all kinds of crazy side-effects, though, I'm sticking with Juice Plus.EDIT - 09-13-2012: So I've taken a lot of heat (and have even been personally attacked in the comments) for referencing Wikipedia information from a couple years ago that indicated that JuicePlus distributors worked under a multi-level marketing arrangement, which functions similarly to a pyramid scheme, but is completely legal. The Wikipedia article has since been amended, and now states: "Juice Plus products are marketed by individual distributors who receive sales commissions ranging from 6% (for enrolling five customers in 30 days) to 14% (for enrolling twenty customers in 30 days)."I also made reference to the many studies that tout the benefits of this product, and that many of the claims in these studies are "disputed by consumer watchdog organizations and governmental agencies as misleading". If you read the comments attached to this review (and my other, almost identical, JuicePlus review), you'll see that these studies are defended in the comments here (most likely by JuicePlus distributors) with almost cult-like enthusiasm. However, here is an interesting tidbit from Wikipedia in regards to these myriad "independent" studies. Discuss: "Of the published peer-reviewed studies on Juice Plus products, the majority were funded and/or authored by the manufacturer, Natural Alternatives International (NAI) or the main distributor, NSA. two were funded by individual Juice Plus distributors; and one was conducted independently."My review above praises the product for reducing tension in my neck and shoulders, but I feel as if I'm paying too much for this benefit. Wikipedia backs this up, referencing studies by the University of Berkley, as well as the Center For Science In The Public Interest, stating "it contains too little fruit and vegetable powder to offer significant clinical benefits, its effects can be attributed to the inclusion of added exogenous vitamins and micronutrients, and it is excessively priced relative to its potential benefits."I mentioned that I had not yet been able to find an inexpensive alternative to JuicePlus that offered the same benefits without any negative effects. However, for the past few months, I've discontinued JuicePlus, and have instead tried a product called JuiceFestiv (available through Amazon, Costco, and other retailers), which is similar to JuicePlus in that it contains powdered fruits and veggies in separate capsules. I've determined that JuiceFestiv offers similar benefits to JuicePlus, but at about 1/2 to 1/4 the cost (I've found the best savings when purchased on sale at Costco). That's right, you can get a 2-month supply of JuiceFestiv for $20 compared to a 1-month supply of JuicePlus for $40.I feel that it's important to take care of your body - you only get one - and that carefully researching and trying different natural supplements is a wise investment of your time and money. In this case, MY OPINION (which is backed up by research) is that JuicePlus is overpriced for the benefits it offers. I encourage everyone to try both JuicePlus and JuiceFestiv for themselves; compare the benefits your body receives, and compare the cost per benefit. You may find differences - nobody's physiology is exactly the same - but it's our differences (even of opinion) that make the world go 'round, right? :)

This is an OK drink to have in the fridge, high cute value but I was not overly impressed with the taste. I've never been to this restaurant chain, and perhaps it is better off the tap at these "Dog n Suds" restaurants or something. I doubt I'll buy this brand again unless I happen to have some other business in Indiana and occasion thereby to imbibe at such a franchise.Note this root beer is sweetened with high fructose corn syrup, and contains sodium benzoate as a preservative. There is no  statements as to the herbs and spices in it, and none particularly standing out to me on the palate. It's mainly a strong vanilla taste, it's almost as much like a cream soda to me as a root beer, really. The mouth feel seems somewhat better and smoother than run of the mill brands like Mug or Hires, but I seriously question if it justifies this Amazon price which is over $2 per 12 oz. bottle presently.

Sipping this rootbeer takes me back to when I was in high school in the 90s.  My buddy worked for my Mom's business and after a long days work, we'd walk to the corner store.  At this gas station (that no-longer exists) we stumbled upon this surprisingly excellent root beer that came in a very big glass bottle at that time for $1 that blew all the other "normal" rootbeers away.Now moved far out of the midwest, imagine my surprise when I happen to come upon a couple bottles at a store.You might be able to find fancier rootbeer with more natural ingredients, sure.  But you won't find much that beats this one in flavor.  This root beer is much MUCH smoother than any of the big name brews.  The flavor has a great but not overwhelming complexity with a very subtle initial "bite", a tasty middle with herbal overtones that stack up to high-class brews, but a longer creamier finish than anything else I can recall.  Great straight with an Americana-type meal or with ice cream.

this is THE BEST rootbeer!!  i grew up going to the dog 'n suds rootbeer stand.  every time i go back to visit family i have to go to the dog 'n suds.  YUM!  i wish that more grocery stores could order it because i'd order it.

column9: Ridiculously blatant lies-there are no round puffs of CC
column10: If you are buying this rather than some other bag of cotton candy, because you want CC "balls" like bunny tails for EASTER - DON'T! this is one rectangular chunk of CC, not to mention, there is no fluff about it.  It is a solid, compact piece with pale colors occasional in a bite but mostly it's all white.  Pull it apart in a chunk and you might get a stripe of a color in there somewhere but not always - its often just white.I accepted the title and the picture and bought it figuring I might have to reshape a bit but I would likely get slightly mishapen bunny tails in bright spring colors. None of it is true - including the FLUFFY part.Not FluffyNo spring colors - a little bit of really faded pink and really pale blueNo balls - one thick compact chunkNo cotton tails in any regard, just a complete and utter LIETastes alright if you don't mind it not being fluffy, like cotton candy. I've bought bags of cotton candy before so I'm not naive, they are not as airy as a plastic tub but they are usually cotton candy like.

When I was growing up, every year just after Thanksgiving, our home would be filled with multitudes of boxes from the Swiss Colony. From cheese spreads, meat logs, candies, and most importantly, the petit's fours! I remember Swiss Colony Petit's Fours being much larger, tastier and not dry as stale cake that has been sitting around for months before shipping. I was very disappointed in the flavor and quality of these little cakes and they are not at all the quality I remember growing up. It has been about 14 years since I had anything from the Swiss Colony and I have to say, it will be the last time I order anything from them. There are so many companies out there now that make them bigger, better and fresher (I know, I picked up a box from a famous brand at a local mall kiosk) than what I had when I purchased these. Granted, the price was cheaper...but I guess I got what I paid for. Very disappointed Swiss Colony!

We use the Wellness Core Grain Free Original Formula for our adult dog and I love the product. She has a healthy coat and has been a very healthy dog with no illness. It was automatic when we adopted a new puppy to stick with the same brand but we purchased the puppy formula. Our new pup became very gassy and her stomach was constantly gurgling after each meal. We figured it was just because it was new to her system and we would give it a few weeks. Our vet told us she should be adjusted to it in a couple of weeks as well. She loved the food so there wasn't a problem there but the gas was BAD, constant all day and night long. She could clear a room! After 4 weeks we gave up and started giving her the same formula we give our adult dog. The gas disappeared after the 2nd feeding. Not wanting to waste all the unused puppy food, I thought I'd see if our adult dog would eat it. She liked it but it gave her horrid gas as well and she has never had gas! So back to the original formula for her and about $30 of puppy food to waste.I'm not saying it's a bad product but if you decide to try it and the gas starts...good luck! :) It didn't agree whatsoever with our pup.

I spent HOURS researching dog food.  I had it down to Wolf Pup, Taste of Wild, and this Wellness Core.  WC was my last choice as I researched that some dogs can be allergic to chicken.  I asked the vet, and she said it's true, but she wouldn't say it's common.  She said to go with chicken and save the lamb and bison as alternatives IF she would become allergic.  So then WC became my #1 choice.  It's grain free which I liked.  (With all my research on how grais affect people, I thought this would be wise.) So we picked up the food, picked up our new puppy and started the half and half with the dog food the breeder was giving (as they recommend a slow...one week...transition of the one food into the other food).  After all the research I almost cried as I poured in the "other brand" (knowing how bad all the fillers/corn/garbage was in the other stuff).  So we only went two days with the mixing, then I went to straight WCore.  She did great (7 and half weeks at this point)!  Never had any digestion problems, never had any loose stools.  I am hoping for the miracle food that everyone is claiming that it will produce much better fur and low dander.  We've bathed her 3 times in one week (I know, a bit compulsive) and she has no skin problems.  She is a little over 8 lbs. now, and just moved up to about a cup a day.  So they do eat less than the typical dog food.  The "other brand" was recommending almost 2 cups while WC was right on track with what she was eating at 1 cup/ day (divided into thirds or fourths throughout the day).  So I feel a little better spending the extra money knowing that it's lasting me longer than the typical bag of "other brand" dog food.  Love that the ingredients are healthy!  The only hangup I had was a comment I had read that their dog didn't like it.  I wasn't spending sixty dollars to find out she didn't like it.  I called customer service and she explained I would have a money back guarantee.  So that sealed the deal.  Our lab mix loves it, and we haven't looked back.

My local grocery store charges four times what I pay here-when they have it in stock! I bought several varieties of S&W and Gourmet House rices... all good!Even with shipping cost best value is at Amazon.Particular taste of this Long Grain & Wild improves greatly when you tweak your seasonings.Enjoy!
This product was rich and full in taste. one case will go along way. a little expensive but  just 1 will go a long way... enjoy.

I'm a long time drinker of Jasmine Pearl tea -- when I saw this product listing I thought it was too good to be true (a pound?  at such a low price!).  I was right:  it's *very* low quality tea.  It doesn't have the subtle jasmine flavor that's supposed to be present in this tea -- it's bitter and simply doesn't taste good.  Stick with the Numi brand of Jasmine Pearl ... it's fresh with wonderful flavor, and it's reasonably priced.  You can find it here:  Numi Tea Jasmine Pearls, Numi Tea Jasmine Pearls, Flowering Loose Green Tea, 16-Ounce Bag

I ignored the truism that if something seems too good to be true, it usually is. It is certainly true in this case. It is bitter and of inferior quality. Rather than the tea leaves and blossoms rolled up into pearls, on brewing the tea, the pearls unroll into tea stems rather than tea leaves.

column9: Bag is half pound, Not one pound.  Poor taste
column10: The bag I received contained 8 oz. of tea, not the advertised 16 oz.  This is the reason it now sells for $24 when it used to sell for $48.  The manufacturer's label on the bag said it held one pound, but the bag was not physically large enough to accommodate that much tea.  Amazon gave me the option to accept half of my money back, which I went for.I might also note that the glossy-finish bag appeared to have been well worn.  It looked like it had been reused many times.Regarding the stems that another reviewer mentioned, over the years I have purchased Pearl Jasmine from three other suppliers (Numi, TeaSpring, SeattleTeaCup.com).  All of them looked like this.  With Davidson's product I actually noticed much shorter stems attached to the leaves than with other Jasmine teas, and the leaves were larger.  I also noticed that the pearls are slightly smaller than what I have purchased from other suppliers.The aroma from the open bag was pleasant and similar to what I have experienced with other suppliers' products.  The taste is another matter.  I brewed a cup and found a bitter taste not observed with any of the other brands.  Tea from other suppliers has always offered a pleasant aroma and taste that makes Pearl Jasmine worth the extra cost.  These are sadly lacking in Davidson's product.  I do not recommend it.

This tea is a rip off- is not 16 oz and tastes terrible. I will never purchsae again and feel that Amazon should remove it from it site due to ruining the reputation of Amazon. All other products have been great except this one.
These turnip greens are better than I can make from scratch. Seasoned just right.OUTSTANDING.Serve with your choice of meat. Cornbread completes the perfect meal.

I love any kind of greens --but Sylvia's is packed tight and I especially love to add it to vegetable soup. There is no waste with the can being filled with liquid--just great Turnip Greens. I will keep it on my order.

I am on my second 5 Lb bag of beans from Palouse, and I will keep coming back as long as the price is consistent. The quality of the beans is high: they are delicious, cook well, are packed nicely, and arrived with Amazon Prime shipping-speed (two days). I don't take advantage of the QR code identifier (to see which specific fields the product comes from), but it's a nice touch, and builds my trust in Palouse, the manufacturer.Palouse is now my preferred option for both these garbanzo beans and brown lentils.Also: I have found one pebble going through 7.5 Lbs of beans--this is a very good ratio, and means they properly sift through their beans before packaging them. Worth the price.

Upon receiving the product, I started a batch soaking to get them ready to cook. I soaked the beans overnight and cooked them up in the pressure cooker (after watching Good Eats episode on garbanzos/chickpeas). I am very happy with the quality of the beans. The cooked up tender and tasty. I used some in a soup, added some to a couple of salads and blended the rest up to make hummus. Each time I reflected on how much better I liked them over canned beans (even when cooked unsalted) and the last batch of dried chick peas I bought in the store. The burlap bag is kind of cool and the beans are in a plastic bag inside of that. Out of four cups of measured uncooked beans, I only encountered two beans that did not cook up soft. I will buy these again.

I am ordering these right now, simply because they are grown in the USA.  I am thrilled to buy American and will do so whenever I can.  Thank you for giving me this opportunity, I am sick of foreign foods with questionable safety standards.

These are very good, high quality Garbanzo Beans. I purchased these Garbanzo Beans for making raw hummus with, and I was not disappointed. They are very large and very good. They don't have that "off" taste that some garbanzo beans have. They make the best raw hummus I have ever made. They arrived plastic bag, inside a nice burlap sack. The beans were very clean and I have yet to come across a bad bean.High quality bean, excellent taste. You can't beat the price, and 5 lbs. goes a very long way!I would highly recommend this product.

I was a little nervous about ordering beans online, but am I glad I did! I make a lot of chick pea stews and hummus and I am amazed by the quality, texture and taste of these beans. If you are tired of canned beans, get these from Palouse and cook them up yourself. You will not be disappointed!

column9: I never want to eat canned beans again!
column10: WOW!  I don't think I've ever had a real fresh garbanzo before because I've never tasted one this good.  I've never worked with dry beans before but this was real easy.  Soak over night and boil for an hour.  Couldn't be easier.  And the taste of these is so amazing, I enjoyed eating them plain, in salads, cooked with a little chorizo, possibilities are endless.  Next I'm going to make hummus with them.  And they are on prime!!  (I LOVE prime!)  So I never have to be without them.  I can't believe I waited so long to try these.As far as the company goes, I had an issue with my whole shipment so I contacted them and they responded in minutes. (excellent customer service).  First I had to contact amazon and then them again if it couldn't be solved.(I know, rookie mistake, contact amazon first)  But of course amazon took care of it with out problem (also excellent customer service).  Things are going to happen and it's comforting to know that if I have an issue it gets taken care of so easily.  I will definitely be ordering these garbanzos and other products from this company through amazon again.  I hope you love them as much as I do!

I had been eating, and thoroughly enjoying, Bush brand canned garbanzos as a vegetarian low glycemic index source of protein.  Sometimes my store doesn't have them in stock so I decided to buy dry and cook them myself.  I must say I prefer this way because I have the option of adding salt ot not.  These garbanzos are delicious plain and I often eat them that way.  Especially when I'm just having a couple tablespoons to get me through a hungry patch during the day.  I also add them to my bowls of cooked vegetables, along with olive oil, sea salt, pepper, etc., and nutritional yeast flakes. The garbanzos really round out the meal by adding substance and staying power to the vegetables.  I always make hummus for company and although I haven't made it yet with these garbanzos I have no doubt whatsoever that the hummus will be even better made with fresh beans.  After ordering I received an email from the grower thanking me and providing a link to their website.  To me this was a nice touch and the website is useful.  I found cooking directions there and as someone who can no longer read print I very much appreciate it when I can find directions online.  If you follow their cooking directions you cook one cup of beans and you get 2.5 cups of cooked.  Now I can easily eat 2.5 cups within the three days that they should be used but for calorie control reasons I freeze half of the cooked beans so I can stretch out how many days a batch lasts.  I'm totally happy with these beans and grateful for Amazon as a way to buy quality food I could not otherwise obtain.

column9: Wonderful product- can't wait to get more
column10: The product arrived in less time than expected, in a neat burlap sack, with a QR code showing te exact lot of land this particular bag of beans was harvested from. I cooked up a large batch right away, and they are delicous and perfect. We love that they are a USA grown product. I found my new source for dry staples, and will be back to order more.

column9: Dried Garbanzo Beans from Washington state
column10: Hesitantly I purchased these dried beans but they turned out to be wonderful. Soak over night and they are ready for your recipes in the morning. I made hummus with these beans and some Sesame King Tahini... it was WONDERFUL. I made several batches and added different flavorings. Serve with fresh vegetables and so good for you!

My wife likes hummus and I didn't so I figered I would try to make it myself and if I needed to I could make it with a flaver that I liked. Didn't have to do alot of trying with these as the base. They were fresh, clean and tasted great. I like the burlap bag too.

great garbanzo beans... was very pleased.. I have cooked some and used them in salad as well as making some hummus.. I have also sprouted some .. I will definitely re-order them . I am glad that they are gmo free and grown in the U S A.
I was very impressed with the freshness of these beans.  They sprouted within 24 hours.  I will definitely buy again.

These are absolutely delicious. The flavor, texture, everything is wonderful. There is no similarity between these & those canned things.I just placed a 2nd order because I didn't want to risk running out of them.

I had never used dried beans before so I was a little apprehensive about buying these, but it turns out they are super simple. I soak them over night in water. I then boil them with salt for about 90mins or until they are very soft. I use them to make hummus with. I use about two cups of cooked beans, 2-3tbs of tahini, 1/3 cup of olive oil, 2tbs of fresh lemon juice, and 3tbs of capers. I know that capers may sound weird but they really do add something. Everyone who eats this hummus loves it. There is also a recipe on Dr. OZ website for chickpea popcorn and that was my intention with these but have yet to get around to making it, but its another way to use these beans if you get tired of hummus. They don't taste anything like canned beans. Its truly amazing how different they taste.

Looking for affordable organic food that will stock the pantry.  I tried this company for the first time and are very pleased with them.  The beans are clean and nicely packed, and I feel safe eating them and serving them to the people I love.  Thanks go out to the kind and wonderful farmers who grew them for me.  I appreciate the work very much.  And btw, 5 pounds of beans works out to a lot of garbanzo beans!  They will last us for several months!  Highly recommend.
very fresh garbanzo beans, soaked only for couple hours, boiled for 1 hr - that's how fresh they are. Clean and fresh. Didn't have such a good quality for long time Thanks a lot
