I'm not diabetic and I don't have any issues with processing sugar. I do love gummi bears (especially Haribo). These are soft, not too sweet, less calories (about 1/3 less than sugar sweetened), and flavorful. They are sweetened with sugar alcohol (malitol), so moderation is key. A small handful is all you want to eat at once in order to avoid gas and gastrointestinal distress. These are a great alternative to sugar sweetened candy if you can't eat sugar, are dieting, or are looking to protect your teeth from decay. The sugar alcohol consequences are a good way to limit yourself! Also, if you aren't sure if you are sensitive to sugar alcohols, it's a good idea to try a small bag like this before buying the 5 lb bag!

column9: Essential for Us Louisiana and Texas Foodies
column10: Tabasco is an important staple in Louisiana and Texas pantries.  We like it on scrambled eggs for breakfast.  When we have barbecued pork sandwiches for lunch, we like them extra hot; so we sprinkle on some Tabasco.  Many of our restaurants have bottles of it on the table with the salt and pepper.Tabasco is a natural with collard greens.  In The Collard Patch we use it on all kinds of dishes with collards.  Several of the recipes in Flavored with Love: Mary Lou's Family and Friends Can Cook contain Tabasco.  Here's one we like:Crawfish and Shrimp Bread1 loaf French bread, split lengthwise1 stick butter (¼ pound)6 ounces Philadelphia® Cream Cheese1 pound crawfish tails, cooked1 pound shrimp, cooked and peeled1 pound Colby cheese, shreddedDash of Tabasco®2 splashes Pick a Peppa® sauceDash of crushed red pepperMelt the butter and add the cream cheese, heating and blending until smooth. Add the Tabasco® and Pick a Peppa®.  Add the crawfish tails and shrimp.  Heat approximately 5 minutes: do not let boil.  Spread the mixture over the bread.Heap mounds of shredded cheese over the crawfish.  Lightly sprinkle a dash of crushed red pepper over the mixture.Bake at 375° for about 5 minutes.  Cut into 1-inch wedges.----When we say a dash of Tabasco, we mean as much as we want.  For us Spice Mouths, it is a big old shake of it.I must confess that we enjoy all the flavors of Tabasco, and we grab whichever bottle is handy.----Our idea of entertainment is to go to the Avery Island Tabasco plant south of Lafayette, Louisiana.  We highly recommend this powerful and pure seasoning.

I always stay at least "two ahead" on my inventory of Tabasco sauce. I use a LOT of it as a key ingredient certain dishes, and I cook "from scratch" every day. It has an excellent pepper flavor, (no bad or other dubious "off taste" such as you'll find in some other brands), and Tabasco is somewhat more concentrated than, say, Frank's RedHot, (which is also an excellent product).Tabasco holds up very good in cooking, making its superior and unique flavor and spicy heat known at the end of cooking time in dishes such as chili, huevos rancheros, etc.But there are some specific recipes which call ABSOLUTELY for Tabasco as a seasoning/condiment/garnish, and other pepper sauces, (and I have tried MANY!), simply produce an inferior dish. These specific recipes/dishes include the following:1. Cincinnati Chili (a delicious and hearty "chili over spaghetti" dish, sold at restaurants such as: Gold Star, Skyline, Empress, and/or Dixie chili. You can also make it from scratch at home)2. Bloody Mary cocktails3. chilis rellenos (these are usually made with either Anaheim or Poblano peppers which, in themselves, aren't very spicy hot -- a few drops of Tabasco on top definitely improves the dish)4. Shrimp diablo (grilled, or in a pasta-with-sauce dish)Tabasco is also a great choice for any other recipe which calls for "hot sauce" or "pepper sauce" as an ingredient, although you may wish to use only about 1/3 as much Tabasco as you would any standard pepper sauce.Be aware that many of these discount price hot sauces and pepper sauces often yield some very dubious FLAVORS, so, such "bargains" can compromise an entire recipe! With Tabasco, you'll always be safe on that front.By the way, if you want great (free) recipes for any of the above items which I mentioned, you can go to my public recipe page at Recipezaar. My screen name at that site is "Bone Man" and I have about 300 recipes posted there.My highest recommendation for this fine product!

The sharp vinegar/spicy taste is also a nice addition to homemade salad dressings and a little helps out marinades as well.I'm a wimp when it comes to spicy foods, so I'll add a bit in when I'm cooking, then leave the bottle on the table for the spice addicts to add more to their tastes. In small amounts it adds nice flavor without being too much heat for me.My daughter likes it on ramen, with peanut butter on sandwiches, and wants to work with me on a Tabasco cookie recipe.

An American original, this is the Granddaddy of them all, an essentially unchanged, bestselling product for more than 140 years.  New flavors have been added in recent years:Green Pepper Sauce (milder yet) (600-1200 Scoville Heat Units),Habanero Sauce (hottest) (>7000 Scoville Heat Units),Garlic Pepper Sauce (milder) (1200-2400 Scoville Heat Units),Chipotle Pepper Sauce (mild) (1500-2500 Scoville Heat Units),Sweet & Spicy Pepper Sauce (mildest) (100-600 Scoville Heat Units),but this is Orginal Pepper Sauce (hot) (2500-5000 Scoville Heat Units).Dueling histories of the McIlhenny Company are available: (authorized) Tabasco: An Illustrated History and (unauthorized) McIlhenny's Gold: How a Louisiana Family Built the Tabasco Empire, for those curious about how this most remarkable product and business empire came to be.Note: "A pharmacist named Wilbur Scoville invented the Scoville Scale in 1912 to measure the heat of peppers. A 'Scoville Unit' is actually a measure of capsaicin (the chemical in hot peppers that is responsible for their heat).Scoville's test was a comparative taste test that is considered subjective by today's standards. A more sophisticated method is in use today, but in honor of Wilbur Scoville, the unit of measure is still called the Scoville.The capsaicin level in peppers can vary from plant to plant due to local environmental conditions. This means that a pepper's rating is an average measure.The hottest pepper on record is the Bhut Jolokia with a pungency of over 1 million Scoville Heat Units (1,001,304, to be exact). By contrast, the Bell Pepper comes in at less than 100 Scoville Heat Units."

So I'll be back to let you know how that works out!To get your own tasty Cotton Candy Matcha from Red Leaf Tea - GO HERE NOW!!!![...]In closing - YUM!!!!

Also, I have this vast collection of cotton candy flavoured drink recipes to be made - and remade - matcha style! Pinterest can be very inspiring! The one that is most intriguing in a cotton candy lemonade, where you just pour sweet lemonade over a glass full of cotton candy. Has anyone ever tried matcha lemonade? That is pretty much what this matcha was MADE for, and I wish I had some friends to come have a summer party so I could make some and not get heartburn from drinking the whole pitcher. So, you're invited! Just let me know when you're coming so I can clean!Yay! This Cotton Candy matcha takes me to my happy place! So much yummy cotton candy flavour - and it really blows my mind, because it doesn't just taste generally sweet and sugary - it actually tastes like spun sugar! It's usually made with a pretty cheap ice cream brand, and although it's usually delicious anyways, it doesn't even hold a candle to a high quality ice cream sprinkled with this wonderfully flavoured cotton candy matcha. A cold, sweet treat on a hot day!

Guh, cotton candy. This was the flavor I most looked forward to, and it's the one I ripped into and gleefully made a cup as soon as the package arrived. So much for my nap, I have matcha to drink! I didn't even read the description on the site, it just instantly wound up in my cart. Cotton candy is childhood to me, as well as a good number of college years spent drinking cotton candy cosmos. I can hear my mother in my head right now. "No, you can't get cotton candy, if we're going to pay $5 for a snack, it's going to be something more than just spun sugar!" But rarely she would cave and oh man. Oooooh man. I remember at one company picnic, they had a cotton candy machine, and you could have all the cotton candy you wanted. They even showed you how to make it! It was amazing. It was the ultimate snack of my childhood. Fast forward a few years to the summer between my first and second year of college. I had an apartment with three other girls, two of whom I didn't know, and I was working at Beech Bend Park. Now, if you know where that is, you either a) went to Western Kentucky University or b) are a biker, because it's adjacent to the Beech Bend racetrack and the Beech Bend Campground, where Harley days are held every year. Usually, I got stuck working the teacups (ironic, huh?), but every once in a while, I got to work food services and I got to make the cotton candy. Oh my goodness. Heaven. Hot work, but heaven. A year or two later I went to O'Charley's with a friend and spotted the Cotton Candy Cosmo on the menu. Unable to resist anything cotton candy, I had to try out. Out came a martini glass overflowing with fresh cotton candy. A little shaker contained vodka and when your poured the vodka over the cotton candy, it melted and mixed in so beautifully that you forgot you were drinking way too much alcohol.Now it's my go-to snack when the wife takes me to the movies. It's $3 and it makes my inner kid go bouncing all over the place. This tea does the same thing. It's...it's amazing how much it really does taste like cotton candy, especially when cold. The cooler my cup got, the more it tasted like those little fluffy clouds of heaven. You can still taste the matcha, and it has an odd creaminess to it, but it's just...wow. Wow. It all blends together and it even has that burnt sugar bit at the end of the sip. I'm going to take a cup of this to the Zoo next Tuesday, ride the carousel, and just go back in time to the carnivals and theme parks of my youth.

Bob's Red Mill Gluten Flour is perfect for making seitan.  Your success will depend on the recipe that you use.  An online search for "seitan recipes" will net you several, including videos showing the steps to success.  Here is my Chicken-ish Seitan Patties recipe.Chicken-ish Seitan PattiesDry Ingredients:1 cup gluten flour2 TBS garbanzo bean flour2 TBS nutritional yeast1/4 tsp thyme1/2 tsp rosemary1 tsp sage1/2 tsp marjoram1 tsp onion powderPepper to tasteWet ingredients:2 TBS cashew butter2 Edward & Sons Not-Chick'n Bouillon Cubes1 +/- cup cold waterMix all of the dry ingredients and set aside. I used 4 turns of the pepper mill. I grind the rosemary and thyme with a pestle in a mortar before adding to the dry ingredients.Mix all of the wet ingredients. I put all of the wet ingredients into a personal blender and mixed it up. Add the blended wet ingredients to the dry and mix well. If necessary, add additional water. If the mixture is a bit sloshy at this point, you've added too much water. This can be fixed with the addition of a tiny bit of gluten. I also let the mixture set for a couple of minutes to let the water be absorbed.Measure out some aluminum foil squares approximately 8 inches wide. Measure out a heaping 1/4 cup of the mixture onto the middle of your foil. Pat the mixture down into a patty, then fold the aluminum foil making a tight pouch. Continue until all of the gluten mixture is used up. I believe that I got 6 patties out of the mixture.Place packets into a steamer and steam over boiling water for approximately 35 minutes. Remove from heat. The patties can be used at this point however you wish.Possible changes: Tahini can be used in place of the cashew butter. Obviously any kind of chicken bullion can be used.

column9: An above average, authentic, smooth, organic Oolong Tea.
column10: This "Tao of Tea" Oolong tea is authentic Wuyi Oolong from Wuyishan, China, packaged in Portland, Oregon, and it is organic. Oolong tea leaves are midway between green tea and black tea in terms of processing because Oolong leaves are semi-oxidized, whereas black tea leaves are fully oxidized. The oxidation of the leaves affects the chemical properties as well as the taste of the tea. When brewed according to the directions on the container, this particular Oolong tea turns light amber in color and tastes very smooth and mild with hints of fruit flavor. It does not leave a "grassy" aftertaste the way some other Oolong teas do. Oolong in general does not taste as strong as most black teas. I usually get three infusions from this tea, starting with the original brewing, the third infusion tasting a bit weaker than the first. The flavor is better than some other Oolong tea brands, such as the Oolong variety sold under the Stash label and a few others commonly sold in grocery stores. It is mild, however, and does not have the robustness and richer flavor of "Da Hong Pao" (the most famous of all Wuyi varietals). What makes this Oolong tea stand out is the fact that it is authentic Wuyi tea and organic, in addition to tasting good.

I typically purchase my oolong from a local loose leaf tea/coffee shop, but was snowed in for almost two weeks, while my tea stash dwindled. I decided to purchase The Tao of Tea, Wuyi Oolong tea from Amazon, and am very satisfied with my decision. This oolong tea is smooth and without the bitter aftertaste that many oolong teas (especially cheaper ones) exhibit. For the price, I don't know that you can find a better everyday oolong tea.

This tea is more on the black side than many of the green oolongs.  The leaves are quite dark and full leaves that provide several good infusions.If you like a oolong that is more black tasting than green, this one is worth a try.

It may taste great, but Colavita's "White Balsamic Vinegar" isn't real balsamic vinegar. Neither is their regular. Check the ingredients. Both list first "wine vinegar." Balsamic vinegars are not made with wine vinegars. Real balsamic vinegar, and there is a white balsamic vinegar version, is made from white Trebbiano grapes in the Modena and Emilia-Romagna region of Italy. Regular balsamic vinegar is cooked down 30%-50% and concentrated to produce a dark color and deep, rich flavor. Then it's aged in various wood barrels that are switched-out each year. White balsamic vinegar is cooked at high pressure to prevent caramelization, which gives the vinegar a golden color and gentler flavor. The white balsamic vinegar is then aged for one year; yielding the light color and flavor. I hope you find the real stuff - it's great!

I grew up in a family of tea drinkers; and although I now tend to have a lot of coffee while I'm at work, I still drink almost exclusively tea when I'm at home. I generally prefer loose leaf teas - that way I know I'll get "the real thing," whereas tea bags tend to contain merely the leftovers of a harvest; little crumbs too poor in aromatic and other content to otherwise pass quality control standards.The exception are Bigelow teas: and first and foremost among those their flagship, Ruth Bigelow's original "Constant Comment" with its recipe of black tea, orange grind and holiday spices (primarily cinnamon). Created by Mrs. Bigelow on the basis of an old colonial recipe over half a century ago, the blend soon became so popular among her friends that their "constant comments" of approval prompted Ruth and husband David Bigelow to found their own tea company. Since then, "Constant Comment" has long become a true classic ... and if you love tea, it is indeed the perfect refreshment; whether or not it's Christmas time. (E.g., it also makes for great iced tea in summer; particularly if you add a bit of lemon.)If you're making more than a single cup of tea, and unless you like your tea *very* weak, you may want to rethink the company's measuring directions - based on the the "one bag per cup" ratio, you'll likely need two or more bags for an entire pot (depending on size), even when steeping an extra minute or two. column9: Wonderful tea!  We've brewed and drunk this for over 40 years!
column10: Ruth Bigelow created this tea about 1945.  By about 1960, Constant Comment was sold as bulk tea, in a tea tin, at Jitney Jungle at I-44 & Peoria in Tulsa.  I've still got one of the tins!  My mother used to send me to the store.  She'd brew the bulk tea in a tea caddie and have a glass of iced tea at hand all day long.  I'd come in from playing and drink about half of her glass.  (Half was the most I could get away with without scolding.)  So I grew up drinking this.  (Never learned to like American coffee.)  We've traveled all over and have tried many fine teas, but this is our all-time favorite.  Both Bigelow and Twinnings have many good teas, but nothing is quite as good as Constant Comment!  ;^)Now Constant Comment comes in bags in individual foil pouches.  This has at least two advantages:  the foil preserves freshness and allows one to carry his tea with him to work or school to brew fresh!  The best way to brew Constant Comment is in an Iced Tea Pot.  We have two Iced Tea Pots from about 1998.  Just put two teabags in the holder at the top of the pot, fill with water and turn on.  When the first container of water is done, refill and you'll have two quarts of strong tea from two bags!  When brewed this way, the tea has no bitterness at all, so you don't even need lemon to adjust the bitterness!The best way to sweeten tea is with local honey.  Local honey will also tend to prevent allergic reactions to the local pollen and allieviate any hay fever that you may be experiencing.  But be sure to get at least a quart of honey and put about 1 or 2 teaspoonfuls in a quart of tea!  Enjoy!

column9: Delicious flavor that never goes out of fashion
column10: This aromatic, utterly delicious tea has been on sale in the U.S. for almost 70 years. Nowadays we have endless varieties of tea available, but this one remains one of my all-time favorites.It is so flavorful that I make a whole half gallon of tea with one teabag employing the cold-diffusion method. It works like this: I fill a two-liter glass pitcher with distilled water made with our coutertop distiller. (You can also use tap water put through a carbon filter such as the Brita pitcher.) I remove the paper tag on the tea bag and place it in a stainless steel mesh tea ball. (The tea ball isn't absolutely necessary, but I've learned the hard way that any tea bag can break when tea is stirred briskly, which I always do.) I put the lid on the pitcher and set it in the refrigerator overnight. The next day the tea has completely defused, though there will naturally be more brown color in the bottom portion of the pitcher near the tea ball. To distribute the flavor/coloring evenly, I stir the tea well, and it is ready to serve immediately.If you make ice tea this way, you can sweeten it any way you choose. I personally use NOW stevia, but honey is an old standby that works really well, too.This tea comes in two sizes, 40 teabags per box, as for this product, and also 20 teabags per box. It also comes in a decaffeinated version.
Ecellent flavor full bags only need one per cup and i use a giant cup,Cant Start mt day going with out it.

column9: Add it to your ice tea brew
column10: This is great hot tea, but I use it half and half with regular tea to brew ice tea.  It gives it a whole new flavor.

This is a long term supply of my favorite tea, well packaged and quickly received.  I drink other types of tea too but Constant Comment is by far my daily drink and Amazon gets it to you double quick.

This is gorgeous tea. I didn't start drinking tea till this year and am almost 40. My mom had a sampler pack from Bigelow and this was among them. I love the story behind the name of the tea. I can just see her working in the kitchen like my Grandma used to do with her cinnamon rolls. Getting the recipe just perfect. Well it has stood the test of time. I love this tea. As soon as it started to turn into fall I had to buy a bunch of this stuff. It just smells like fall to me and for that matter Christmas. I usually drink Bigelow's French Vanilla and Caramel Vanilla as the FV was another in the sample pack. My mom made it for me when my beagle passed away this year. It was very comforting. Vanilla tea doesn't sound like it would be good---sounded like the last thing I would want to even try, but when she brought it in I was in love!!! So that i drink all year along with their soft mint in a green box (? tastes like the mint in Wrigleys Doublemint gum-real soft and mild) (they have many peppermints though!). BUT this is just perfect this time of year.

column9: Constant Comment Tea is the BEST!
column10: This is my favorite tea...whether you are having a cup because you just want one or you are fighting off a cold - it is comforting tea to drink.

column9: Love Constant Comment Tea hot or cold
column10: After trying the sugar free Jolly Ranchers I thought I'd check out the prices for Constant Comment Tea. I was down to my last few teabags. I knew Amazon would ship them quickly. I got my order before I needed it. Again, I bought these here at Amazon because this was the best deal I could find. I even saved more on auto-shipment. Cost-wise I saved about 50%. I love to save my hubby money so I can spend some more.

I love this tea - light and refreshing - soothing and energizing. Whenever I have a cup of Constant Comment, it seems it is just what I needed right at that moment. It doesn't compete with anything I'm munching on, but I usually just have the tea by itself.Ahhh... think I'll brew a cup now!
Can you imagine having to pay $5.40 for 20 bags? This is a deal !!

I am a big tea drinker.I have tried many kinds but my all time favorite is Bigelow's Constant Comment Tea.Since I like it so much I was delighted to find that it was cheaper if I ordered it from Amazon.com. Of course you are having to buy more tea but it keeps well so there is no problem!
I love this tea. The chance to buy it in bulk was to good to pass up.

For some reason this is hard to find in stores lately.  I am very thankful for Amazon for stocking it and you can't beat the price.  My mother has drank this for as long as remember and it's still the same wonderful quality.  Taste is subjective of course, but I find this is be a very pleasant spiced tea.
What's to write about this tea?  It is fabulous.  I love being able to buy it in bulk -- it saves time and money.  I like most Bigelow teas, but this one is by far my favorite.

This type of tea has gathered constant complements from early times in America and especially in the variant created by Ruth Bigelow in 1945. It is a fine rich black tea with a spice-mix based on orange zest, cinnamon and cloves. Even in its bag form, it seems like a tea follower's favorite personal blend. It is a rare tea that one can drink hot, icy or even lukewarm -- anytime with anything. Like some have remarked, as with most black teas, it is actually good brewed to a standard ratio of one bag per tea cup [five for a quart] -- and can be added to most other black teas -- so one can extend a supply of "Constant Comment" upon want or need. It is great hot with milk or cream and sugar or honey. When making iced-tea, it is well to add some lemon or lime and sugar or honey to taste, before adding ice -- as this tea seems just a bit sweet due to its spice-mix. It is good with a bit of rum too. "Constant Comment" can hold its own, alone, as well. "Constant Comment" looks good, smells good and tastes good +++
My husband loves this tea.  What a great way to surprise someone special.  Price is great and taste is wonderful.  Bigelow Constant Comment Tea, 40-Count Boxes (Pack of 6)
The aroma is just incredible, the flavor is great also. I'm using it to make iced tea, but I'm sure it's good hot also. Everyone who has tasted it really loves it.
It was a 1st rate. The little pkts are nice to take to work or put in a gift pack.
This is a good deal, and Amazon is responsible for a good deal of the good deals. :)

column9: Great tea, fast delivery right to my door!
column10: Within 1 business day of ordering this item, the tea was delivered to my house! Talk about service!  As always this tea is one of my staples, nothing has changed, so another great purchase experience on Amazon!
The tea came quickly and was packaged well.  It was as expected.  Now I'll have my favorite tea on hand for some time and at a lower price.

column9: Not as good as I hoped it would be.
column10: I just recently tried Stash's "Orange Spice" tea on a trip to Hawaii. I have known of orange spice tea for a long time but it never interested me before. There were some various tea bags available in the lobby of our hotel, so I thought, what the hell, I'll just toss it out if I dont like it. I actually did like it very much to my surprise.Now that im back in the mainland, I wanted to buy some more "orange spice" tea, so I picked up Bigelow Constant Comment. I was dissapointed with the flavor, it is weaker than Stash's, less orange flavor and less spice flavor as well.Now, far as I know, I think Bigelow invented orange spice tea, or were at least the first ones to sell it. But I think they could add more orange and spice to the tea, as well as some more tea in the bag too. Both Stash and Bigelow seem like they are stingy on the amount of tea in their bags, makes for a somewhat weak brew.Anyone try Celestial Seasonings orange spice? more or less flavor than Bigelow?

I'll admit it. I'm a tea snob. Most of the tea sold in American supermarkets is just... junk. Floor sweepings, as my Indian friends would say. I buy almost all of my tea directly from China, and it's always loose leaves, not tea bags. But Constant Comment has a special place in my heart, and I go on binges where it is pretty much all I drink. The aroma is lovely, and the combination of orange rind and cardamom makes for an interesting and flavorful cup of tea. CC is probably floor sweepings, too. But it tastes great and is very comforting. I do love these large boxes of 40 tea bags (4 bags per foil pouch) that Amazon sells, as it is convenient and long-lasting. One note: it does seem to give me a bigger caffeine "jolt" than I would like, so I usually de-caf it by brewing it for one minute, pouring out the water and then brewing for 3 minutes in fresh water. Your mileage may vary regarding the caffeine.
Leonard Cohen fans take note this is the very tea that inspired the line in SUZANNE, "and she brings you tea and oranges that come all the way from China."

This is the second time I have purchased this fruit of the month club for a gift to my Mom.  My Mom looks forward to every month receiving a different fruit.  The fruit is wonderful.  It tastes great and packaged beautifully.  I would purchase Golden State DeLite Fruit Club again and again.

column9: FIVE STARS...EVERY PIECE OF FRUIT...EVERY MONTH !
column10: Given the cost, one might well hesitate before purchasing this assortment of fruit.Similarly, I was struck with post-purchase questioning of the 'did I pay too much?' kind..For the record, this was a great purchase.The fruit arrives on time-once a month...in uninjured...perfect condition....3,000 miles fromthe home base of this operation.(e.g. the strawberries just arrived...individually protected in foam).Not one piece of fruit has been anything other than what you would expect, for the price.No disappointments...just continued raves and thanks from the recipients.The overall impression of the packaging, and the courtesy of the employees withwhom I corresponded was exemplary, but - best of all - the products are of the veryhighest order.

love this parmesan i use a lof of it in my cookingand it has no fillers unlike the supermarket kind and it made by kraft  enjoy
Love this cheese. I use 2-3 of these containers per year. Refrigerate once opened and it will last till the expiration date.

I don't belong to Sam's Club anymore, so this is great fo me:). The price is more then the $19 for sam's club, but this price has free hipping if you pick the correct seller. We use this cheese all of the time in our food.  It is still the best price that I can find for online food orders.

column9: Just try it... you will be glad you did.
column10: During the summer I barbecue every weekend. So, I am always looking for something to spice it up or make the feast better. This Jake's Righteous Rub is a winner. All my guest love the flavor and agree this rub is a winner.

I adopted two very undernurished kittens from the Humane Society, whose on-staff vet said that AvoDerm dry and canned food is the best on the market for cats. When I took the kittens for their vet checkup 6 months later, my own vet also agreed that this is the best food available and was so pleased with the health of the kittens. My older cats have also seen a huge improvement in their coats -- much more silky and shiny, shedding is reduced and their weight is easily maintained on this food. I recommend trying this food if you have finicky cats or they have health problems.My cats absolutely LOVE all the Avoderm Select Cuts (chunky-style) flavors AND all the flavors of this pate-style food. The seafood flavors seem to be the most popular among the cats, but many vets recommend avoiding too much seafood for male cats due to the urine crystals it can cause. I started feeding the beef and chicken exclusively and they eat every last drop.Bottom line: It costs more than your average food, but it's worth every penny (buying it by the case can give you a pretty good discount from most vendors). If you consider that it keeps them healthier, which can save you from expensive vet bills in the long run, then it's worth it. Plus, think of the time you'll save not having to clean up after their shedding! Also, I've noticed that this brand does not result in the runny, smelly poo that some other, cheaper brands do. Try this food out on your cats -- you'll be pleasantly surprised.

column9: even the pickiest eaters love AvoDerm
column10: We have three cats, and they all have VERY different tastes when it comes to food. One of them, my eldest (she's 15), will go through periods where she just turns up her nose at all foods, so it's a bit of a problem to find a food that all three cats will eat, isn't totally bad for them, and doesn't leave a lot of waste as well.AvoDerm is the favorite around here- even my 15 year old prefers it. It's the one food we can count on her to eat. And it's a good quality food- I'm not a feline dermatologist but we've been feeding it to our cats since it hit the market, and they all have lovely, fluffy, shiny coats and we have definitely noticed a big decrease in hairballs (one of our cats has the coat of a Maine Coon, so he's got a LOT of fur and spends a lot of time grooming).Also, the food can stand to sit out for a bit- with multiple cats, not all three of them are asking to eat at the same time, so finding a food that could sit in the bowl for longer than ten minutes without turning into a biscuit is a challenge. Whenever the 15 year old asks for food we tend to give it to her to try and inspire her to eat, so if the bowl she eats from sits out for a little bit and one of the other cats wanders into the kitchen a while after, the food is still fresh and not dark brown and crusty.So the cats like it, they eat a lot of it (even the refrigerated leftovers), it stays "fresh" in the bowl, and it seems to benefit their coats and health. I'm a fan and will continue to buy this food for my cats as they as they continue to benefit from it.

column9: Not very good and may contain non-organic ingredients
column10: I found these cookies to be very dense and difficult to bite through. There are nowhere near enough chocolate chips -- many of the cookies in my bag didn't have a single chip in them.Regarding the "organic" advertising: the ingredient list does not say that the chocolate chips used are organic and they contain soy lecithin. Since products that are not advertised as "100% Organic" and do not carry the "USDA Organic" seal may contain up to 30% non-organic ingredients it is very likely that these cookies contain lecithin from GMO soy because the label does not specify that the soy source used is organic or non-GMO.

My son is away at college and wanted healthy snack choices.  I alway buy Newman's products at home but he couldn't find any within walking distance of his school.  I found Newman's cereal for him and the cookies too.  He loves them and so do his roommates.  Great way to get supplies to a college student !!! So happy Amazon has healthy options that can be mailed to my son.  Thank you Amazon !!!

column9: wonderful cookie;  old-fashioned aroma, just the right size
column10: Recommended. These little cookies are about two bites each.  +Organic ingredients and wonderful old-fashioned cookie smell. So glad the Newman family is making these.  Six packages of 7 ounces each arrived in their own box labeled Newman  family cookie recipe.  Organic food goes farther, I've learned.  So don't be tooconcerned about package size. Having given up eating almost everything at the supermarket,  was especially pleased to find these and think you'll like them, too.

As a previous reviewer mentioned, the chocolate chips are very, very sparse - sometimes there's only one chip in a whole cookie. The cookie itself is pretty bland, and forgettable. On the other hand, Newman's Own Organics Cinnamon Graham Alphabet Cookies and Fig Newmans are great!

column9: Great for when you want to make a single glass of Kool-Aid
column10: I keep these on hand for car trips with the grandkids. You can turn a boring bottle of water into a flavorful Kool-Aid drink by just adding a single packet to it. Just open the bottle, pour in the contents of one packet, then close and shake. Each packet contains both the Kool-Aid mix and the amount of sugar that's needed for a single drink. Perfect size for a typical water bottle. We use reusable watter bottles with them, so we can fill them up with water when ever we need something to drink and then add the Kool-Aid.They taste just like when you mix a regular full sized pitcher of Kool-Aid, just in a single serving size. These single servings work really well for us since we never drink a whole pitcher when me make one, and end up pouring half of it out. These were such a great idea!

I'm happy with this popcorn.  It has a burn to it, but it's not too bad.  The spices hit the back of the mouth and it seems to be a delayed reaction giving you time to really enjoy the flavor first.  When it pops it has a smell almost like cardamom or cinnamon, possibly a slight nutmeg smell - but the taste is smoky and buttery with maybe a hint of sweet, but not much, before the burn begins.One thing to note on the nutritional information they offer on Amazon --  One bag has about 3 servings..  so it's 160 calories and 8 grams of fat per serving - or 480 calories and 24 grams of fat per bag.It seemed to pop well and the corn itself seems to be of good quality and flavor.  The popping instructions say that it takes between 1 and 4 minutes to pop (it took 2 and ½ minutes in my microwave).  It also suggests that you heat a cup of water for one minute before cooking the popcorn and suggests putting the bag on top of something else to raise it off the bottom of the oven prior to popping if you are finding you are having popping issues.  I didn't take either suggestion and the bag popped up well with a minimal number of kernels left over.  You will want to make sure to shake the bag really well before opening to help distribute the spices.Over all it's good popcorn with a nice after-burn.  I didn't give it 5 stars because it's not as good as other popcorn I've had (Orville Redenbacher's Salt and Lime and Salt and Pepper) but I would order it again.

column9: Wonderful Product! Only one on the market I'd use for my little one!
column10: After doing lots of research on the different rice cereals out there, this is one of the few on the market I would give to my little one. Some of the brands, even organic, contain soy or wheat. Both of which I personally don't believe are good for infants, especially when they are first getting use to solids. We have been using this since he was 6 months old (now almost a year). It worked great with breastmilk in the begining and now we alternate between that and purified water, which also works well. I have found if you mix a fruit or veggie purée with it before adding water or milk, it mixes a little bit better without so much clumping. I would highly recommend this product to anyone, along with the entire line of plum organics!

column9: Smells terrible and daughter projectile vomits!
column10: I bought this hoping the pro/prebiotics would help my daughter's tummy. Upon opening there was a distinct chemical smell. The earth's best rice I normally use has no smell whatsoever. But I wrote it off as the add ingredients. Within a half hour of drinking this my daughter shot it all back up. She was not sick. I tried again the following day and same deal. I'm sticking to the less is more approach and going with earth's best organics.

column9: A great start to healthy eating!
column10: I chose Plum Organics Brown Rice Cereal as the very first solid food for my daughter because I felt this was the best choice on the market for my home. I love that it's certified organic and that it also contains pre/probiotics for easier digestion. I mix my daughter's rice with breastmilk and I find it to be fluffy, not gummy or slimy like the other commercial brands. I also like that it tastes good too (I also taste whatever I feed my daughter first). She loves this cereal and she's never had an allergic reaction or digestive problems afterwards. I also want to note that I haven't had an issue with weird smells or having a rancid container like others stated. While I wished the price was a bit more affordable, I have no regrets about feeding my child this infant cereal! I highly recommend parents who are looking for healthy and organic rice cereal to purchase this brand. Your child will be quite happy and it's a great choice to introduce healthy solid foods too!
My 5 month old took to this cereal immediately. I love that it is Brown Rice and Organic. Excellent choice for a first food.

This is a brand we hadn't seen in Alaska before and I was excited to see it on the shelf.  It pairs wonderfully with the Sprout Organics baby food I use. What a difference!  Whereas the other organic rice cereal I used created a lot of gas and tummy aches this cereal did not.  The other thing I appreciate is the the packaging.  Its a bag, and BPA-free and so when it's empty I roll it up and there's next to no trash.  The only thing that would make it better is to have the package be recyclable and come in a larger size.

column9: Good bag, but they don't fit a Bags on Board dispenser
column10: I don't know why I thought these bags would fit in my Bags on Board bone dispenser.  Maybe I was just hoping.Still, a great bag that is truly biodegradable (unlike Bags on Board)

I love the BioBag poo bags -- they're plenty roomy, opaque, soft and flexible.  My only complaint is that they don't have handle ties.  I like to tie my bag and then carry it by the handle until I get to a trash receptacle.  With these, you only have a knot at the top.  Otherwise, they are perfect!

column9: Good product, but sort of expensive
column10: Our family used these bags for a while... it's great to find a non-gmo cornstarch bag that is REALLY biodegradeable, unlike some of the poop bags, which say they are, but really they just break down into a billion tiny scraps of plastic (so they theorize they "degrade" faster than regular plastic. However, this just means more tiny micro-bits of plastic in the landfills and ocean!). Beware what you read in the product descriptions! It should be 100% "compostable".However, seems these bags just keep getting more expensive. Good product, but I want to pay as little as possible to throw out poop! I recently discovered another similar product at about half the cost, which are called Nature Babycare Eco Diaper Disposal bags: http://www.amazon.com/dp/B001EWDPPU/ref=rcxsubs_mys2_product_titleObviously, these are intended for disposable diapers, but work just as well for poop. They are a little thin (a little thinner than the Bio Bags), but they work just fine and I haven't had any problems with them. They are about the same size as the Bio Bags with tie handles. They are white, not black like the Bio Bags, but don't show through, so they are a winner for us. I'm really not too picky about what to throw out poop in as long as it works, it biodegrades, and I don't end up with poop on my hands. I'm happy to find another product that costs less, hope this helps someone else.

While I feel better throwing these away because I know in time the bag and it's refuse will biodegrade in a good manner the bags themselves are on the weak side. You get more than enough in this package but after tearing one off the roll they have a tendency to rip along the seams when I try opening them. There are nights where I have gone through 3 or 4 bags and other times I can go weeks at a time without wasting one. While I appreciate the concept I will be searching for another brand that can withstand my Hulk like strength.
We use these bags every day and we love them. I couldn't sleep at night knowing I just sealed dog "leavings" in plastic for an eternity. I wish they made their large dog bags available in rolls.

We love these bags and use them daily for our 2 large-breed dogs. They are roomy enough to hold both of their waste on the same walk. The bags have pre-cut holes in the top so you can slide one of the bag through a hole and it seals without messing with tying it, which is super helpful with 2 dogs pulling you along for a walk. Can also clip the bag via the hole onto their harness for long walks where there isn't a trash can so you don't have to carry/smell the waste. Best part is it's biodegradable and compostable.

I love these bags.  I try to be as green as I can and these bags help me get one step "closer."  I actually use these bags to scoop the cat litter frome the multiple cat boxes around the house.  They are the perfect size and I love the fact that they come in a roll that allows you to just tear off one at a time.  Some stores do not carry the "rolls" anymore so it was great to find them here at Amazon.  They are also great (perfect size) for picking up dog waste (their original intention I guess).  I have several friends with dogs and I always keep a roll in my car - very convenient to store neatly in the glove box or console.
The bags on a roll are terrific.  They take up less space and work wonderfully.  I especially like being able to use a biodegradable product.

My only gripe is that they don't really fit into the bone shape carrier, so we had to attach a small pouch to the leash to hold these bags.  Other than that, these bags are great.  They separate from the bunch easily and they are easy to open.  They cover the smell well enough and you feel better about using them over the environmentally harmful bags.

Great for picking up doggie poo. Sometimes she has larger piles so I wouldn't mind it they were slightly larger themselves, but overall, great bags. Love that they biodegrade, we use other products of theirs as well, but this was my first introduction. Great idea. Poop breaks down, why keep it locked up in plastic for years?

These BioBag Dog Waste Bags are easy to use. They are big enough for my husband's hand to fit in to. I use them with my Li'l Pals Waste Bag Dispenser.You do have to take your time tearing the bags apart. They are thin and if you tear too fast you can tear a hole in the bottom of the bag and the consequences are not pretty. I take my time tearing the bags and have not had any problems with them. I have been walking in 100 degree weather using them. Once they are tied I do not have any odor coming from them as I walk.

Great biodegradable bags! My only complaint is that I wish the bags were a little longer but other than that they're great! Also, the roll is pretty thick so you might have trouble fitting it in your bag dispenser (I just tear several of the bags from the roll so it's skinny enough to fit in my dispenser - not a problem for me).  I've already placed 3 orders of these bags and I plan on placing more orders in the future.
I have just ordered my second pack of 5.  These work great for my 60 lb dog.  We have had no problems whatsoever.  I'll keep ordering!

These bags have worked well for me. They are large enough (for my 70lb lab mix), they are sturdy enough (I've never broken through or ripped a seam), and they are truly biodegradable. My only gripe is that the rolls don't fit in standard bag dispensers- not that they claim to, but it would be nice if they did. In any case, I'll continue to buy these bags.

column9: Doesn't fit in bags-on-board style dog bag dispenser
column10: My singular complaint is that these bags don't fit in the dog bag dispenser I already own; The bags are not wound around a center core and they are loosely wound so they can't even be made to fit in my holder. (I even tried to remove half of the bags and kind of shoving them into the holder).Other than that, the size and quality of the bags is great. I have 2 small dogs (chihuahuas) and 1 bag works for picking up after both of them.I read the previous reviews and it's important to me that these bags comply to the strictest composting standards.

column9: Great bags on a roll, but treat them gently
column10: I love that these bags are on a roll and the Amazon price is great. A minor complaint is that an entire 20-bag roll doesn't fit into most standard-sized poop bag dispensers. However, it's not that much work to count and tear off a section of 10 bags and roll those up (start with the sealed end and work towards the open end).The one-star deduction is because these bags easily rip and puncture. Be careful when you are tearing each bag off as you can easily rip the bottom of the next bag on the roll. And don't even try to use that hole at the top of the bag; I'm not even sure what that hole is for. If you try to follow the diagram for closing the bag, the hole will tear open. Hopefully it will tear towards the top and not towards the bottom. Just tie a knot at the top and ignore that diagram. Also, if you drop a full bag on the sidewalk, it's very possible to put tiny holes in the bag when it hits the sand in the sidewalk cement. Hopefully a garbage can is nearby, because the bag is no longer odor-proof.

I don't have anything bad to say about these bags. It's pretty straightforward- they do the job and they're bio-degradable... done. The opening in the box for pulling the roll works well and they're easy to just throw in your pocket.The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars was ease of use of the bag. They're a tiny bit tough to open (but that's because the material sort of sticks to itself) and they could maybe tie a little easier. Let's just say I'm glad I have a small dog! Otherwise, they're great!

Although these bags don't fit into the roll carrier I already own, I still prefer them to other bags.  They are super easy to open in the dark, or wearing gloves, or wearing gloves in the dark.  They don't crinkle too much either so if you have one or two stuffed in your coat pocket it doesn't make a racket. After running through a 5-pack of boxes, I'm about to make my first re-order.

We are a pretty 'green' family and these biobags are great for those that want completely biodegradable doggie bags! They are not flimsy or thin - your hand feels very protected against doggie's busines. I did prefer the flat boxes vs the roll but this way has less packaging. The bags are nice a roomy and easy to tie. The directions on the actual bags are little confusing so we just tie it the way we like. The price is worth the peace of mind for me knowing that all these bags will eventually break down. Will continue to purchase!

I've had a Welsh Corgi for almost a year now.  I tried using a pooper-scooper and normal plastic bags at first.  A friend gave me a roll of the biobags for a puppy present.  I haven't looked back since.  They're easy to use.  :)

I used Bags on Board refills for several years but was looking to switch brands after BOB removed some of the texture that allowed you to open an individual bag.  I gave these a shot and am now a brand-convert.  The bags are easy to open and won't easily tear.  I wish they fit into the BOB dispenser; perhaps future versions will.  Overall, great!

column9: Amazing value for these quality bags!
column10: I will never stop buying these bags.  It's a great price for the number of bags you get.  It makes the frequency of buying poop bags tolerable!  They're easy to use, aren't a pain to tear off or unroll, grab easily... As far as poop bags go, haha, you really can't beat the price and product.
great product, but boxing it seems like a waste to me. other sites sell these without the box. (i hope they aren't just throwing the box away!)

We have three cats in our house and two litter boxes. I love these are biodegradable. We use World's Best Cat litter so all material is recycled back to the Earth. The bags are a great size for changing the boxes; we only use one bag to empty both out. The boxes are changed at least twice a day. They are not too big and not too small. It can be a little awkward at times scooping into the bag, but you get the hang of it after a few times. I also use the thirteen gallon bags for my shredder.

I really love these bags and use them with a Li'l Pals dispenser found here on Amazon.  The two together work great for my kids diapers.  One improvement, is make the bags a little longer, to fit diapers a bit better.  My daughter is wearing size 5 diapers, and if she goes up a size, I fear they won't fit well enough to allow me to tie a knot.  This goes for both Seventh Generation diapers and also the gDiaper compostable inserts.

Half of these bags are defective where one side is split (torn) from the top to the bottom. Makes it more like a tissue than a bag. Beware! I would return them except that it's not worth the trouble and fortunately I have a small dog:)
This is a Wonderful product to have. Knowing that this formula is made with organic ingredients gives me great pace of mind.

This product is not as creamy as normal milk chocolate beans.But it shows the original taste of dark chocolate and coffee beans.The light sweetness is free from cloyingness.Good choice for people who love dark chocolate and coffee.

column9: Things I remember from my time in Japan
column10: I've missed the flavors of Japan so now I cooking more and more of them.

column9: My pit bull won't eat these
column10: My first review didn't show up, so am trying again. These look and feel like plastic and my pit bull that will eat anything will not eat theses. Thirty bucks lost as I had to order regular pig ears

column9: My dogs can't get enough of these.
column10: My Mastiff and beagle love these. They last longer than normal pig ears, and seem to be less fatty. Great product!

I bought this spice @ Costco, I was not shore if I would be able to se it in my cooking, but I was wrong. I used every where soups, stews, grilling :, beef lam chicken and sea food!  this spice lasted me 6 month ... when I went back to Costco it was gone :( I was not able to find any where in a regular stores. so I am glad that I can order on Amazon :)

column9: Just as fantastic as the regular blue sky cola
column10: The closest store that I can find blue sky soda is an hour away and it sells it for $1.25 a can so finding it here was fantastic. The New Century soda doesn't differ too much from the regular soda, I can tell a slight difference but probably wouldn't notice unless I knew it was a different kind. Really fantastic, it is more expensive than coke or pepsi but at least I know that the ingredients weren't coming from a lab.

I LOVE this soda.  It is made from real cola nuts and sugar and you can taste the difference.  To be fair, I don't drink much soda and feel fairly guilty when I do.  Soda is just one of the top ten worst things you can consume on a regular basis, let's be honest.  So when I do get an occasional craving for it, I try to at least moderate the badness of the choice.  I started drinking this soda whenever I'd stop into a local pizza place, until I started craving the soda more than the pizza.  At almost $2 a can elsewhere, I decided to spring for a case on Amazon.Is this Coke or Pepsi?  NO!  If you love those brands, you may not like this and as it is the more expensive of the choices, you're probably better off sticking with those chemical and corn syrup-laden options.  However, if you are like me and eat mostly natural, organic and healthy fare (or want to), this is a delicious occasional indulgence.  It is unusual in taste... it is almost more carbonation than flavor, if that makes any sense, but it is very appealing to me.  While I hope the 24 cans I ordered last a long while, I will probably order more when they run out.

Good, but not a replacement for what I usually drink. I'm into soda mainly for the caffeine, so I was disappointed to find that this beverage is caffeine free. I love that it's organic, though, and the taste is still great... but if you're after a caffeine buzz, this is not the soda for you.

There are times when I just need a little sweet brown carbonation.Considering all the high fructose corn sweeteners and who knows what else in the major commercial sodas; I feel better with Blue Sky. It may not taste exactly like Coca Cola but it's close enough and has a good carbonation kick. Plus, the subscribe & save option makes the cost a bit better.

The flavor of this cola is true. This is what a cola drink should taste like, enough that I am on the subscribe and save deal. Two cases every 3 months. Understand that even though the ingredients are real, doesn't mean that the high carbs are good for you. I do share with friends and family and everyone loves it.

The Organic NEW Century Cola by Blue Sky is a nice crisp and refreshing drink.  Just a word of warning...it taste more like a cream soda than the standard COLA flavor; if you are wanting the standard COLA flavor that is also crisp you may try their other product that is just BLUE SKY COLA. It is still a delight to drink.

column9: Not for people who like HFCS and 'fake' cola
column10: I don't know what some of the negative reviewers are used to drinking, I'm guessing major name brands with HFCS as the main ingredient.We bought this at a local organic store, and loved it. We also love the Root Bear Encore by Blue Sky. It tastes like real cola did, back in the days before P and CC adulterated it with chemicals and flavor enhancers. It does not have a heavy after taste, nor does it taste like cough syrup. Maybe they reformulated the recipe since the negative reviews were posted. But I also think that if someone is used to commercial soda by major manufacturers, which tastes nothing like REAL cola, root bear, cream soda or ginger ale, then they will not like this.If you aren't sure about it, don't buy the 24 pack. Find it locally, try it, then buy it in bulk. And if you are not used to a chemical free, mainly organic, diet, stay away. Your tastebuds are skewed to crave things like HFCS and this definitely will affect your palate.

column9: Not the worst cola in the world, but not for me
column10: I have been on a kick trying to find the best natural/organic soda and I was excited to try this one. I found a 6 pack at a local health food store and rushed it home to the fridge with care. When we tried it the next day, after a few swigs my wife and I both noticed a weird "fruity" aftertaste... It almost tasted like prunes or sour grapes. I really enjoy a complex-tasting cola with different oils and spices, but this wasn't it. We didn't even come close to finishing the can and there are 5 of these left in our fridge. It's not horrible or simply undrinkable, but for me it's simply not good enough to waste the calories.

column9: Rather bland, but I like it.
column10: This soda has a more fruity flavor than Coca Cola or Pepsi, but not as fruity as Hansen's which I used to drink some years ago, but have not seen in the stores recently. Blue Sky is sweet and does not have much bite. I like it. I like that it's organic and has real cane sugar. It has no bad after taste. Our favorite of course is Flatt, which is very spicy and loaded with caffeine and vitamin C. There are those times when nothing but a cola will do, when it's just so thirst quenching. This cola fills the bill.

I love this Organic Cola. I must say, I was very hesitant when buying this, as I love the Switch Sparking Soda and have some Mexican Coke. I was very satisfied by the cola taste Blue Sky Cola gave. As usual after the first can, I was a little bit disappointed but like most things, it takes about THREE tries for you to either appreciate it or not like it. By the third, I was hooked by the taste and sweetness was perfect. I place it ahead of the Mexi Coke and plus Blue Sky lets us know on the can it is ORGANIC and one of the ingredients is a "cola Nut;" How can I go wrong? Definitely give it a try, and drink a few cans before reviewing the best tasting cola in my very humble opinion.

column9: Awesome cola in the healthiest form it can come in.
column10: I buy this soda because it is organic. Every ingredient is as safe as it can be. Organic sugar as the sweetener. Caramel coloring and tartaric acid, as opposed to phosphoric acid, that are derived naturally from the sugar and acid in grapes. Of course the cola flavoring is also organic. These days nearly every drink available at any given gas station is so loaded with toxins/carcinogens it's really actually not funny. So it's nice to have a truly delicious alternative that quite EASILY stands up to the flavor of Poopsi or Coo-Cooo Cola. I am ashamed I grew up drinking Coo-Coo cola, no really. They know darn well what they put into their drinks and they know it's not natural. If there is any shadow of a doubt about a chemical, why in the world would you still use it citing lack of evidence as reason for your continued use of artificial caramel coloring? If someone wants to smoke pot or ingest these ridiculous designer smokes, example K2, the government then tells you that you can not ingest/sell/buy that citing lack of suppporting evidence as the reason for your denial of anyone's human rights. All this is why I'm willing to spend a few extra dollars on a delicious cola that is made with non-toxic ingredients. Thank you Blue Sky and thank you Amazon for selling this tasty drink. It's a much better deal than buying it at the health food store.

I have been a Coke drinker for all of my life, and I still drink it sometimes.  But if given the opportunity, I would choose an organic sugar soda over HFCS any day.  It is an added bonus that this cola is caffeine free.  I get enough caffeine from my coffee.  I eat organic whenever possible, but I grew up on junk food and still get cravings.  I thank the stars for organic junk food!!!
Best cola I have ever had in my life!!!! I usually don't drink sodas but I am hooked on this one.

Coke and Pepsi used to be made with cane sugar, like this stuff. And as soon as I tasted it, it reminded me of what cola tasted like back then. A pizza shop gives me a free coca-cola with my lunch, and when I took it home and tasted it, it had no cola taste, and that fructose overload. Popped open a can of this blue-sky organic cola, and the difference was major. Sweet, but delicious sweet.

I am not a soda drinker, but on occasion I choose this one. It is organic and really good. All of the food I consume is organic so I'm not used to high-fructose corn syrup and chemicals in the popular sodas. This of course will taste different than those, but that's a GOOD thing!

LOVE LOVE LOVE the Blue Sky Colas. We've started eating better and have given up cokes and similar drinks. Every once in a while, however, we crave a sweet, fizzy drink. We've found these are excellent substitutes. They certainly have a different taste, but over the past few months we have grown to prefer these over a real coke. The cane sugar/syrup doesn't give you that 'yuck' feeling in your stomach after drinking, either. Can't say enough good about them.

column9: Where does the caramel color come from?
column10: I purchased this soda because of concerns about the caramel coloring being used in colas.  I thought I would try the organic blue sky cola, and while I think it tastes fine, I noticed that the "caramel color" in the ingredient list does not indicate where it comes from or how it is processed.See Link below:[...]FDA Urged to Prohibit Carcinogenic "Caramel Coloring"I've emailed the company a few days ago, but to date, no reply.  Anyone know about this?

column9: It's not cheap, but it's the best "pure cane sugar" cola available nationally
column10: With all due respect to Pepsi for at least trying, "Throwback" isn't for all cola drinkers fleeing high fructose corn syrup; it's for regular Pepsi drinkers.  After trying at least four twelve packs, I simply cannot get past the Pepsi flavoring (which I have never liked).  I recently spent some time in Texas, and H-E-B (which all but dominates the Texas grocery market) came out with its own "pure cane sugar" cola, which costs half of "Throwback" and just over a third the cost of Blue Sky, and it is great stuff.  Unfortunately, they don't do mail order.  So, until I can get my hands on more, Blue Sky is the best available unless you like paying more for the microbrewery equivalent to "pure cane sugar" cola, organic or non-organic.Oh, and curiously, Amazon is selling the organic version of Blue Sky cola for the same price as the non-organic six-packs you might find in your local grocer's Natural Foods section.

I have been addicted to Coke-a-Cola since I was in High school (2000-2004). Eventually I got to the point where I preferred drinking then eating. I gained a lot of weight and went through horrible caffeine withdrawals (if I went more then 12 hours without my coke -a- Cola caffeine fix). I tried to quit soda with caffeine/hfcs many times but eventually always giving in because Coke always helps with my migraines. This soda became not only a substitute but by favorite,  It has a  lot of sugar and that is why I only gave it a 4/5.  I prefer this one verse the other COla.  This one is less expensive and organic compared to the Blue Sky Cola (vs this one which is Organic Blue Sky New Century Cola).  I usually water it down with over a cup of ice to dilute the sugar. Score: 4/5 It is literally the best Soda out there with or without HFCs.  It didn't get 5/5 because of how much sugar in each can. I  end up having to dilute it with lots of ice.I  had always been super picky of how my Cola was. It needed to COke Cola it needed to be fresh, crisp, and super cold.  I am one of those people that can tell the different between coke and cola... I now perfer this one.  FHC's are horrible for your body  and I do see great improvement and alleviation from some of my lupus symptoms since I stopped taking in HFCs (through Coke-a-Cola)  .

OK, allow me to make the following disclaimer prior to the review:I have drank a LOT of soda in my life...Coke, Pepsi, RC, store brands, Lemon-Limes, Oranges, Grapes, Cherry, Root Beers,etc., in both Regular and Diet versions of all the above. I generally do not purchase "organic" products b/c of the associated costs, so it might be that if you are likely to purchase this product, you might deem my tastebuds dead anyway. Having said that:A vegan co-worker had a six pack of this product in the office fridge of which five cans have remained for about a week and half. I asked him about 30 minutes ago if he minded if I tried one of his sodas, he said sure, that he didn't care for it, but he could see how others would. Me being a die-hard carnivore, I mistakenly thought his dislike of the product to be a good sign. Wrong!This is not good. It starts off fizzy, then you get the cola taste, then you get some sort of bizarre tannic sort of aftertaste. I couldn't figure out what it was, then saw on the label that one of the ingredients is tartaric acid (from grapes). Ugh. After several more sips, I concluded that the aftertaste is the same as that of very tart, almost sour grapes.I still have half the can left. Slow sipping doesn't help, neither does a quick gulp. I thought Moxie was the most "different" soda I had ever tasted, but I think this has it beat. To each his own, I suppose, but buyer, you have been warned.

My 7 y/o daughter and I LOVE LOVE LOVE these crackers.  They are dense and crunchy and hold up well to soups and cheese toppers.  They do not have as full of a cheese flavor as a Cheez-it-type cracker; these are more subtle.  They are also not for you if you are looking for a flaky Ritz-type cracker.

column9: If You Want to Make a Smoothie with It FORGET IT!
column10: It really isn't a POWDER.  It is more like a finely ground loose tea and won't blend in a smoothie because it is not ground finely enough.  Get Tradition brand if you want to make smoothies.  (It isn't organic, but at least it blends and it is also pure, meaning unsweetened.) Items arrived sticky and starting to melt.  Discolored - they were all kind of brown.  Super tough and chewy.  Flavors were off.  Wouldn't recommend to anyone.  Overall very disappointed.

These giant gummy bears are horrendous! They taste like ****! They smell just as bad! Note in the picture that the blue raspberry bear is GREEN! I only made it a couple of bites into my blue raspberry one. My husband thought it was awful too.
This is a LOT of money.  I can purchase this same thing from Dunkin Donuts storefor $11.99. I do not know who came up with this price but it is totally over priced.The coffe is great!

This kcup was pretty tasty once you get past the weird smell while brewing.  It was described as a bit "funky" by some coworkers.  I tried it out anyway and was impressed.  It's very smooth and has a nice pumpkin flavor.  It gets better as it cools.  The clove flavor is only slighty noticeable which is a very good thing.  The flavor was pretty close to pumpkin pie.  This would mix really well with a good french vanilla kcup and some cinnamon.  The flavor is light years better than the Green Mountain pumpkin spice kcup. It took me a year to get through that box.  I threw out the last few.
I normally prefer Starbucks pumpkin lattes to Dunkin donuts' but these kcups are amazing!  Won't have to make my daily Starbucks visit!

Sooooooo delicious!!!  This coffee is so good that it's almost orgasmic!  I have tried a lot of coffees and none have ever beat out DD's Original Blend...NONE.  And now I can buy it in K-cup style; it is a little pricey, but you can best believe I will scour the web for a better deal.  This stuff beats Starebuck's Sunrise Morning Blend--hands down!!!
This is the ultimate in flavored coffee. Excellent body. Enjoy it while you can. But purchase at a Dunkin Donuts if at all possible since buying elsewhere is artificially high.
The best instant cafe maxwell house has but unfortunately they havs discontinued it.  I am very disappointed and would like the decision to discontinue reconsidered
The jam is great! Everybody loves it. If it were a little bit less sweet, it would be even better.
The product was excellent and so was the customer service. I will a returning customer.

Butter rum has always been my favorite Life Saver flavor. I don't know why they are so difficult to find around town, but I am glad Amazon is selling them in bulk. I ended up getting them much cheaper than I usually do, when I am lucky enough to see them for sale in an airport.

This oil is as good as the Dr. Oz show said it would be. I use it for everything. It does not really have a flavor of it's own.It was very difficult to find in my area so I took a leap of faith and bought the jug full. The only other issue was that I had to have my husband buy me a transfer pump because you can't just pour out what you need. All in all a big hit in our house

I buy this olive oil for my oldest son. He has Hypoglycemia and he uses it as part of his diet. This olive oil is as close as you can get to organic olive oil and has very few if any chemicals. It works out fine for my son and his special hypoglycemic diet. Its made in Greece.

column9: Hazelnut flavor was way too strong
column10: I read a previous review that complimented this hazelnut flavored coffee as having just the right amount of flavor.  I could not disagree more.  From the first sip until I threw all 3 boxes away I could not tolerate the overwhelming hazelnut flavor and I love hazelnut.  I tried using one regular pod with one hazelnut but it was still intolerable. Live and learn I suppose, but all that that was offered was the 3 boxes of 18 servings.On another note I really enjoy the Baronet Decaf Medium Roast is excellent and I have purchased it multiple times.

Love this coffee!  Tastes fresh and can taste the hazelnut flavor (but it's not overwhelming).  Also, I'm pretty sensitive to caffeine and this is one of those decaf coffees that is truly low caffeine (some decafs have higher levels).  But best of all, it tastes great.
Baronet coffee pods make a great cup of coffee and it is always fresh. Thanks to the sealed pouch for each pod.

After trying several, and I mean several, other brands of coffee pods, I can tell you, flat out, Baronet, in ANY flavor, blows the other brands out of the water (no pun intended!) PERIOD!  It is the difference between "artificial" tasting flavors, and the real, true, extract of whatever flavor you want. DO NOT go any further in your pod experience without  knowing what "excellence" is.....it's Baronet. Enjoy,
love the water, but the order came from italy and the freight killed me.buy it at sams club instead and you'll have the same great water on someone elses freight bill
Great water.  Glad I can purchase on line because the six packs do not appear to be available in the grocery stores.

column9: Not the same as the box
column10: We love Nilla Vanilla wafers here, but these were not the same taste or texture as the usual grocery store boxes.  Still a good cookie, but crispier and with a hint of lemon not found in the originals.  Your decision!

column9: I like these better than Nilla
column10: As the other gentleman described - crisper - I thought i almost tasted a hint of lemon. I like these better.  I had these on a Southwest flight and was trying to find them to buy like normal Nilla boxes at a grocery store.

These are not Nilla® brand vanilla wafers by Nabisco. They are generic vanilla wafers made by Nabisco. This is not to say they are bad; they're just not what most of us think of as Nabisco vanilla wafers. They are a little smaller, a little flatter (no curve), and a little crisper than the Nilla® brand wafers. They are larger than the Nilla® brand mini-wafers. I'm not disappointed in my purchase; I just had no idea that Nabisco made a generic product of this type.

I could no longer find these in the store I go to so I decided to look for them online. Finally saw these and went ahead and bought them. Just as delicious as I remembered! Lasted for awhile and got here nice and quick. Definitly going to purchase these again!
My husband and I tried the crisps at a party, and it was love at first bite.  The small bags are supposed to have 3 servings, but it is hard not to eat an entire bag at once.
This product was very tasteless and boring. I felt like I was eating packaging material..awful awful awful awful!!!!!! Very bland!!!

column9: good but not as great as the smaller packs
column10: The larger bags of these are not as good as the smaller bags. Even my 2 year old agrees. The pieces are smaller and there's not as much seasoning on them as the 3oz bags or whatever size the smaller ones are. It won't take long for us to eat these but we will buy the smaller sizes from now on. Sad because these were a little less in cost. Oh well.

I have been looking for saladitos for years it seems.  I to grew up in Arizona so I grew up on these and havent been able to find them since.  These are big and very tasty.  I am pleased and glad I decided to get them.  I was hesitant about doing it because if they were no good I would have been stuck but they are GREAT.  The process was also very smooth and I had them very quick.  I will be buying more when I finish my 19 bags LOL

column9: I looooove this popcorn but can't find it anywhere to buy!
column10: Unfortunately none of the stores local to me sell this patricular type of Smart Balance Popcorn.  I love this movie theater Smart Balance because it needs no extra butter or salt added to it.  I just wish I could find it in-store or online to buy.  The only time I've been able to buy it was in 2009 when I was out-of-state.

I bought a box of Smart Balance popcorn at Big Lots a few years ago and I think it's pretty fair to say I've been obsessing over it ever since.
